# Flour Bakery Review

Published  By [Julia](https://www.savorytooth.com/author/julia/) [1 Comment](https://www.savorytooth.com/flour-bakery/#comments)This post may contain [affiliate links](https://www.savorytooth.com/privacy-policy/).

Flour Bakery started in Boston’s South End neighborhood in 2000, and today has nine locations in Boston and Cambridge. They’re known for breakfast pastries, cookies, pies, cakes, salads, and sandwiches — all of which are prepared daily. This review is based primarily on their Beacon Hill location.

## Flour Bakery (Beacon Hill)

**Overall Rating:** ★★★★★ out of 5 stars  
**Address:** 209 Cambridge St, Boston, MA 02114  
**Neighborhood:** Beacon Hill  
**Perfect For:** High quality foods in an inviting atmosphere  
**Hours:** Mon – Fri 6:30am – 7pm, Sat – Sun 8am – 6pm  
**Reservations:** No  
**Parking:** Street  
**Links:** [Website](https://www.flourbakery.com/), [Menu](https://www.flourbakery.com/menu)  
**Cost:** $15 per person (food only)

Upon entering the cafe, food can be ordered at the counter for either take-out or dine-in. Next to the ordering counter is a display of fresh savory and sweet treats for your perusal, including their famous sticky buns. After ordering, you can select your own table and food will be brought out to you.

The Beacon Hill location has two stories of seating: the ground floor has some bar seating and a few small tables but the space is mostly taken up by people who are ordering, waiting, and picking up orders, and upstairs is primarily for dine-in guests with more available tables and bar seating. I sat at the upstairs bar table, which had great views of the street below.

The breakfast pizza is a beautiful creation: an egg, shredded parmesan cheese, creme fraiche, slice of tomato, and arugula atop a round brioche crust. It’s perfectly sized for one person. It was full of savory flavors and the cheese had a delicious consistency. I would enjoy having this again.

I normally don’t like pop tarts, but I decided to try their raspberry pop tart. It had a thick raspberry filling, super flaky crust, and a sweet glaze on top. This pop tart far surpasses the packaged supermarket version, although it was a bit too sweet for my liking.

I also ordered their sugar brioche bun — a plain buttery brioche coated in vanilla sugar — which was airy and delightful.

Flour’s most famous pastry is the sticky bun — a brioche dough swirled with cinnamon sugar and topped with caramelized honey and toasted pecan gooeyness. You can ask for it to be heated. It’s very sweet and intense so I recommend splitting it with a friend.

A number of made-to-order sandwiches and salads are also offered at Flour. I tried their chopped Greek salad, which surpassed my expectations for a place that is primarily a bakery (almost as good as my [homemade Greek salad with avocado dressing](https://www.savorytooth.com/best-greek-salad/)). It has yogurt marinated chicken with feta cheese, chickpeas, kalamata olives, and green goddess dressing. I liked how it tasted refreshing and had a generous amount of protein.

In the past, I have also ordered items not photographed here, including:

* **chicken tikka masala naan**: flavorful chicken with green chutney, tamarind sauce, paneer cheese, and cucumbers
* **breakfast egg sandwich**: sausage with cheddar cheese, arugula, tomato, and dijonaise
* **lemon ginger scone**: lemon juice and zest with fresh ginger

All of these items tasted great, and I can tell that everything is consistently made with fresh ingredients and well executed. I am also pleasantly surprised that a bakery’s savory creations are as thoughtful and delicious as its sweet ones. Additionally, I’ve appreciated how Flour consistently provides enthusiastic and welcoming service at the ordering counter.

I look forward to returning again and trying out slices of their Boston cream pie, midnight chocolate cake, and lemon raspberry cake. I’d also be interested in trying more savory dishes such as the achiote chicken sandwich.

**Levain Bakery,** pronounced as (luh-ven),[[1]](#cite_note-1) is a retail bakery that opened in 1995 and is located at 167 [West 74th Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_74th_Street "West 74th Street"), on the [Upper West Side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_West_Side "Upper West Side") neighborhood of [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"). In June 2000 a second retail location was opened for seasonal business at 354 Montauk Highway, [Wainscott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wainscott,_New_York "Wainscott, New York"), in the [Hamptons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamptons "Hamptons") area of eastern [Long Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island "Long Island"). A third store is located in the [Harlem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlem "Harlem") neighborhood of [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"). In 2017, a fourth store was opened near the original location on the Upper West Side, and since then three more locations have opened on the [Upper East Side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_East_Side "Upper East Side") and in [NoHo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NoHo,_Manhattan "NoHo, Manhattan") and [Williamsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamsburg,_Brooklyn "Williamsburg, Brooklyn").[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3) In 2020, Levain opened their first store outside of New York, in [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_(Washington,_D.C.) "Georgetown (Washington, D.C.)"), [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[4]](#cite_note-4) In 2023, Levain opened a location in the Larchmont area of Los Angeles. As of June 2024, there are seventeen locations: nine in the New York City area, two each in Chicago, Washington D.C., and Boston, and one each in Los Angeles and Philadelphia.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Levain_Bakery&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Storefrontwainscott.jpg/250px-Storefrontwainscott.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Storefrontwainscott.jpg)

Front of Wainscott store

Founded and co-owned by Constance McDonald and Pamela Weekes, the bakery initially opened to serve a variety of fresh-baked [artisanal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slow_Food "Slow Food") breads.[[6]](#cite_note-6) The bakery has since become notable for its 6-ounce chocolate chip walnut cookies.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

McDonald and Weekes developed the signature cookie recipe while training for an [Ironman Triathlon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ironman_Triathlon "Ironman Triathlon"). They discovered they needed a large number of calories to offset the rigors of training and decided on a traditional chocolate chip cookie, but much bigger. The 6-ounce chocolate chip walnut cookie served the purpose and ultimately became a signature item in their bakery. The cookie has spawned copycats.[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9) In 1998 Levain Bakery expanded its cookie business to include mail order and in 2022 expanded their services to offer catering as well as nationwide shipping through Doordash.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

## Appearances in media

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Levain_Bakery&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Appearances in media")]

The Food Network has featured Levain Bakery in episodes of [Throwdown with Bobby Flay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Throwdown_with_Bobby_Flay "Throwdown with Bobby Flay"), Roker on the Road, [Unwrapped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unwrapped "Unwrapped"), Top 5, The Best Thing I Ever Ate, Sweet Dreams, and Worth It. In December 2007, Levain Bakery was featured on an episode of [Fashionably Late with Stacy London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashionably_Late_with_Stacy_London "Fashionably Late with Stacy London"). In June 2008, Budget Travel listed Levain Bakery #3 of “50 Reasons You Love New York City.”[[11]](#cite_note-11) They have been featured in the following books:

* *The Slow Food Guide To New York City*, Patrick Martins and Ben Watson.
* *New York's 50+ Best Places to Enjoy Dessert*, Andrea DiNoto and Paul Stiga.
* *A Day at the Beach*, Helen Schulman.
* *Cook What You Love*, Bob and Melinda Blanchard.
* *Jodi’s Shortcuts 2000* and *Jodi’s Shortcuts 2002*, Jodi Della Femina and Daniel Benedict
* Food and the city, Ina Yalof.

## Location & Hours

Clinton St Baking Co. is a chef-owned classic American restaurant & bakery located on NYC’s Lower East Side. Since 2001, we’ve maintained our mom and pop roots by using the highest quality ingredients from local purveyors we know and trust. We're open 7 days a week and serve breakfast, brunch, dinner and dessert with a full pastry display, takeout window, specialty coffee drinks to go, plus milkshakes, liquor, wine & beer. We take reservations via @resy and also welcome walk-ins (first come, first served). Visit our outpost in DUMBO, Brooklyn at the Time Out Market New York!

The **Clinton Street Baking Company & Restaurant** (CSBC) is an American bakery and restaurant. It is located at 4 [Clinton Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_Street "Clinton Street") (between East [Houston Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Street "Houston Street") and [Stanton Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanton_Street "Stanton Street")), on the [Lower East Side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_East_Side "Lower East Side") of [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").[[1]](#cite_note-google1-1)[[2]](#cite_note-google2-2)[[3]](#cite_note-google3-3)

The restaurant is noted especially for its pancakes, its burgers, and its biscuits and other fresh-baked goods.[[3]](#cite_note-google3-3)[[4]](#cite_note-4) In December 2010, *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* described it as a "brunch magnet", and *[The New York Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Daily_News "The New York Daily News")* said the "legendary" dining destination was "the city's hottest breakfast nook".[[5]](#cite_note-nytimes1-5)[[6]](#cite_note-nydailynews1-6) *[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")* called it a "cult favorite".[[7]](#cite_note-autogenerated1-7) In 2011, *Poor Taste Magazine* rated it # 1 in its list of the 100 Best Brunch Spots in America.[[8]](#cite_note-poortastemag1-8)[[9]](#cite_note-villagevoice1-9)

## Restaurant

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Restaurant")]

The restaurant seats 32 people.[[6]](#cite_note-nydailynews1-6) It is located on Clinton Street, just off Houston Street, which the *[New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(magazine) "New York (magazine)")* magazine described as the "hippest restaurant row" on the Lower East Side.[[10]](#cite_note-nytimes2002-10) The restaurant is next to an 1853 [Romanesque Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanesque_Revival "Romanesque Revival") traditional synagogue, [Congregation Chasam Sopher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congregation_Chasam_Sopher "Congregation Chasam Sopher").[[10]](#cite_note-nytimes2002-10)[[11]](#cite_note-gothamist2006-11)[[12]](#cite_note-nymag2005-12)[[13]](#cite_note-13) It attracts a weekend brunch line that stretches around the corner of the block, which includes New York foodies and many foreign tourists.[[6]](#cite_note-nydailynews1-6)[[11]](#cite_note-gothamist2006-11)[[14]](#cite_note-nypost1-14)[[15]](#cite_note-eater1-15)

### Menu

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Menu")]

The restaurant serves refined [comfort food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comfort_food "Comfort food") and baked items, which are made daily on its premises, with breakfast (which it serves all day), lunch, brunch, and dinner.[[2]](#cite_note-google2-2)[[15]](#cite_note-eater1-15)[[16]](#cite_note-google4-16)[[17]](#cite_note-google5-17)[[18]](#cite_note-18)

Among the items that it is known for are its blueberry pancakes. *New York* magazine called them the best pancakes in town.[[12]](#cite_note-nymag2005-12) February is "Pancake Month" at the restaurant.[[19]](#cite_note-metromix2-19)[[20]](#cite_note-20)

It is also noted for its fluffy buttermilk biscuit sandwich with home-made tomato jam, and lauded for its baked goods, including its [scones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scone_(bread) "Scone (bread)") and muffins.[[12]](#cite_note-nymag2005-12)[[14]](#cite_note-nypost1-14)[[16]](#cite_note-google4-16)[[21]](#cite_note-21)[[22]](#cite_note-22)[[23]](#cite_note-nymag1-23) Its home-made desserts, including muffins, organic apple crumb, chocolate cake, maple-bourbon-pecan pie, creamy pumpkin cheesecake, and cherry pie, are topped with ice cream from the [Brooklyn Ice Cream Factory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Ice_Cream_Factory "Brooklyn Ice Cream Factory").[[17]](#cite_note-google5-17)[[24]](#cite_note-24)[[25]](#cite_note-25)[[26]](#cite_note-26)[[27]](#cite_note-27)

Its meals include [cage-free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cage-free "Cage-free") eggs, omelets, granola, brioches, grilled organic [free range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_range "Free range") chicken, buttermilk [fried chicken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fried_chicken "Fried chicken"), hamburgers, large warm buttermilk biscuits, cheese [grits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grits "Grits") fries, salads, and market soups.[[2]](#cite_note-google2-2)[[10]](#cite_note-nytimes2002-10)[[12]](#cite_note-nymag2005-12)[[16]](#cite_note-google4-16)[[28]](#cite_note-metromix1-28)[[29]](#cite_note-mirror1-29)[[30]](#cite_note-30) Drinks include lime [squash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squash_(drink) "Squash (drink)") and [bellinis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellini_(cocktail) "Bellini (cocktail)").[[31]](#cite_note-31)[[32]](#cite_note-32)

### Owners

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Owners")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/ff/DeDe_Lahman_and_Neil_Kleinberg.jpg/250px-DeDe_Lahman_and_Neil_Kleinberg.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DeDe_Lahman_and_Neil_Kleinberg.jpg)

Owners Neil Kleinberg and DeDe Lahman

It is owned by a husband-and-wife team of restaurateurs, seasoned chef Neil Kleinberg and DeDe Lahman.[[1]](#cite_note-google1-1)[[16]](#cite_note-google4-16) Kleinberg had originally planned to open the business with another partner, but Lahman, who was a former [advice columnist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advice_columnist "Advice columnist") and a [freelance writer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freelance_writer "Freelance writer") at the time running an apparel company, bought the partner out.[[11]](#cite_note-gothamist2006-11)[[33]](#cite_note-33) Kleinberg has responsibility for the restaurant's kitchen. Lahman is the restaurant's catering director and handles back-end responsibilities such as public relations.[[11]](#cite_note-gothamist2006-11)[[19]](#cite_note-metromix2-19)[[34]](#cite_note-34)

### History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: History")]

The restaurant began in 2001 as a bakery and a small coffee cafe, and over time became a full-fledged seven-days-a-week restaurant with a [liquor license](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquor_license "Liquor license").[[11]](#cite_note-gothamist2006-11) Kleinberg and Lahman host free cooking and healthy eating classes at the restaurant for neighborhood children.[[1]](#cite_note-google1-1)[[35]](#cite_note-35)

### Awards and accolades

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Awards and accolades")]

In December 2010, *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* described it as a "brunch magnet", and *[The New York Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Daily_News "The New York Daily News")* said that the "legendary" dining destination was "the city's hottest breakfast nook".[[5]](#cite_note-nytimes1-5)[[6]](#cite_note-nydailynews1-6) *Time* called it a "cult favorite".[[7]](#cite_note-autogenerated1-7)[[9]](#cite_note-villagevoice1-9) The restaurant has been one of [Zagat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zagat "Zagat")'s top picks on the Lower East Side.[[36]](#cite_note-usatoday1-36)

*Time* magazine cited it for having New York City's best pancakes in both 2005 and 2008.[[12]](#cite_note-nymag2005-12)[[23]](#cite_note-nymag1-23) The restaurant is noted especially for its fresh-baked goods.[[3]](#cite_note-google3-3) *[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")* described it as a "charming cafe with outstanding cherry pie".[[36]](#cite_note-usatoday1-36)

In January 2009, [Bobby Flay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Flay "Bobby Flay") challenged the owners of the restaurant to a "blueberry pancake showdown", which was filmed in an episode of *[Throwdown! with Bobby Flay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Throwdown!_with_Bobby_Flay "Throwdown! with Bobby Flay")* at the restaurant.[[37]](#cite_note-37)[[38]](#cite_note-38) In 2010, Kleinberg won [Godiva Chocolatier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godiva_Chocolatier "Godiva Chocolatier")'s SWEETest Challenge Award for his Warm Upside Down Pear Cake with pecan ice cream, caramel sauce, and [pecan brittle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pecan_brittle "Pecan brittle") at the third annual [Food Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_Network "Food Network") New York City Wine & Food Festival.[[39]](#cite_note-39)

In 2011, *Poor Taste Magazine* rated it # 1 in its list of the "100 Best Brunch Spots in America".[[8]](#cite_note-poortastemag1-8)[[9]](#cite_note-villagevoice1-9) In 2011, [Zagat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zagat "Zagat") ranked it 2nd out of 204, among traditional American restaurants in New York City.[[40]](#cite_note-40)

## Cookbook

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Cookbook")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/Clinton_Street_Baking_Co._%26_Restaurant_Eggs_Benedict.jpg/250px-Clinton_Street_Baking_Co._%26_Restaurant_Eggs_Benedict.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Clinton_Street_Baking_Co._&_Restaurant_Eggs_Benedict.jpg)

CSBC [Eggs Benedict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eggs_Benedict "Eggs Benedict")

The *Clinton St. Baking Company Cookbook: Breakfast, Brunch & Beyond from New York's Favorite Neighborhood Restaurant* (2010) was authored by Kleinberg and Lahman.[[41]](#cite_note-41) The book includes what *The New York Times* describes as the "celebrated" pancake recipe served at the restaurant, as well as the restaurant's other most popular recipes for [Eggs Benedict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eggs_Benedict "Eggs Benedict") and other preparations.[[5]](#cite_note-nytimes1-5)[[6]](#cite_note-nydailynews1-6) The book was identified by Julia Moskin of *The New York Times* as one of the year's best cookbooks, in December 2010.[[5]](#cite_note-nytimes1-5)

## Sister restaurant

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Sister restaurant")]

The owners opened up an eco-conscious sister restaurant, named "Community Food and Juice", that also serves American food.[[42]](#cite_note-nysun1-42) It is located at 2893 [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_(Manhattan) "Broadway (Manhattan)") between [112th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/112th_Street_(Manhattan) "112th Street (Manhattan)") and [113th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/113th_Street_(Manhattan) "113th Street (Manhattan)") Streets in [Morningside Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morningside_Heights "Morningside Heights"), Manhattan, and has an open kitchen and a bi-level dining room.[[43]](#cite_note-eater2-43)[[44]](#cite_note-nytimes3-44)[[45]](#cite_note-45)

## In popular culture

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: In popular culture")]

The restaurant and its pancakes are mentioned in the 2011 book *Where I Belong*, by Gwendolyn Heasley.[[46]](#cite_note-46)

## About Clinton St. Baking Company

American restaurant known for its weekend brunch and pancakes, with a takeout section.

## What People Are Saying

from Google

"Waiting time during public holidays can get crazy so be prepared. Nonetheless, the restaurant was really good. The service was top notch. Our server named Matthew was very kind and very informative and helpful. The food was so good. We had the buttermilk biscuit sandwich and also the pancakes with chocolate. It's really nice 100% would recommend."

"If there’s one NYC spot that truly lives up to its breakfast reputation, it’s Clinton St. Baking Company. I finally tried their famous pancakes this weekend, and let me tell you.. they deserve every bit of the hype. Fluffy, lil crispy on outside, and served with their homemade maple butter sauce that’s honestly addictive.. it’s what makes this dish so uniquely delicious. We also ordered the raspberry yogurt cupcake (light, tangy, and perfectly balanced) and their fried chicken, which was crisped to perfection with a beautiful honey dressing and some hot sauce that tied everything together. Every bite felt like comfort food done right. Simple ingredients, but executed flawlessly. The best part? Despite it being a weekend morning, I didn’t have to wait in the infamous line (which can get really long). I booked ahead on Resy, and it made the experience seamless, definitely recommend doing that if you’re planning a visit. Bottom line: come hungry, book ahead, and don’t skip the pancakes. They might just be the best in NYC"

★★★★★

"Clinton Street Baking Co. absolutely lives up to the hype. The service and atmosphere were amazing — warm, welcoming, and super friendly. The staff recommended the blueberry pancakes and OMG that was the best decision ever. They were so soft, fluffy, and just incredible! We also ordered the spinach & mushroom omelette with sourdough bread, and honestly… I could cry, it was THAT good. Perfectly cooked, flavorful, and comforting in every way. The latte and cappuccino were smooth, rich, and the perfect pairing. Overall, such a delightful experience. Highly recommend this place to anyone looking for fantastic food and great vibes. I’m definitely coming back! 🫶✨"

★★★★★

"Cool popular diner. A weekend reservation is a struggle but got one on a Thursday - seems like they do lots of walk ins also if you wanna just try that way! Got the classic blueberry pancakes (warm maple butter to die for) and the fried chicken sandwich. The fries were standout and sandwich juicy. Chai latte was massive and creamy but our drinks did come out same time as food so a little order of service blip there. Server was great, attentive and friendly and I would go back."

★★★★★

"Delicious breakfast. We got the hot chocolate, coffee, cream cheese + strawberry biscuit, potato pancakes (latke) , and the amazing blueberry pancakes. Everything was soo good. There were a lot of people waiting but it was a short wait for 2 people at the counter. Well worth the visit"

When husband and wife team, Neil Kleinberg and DeDe Lahman, opened Clinton St. Baking Co in April 2001, their mission was to make the best baked goods in the city, using the freshest ingredients, hand-mixed in small batches. They bought dark French-roast coffee, ground it in house, and hired a college student to serve it with warm muffins, biscuits and scones. Soon the locals stumbled in, and mornings on Clinton Street came alive. Rumors of Neil's simple, delicious omelets, sandwiches and soups moved people to cluster, then crowd, and now form lines up the block. We're an unassuming storefront, with just 32 seats, and yet people travel from Tribeca and Toronto, and Tokyo to eat here. New York Magazine voted Neil's blueberry pancakes best in the city ( twice! ). Naturally, we agree, but the locals still come in for no-fuss-just-plain good food: a juicy burger and Brooklyn Lager, fried oysters with a spicy bloody Mary, or a decadent hot fudge sundae made with artisanal vanilla ice cream from the Brooklyn Ice Cream Factory. The lore about our brunch lines we cannot deny... but try us at dinner, when the lights are dim, the crowds calm, and the food is anything but ordinary, says the New York Observer. Okay, and Yes: You can still get a stack of pancakes after dark. Co-owner of Clinton Street and Community Restaurant, Neil Kleinberg raised himself in a crazy kitchen in Flatbush, Brooklyn, among 4 kids, 2 parents, 16 neighborhood cousins, and 6 aunts and uncles. At 10 years old, he became a one-boy culinary wonder who'd do anything to avoid his mother's famous dish: chicken in a pot ( the only dish in her repertoire ). His lunches, made assembly-line style for his relatives, were simple but classic: Tuna fish sandwiches on rye toast with crisp lettuce and beefsteak tomatoes, fresh corned beef w/mustard and sauerkraut, turkey and Swiss w/ Russian and slaw.

Huckleberry is an American cafe/bakery that opened last month in Santa Monica. I went there with my husband, my BFF and her husband for what I thought would be a nice Sunday brunch. Hubster and I enter through the front door, he grabs a seat, I stand in line to order our food. The place is packed. I fall in love with the decor, it's modern Americana with wood tables, red chairs and a chalkboard menu. It feels like a San Francisco cafe that was gently picked up and moved to sunny Santa Monica. # Huckleberry — Bakery, Café, Catering

# huckleberry bakery & cafe

Huckleberry is THE Santa Monica Farmers’ Market bakery, café and marketplace that’s a one-stop destination for beautiful pastries, artisan coffee, gourmet provisions and a casual breakfast or lunch. We’re a living expression of the hard work and beauty that the local farmers provide us, and we’ve become a beloved, neighborhood gathering place since opening in 2009.

# THANKSGIVING CATERING

This year, we’re welcoming a new chef and a refreshed Thanksgiving menu, bringing a little something new to the table while keeping the dishes that make the holiday itself something to be grateful for.

We’re starting with **Milo + Olive breads and a whole new lineup of spreads**: from Cranberry Walnut Goat Cheese and Whipped Pumpkin Butter to Vegan Spinach & Artichoke Dip. Add a box of our house-made cornbread, pull-apart brioche rolls, or buttermilk biscuits, and you might find yourself filling up before dinner even starts.

For the main event, there’s **Mary’s Free Range Turkey with all the fixings**: slow-simmered gravy, Braised Leek & Celery Stuffing, our very special “Marry Me” Mashed Potatoes, Baked Mac & Cheese, Sweet Potato Casserole, Blistered Haricot Vert, Autumn Harvest Salad, and Cranberry Sauce.

And for your second dessert stomach: **Pumpkin Pie, Chocolate Pecan Pie, Apple Tarte Tatin, Turkey-Shaped Ginger Cookies**, and **Sweet Rose Creamery** **Ice Cream**.

Let Huckleberry handle dinner. You handle the people, the politics, and the inevitable leftovers, which, naturally, we’ve prepared for with a next-day Leftover Sandwich Kit.

***Thanksgiving orders are available for pickup on Thanksgiving Day, with orders closing Thursday, November 19 at 6pm.***

There’s so much to take in at this perennial Venice hotspot. The glass pastry case in the front will likely be the first thing to catch your eye, a sprawling treasure trove filled with beautifully executed cakes, pies, and galettes. At breakfast, try the flaky tahini or ham and cheese croissant. Grab a loaf of bread for the road or settle in for a larger meal of a tuna conserva sandwich and kale salad. If the Basque cheesecake is available, make sure to try a slice. On weekends, the outdoor seating area remains one of the vibiest patios in all of Los Angeles. Best advice for first-timers: Take a number and look at everyone around you to figure out the flow of the line.

**Dahlia Bakery** is a pastry shop in [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle")'s [Belltown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belltown,_Seattle "Belltown, Seattle") neighborhood, in the [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3)

## Description

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Dahlia_Bakery&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Description")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Seattle%2C_Washington%2C_U.S._%28November_2022%29_-_165.jpg/250px-Seattle%2C_Washington%2C_U.S._%28November_2022%29_-_165.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Seattle,_Washington,_U.S._(November_2022)_-_165.jpg)

Interior, 2022

Dahlia Bakery is a [bakery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bakery "Bakery") and pastry shop in [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle")'s [Belltown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belltown,_Seattle "Belltown, Seattle") neighborhood, operated by [Tom Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Douglas_(chef) "Tom Douglas (chef)"). The business serves bread, sandwiches (including [breakfast sandwiches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakfast_sandwich "Breakfast sandwich")),[[4]](#cite_note-4) and pastries for breakfast and lunch.[[5]](#cite_note-5) According to the [Food Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_Network "Food Network"), "This bakery serves up a triple coconut cream pie that keeps the crowds coming back for more. The pie has coconut in the crust, shredded coconut and coconut milk in the creamy filling, and toasted coconut on top, along with curls of white chocolate. It’s available as a whole 9-inch (230 mm) pie, a baby pie, a slice of pie or a coco pie 'bite.'"[[6]](#cite_note-6)

## Reception

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Dahlia_Bakery&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Reception")]

Adam H. Callaghan of *[Eater Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eater_(website) "Eater (website)")* said the Triple Coconut Cream Pie is "a dessert so famous, President Obama asks for it by name, and seems to have it at every Seattle fundraiser he hosts".[[7]](#cite_note-7) The Seattle Post-Intelligencer included the pie in a 2021 list of 26 "iconic Seattle bites".[[8]](#cite_note-8) Allecia Vermillion included the business in *[Seattle Metropolitan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Metropolitan "Seattle Metropolitan")*'s 2022 overview of "exceptional" breakfast sandwiches.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

## About Dahlia Bakery

Dahlia Bakery offers delicious coconut cream pie and donuts, as well as a standout bacon egg sandwich with a fresh house-made English muffin and flavorful aioli. The cafe also serves excellent caramel lattes and has a variety of bakery options, including amazing pastries that change daily. The bakery is known for its unique mochi donuts with great texture and flavors like cherry chocolate, earl grey, and key lime, with blueberry being a less favorite but still tasty. The downtown Seattle location has parking depending on the time of day and is kid-friendly with space to wait with a stroller. Customers have praised the quality of products, describing it as possibly the best bakery in town, with friendly customer service and outdoor seating available. While it may not look busy, it can take some time to place an order and receive drinks, so planning ahead is recommended.

Ken's Artisan Bakery Portland.content:
Ken's Artisan Bakery is a bakery in Portland, Oregon's Northwest District, in the United States.

## History

[edit]

Ken Forkish established the bakery in 2001 and operated it until his retirement in 2021/22. Longtime employees Randy Dorkin and Theo Taylor are now co-owners.

## Reception

[edit] [...] [edit]

In 2022, Eater Portland "Eater (website)")'s Brooke Jackson-Glidden called Ken's Artisan Bakery "an iconic Portland destination for bread and pastries". She also included the Oregon croissant in a 2024 overview of "iconic" Portland dishes. Michelle Lopez and Janey Wong included the business in Eater Portland's 2025 overview of the city's best bakeries. Michael Russell included the business in The Oregonian's 2025 list of the 21 best restaurants in southeast Portland.

**Ken's Artisan Bakery** is a [bakery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bakery "Bakery") in [Portland, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon")'s [Northwest District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_District,_Portland,_Oregon "Northwest District, Portland, Oregon"), in the United States.

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Ken%27s_Artisan_Bakery&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[Ken Forkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Forkish "Ken Forkish") established the bakery in 2001 and operated it until his retirement in 2021/22.[[1]](#cite_note-1) Longtime employees Randy Dorkin and Theo Taylor are now co-owners.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

## Reception

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Ken%27s_Artisan_Bakery&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Reception")]

In 2022, [*Eater Portland*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eater_(website) "Eater (website)")'s [Brooke Jackson-Glidden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooke_Jackson-Glidden "Brooke Jackson-Glidden") called Ken's Artisan Bakery "an iconic Portland destination for bread and pastries".[[3]](#cite_note-3) She also included the Oregon croissant in a 2024 overview of "iconic" Portland dishes.[[4]](#cite_note-4) Michelle Lopez and Janey Wong included the business in *Eater Portland*'s 2025 overview of the city's best bakeries.[[5]](#cite_note-5) Michael Russell included the business in *[The Oregonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Oregonian "The Oregonian")*'s 2025 list of the 21 best restaurants in southeast Portland.[[6]](#cite_note-6)

Ken's Artisan Bakery Portland.title: Country Blonde - Menu - Ken's Artisan Bakery - Portland
Ken's Artisan Bakery Portland.content:
Before Portland was known as a foodie destination for the masses, Ken's Artisan Bakery was one of the earliest institutions that laid the foundation for others to follow in its footsteps.  Opened in 2001, Ken's Artisan Bakery is a labor of love by Ken Forkish, a former Silicon Valley IT specialist who was inspired by prior trips to Europe to forge a new career path as an artisan baker (or in tech speak, this would be like a small bread-based startup).  Armed without any former training but [...] Ken Forkish, the owner of Ken's Artisan Bakery, received James Beard 2013 Outstanding Pastry Chef award nomination for his cookbook "Flour Water Salt Yeast" (jamesbeard.org/blog/q-jb…). In addition to   
  Ken's Artisan Bakery (opened since 2001), Ken also owns Ken's Artisan Pizza located 3 miles away from the bakery. [...] I love bread, and while I haven't tried all the bakeries in Portland, of the many I've tried, I do believe Ken's is the best in the bread department.  The bakery also does fabulous pastries, cookies, and great lunch options in the form of sandwiches, salads and soups.  I also love the bakery itself with its big windows and open kitchen.   My one year living in Portland, OR was a watershed in my understanding of good coffee, baked goods, and pizza, and Ken's Artisan Bakery being located one block from my apartment served to provide the trifecta in educating me on all the above.  
    
  Before Portland was known as a foodie destination for the masses, Ken's Artisan Bakery was one of the earliest institutions that laid the foundation for others to follow in its footsteps.  Opened in 2001, Ken's Artisan Bakery is a labor of love by Ken Forkish, a former Silicon Valley IT specialist who was inspired by prior trips to Europe to forge a new career path as an artisan baker (or in tech speak, this would be like a small bread-based startup).  Armed without any former training but possessing a keen sense of intense observation and meticulous study along with an obsessive attention to detail including plotting out tables to adjust bake settings and yeast proofing based on the surrounding temperature and humidity, the output is a continuous pursuit of baking perfection using the finest ingredients baked from scratch everyday.    
    
  Coffee: Serving Stumptown coffee, which has now gained national recognition, you'll be hard pressed to find a barista in this town that does not know how to craft an excellent latte.  
    
  Pastries:  If you've had the privilege to check out Tartine in San Francisco, the croissants and morning buns are made very much in the same style and form, although probably a little less decadent.  Their signature item is the Oregon Croissant made w/ mixed local berries, hazelnut cream, and playfully presented with fresh berries and sugar pellets lined within its open-faced lattice.  Other standout items include the Morning Bun w/ orange zest, the pain au chocolat, and the ham/gruyere/thyme savory croissant.  The almond croissant and cannelles are not quite as good.  There are also several seasonal fruit tarts and finer pastries on rotation.  
    
  Bread:  Great alone or paired w/ cheese and charcuterie, the walnut bread and country blonde are probably my favorites.    
    
  Ambience:  a neighborhood bakery in the truest sense, laid back unpretentious vibe with an open facade and regulars known on a first name basis, don't be surprised if you see a PhD with multiple tattoos and piercings riffing on astrophysics or a member from a local band coming in for their daily cup of joe.    
    
  Protip:  It's been awhile since I've been back, but Monday night at 530pm is Pizza Night, where they bake Neopolitan style pizzas out of their ovens, and a complimentary loaf of bread is thrown in for good measure.  Funfact: The success of this little side event led to the opening of Ken's Artisan Pizza in 2006, which is another beloved institution I will save for another review.

  I love bread, and while I haven't tried all the bakeries in Portland, of the many I've tried, I do believe Ken's is the best in the bread department.  The bakery also does fabulous pastries, cookies, and great lunch options in the form of sandwiches, salads and soups.  I also love the bakery itself with its big windows and open kitchen.  It's so nice and inviting and makes me want to sit with a book and a coffee and just spend a few hours relaxing.    
    
  Back to the bread...The baguettes are delicious, crisp on the outside and chewy in the middle and their Walnut Loaf is dense and nutty, perfect toasted with some butter or smothered in a soft cheese.  My favorite bread from here though is the Country Blonde.  The Country Blonde is the perfect, everyday bread.  My Dad was so impressed with it when he visited Portland that now every time I go back to the bay I get in trouble if I haven't brought at least two loaves down with me.  The Blonde and it's sister bread, the Country Brown are great as an accompaniment to any meal with their crusty exterior and lighter airy interior.    
    
  I've also been here for lunch a few times and the sandwiches are good, the soups are great and the pastries are always tasty.  I love the butter croissants which are large and flakey and the Cannelle cakes that are crisp and caramelized on the outside and moist and custardy on the inside.  The Tuna Sandwich, served on a croissant was great and the Curried Cauliflower soup I had here warmed me up on a cold winter afternoon.    
    
  Ken's Bakery is great!  As an added bonus they also do pizza on Monday nights that is also quite good.

Ken's Artisan Bakery Portland.title: Ciabatta - Menu - Ken's Artisan Bakery - Portland
Ken's Artisan Bakery Portland.content:
Ken's is the best for breads in all of PDX and beyond.  The most perfect baguette imaginable.  You can get the regular one or the smaller size. Crisp on the outside, soft and delicate on the inside. They make them fresh twice a day.  These are French tested, as any Parisian that has encountered them has said these are as good if not better than in the old country. in addition, Ken's has phenomenal breads of other variations.  The Walnut Roll/Loaf is great.  if you get the roll, have them [...] Wonderful, friendly and very knowledgeable staff! The shop is really cute too. The entire visit there was perfect. I would recommend Ken's Artisan Bakery without hesitation to anyone looking for a great sandwich, delightful bread or sweet treat. I can't wait to get back to Portland and visit again! [...] Cool neighborhood vibe bakery with great baked breads and even makes for a good lunch joint too!  
    
  Got a couple breads, one 3 lb circle bread and a ciabatta, both were unique in their own way, and tasted exactly like how you'd expect from a good bakery! I was tempted to get their 10 lb'er circle bread but makes it hard to take on an airplane naturally.

The croissants were... quite good. I tried the lemon one, and I won't deny, it was pretty tasty, but I wouldn't say it was mindblowing, it was just very good. Both were, likewise, quite delicious, but nothing earthshattering - again, I felt $8 for them was a totally reasonable price, they were both delicious and filling, but I wouldn't go out of my way for them. It became quickly clear to me, however, that the real star of both the sandwiches was definitely the bread, so after eating the sandwiches, I got back in line and bought a $1 plain ciabatta roll for later, to test that hypothesis, which was indeed correct: their regular plain old bread is definitely the star here. If I lived in Portland, I would probably never buy bread anywhere else. That is an absolutely amazing ciabatta roll - I'd just always stock those, and make my own sandwiches on them at home, if I didn't live thousands of miles away. (Also when I got back in line, I also couldn't resist trying one of their macarons, and it was also extremely good.   The dough angels at Ken's transform the humble ingredients of flour, water, salt, and yeast into deliciously flaky monuments to glutenous perfection. Lose yourself in the luscious layers of the tiramisu and chocolate-spiked greatness of the opera cake. But baked goods and desserts are just the beginning. The rest of the well-rounded menu is equally as palate-pleasing.   
    
  The tomato basil soup is a smooth and creamy puree of soothing goodness. It is lightly spiked with a pleasant herbiness from the fresh basil, which comes sprinkled on top. Three small pieces from a baguette came alongside the soup for soup-scooping. An additional airy ciabatta was required for encore scooping once the baguette supplies were exhausted. I was shocked when I recently came in to get my tomato basil fix and I was informed it was no longer on the menu. This needs to be a year-round offering.   
    
  The house salad was an example of well-executed simplicity.  What it lacked in uniqueness made up for in the impeccable quality of the ingredients. Nuggets of sour and crumbly blue cheese cozied up next to a dash of toasted walnuts and tiny strips of apple. A light toss with a delicious vinagrette tied together the fresh mixed greens.   
    
  I ordered a ciabatta for the walk home. The thick flaky crust gave way to an airy interior with just the lightest sourdough flavor that would balance out any sandwich or cheese.  
    
  A few days later I stopped by and ordered an Oregon croissant. Marionberries laid upon a flaky and chewy bed of buttery croissant-ness. Do yourself a favor and stop by if you find yourself walking down the tree-lined sidewalks of beautiful northwest Portland.

  Okay, I'm sure there are better bakeries out there, but after growing up in small southern towns where local bakeries simply order frozen pastries from Sysco and bake them off, I'm freaking delighted by this place. Also, we live around the corner, and there are few things better than waking up, walking out the door, and getting a fresh croissant.  
  If they haven't sold out of their almond croissant by the time I get there, that's my go-to. But I'm also partial to the plain croissant and the Oregon croissant. The Oregon croissant contains house-made hazelnut paste and Marionberries and is topped with pearl sugar. Absurdly delicious. I have not tried their morning buns or pains aux raisins, but both look amazing. It's only a matter of time before I indulge in those--I'm just a little set in my ways...  
  Oh and Ken's bread is just incredible. I bake my own sourdough bread, but in the summer when it's too hot to bake, I buy Ken's. If you're ever having a party, get their huge boule. You will not regret it, and it's impressive as a centerpiece. Their ciabatta and country white and brown loaves are wonderful. They also happen to do a lovely pain de mie, and their walnut ficelles are just perfect. Great crust, wonderful flavor, and beautiful to boot. Ken's does it right.  
  I have not ventured to try Ken's desserts, but they all look wonderful, and I can't imagine them being less than exemplary. As a baker, this place is a constant inspiration to me. They do things right here.

  Ken's is the best for breads in all of PDX and beyond.  The most perfect baguette imaginable.  You can get the regular one or the smaller size. Crisp on the outside, soft and delicate on the inside. They make them fresh twice a day.  These are French tested, as any Parisian that has encountered them has said these are as good if not better than in the old country. in addition, Ken's has phenomenal breads of other variations.  The Walnut Roll/Loaf is great.  if you get the roll, have them slice it and get some butter and jam with, it is great.  You have many other options, like on Saturday they offer their Rye bread!  You also can get the Ciabatta, and many other varieties of different breads.  Its a one stop place for Bread Heaven. While you are there get anything from the case - like the croissants, Cookies (Delicious!!), Quiche, Ham and Gruyere Croissant, or literally anything - you wont be disappointed. Ken's also does a nice lunch time sandwich with several options like the Croque Monsieur; An Italian sandwich; Egg Salad, and a few others.  They have Eclairs, different cakes, and the list goes on.  You can not go wrong with any choice that you select.  They offer great coffee as well, and the staff is always accommodating and nice.

  For me, Ken's Artisan Bakery is a mixed bag. The bread is fabulous, my favorites being the walnut, cranberry boule and the pecan, raisin loaf. Dark grains with the dried fruit and nuts make for a fabulous taste combo. Toasted with Kerrygold butter, yes, please!  
    
  The Oregon scones are also delightful. Loaded with Marionberries they have the perfect amount of sweet interspersed with the buttery, flaky croissant.   
    
  Morning buns are also delicious, the croissant dough rolled into a muffin shape with just the right amount of sugar to add caramelized sweetness.   
    
  While I do like my sweets, I equally like savory and their leek and goat cheese croissant is the best of both. The slightly sweet croissant peppered with tangy goad cheese and big chunks of leaks is the perfect choice for breakfast along with a cup of good coffee. Which they serve. I like the croissant slightly heated.   
    
  The lemon merengue tarts are absolutely beautiful, the merengue piped with lots of little peaks, all toasted to golden perfection. They taste as good as they look! The tart lemon custard and slightly sweet and gooey merengue the perfect companions. Buy them for your next dinner party and wow your guests with no effort!  
    
  Sandwiches are hearty, quality meats layered on various slices of their amazing bread. For around $11-12, they are pricey but for me, they make two meals.   
    
  While I have not had their quiche, I can say they offer a very large slice for about $4.50-5.00. Pair with your own salad for a satisfy lunch or dinner.   
    
  Now to the disappointment, and it pains me to say this because imo this should be a given at a bakery. The almond croissant was just awful. Inedible. When I picked it up it came apart as they evidently slice off the top to put in the almond filling rather than inject it as many bakeries do. This made it difficult to eat because you had to hold it like a sandwich to keep it together. But that isn't my biggest complaint. The almond filling was all liquid, not a paste which typically is inside of an almond croissant. It was runny and tasted of the individual ingredients. And the dough was super dry and crisp, not buttery, no chew. For the taste and calories, it just was not worth eating.   
    
  This may have been an off day or maybe it's how they make their almond croissants, I'll never know as I would never order one again. Was hoping for the real deal because for $4.50 I wanted it to be an alternative to Bakeshop incredibly divine almond croissants that are $7-7.50 each. Although they are the best I've ever had anywhere, the price continues to increase making it a special rather than regular purchase.   
    
  Still a fan of Ken's Artisan Bakery, one of the first in Portland, a pioneer and an icon. But can't give the five stars without having a solid almond croissant.

  There's a good selection of French pastries to choose from (two of owner's favorite items were Country Blonde bread and Oregon Croissant), but they will run out certain pastries if you do come here a bit late (almond croissants were sold out at 1 PM). This place was completely packed and I couldn't grab a table, so I got my pastry to-go  
    
  \*\*\*  
    
  Ham, Thyme, and Gruyere Croissant ($4.75): Croissant was a bit cold, but it tasted very delicious. Just the right amount of ham, cheese, and dough.  
    
  \*\*\*  
    
  If I actually live around this area, then I would visit this place multiple times and try their other breads.  
    
  P.S. - They serves Stumptown Coffee.

  4.5  
  Based on almond croissants only.  
    
  This was my second attempt at research. The first attempt, being a late Sunday morning, Ken had sold out of his almond croissants. I returned on a Monday, late morning to find plenty of sugar snow dusted beauties lined up for the taking.  
    
  Ken's almond croissants ($3) are better than the majority I've sampled over the last month and a half. For one, the croissant dough is flaky with lots of air pockets.  
    
  The almond filling is high quality: real almonds - with their skins on - suspended in a cream base spiked with  something reminiscent of almond liquor. Wait, is that booze in my croissant? I like it!  
    
  Because of the delicious and very homemade filling (NOT marzipan) and airy-fresh croissant dough, Ken's Artisan Bakery almond croissant has a solid 2nd place in the Smack Down standings.

### Google Reviews [...] Arrived as the farmer's market was setting up, so we tucked into Bakery Lorraine at the Pearl for coffee & pastries while we waited. Coffee was made perfectly and I am picky about that! However, the pastries were the star of the show!! We each tried something different and they were all amazing. Crispy and sweet and buttery and flavorful. We enjoyed our treats and felt very comfortable visiting on the patio watching the market vendors get ready. Staff members came by to check on us and were [...] 3 years ago

What a lovely little bakery! We discovered it on our first night in San Antonio but ended up eating elsewhere, and so we made it a point to visit on our way out of town. So glad we did! The food was delicious and the atmosphere was lovely. I had the croque madame which was a savory delight. Kids had some sort of breakfast sandwich and some pastries. The cookies were amazing! Highly recommended if you're at The Pearl and want a sweet treat.

![Rae Norton profile picture](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='50'%20height='50'%20viewBox='0%200%2050%2050'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

2 years ago

Arrived as the farmer's market was setting up, so we tucked into Bakery Lorraine at the Pearl for coffee & pastries while we waited. Coffee was made perfectly and I am picky about that! However, the pastries were the star of the show!! We each tried something different and they were all amazing. Crispy and sweet and buttery and flavorful. We enjoyed our treats and felt very comfortable visiting on the patio watching the market vendors get ready. Staff members came by to check on us and were kind and friendly. Afterward we also enjoyed the farmers market which has a wide variety of produce, baked items, organic meats, cheeses, plants, home-made items, and fascinating international foods. Highly recommend this Bakery and the Pearl area.

![Ozan Ustundag profile picture](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='50'%20height='50'%20viewBox='0%200%2050%2050'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

2 years ago

Great bakery shop at the heart of Pearl, San Antonio. We had chocolate croissant and a few macarons. Everything was so tasty. A perfect stopover area in the heat of Texas.

![Emily Myerly profile picture](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='50'%20height='50'%20viewBox='0%200%2050%2050'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

3 years ago

French toast, Croissant Sandwich and Turkey Pesto. Everyone thoroughly enjoyed their choice. My turkey pesto was excellent, the potatoes that came with the croissant sandwich were insanely tasty! Our daughter sat happily nomming on the French toast. We took half the food home because they give you a lot. Always a treat to eat here.

![Next Level Explorer profile picture](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='50'%20height='50'%20viewBox='0%200%2050%2050'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

The variety at Bakery Lorraine is truly outstanding. They offer an extensive selection of pastries, bread, cakes, and other baked goods that are sure to satisfy every craving. Whether you’re in the mood for a flaky croissant, a decadent chocolate tart, or a perfectly baked baguette, Bakery Lorraine has got you covered.

![Benjamin Thompson profile picture](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='50'%20height='50'%20viewBox='0%200%2050%2050'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

[Benjamin Thompson](https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/107125393597917782423/reviews)

What a lovely little bakery! We discovered it on our first night in San Antonio but ended up eating elsewhere, and so we made it a point to visit on our way out of town. So glad we did! The food was delicious and the atmosphere was lovely. I had the croque madame which was a savory delight. Kids had some sort of breakfast sandwich and some pastries. The cookies were amazing! Highly recommended if you're at The Pearl and want a sweet treat.

James Beard Award-winning pastry chef Dominique Ansel's flagship New York City bakery, world-famous for its innovative desserts and signature pastries. Home of the iconic Cronut®, DKA (Dominique's Kouign Amann), Cookie Shot, Blossoming Hot Chocolate, and Frozen S'mores, this Soho bakery showcases creative French pastry with a modern twist. ### Papa d’Amour – Greenwich Village, NYC

**NOW OPEN!** A new concept by Chef Dominique Ansel exploring his love of Asian bread culture. Dedicated to his two young children, who are Taiwanese and French, “Papa d’Amour” means “Papa, my love” in French. “It’s what my kids call me,” says the chef. “Especially when they want something.”

We love blending cultures, techniques, and memories in the world of pastry. And we all know that when Papa is in the kitchen, there are no rules.

## About Dominique Ansel Bakery

This bakery-cafe headed by pastry chef Dominique Ansel serves up creative & beautiful French treats.

## What People Are Saying

from Google & Yelp

"This is the ultimate destination for high-end luxury pastries. I never knew pastries could be this good. My favorites are the cronuts and the cookie shots - and the Frozen S'more is one of the greatest things on the planet. The items in the pastry case change on a rotational basis and there's always new things to try. They know how to keep the menu interesting and creative. The taste and texture is always amazing - and it's always fresh. The back seating area has great coffee shop vibes, looking onto more seating outdoors with vines growing up an overhead trellis. Jerry Seinfeld was here to film an episode of "Comedians In Cars Getting Coffee" with Tina Fey."

"What a wonderful place! It does get a lot of traffic so you way have to wait outside- but in the winter they do offer hand warmers while you are out there! And the sample of their signature pastry the DKA, which is basically a caramelized croissant, was absolutely divine. Their cronut flavor of the month was brownie batter and Colombian coffee - it was delicious and completely worth the wait. We also got their holiday special mini Bûche de Noël in the triple chocolate and sticky toffee pudding flavors to go."

★★★★★

"Visiting was such a joyful experience. I loved the pumpkin cronut and I do not like pumpkin- it's that good! I also had avo toast which was a work of art and tasted amazing. Eating in flower garden was amazing. But the thing that really stood out was the service. The two men behind the counter were so friendly, patient and helpful- yes in NYC! You could tell they really enjoy what they do. This is a must visit in Soho."

★★★★★

"I went here with my husband because I saw the video on this place making cronuts. I loved the flavor of the month for the cronut. My husband got the DKA which he absolutely loved but my daughter ate most of it and my daughter got the cookie shot. she didn’t care for the cookie shot, but I think it’s because she’s used to a certain type of milk. The cookie was good, but if you left the milk in too long, the cookie became very soft. It is a hard cookie so if you’re not into crunchy cookies, I wouldn’t get it."

★★★★★

"This place lives up to the hype. I typically avoid the trendy places, but had to see what a DKA and Cronut were all about and YES, ma'am! I will be back for this yumminess again. They also have a little (TEENY) inside seating area and a little patio with some tables out back, along with some regular menu options. Their desserts also look delicious. So many reasons to keep visiting. The DKA - I don't even know how to describe it.... I think they described it as a glazy type croissant. They have samples of it and yep. There is NO eating one bite. The Cronut was interesting.... Not at all what I was expecting, but packed full of fun and flavors. #dominiqueanselbakery #bakery #nyc"

★★★★★

"I had such a lovely experience particularly at this location because the people working here were so sweet. I needed gifts for three separate people, and..."

3

Reviewed 17 March 2018

[So worth the calories!](/ShowUserReviews-g60763-d2629009-r566886225-Dominique_Ansel_Bakery-New_York_City_New_York.html)

We were really keen to try the famous 'Cronut' and we were so glad we did. We had been told to expect a big line, but we actually didn't queue for that long at all - maybe 8 mins tops and the queue was inside the bakery itself so we weren't standing outside in the cold. While we were waiting, we saw a big batch of Cronuts come out from the kitchen and one of the managers was hand selecting which ones were good enough to sell (what do they do with the rejected ones I wonder?) which gave the impression that they really do care about their product.   
  
We ended up getting two ham and cheese croissants, which we really great and their cronut for the month (I think it was Blackberry Buttermilk) and they were really amazing. Fully recommend if you are in NYC and in the area.   
  
They also have a lovely garden room at the back which was very sunny and a lovely space to have breakfast.   
  
All in all, we loved it and will absolutely go back.

This was my second visit to Dominique Ansel Bakery. Last October, I pre-ordered and was able to skip the line and pick up my Pumpkin Cranberry Cronuts directly at the register. I would recommend planning ahead and doing the preorder. You can add other items to your order when you pick up. I wasn’t able to plan ahead for this visit to NYC, so on a snowy Tuesday morning I walked 10 minutes from the West Village to the bakery in Soho. The line was short, due to the weather and early/mid-week time.  
  
I picked up two Blackberry Buttermilk Cronuts (March flavor), a DKA, a Canelé, and the cutest polar bear Religieuse (filled with brown butter ganache and caramelized apples). We enjoyed these all so much. I highly recommend visiting this lovely pastry shop.

Zak the Baker Miami.content:
Bakery or Zak the Baker is a kosher restaurant in the Wynwood neighborhood of Miami, Florida. After the bakery was moved into a larger building, Zak the Baker opened a new glatt kosher delicatessen in January 2017 in the old bakery location. The associated bakery and café were both founded by local baker Zak Stern. The bakery closes on Saturdays, in keeping with kosher requirements.

The bakery has developed a reputation for its sourdough bread, among other items such as challah bread. [...] Print/export

**Bakery** or **Zak the Baker** is a [kosher restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosher_restaurant "Kosher restaurant") in the [Wynwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wynwood "Wynwood") neighborhood of [Miami, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami,_Florida "Miami, Florida").[[1]](#cite_note-haaretz-hand-1)[[2]](#cite_note-miamiherald-baker-2) After the bakery was moved into a larger building,[[2]](#cite_note-miamiherald-baker-2) Zak the Baker opened a new [glatt kosher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glatt_kosher "Glatt kosher") [delicatessen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delicatessen "Delicatessen") in January 2017[[3]](#cite_note-nyt-florence-3) in the old bakery location.[[2]](#cite_note-miamiherald-baker-2) The associated bakery and café were both founded by local baker Zak Stern.[[4]](#cite_note-vice-bakery-4) The bakery closes on Saturdays, in keeping with kosher requirements.[[2]](#cite_note-miamiherald-baker-2)[[5]](#cite_note-bonappetit-bakery-5)

The bakery has developed a reputation for its [sourdough bread](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sourdough_bread "Sourdough bread"), among other items[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7) such as [challah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Challah "Challah") bread.[[1]](#cite_note-haaretz-hand-1)

## Recognition

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zak_the_Baker&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Recognition")]

In 2013, Zak Stern was named Best Baker by the *[Miami New Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_New_Times "Miami New Times")* in their Best of Miami Awards.[[8]](#cite_note-8) In 2014 the Zak the Baker Wynwood Bakery & Cafe won Best Bakery in the Best of Miami Awards,[[9]](#cite_note-mnt-award2-9) and Stern won the Baking & Pastry Chef of the Year award at the JWU Zest Awards for his work with the restaurant in 2015.[[10]](#cite_note-mnt-award-10)

Look for the color-splashed facade to find this all-day operation which is the brainchild of baker Zak Stern. He grew up in Miami, then apprenticed at a number of organic farms in Sweden, France and Israel before returning to his hometown to fulfill his culinary dreams. The crux of his kosher menu is baked, as in breads and pastries, along with sandwiches, soups and salads. The likes of avocado toast, a frittata sandwich and crispy local fish on brioche sate the legion of ravenous fans who descend upon this Wynwood favorite. Save room for something sweet, say the seasonal concha.

# A Day In the Life of Zak the Baker | Video

* [Copy to clipboard](javascript:void(0); "Share")

A brightly-hued bakery stands on the corner of 26th Street in the [Wynwood Arts District](https://www.miamiandbeaches.com/neighborhoods/wynwood), home to a bustling bread culture and culinary communal hub for [Miami, Florida](https://thelocalpalate.com/articles/destination-miami-miami-beach/). Zak Stern, founder and owner of [Zak the Baker](https://zakthebaker.com/), started the shop in 2012 as an artisan, kosher, retail, and wholesale providing the Miami area with fresh baked bread via their own store, but also distributing through a partnership with [Whole Foods Market](https://www.wholefoodsmarket.com/).

Known for their sourdough and challah, Zak the Baker is a frequent destination for a loaf of classic Jewish rye or an olive za’atar batard, but they also host an impressive pastry program. Flaky croissants, delicate cakes, and scrumptious cookies line their shelves with flavors mirroring regional produce and cultural influence of southern Florida. With pastries like a concha with mamey cream, Stern proudly serves Miami-centric cuisine.

For Stern, an artisan bakery is a home to people dedicated to the learning, continuation, and flourishing of a craft within a community. There’s an inherent connectivity to community at Zak the Baker, heavily influencing how the bakery evolves and meets the needs of those around them. Stern refers to Zak the Baker’s walls as permeable, a space where the community intertwines with their craft, actively participating in their production. Keeping with this integration, Zak the Baker’s production kitchen hums within the center of their shop. From twisting challah, to brushing egg wash onto pastries, the staff moves elegantly alongside the lively shop. Stern credits his success to a mix of humility, incremental growth, independence, and luck; but more than these, he values the passionate team he has built through the years.

## Live and Let Leaven

Sullivan Street Bakery started with the belief that good bread should be available and affordable for everyone. Italian bread bakeries serve everyone in society, and our mission is to do the same – making the best possible bread. We opened in 1994 with the mission to raise the standard for handcrafted, small-batch bread, and we work continually to better our methods, techniques, and craft. We source excellent ingredients, avoid every kind of additives and enhancer, and shape every piece of bread by hand. We work closely with our suppliers to find exceptional products and strive to make every part of our business sustainable, fun, and delicious—we want to continually set the bar for what great bread can be.

Jim Lahey thought he was going to be a sculptor. After noticing he couldn't find bread in New York like the beautiful, crusty loaves he ate in Italy while traveling there as an art student, he took it upon himself to recreate those loaves. In 1994, with the help of Joe Allen, Lahey opened Sullivan Street Bakery and eventually began producing bread for many of the city's best restaurants. In 2006, The New York Times published Lahey's [No-Knead Bread method](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/11376-no-knead-bread), allowing home bakers to make bakery-quality loaves right from their ovens. The recipe remains one of the newspaper's most popular recipes, and has changed the way people bake all around the world.

Following the success of that recipe, Lahey authored [*My Bread*](/books), opened up a pizzeria Co., and a [café in Chelsea](/location/chelsea-sullivan-street-bakery/). [*My Pizza*](/books) followed soon after, allowing readers to try their hand at pizza dough and beautifully simple toppings.

In 2015, Lahey was the first recipient of the [Outstanding Baker James Beard Award](https://www.jamesbeard.org/chef/jim-lahey), followed, in 2016, by an induction into the foundation's "[Who's Who of Food & Beverage in America](https://www.jamesbeard.org/education/whos-who-food-and-beverage-america)."

Today, Sullivan Street Bakery delivers bread for over 300 restaurants in New York. In 2017, Sullivan Street Bakery opened in [Miami](/location/miami-sullivan-street-bakery/), and Jim released [The Sullivan Street Bakery Cookbook](/books).

Connect with Jim online [@jimlaheyssb](https://www.instagram.com/jimlaheyssb/).

# Ritual Coffee Roasters

Design-driven shop with pour-over coffee made using a V60 dripper.

## Photos

Reviewed by [Lexi Pandell](/contributors/lexi-pandell)

**Tell us about your first impressions when you arrived.**  
When you come to Ritual, you might think you're stepping into some weird, hipster ode to the USSR, with its modified hammer-and-sickle logo and red-and-white branding. But it's not a Marxist joint; just a coffee shop with an informed design aesthetic.

Inside, it sets the standard for a high end (and, with their prices, decidedly capitalistic) San Francisco cafe. It's spacious and modernist, with intricate tube lighting over the register and art on the walls. Near the register, there's a line of V60 pour-over stations behind clear glass, so you can watch the baristas work their magic. There are several tables inside, plus outdoor seating, which is always full on nice days.

**What was the crowd like?**  
Ritual is a place where people come to get work done. Most everyone—from writers to coders to graphic designers to students—sits behind their laptop. Start-up founders huddle in one corner, a philosophy club meets in another.

At times, the only sound you can hear is the espresso machine and the clacking of fingers on keyboards. At other times, it's buzzing with the sound of people collaborating.

**What should we be drinking?**  
Ritual roasts their own beans and serves some of the finest coffee San Francisco has to offer. They have cold brew and nitro, lattes and cappuccino. But they're best known for their pour-over coffee, made using a V60 dripper.

Walk in at any given moment, and you'll see baristas lined up gently pouring steaming hot water into the grounds with Zen-like, circular motions. The process seems pretentious, but it works well, producing a rich, smooth brew.

Give their espresso a try; it's a rotating blend depending on the season, but flavorful, never bitter, and will give you just the right buzz. Their tea, sourced from the incredible Song Tea near Japantown, also is excellent.

**Main event: the food. Give us the lowdown—especially what not to miss.**  
Ritual has a nice selection of pastries, including pretzel buns, croissants, and muffins. They also serve organic, vegan donuts.

The donuts, made by Pepples across the Bay in Oakland, come in unique flavors, like lemon poppyseed and blueberry. They're so moist and tasty that you'll forget that they're (er, kiiiinda) healthy.

**And how did the front-of-house folks treat you?**  
The staff respects the work space. That means minimal conversations with customers and effective service. But they all take their coffee seriously. If you're not sure what to get, leave it up to the pros to help you decide.

**What’s the real-real on why we’re coming here?**Ritual fuels Valencia Street, a strip in the Mission District known for boutique shopping, excellent eats, and chic art scene.

# One of S.F.’s third wave coffee pioneers opens its first standalone café in 10 years

By [Mario Cortez](https://www.sfchronicle.com/author/mario-cortez/), Staff WriterUpdated

[Add Us](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=sfchronicle.com)

Baristas Katelyn Parks, left, and Parker Leabo prepare drinks at the new Ritual Coffee on California Street, which opened Thursday.

Lea Suzuki/S.F. Chronicle

Nancy Ivison, center, and Anthony Kleppe, chat during the soft opening at the new Ritual Coffee in San Francisco. Kleppe worked in the offices above years ago and he and his wife, Nancy Ivison, met owner Eileen Rinaldi then when she worked at the same space, when it was occupied by Torrefazione Italia.

Lea Suzuki/S.F. Chronicle

Before Eileen Rinaldi founded San Francisco’s Ritual Coffee Roasters in 2005, her first foray into the local coffee market was operating a location of Seattle’s now-defunct coffee chain Torrefazione Italia in the Financial District. Two decades later, as the owner of a popular specialty coffee roasting company, she has opened the latest Ritual in the same space.

Ritual Coffee’s first standalone café since 2015 opened Thursday at 259 California St. and will offer drip and espresso drinks made with the company’s single-origin beans and blends roasted in the Mission District. Pastries from [Saltwater Bakeshop](https://www.sfchronicle.com/food/restaurants/article/saltwater-bakeshop-san-francisco-22257730.php), doughnuts from Dynamo Donut and breakfast sandwiches are also available.

Rinaldi opened the first Ritual in the Mission District in 2005. The shop was among the first in the Bay Area to embrace Third Wave coffee, a movement that shifted the perception of the drink from a commodity to a more artisanal product. Ritual focused on sourcing coffees from specific regions and farmers, whom it highlighted to better showcase the terroir of coffee. In the past six years, Ritual has contracted and grown, closing three locations in San Francisco and adding one at San Francisco International Airport. With the new location, Ritual will have five cafés in San Francisco and Napa.

Advertisement

Article continues below this ad

A cortado and chocolate vegan doughnut from Dynamo Donut from Ritual Coffee’s new downtown location.

Lea Suzuki/S.F. Chronicle

On California Street, Ritual took over a refurbished ground-level space where a Starbucks operated [until last August](https://www.bizjournals.com/sanfrancisco/news/2025/08/01/starbucks-closure-295-california-fidi.html)— one of scores of stores that the coffee chain [shuttered](https://www.sfchronicle.com/bayarea/article/starbucks-closures-sf-east-bay-21069253.php) as part of a billion-dollar restructuring effort that began last year. More local Starbucks [are slated to](https://www.sfchronicle.com/bayarea/article/starbucks-bay-area-store-closures-22449337.php) close this year. The closures have opened the door for local coffee companies such as Ritual, [Spro Coffee Lab](https://www.bizjournals.com/sanfrancisco/news/2025/12/18/spro-coffee-lab-embarcadero-starbucks-retail.html), Flywheel Coffee, Red Bay Coffee and [Andytown Coffee](https://www.bizjournals.com/sanfrancisco/news/2025/12/01/andytown-lendingclub-headquarters-downtown.html) to expand into downtown spaces that may have previously been out of reach.

Rinaldi said she is happy to see more homegrown Bay Area coffee shops and [restaurants](https://www.sfchronicle.com/food/restaurants/article/sutro-hall-opening-downtown-sf-22426230.php) open downtown. Nearby, popular bagel shop [Schlok’s opened last summer](https://www.sfchronicle.com/food/restaurants/article/schloks-bagel-lox-san-francisco-20784301.php) and a [new Tartine Bakery is in the works](https://www.sfchronicle.com/realestate/article/tartine-bakery-downtown-san-francisco-22366216.php). Across the street from Ritual is also Japanese-inspired café [the Wild Fox](https://www.sfchronicle.com/food/restaurants/article/wild-fox-sf-coffee-22103105.php), which opened last year as part of the city-sponsored Vacant to Vibrant program.

“We really needed to have businesses that are representative of San Francisco downtown and that is finally happening now,” she said.

Eileen Rinaldi founded Ritual Coffee in 2005.

Lea Suzuki/S.F. Chronicle

The 1,800-square-foot Ritual is similar in size to the company’s Valencia Street flagship in the Mission. The menu includes classic espresso drinks such as macchiatos ($5.25), lattes ($8) and mochas ($8.50) made with chocolate from the Mission District’s Dandelion Chocolate. The bar will keep several single origin beans for pour-overs. One new item is a pour-over for two ($11).

Advertisement

Article continues below this ad

Local architect [Seth Boor](https://www.sfchronicle.com/homeandgarden/article/Boor-Bridges-Architecture-influencing-Bay-Area-6066797.php) — whose firm, Boor Projects, is behind some of the [Bay Area’s most beautiful restaurants](https://www.sfchronicle.com/food/restaurants/article/most-beautiful-bay-area-2025-21171016.php) — reworked the standardized Starbucks interior by stripping back drywall and wood panels to reveal concrete and travertine pillars.

“The building we’re in is this really beautiful, iconic mid-century building. We wanted to expose some of its elements,” Rinaldi said. Inside, floor-to-ceiling windows and a high ceiling make the 20-seat space feel more spacious than before. On a wood shelf behind the espresso bar, Rinaldi placed several mementos, including espresso cups from Torrefazione Italia and old Ritual diner mugs.

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Ritual_Coffee.jpg/250px-Ritual_Coffee.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ritual_Coffee.jpg)

Ritual Coffee

**Ritual Coffee Roasters** is a [coffee roaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_roaster "Coffee roaster") based in [San Francisco, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco,_California "San Francisco, California"), with six cafes in San Francisco and [Napa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa,_California "Napa, California").[[2]](#cite_note-NYT-2) Founded in 2005,[[3]](#cite_note-3) Ritual Roasters is considered part of the "[third wave of coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_wave_of_coffee "Third wave of coffee")" independent companies which both roast their own beans, wholesale, and operate cafes. Their peers include [Blue Bottle Coffee Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Bottle_Coffee_Company "Blue Bottle Coffee Company") and [Four Barrel Coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Barrel_Coffee "Four Barrel Coffee"),[[4]](#cite_note-4) among others. In March 2017, Somatik partnered with Ritual Coffee to make $12 marijuana-infused cold brew.[[5]](#cite_note-5)[[6]](#cite_note-6)

In 2021, the [Haight Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haight_Street "Haight Street") location of Ritual Coffee Roasters was damaged during a shooting in the area, when the café was struck by gunfire.[[7]](#cite_note-7) The incident was cited in later reporting as one of several challenges affecting the operation of the location. In March 2025, the company announced the closure of its Haight Street café, ending a nine-year presence in the neighbourhood, with the location scheduled to close on April 11.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

They have a line of canned coffee, partnered with [Juanita More](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juanita_More "Juanita More").[[9]](#cite_note-9)
