# Build-Outs Of Coffee: Ritual Coffee Roasters In San Francisco, CA

![ritual coffee 8](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ritual-coffee-8-527x351.jpg)
![ritual coffee 8](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ritual-coffee-8-1044x696.jpg)

These are exciting times for [Ritual Coffee Roasters](https://ritualcoffee.com/), the seminal San Francisco specialty coffee brand founded in 2005. They’ve spent the last 21 years going from strength to strength whilst leading from the front, and now they’re opening a brand new cafe in the San Francisco Financial District. Let’s learn more!

*The 2026 Build-outs of Coffee is presented by [DONA](https://drinkdona.com/),[Pacific Barista Series](http://instagram.com/baristaseries), and [La Marzocco](http://instagram.com/lamarzocco.usa).*

[![DONA](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/dona-holiday-library-sprudge-booc.jpg)](https://drinkdona.com/pages/wholesale?utm_source=sprudge&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=library)![](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAP///////yH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

*As told to Sprudge by Eileen Rinaldi.*

**For those who aren’t familiar, will you tell us about your company?**

In 2005, when corporate coffee dominated American culture, Ritual unknowingly started a fun and exciting revolution that would ultimately help launch the new specialty coffee movement. By prioritizing sustainability and quality in our buying practices, we ensure we get our hands on the best beans in the world, but more importantly, that coffee farming remains a profitable business for coffee producers. Now a bona fide San Francisco original, we’ve also earned our iconic status as one of the best coffee roasting companies in the world. The mission of Ritual Coffee is simple: to make people happy by giving them the best coffee experience they’ve ever had. Ritual roasts in SoMa, and has cafes in San Francisco and Napa.

![ritual coffee 4](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ritual-coffee-4-1200x800.jpg)

**Can you tell us a bit about the new space?**

Our new cafe is a large, light-filled corner location in a gorgeous mid-century modern building in the Financial District. The location is iconically San Francisco, as it’s right along the California Cable Car line. We took inspiration from classic Italian coffee bars, our neighbor the Tadich Grill, and Edward Hopper’s painting “Nighthawks” to create a coffee oasis.

Fun fact! It’s the very same cafe where owner Eileen Rinaldi was dreaming up Ritual and managing a cafe there 23 years ago!

**What’s your approach to coffee?**

We want to give people an experience that will change the way they think about coffee. For us, there’s no better way to do that than to introduce them to some of our favorite coffees in a brewing method they enjoy. Our coffee program focuses on single-origin coffees (and one seasonal espresso blend!) sourced from small-holder producers, cooperatives, and coffee growing communities. Our cafe menus rotate often to reflect the seasonality of coffee, and we provide different flavor profiles for batch brew, pour-over, signature-beverage, and espresso options.

![ritual coffee 3](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ritual-coffee-3-1200x800.jpg)

**Any machines, coffees, special equipment lined up?**

Pour-over bar featuring V60s, and coffee for two, via Kalita plus a [La Marzocco](http://www.larmarzocco.com) espresso machine.

**How is your project considering sustainability?**

For this project, we looked primarily at sustainability through the lens of selecting materials that will be durable and age well with high volume. Having the experience of several other cafes under my belt, there are certain materials that are now go-tos for the cafe environment. We purchased as much of those products and materials as possible, using [Heath Ceramics](https://www.heathceramics.com/) tile, for example. Additionally, we’re in a LEED Gold certified building, so there is an additional layer of ensuring that we’re meeting that as a minimum standard, in terms of energy usage, ventilation and air quality, etc.

![ritual coffee 7](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ritual-coffee-7-1200x800.jpg)

**What’s your hopeful target opening date/month?**

Grand opening is slated for Thursday 10/22.

**Are you working with craftspeople, architects, and/or creatives that you’d like to mention?**

Yes! Seth Boor—[Boor Projects](https://boorprojects.com/)—he’s the brilliant architect behind many amazing coffee spaces, in the Bay Area and beyond. What I love about working with Seth is that he can translate the desired vision for a space into the architectural concept. I first worked with him back in 2007 on our second location, and it’s such a joy to get to work with him again on this and to see how his creative process has evolved.

**Thank you!**

Thank you!

Ritual Coffee Roasters is located at [259 California St, San Francisco](https://www.google.com/maps). Visit their [official website](https://ritualcoffee.com/) and follow them on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/ritualcoffee/).

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

American coffee roasting and retailing company

This article is about American coffee chain. For historical coffee house in Vienna, Austria, see [The Blue Bottle Coffee House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blue_Bottle_Coffee_House "The Blue Bottle Coffee House").

**Blue Bottle Coffee, Inc.**, is a [coffee roaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_roaster "Coffee roaster") and retailer once headquartered in [Oakland, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland,_California "Oakland, California"), United States. In 2017, a majority stake in the company was acquired by [Nestlé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nestlé "Nestlé") (68%). In 2026, [Centurium Capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centurium_Capital "Centurium Capital") acquired Blue Bottle's global retail operations from Nestlé for approximately $400 million. Blue Bottle Coffee is a major player in [third wave coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_wave_of_coffee "Third wave of coffee").[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1) The company focuses on [single-origin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-origin "Single-origin") beans.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

## Locations

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blue_Bottle_Coffee&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Locations")]

Originating in [Oakland, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland,_California "Oakland, California"), the company soon expanded to other areas around the country. Blue Bottle first expanded to several cafés in locations around [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), including the [Ferry Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Ferry_Building "San Francisco Ferry Building") and the [San Francisco Museum of Modern Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Museum_of_Modern_Art "San Francisco Museum of Modern Art")'s rooftop garden.[[3]](#cite_note-CNN-3) The company operates 150 stores as of October 2026, with locations in [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston"), [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), [Jeju City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeju_City "Jeju City"),[[4]](#cite_note-4) [Kyoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyoto "Kyoto"), [Kobe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kobe "Kobe"), [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), [Osaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka "Osaka"), [Yokohama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yokohama "Yokohama"), [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong"), [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai") and [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore").[[5]](#cite_note-5)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blue_Bottle_Coffee&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/James_Freeman%2C_CEO_Blue_Bottle_Coffee%2C_May_2014.jpg/250px-James_Freeman%2C_CEO_Blue_Bottle_Coffee%2C_May_2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Freeman,_CEO_Blue_Bottle_Coffee,_May_2014.jpg)

W. James Freeman, CEO of Blue Bottle Coffee, in 2014

W. James Freeman founded Blue Bottle Coffee in the early 2000s in [Oakland's Temescal District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temescal,_Oakland,_California "Temescal, Oakland, California").[[6]](#cite_note-6) Freeman borrowed the name from one of Europe's first cafés, [The Blue Bottle Coffee House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blue_Bottle_Coffee_House "The Blue Bottle Coffee House"). Initially, he intended to roast coffee in small batches (6 lbs. per roast) to sell within 24 hours of roasting, as a home-delivery service. Blue Bottle soon ceased deliveries and opened as a traditional café.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

Blue Bottle opened additional locations in San Francisco and elsewhere in the [San Francisco Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area") and opened its first New York location in [Williamsburg, Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamsburg,_Brooklyn "Williamsburg, Brooklyn"), in 2010.[[8]](#cite_note-8) The company-owned stores carry off-menu items such as the "Gibraltar", a form of [cortado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortado "Cortado").[[3]](#cite_note-CNN-3)

In 2012, Blue Bottle received $20 million in [venture capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venture_capital "Venture capital") investment, led by True Ventures.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

In January 2014, Blue Bottle raised $25.75 million in a new round of funding.[[10]](#cite_note-10) In 2015, Blue Bottle completed a [venture capital round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venture_round "Venture round") in which it raised $70 million from investors led by [Fidelity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidelity_Investments "Fidelity Investments").[[11]](#cite_note-11)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Blue_Bottle_Coffee_Moynihan_Station_NY.jpg/250px-Blue_Bottle_Coffee_Moynihan_Station_NY.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Blue_Bottle_Coffee_Moynihan_Station_NY.jpg)

Blue Bottle Coffee stand in the [Moynihan Train Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moynihan_Train_Hall "Moynihan Train Hall") (Penn Station) New York

Since its inception, the company has raised $120 million from investors as of 2017.[[12]](#cite_note-12) In February 2015, Blue Bottle Coffee opened its first location in Tokyo, Japan, in the Kiyosumi neighborhood.[[13]](#cite_note-13) In September 2017, [Nestle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nestle "Nestle") S.A., the world's largest food and drinks company, acquired a majority stake of Blue Bottle.[[14]](#cite_note-14) While the deal's financial details were not disclosed, the *[Financial Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_Times "Financial Times")* reported "Nestle is understood to be paying up to $500m for the 68 per cent stake in Blue Bottle".[[15]](#cite_note-15) Blue Bottle expected to increase sales by 70% in 2017.[[16]](#cite_note-16)

In May 2019, Blue Bottle Coffee opened its first location in [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), South Korea.[[17]](#cite_note-17) In December 2019, Blue Bottle Coffee announced they would test eliminating [disposable cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disposable_cup "Disposable cup") at some of their shops to increase sustainability efforts, with the goal being zero waste within one year.[[18]](#cite_note-18) Nothing has been reported to date about this test and whether it was successful. In April 2020, Blue Bottle Coffee opened its first location in [Central, Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central,_Hong_Kong "Central, Hong Kong"). Amid COVID-19, the café opened daily from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. for takeaway only.[[19]](#cite_note-19)

In February 2022, Blue Bottle Coffee opened its first location in mainland China, Yutong Cafe. Yutong Cafe is located at a historic building by [Suzhou Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzhou_Creek "Suzhou Creek") in downtown [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai").[[20]](#cite_note-20)

In August 2024, Blue Bottle Coffee opened a gift-centric store in [Raffles City Shopping Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffles_City_Singapore "Raffles City Singapore"), Singapore.[[21]](#cite_note-21) In April 2025, this location was converted to a café and became the company's first location in South East Asia.[[22]](#cite_note-22) It has since gone on to open its second store in Singapore at [Paragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paragon,_Singapore "Paragon, Singapore") in July 2025.[[23]](#cite_note-23)

In December 2025, it was reported that Nestlé was considering selling Blue Bottle.[[24]](#cite_note-24)

In March 2026, Centurium Capital reached an agreement with Nestle to acquire Blue Bottle Coffee. At the time, Blue Bottle Coffee was operating at a loss.[[25]](#cite_note-25)

## Labor relations

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blue_Bottle_Coffee&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Labor relations")]

In April 2024, Blue Bottle Coffee’s [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") area locations filed to [unionize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_unions_in_the_United_States "Labor unions in the United States").[[26]](#cite_note-26) Baristas cited multiple grievances with the company as reason for unionizing, including not being paid a living wage, mishandling of sexual harassment,[[27]](#cite_note-27) and not being given input into café operations. The union requested voluntary recognition from the company, and subsequently engaged in a state-wide walkout when Blue Bottle Coffee refused to recognize the union.[[28]](#cite_note-28)

In September 2024, Blue Bottle Coffee fired union organizer Remy Roskin.[[29]](#cite_note-29) In May 2025, Blue Bottle Independent Union (BBIU) conducted another state-wide walkout across Blue Bottle Coffee’s greater Boston area locations in protest of multiple alleged unfair labor practices, including the company attempting to install surveillance cameras.[[30]](#cite_note-30)[[31]](#cite_note-31) On June 17 2025, four Blue Bottle cafés in California’s East Bay area (Berkeley, Old Oakland, Piedmont, and W.C. Morse) announced their intent to join BBIU.[[32]](#cite_note-32) The next day, June 18, Blue Bottle terminated union organizer BB Young,[[33]](#cite_note-33) which BBIU alleges was illegal retaliation. On July 31, the four East Bay area locations won recognition through an NLRB election in a 22–5 vote.[[34]](#cite_note-34) This vote resulted in nearly 12% of U.S. Blue Bottle locations being unionized.[[35]](#cite_note-35) In November 2025, roughly 80 Blue Bottle workers around Boston and 35 workers in California went on strike ahead of the Thanksgiving weekend, with workers accusing the company of negotiating with the union in [bad faith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_faith "Bad faith").[[36]](#cite_note-36)

Blue Bottle Coffee Oakland.content:
the Blue Bottle Independent Union (BBIU) in early August, becoming the first California locations of the coffee chain, which is owned by Nestle, to do so. Workers first announced their intent to join the union on June 17, and WC Morse cafe workers organized a picket to protest the firing of a staff member after employees requested that the company acknowledge their union. Blue Bottle was located at 4270 Broadway (at 42nd St.) in Oakland. [...] Blue Bottle is set to leave the iconic WC Morse building in Oakland’s Temescal district on September 26, per a sign on the cafe’s door. Blue Bottle has occupied the historic former car dealership since 2014 and used to offer espresso tech repairs, visible through a plastic partition in the space. The cafe has recently shaved down its opening hours, and an employee said declining business made continuing unviable. The Blue Bottle cafe in the WC Morse building in Oakland is slated to close on Sept. 26, 2025. Credit: Blue Bottle

***Editor’s note:** [Nosh](https://oaklandside.org/nosh/) covers food and restaurant news across the East Bay, and each week we publish one article covering all the restaurant openings and one article covering closings. Have a tip for Nosh? [Submit it here](https://oaklandside.org/nosh/nosh-tips/).*

## **Blue Bottle**

Blue Bottle is set to leave the iconic WC Morse building in Oakland’s Temescal district on September 26, per a sign on the cafe’s door. Blue Bottle has occupied the historic former car dealership since 2014 and used to offer espresso tech repairs, visible through a plastic partition in the space. The cafe has recently shaved down its opening hours, and an employee said declining business made continuing unviable. Blue Bottle workers across its four East Bay shops [joined the Blue Bottle Independent Union (BBIU) in early August](https://oaklandside.org/2025/08/06/east-bay-blue-bottle-coffee-workers-unionizing/), becoming the first California locations of the coffee chain, which is owned by Nestle, to do so. Workers first announced their intent to join the union on June 17, and WC Morse cafe workers organized a picket to protest the firing of a staff member after employees requested that the company acknowledge their union. Blue Bottle was located at 4270 Broadway (at 42nd St.) in Oakland.

## **Roasted and Raw**

Roasted and Raw, a holdover for plant-based bowls, empanadas and pastas announced its upcoming closure on Instagram this week. The cafe plans to sell its space and is actively seeking a buyer.

“With a week or two left of service, we are looking to turn this into a win for us and our landlord by selling to an established restaurateur looking for a beautiful turn-key ready restaurant space in a reviving downtown,” a September 15 [Instagram post reads](https://www.instagram.com/p/DOoJirjEbwC/?img_index=1). Stay tuned on Instagram for updates on their next moves. Roasted and Raw was located at 607 14th St. (at Jefferson St.) in Oakland.

# Blue Bottle Morse Building

A Coffee Workshop

Blue Bottle Coffee’s Oakland flagship blends historic architecture with a fresh take on craft coffee culture.

## Removing Boundaries

Blue Bottle founder James Freeman brought craft coffee to Northern California in the early 2000s, and as he grew his then fledging business, he wanted each new location to express a unique character, just like his single-origin roasts. With his Oakland flagship location in the historic Morse Building, large picture windows and clerestories spanning two facades prompted a rethinking of the familiar server-served café organization. Instead, an open plan centered around a 30-foot-long stainless-steel table cum espresso bar makes the exchange the focus of the location from inside and outside.

![12 BBM](https://jensen-architects.com/wp-content/uploads/12-BBM-1920x1280.jpg)

![07 BBM](https://jensen-architects.com/wp-content/uploads/07-BBM-1920x1280.jpg)

## Working Within History

The Morris building dates back to 1921, and was formerly an automobile showroom. It’s a beautiful old historic structure, with proportions that are distinctly from another era entirely. Those dimensions were emphasized in the redesign, as were textural elements like the well-worn original tile. The new case work and furnishings stand individually within the elegant historic shell. The structure is white and light, and then the pieces are dark and solid within it.

![16 BBM](https://jensen-architects.com/wp-content/uploads/16-BBM-1920x1280.jpg)

![04 BBM](https://jensen-architects.com/wp-content/uploads/04-BBM-1920x1280.jpg)

![14 BBM](https://jensen-architects.com/wp-content/uploads/14-BBM-1920x2401.jpg)

## At Your Service

In its earliest days Blue Bottle delivered its roasts to customers’ homes and helping people make better coffee at home remains a core mission. In the Morse building this philosophy is expressed by the introduction of an “espresso repair” shop. Customers can see old espresso machines as they’re being tuned up or brought back to life. Containing the messiness of machine repair without chopping up the building was a challenge. A glass wall proved prohibitively expensive due to the double-high ceiling, but clear vinyl curtains made for an ethereal division that enhances the unexpected presence of the shop.

![13 BBM](https://jensen-architects.com/wp-content/uploads/13-BBM-1920x2401.jpg)

![06 BBM](https://jensen-architects.com/wp-content/uploads/06-BBM-1920x1280.jpg)

![11 BBM](https://jensen-architects.com/wp-content/uploads/11-BBM-1920x1280.jpg)

![15 BBM](https://jensen-architects.com/wp-content/uploads/15-BBM-1920x1280.jpg)

## Interior Planning

JENSEN designed and selected all the furnishings in the Morse Blue Bottle. These include the vast workshop table, the big round family table, and the communal seating with stools. The interior planning began with as many as a dozen variations on where every surface, stool, chair, and case would be placed. Each variation was tested conceptually for relative positioning, customer comfort, and overall workflow. While the open plan added challenges in terms of plumbing and utilities, the flexibility allowed for easy adjustments once the space was in use, just like many modern workplace designs.

**Stumptown Coffee Roasters** is a [coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee "Coffee") [roaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_roasting "Coffee roasting") and retailer based in [Portland, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon"), [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"). The chain's first location opened in 1999. Three other cafes, a roastery and a tasting annex have since opened in Portland, as well as locations in [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle"), [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), and [Pasadena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasadena "Pasadena").[[2]](#cite_note-2) Stumptown is owned by [Peet's Coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peet's_Coffee "Peet's Coffee"),[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-:0-4) which in turn is owned by [Keurig Dr Pepper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keurig_Dr_Pepper "Keurig Dr Pepper"). The company was an early innovator with [cold brew coffee in nitro cans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitro_cold_brew_coffee "Nitro cold brew coffee") and have continued to develop other cold brew product innovations.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stumptown_Coffee_Roasters&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Founder [Duane Sorenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duane_Sorenson "Duane Sorenson") and Stumptown Coffee Roasters have been labeled as part of the [third wave of coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_wave_of_coffee "Third wave of coffee") movement.[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7) Sorenson and his employees visited coffee farms in person and reportedly paid high prices for beans, occasionally three or four times the [fair trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_trade "Fair trade") price.[[8]](#cite_note-8) He once set the record for highest price ever paid for coffee beans.[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-10)[[11]](#cite_note-11)

Sorenson also offered atypical perks to his employees such as paying for a compilation album to be produced of their various bands,[[12]](#cite_note-12) and hiring a full-time on-staff massage therapist.[[13]](#cite_note-Roast_2006-13) Stumptown received the *Roaster of the Year 2006,* an award from a technical trade magazine called *Roast Magazine*[[13]](#cite_note-Roast_2006-13)

In January 2014, the company began selling coffee, pre-mixed with milk, in grocery stores.[[14]](#cite_note-14) In 2015, Stumptown Coffee Roasters was bought by [Peet's Coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peet's_Coffee "Peet's Coffee") for an undisclosed amount.[[4]](#cite_note-:0-4)

### Locations

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stumptown_Coffee_Roasters&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Locations")]

Stumptown operates five cafes in Portland. They are located on SE 45th & Division St., SE 34th & Belmont, downtown at SW 3rd & Ash St., inside the [Ace Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_Hotel "Clyde Hotel") at 1022 SW [Stark Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stark_Street "Stark Street"), and at the Portland International Airport. The company also owns a roasting facility and a retail annex inside their headquarters at 100 SE Salmon St. The original location on SE Division was previously a hair salon called "The Hair Bender," whose name Stumptown adopted for one of their signature espresso blends.[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

In November 2007, Stumptown opened two cafes in Seattle.[[15]](#cite_note-15) In September 2009, the company also launched a cafe in New York's Ace Hotel.[[16]](#cite_note-16) A temporary "pop-up" location appeared in Amsterdam's De Pijp neighborhood in May 2010.[[17]](#cite_note-17) Opened by Sorenson, he claimed it was never intended to be permanent and closed its doors that same year.

In 2013, Stumptown opened a second New York City café and a café/roaster in Los Angeles.[[18]](#cite_note-18) Additional cafes have also opened in Chicago and New Orleans. Stumptown opened their third New York cafe in a historic Brooklyn firehouse in the summer of 2018.[[19]](#cite_note-19) A location at the [Portland International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_International_Airport "Portland International Airport") opened in 2024.[[20]](#cite_note-20)[[21]](#cite_note-21)

## Reception

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stumptown_Coffee_Roasters&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Reception")]

Stumptown won in the Best Coffee (Locally Roasted) category of *[Willamette Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willamette_Week "Willamette Week")*'s annual 'Best of Portland' readers' poll in 2006.[[22]](#cite_note-22) It was a runner-up in the Best Coffee Shop category in 2017 and won in the Best Coffee Roaster category in 2018.[[23]](#cite_note-23)[[24]](#cite_note-24) Stumptown was a runner-up and ranked second in the Best Coffee category in 2020 and 2022, respectively.[[25]](#cite_note-25)[[26]](#cite_note-26) It was a finalist in the same category in 2025.[[27]](#cite_note-27)

Stumptown Coffee Roasters Portland.content:
Stumptown Coffee Roasters in Portland, Oregon, is known for its large downtown café that features a full espresso bar, drip coffee, and cold brew options. Visitors can also enjoy beverages made from Dona Chai and Spirit Tea, along with pastries and breakfast sandwiches sourced from local bakeries, including Shoofly Vegan Bakery and Sparrow Bakery. # Coffee

![Coffee](//www.stumptowncoffee.com/cdn/shop/collections/Stumptown-mug.gif?v=1761607895&width=110)

### How to Choose the Right Coffee

Finding your perfect coffee doesn’t have to be complicated—but a little know-how goes a long way. Whether you're chasing fruity and bright or bold and smoky, here are a couple key things to think about when you're dialing in your next bag.

#### Single Origin vs. Blend: What’s the Difference?

* Single Origin coffees come from [one specific farm or region](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/blogs/news/growing-a-sustainable-future), and they’re all about unique flavors and a sense of place. Like **[Colombia El Jordan](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/colombia-el-jordan)**, which delivers syrupy cherry, dark chocolate, and baking spice from the lush highlands. Or [**Indonesia Bies Penantan**](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/indonesia-bies-penantan), a medium roast with dark chocolate, pineapple, and clove notes from the rich volcanic soils of Sumatra.
* Blends are crafted by combining beans from multiple origins to create balance, consistency, and depth. **[Hundred Mile](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/hundred-mile)** is a smooth, easygoing blend with a chocolatey backbone and just enough fruit to keep things interesting.

Not sure where to start? If you’re curious about terroir and want to taste something distinct, [try a single origin](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/blogs/news/growing-a-sustainable-future). Want a crowd-pleaser that brews up solid every time? [Go with a blend](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/collections/signature-blends).

#### Light, Medium, or Dark: Know Your Roast

* **Light Roast**– Bright, juicy, and complex. A coffee like **[Homestead](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/homestead)** keeps it light on the roast. Expect a balance of chocolate, candied fruit, and nougat sweetness.
* **Medium Roast**– Balanced and approachable. **[Colombia El Jordan](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/colombia-el-jordan)** hits that sweet spot—full-bodied with notes of caramel, red fruit, and subtle spice.
* **Dark Roast** – Big, bold, and roasty. [**French Roast**](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/french-roast) is our classic dark roast that doesn’t mess around. Smoky, bittersweet, and built for those who appreciate a classic dark brew with big flavor.

There’s no wrong way to choose—just follow your flavor and your mood. [However you brew](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/brew-guide), we've got the coffee to match.

## Stumptown Coffee FAQ

### What is Stumptown Coffee Roasters?

Stumptown is a specialty coffee roaster founded in Portland, Oregon. We source our beans through direct trade relationships with producers across four continents, many of whom we've worked with for over a decade. We pioneered the Direct Trade sourcing model in 2003, paying premium prices tied directly to quality, and in 2024 over 90 percent of our purchases came through partnerships of three or more consecutive years. Every coffee we roast is built on those relationships. [Learn more about our story.](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/our-story)

### Does Stumptown sell ground coffee?

We do. In fact, some of our coffees are available in both [whole bean](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/collections/whole-bean-coffee) and [ground](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/collections/ground-coffee) options. Just select your preferred grind when adding to cart.

### Does Stumptown offer coffee subscriptions?

Yes. With a [Stumptown coffee subscription](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/subscribe), you get coffee roasted to order and shipped on your schedule. You can adjust your selections, frequency, or cancel anytime.

### How should I store my coffee to keep it fresh?

Keep your coffee in an airtight container at room temperature, away from direct sunlight and moisture. Avoid storing it in the fridge or freezer, as temperature changes can introduce condensation and affect flavor. For the best taste, try to use your coffee within two to three weeks of the roast date.

#### Forget About It With a Subscription

If you find your perfect roast, subscribe and let us do all the work. With a [Stumptown coffee subscription](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/subscribe) you get:

* Coffee roasted to order and shipped on your schedule
* Flexible options to adjust anytime
* A steady supply of your go-to brew

Explore the lineup and find your flavor.

# Stumptown Coffee Roasters


**Description:** Stumptown was started with the goal of doing things differently, with a vision that’s always been a little left-of-center, and with the focus squarely on quality. We source the best coffees in the world and strive to maintain transparent, quality-based relationships with our farmers along the way. From plant to portafilter, we pay homage to these folks through our own fervent attention to detail at every step, quality control in our cupping labs, meticulous roasting profiles and extensive barista education. We are committed to the well-being of everyone we work with, from the farmers and the communities they live in, to our employees and communities here in the States. We value our relationships with our customers, growers, and each other. With our roastery facility in Portland, multiple cafes, and fantastic wholesale partnerships around the country, we think there’s a lot to be proud of here.

**Counter Culture Coffee** is a [Durham, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durham,_North_Carolina "Durham, North Carolina")–based [coffee roasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_roasting "Coffee roasting") company[[1]](#cite_note-1) founded in 1995. It has regional [training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Training "Training") locations in [Asheville, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asheville,_NC "Asheville, NC"); [Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta"); [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston"); [Charleston, South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleston,_SC "Charleston, SC"); [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"); [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas "Dallas"); [Durham, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durham,_NC "Durham, NC"); [Emeryville, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emeryville,_CA "Emeryville, CA"); [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"); [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami"); [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"); and [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[2]](#cite_note-Why_We_Love_Counter_Culture_Coffee-2) Counter Culture training centers provide education in the fundamentals of preparing and serving [coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee "Coffee") and serve as classrooms and event spaces. Training centers are not only for vendors of Counter Culture Coffee but are also available to anyone interested in coffee production. Training centers also host competition training, food events with guest chefs, and professional [workshops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workshops "Workshops").[[3]](#cite_note-3)

Counter Culture Coffee buys primarily from small coffee producers at prices between $1.30 and $25 a pound.[[4]](#cite_note-Fellner2008-4) As such, they are regarded as a "boutique" coffee roaster, a company which sources from multiple small [estates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estate_(land) "Estate (land)") and [cooperatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooperative "Cooperative") rather than a single large grower.[[5]](#cite_note-Dougherty2008-5)

## Company history

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Counter_Culture_Coffee&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Company history")]

Counter Culture Coffee started [roasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roasting "Roasting") coffee in Durham in 1995. Founded by Brett Smith and Fred Houk, their focus was creating custom coffee blends for some of Durham and [Chapel Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapel_Hill,_North_Carolina "Chapel Hill, North Carolina")'s southern restaurants.[[6]](#cite_note-6) They sold their first coffee to Pop's Restaurant in Durham in 1995.[[7]](#cite_note-A_Different_Kind_of_Coffee_Company-7) The company expanded its operations to areas along the [East Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Coast_of_the_United_States "East Coast of the United States"). The firm also diversified its line of products and services, offering [seasonal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seasonal "Seasonal") coffee selections and [educational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Educational "Educational") programs that focus on [sustainability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainability "Sustainability") and the [coffee brewing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_brewing "Coffee brewing") process.[*[needs update](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")*]

## Sustainability

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Counter_Culture_Coffee&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Sustainability")]

Counter Culture Coffee directly collaborates with [artisans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artisans "Artisans") who grow the coffee, and their partnership with [farmers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farmers "Farmers") is a basis for their [sustainable coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainable_coffee "Sustainable coffee") model, which involves working with [progressive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressivism "Progressivism") and environmentally sensitive farms in the trade. In 2008, they launched a third-party Counter Culture Direct Trade Certification, establishing [direct trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_trade "Direct trade") standards for sustainability, quality, and fairness in the coffee chain.[[2]](#cite_note-Why_We_Love_Counter_Culture_Coffee-2) Additional initiatives include their Sustaining Educational and Environmental Development at a Source (SEEDS) program and the company's Sustainability Scorecard. The SEEDS initiative aims to support sustainability and education on the origins of the products. At the same time, the Sustainability Scorecard measures the impact of the company's efforts toward building a more sustainable supply chain.

## Education

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Counter_Culture_Coffee&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Education")]

The firm also provides consumers, employees, and wholesale partners with educational programs on coffee brewing, origin, and history. Professional development courses include Brewing Science, Barista Fundamentals, Coffee Origins, Cupping Fundamentals, and Brewing: Technique & Troubleshooting.   
Public educational initiatives include free "Tastings at Ten" every Friday morning, as well as homebrew labs for coffee enthusiasts offered at a fee.[[8]](#cite_note-8) Educational courses are offered at twelve Counter Culture Training Centers across the country.[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-Thirsty_South-10)[[11]](#cite_note-:0-11)

## Locations

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Counter_Culture_Coffee&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Locations")]

Coffee is roasted in two production facilities in Durham, North Carolina (also the company's headquarters) and Emeryville, California.[[10]](#cite_note-Thirsty_South-10)[[11]](#cite_note-:0-11)

CCC's ethos centers on the relentless pursuit of coffee perfection, genuine environmental, social, and fiscal sustainability, and the cultivation of cutting-edge coffee people. CCC fosters partnerships with growers globally, prioritizing quality and transparency.

# Counter Culture Coffee

Visit Website

Phone: (888) 238-5282 

Directions 4.6

Counter Culture is brewing beauty from beans, and folks are taking notice. There certainly is a distinct culture to their coffee. Although their brick and mortar is only open to the public at their training room on Fridays at 10 a.m., this Durham-based coffee roasting company has training locations throughout the country and delivers blends directly to your doorstep. # Counter Culture Coffee

[Visit Website](http://www.counterculturecoffee.com)

Phone: [(888) 238-5282](tel:+1-888-238-5282) 

[Directions](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/Current+Location/35.9966548,-78.888519) 4.6

Counter Culture is brewing beauty from beans, and folks are taking notice. There certainly is a distinct culture to their coffee. Although their brick and mortar is only open to the public at their training room on Fridays at 10 a.m., this Durham-based coffee roasting company has training locations throughout the country and delivers blends directly to your doorstep.

[![](/images/transparent.png)

![](/images/transparent.png)](https://files.idss.com/C534/account_listing_images/AJRVUZMzowIjHEv1Cxd2UY9XciUY-Uvy_xHm_AZjfrK2S2fd05XYi5io0fh3.jpg)

Google Rating

4.6  

* ![Carpe Diem Main Branch](/images/transparent.png)   [Carpe Diem Main Branch](https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/111813270199655831523/reviews)    2 years ago

  We would have given this 30 stars, one for each year that Counter Culture has been in business! We are next-door neighbors to this extraordinary coffee roaster, and our leadership team decided to try the Friday morning Tasting at Ten. We are a local business that has also survived and thrived for 30 years, and it was an honor to meet Jesse and Jamie, who not only provided our group with delicious coffee but also shared so much about the finer points of coffee, flavor profiles, and the best way to store coffee. This company knows coffee, and being sustainably minded, we appreciated their sources, practices, and how enthusiastic and knowledgeable they were about their coffee. We tried the Even Keel half-caff and it was our new favorite. We highly recommend the Tasting at Ten and buying a coffee subscription.
* ![Lennon Davis](/images/transparent.png)   [Lennon Davis](https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/101551343623389355366/reviews)    2 years ago

  My daily driver!  
   Full time traveler here (@whatrvdoing)! Being on the road has its challenges. There are so many coffee shops that do not produce quality roasts. That said, and thanks to these guys, I have been able to get my beans delivered anywhere in the country. Big shout out to Ryan from customer service, he is amazing. Go for the single origin 2 bag subscription so that you have variety in your daily brew. My personal favorite is Kushikama from Kenya.
* ![Jesse S.](/images/transparent.png)   [Jesse S.](https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/108645047749222057261/reviews)    3 years ago

  Yo my local coffee roasters. I picked up a bag of your big trouble beans at Whole Foods and just made the best latte I've ever made. Y'all are awesome. I wish I would have given you a try sooner. Looking forward to trying more of your lineup.
* ![Will Nickley](/images/transparent.png)   [Will Nickley](https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/101070263556140784117/reviews)    3 months ago

  Yes, HQ is in that warehouse-lookin’ building with the large tower. Yes, the Friday tasting was well-attended, well-organized, and a great experience for anyone who enjoys coffee; approachable for all, engaging for snobs like me, too. Thanks, Counter Culture, for hosting your weekly, free sessions!
* ![Robyn&Jax N](/images/transparent.png)   [Robyn&Jax N](https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/102319208967065940811/reviews)    a year ago

  The coffee is amazing! But in the past, the coffee tasting was more informative. Years ago, they used to talk about the roasting process and the different ways to brew coffee and more about the origin of the beans. That's all gone now and it was just a tasting of a featured coffee. The other was really MUCH more interesting. Please bring that back.

**Intelligentsia Coffee** is an American [coffee roasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_roasting "Coffee roasting") company and retailer based in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois"). Founded in 1995 by Doug Zell and Emily Mange, Intelligentsia is considered a major representative of [third-wave coffee in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third-wave_coffee_in_the_United_States "Third-wave coffee in the United States"). In 2015, [Peet's Coffee & Tea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peet's_Coffee_&_Tea "Peet's Coffee & Tea") (itself part of [JAB Holding Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JAB_Holding_Company "JAB Holding Company")) acquired a majority stake in the company.[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2)

## History and locations

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Intelligentsia_Coffee_%26_Tea&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History and locations")]

Intelligentsia is headquartered at 1850 W. Fulton Street, Chicago, IL, and has several cafe retail locations throughout the Chicago area. They supply coffee to various Chicago-area cafes and restaurants, as well as other locations in the US and Canada.[[3]](#cite_note-CR-3)[[4]](#cite_note-LA-4)[[5]](#cite_note-WC-5) They generally buy their beans directly from growers in Central America, South America, East Africa, and Ethiopia.[[6]](#cite_note-eG-6) Their roasting facility is in Chicago with a 300 kilogram capacity Probat R1500R roaster alongside two Gothot roasters with a capacity of 90 and 23 kilograms respectively.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

On August 17, 2007, Intelligentsia opened its first store outside of Chicago at [Sunset Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunset_Junction "Sunset Junction") in [Silver Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Lake,_Los_Angeles,_California "Silver Lake, Los Angeles, California"), a district east of [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles") in [Los Angeles, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles,_California "Los Angeles, California").[[8]](#cite_note-LAT-8) Intelligentsia has opened two additional stores in the Los Angeles area, in Venice and Pasadena.[[9]](#cite_note-9) In 2013, Intelligentsia opened its first store in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") inside [The High Line Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_High_Line_Hotel "The High Line Hotel").[[10]](#cite_note-10) The second New York City location opened in June 2014, inside the [Urban Outfitters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Outfitters "Urban Outfitters") store in Herald Square. This is the first location to offer a full food menu.[[11]](#cite_note-11) They also have 2 stores in [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") and one in [Austin, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin,_Texas "Austin, Texas").[[12]](#cite_note-12) A 2008 decision to stop serving 20-ounce coffee and [espresso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Espresso "Espresso") beverages in stores was met with controversy. Zell stated that the proportions are altered at such large quantities and certain drinks become watered-down, arguing that 20-ounce drinks end up "masking and adulterating the pure, intense flavors we work hard to source, roast and produce. We don't want this to just be a [caffeine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caffeine "Caffeine") delivery device."[[13]](#cite_note-13)

In 2009 Intelligentsia acquired Ecco Caffè of [Santa Rosa, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa,_California "Santa Rosa, California"), and has retained the brand.[[14]](#cite_note-14)

In October 2015, it was announced that [Peet's Coffee & Tea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peet's_Coffee "Peet's Coffee") would buy a majority stake in Intelligentsia Coffee & Tea by the end of the year, as part of an expansion of Peet's into third wave coffee that also involved the acquisition of [Stumptown Coffee Roasters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stumptown_Coffee_Roasters "Stumptown Coffee Roasters").[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2) Intelligentsia was expected to continue operating independently, with founders Zell and Mange retaining a role in the company.[[15]](#cite_note-:1-15) The announcement came weeks after Intelligentsia had made known that it was seeking a private equity buy-out over $100 million.[[15]](#cite_note-:1-15)

In May 2022 employees working in Intelligentsia's Chicago locations and Roasting Works warehouse filed a petition for [union representation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_unions_in_the_United_States "Labor unions in the United States").[[16]](#cite_note-16) In August 2022, employees voted to unionize, and ratified their first [collective bargaining agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collective_bargaining_agreement "Collective bargaining agreement") in December 2022.[[17]](#cite_note-17)[[18]](#cite_note-18) They are represented by [IBEW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBEW "IBEW") 1220, the same branch of IBEW that represents [Colectivo Coffee Roasters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colectivo_Coffee_Roasters "Colectivo Coffee Roasters").[[19]](#cite_note-19)

In 2006, Intelligentsia was included on several local[[20]](#cite_note-CS-20)[[21]](#cite_note-21)[[22]](#cite_note-22) and national[[23]](#cite_note-USAToday-23)[[24]](#cite_note-FW-24)[[25]](#cite_note-25) best-of lists. One of their baristas also won national and international honors.[[26]](#cite_note-26)[[27]](#cite_note-27)

It has been winning local best of list recognition from 2000 to 2005.[[28]](#cite_note-28)[[29]](#cite_note-29)[[30]](#cite_note-30)[[31]](#cite_note-31) In 2005, the local[[32]](#cite_note-32)[[33]](#cite_note-33)[[34]](#cite_note-34)[[35]](#cite_note-35) recognition extended to national[[36]](#cite_note-36) recognition. In 2006, Intelligentsia was included on several local[[37]](#cite_note-37) and national[[38]](#cite_note-38)[[39]](#cite_note-39)[[40]](#cite_note-40) "best" lists.

# Our Story

# Our Story

Intelligentsia is a specialty coffee pioneer, rising from humble Chicago roots to a company driven by curiosity, contribution, and the never-ending quest for the most extraordinary coffee in the world.

Intelligentsia is a specialty coffee pioneer, rising from humble Chicago roots to a company driven by curiosity, empowerment, and the never-ending quest for the most extraordinary coffee in the world.

## The Story Begins in 1995

## The Story Begins in 1995

Doug Zell and Emily Mange just wanted freshly roasted coffee. It was really that simple. After moving from San Francisco to Chicago, they found that great tasting coffee in their new city was surprisingly elusive.

Doug Zell and Emily Mange just wanted freshly roasted coffee. It was really that simple. After moving from San Francisco to Chicago, they found that great tasting coffee in their new city was surprisingly elusive.

But instead of complaining or—even worse—settling for bad coffee, they hunkered down and wrote the original business plan for what would become Intelligentsia Coffee. Their dream was to open a café and roaster in the city’s emerging Lakeview neighborhood, and on October 9, 1995, the dream welcomed its first customers.

![ ]()

Roasting their coffee in-store with a Probat L12, they honed their coffee worldview one bag of  Black Cat at a time, building slowly and seeking nothing less than perfection in every aspect of the business. Little did Doug and Emily know, they were launching what would become a fundamental sea change in specialty coffee in the United States. And by placing a deep emphasis on sourcing the most exquisite coffee available on Earth, paying a fair price for that coffee, roasting it with purpose and precision, and connecting with the community—both in Chicago and around the globe—their scrappy little coffee company would grow and help shape an entire industry.

![ ]()

![ ]()

## Intelligentsia Today

## Intelligentsia Today

Fast forward to today, and Intelligentsia still holds these original values close, though at a scale that brings extraordinary coffee to tens of thousands of customers daily.

Through coffeebars, training labs, and Roasting Works in Chicago, Intelligentsia has a unique and growing presence in five American cities—Austin, Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, and New York—and Seoul, South Korea, with more to be announced in the future.

intelligentsia still holds these original values close, though at a scale that brings extraordinary coffee to tens of thousands of customers daily.

In Season coffee subscriptions and national grocery distribution brings Intelligentsia’s rotating selection of single-origin coffees and blends to customers around the world, while many of the world’s finest restaurants, hotels, and cafés proudly call Intelligentsia their house coffee.

**Verve Coffee Roasters** is a [coffee roaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_roaster "Coffee roaster") based in [Santa Cruz, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Cruz,_California "Santa Cruz, California"), founded by Colby Barr[[1]](#cite_note-1) and Ryan O'Donovan.[[2]](#cite_note-2) Verve opened in November, 2007[[3]](#cite_note-3) in [Pleasure Point, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleasure_Point,_California "Pleasure Point, California"). The company currently operates in several California-based locations,[[4]](#cite_note-VerveLocations-4) including four in [Santa Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Cruz,_California "Santa Cruz, California"), four in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), one in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), one in [Manhattan Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan_Beach,_California "Manhattan Beach, California"), one in [Palo Alto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palo_Alto,_California "Palo Alto, California"), and two in Menlo Park at the campuses of [Meta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_Platforms "Meta Platforms") and [SLAC.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SLAC_National_Accelerator_Laboratory "SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory")[[5]](#cite_note-5) They also have seven locations in Japan: five in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), including the [Shinjuku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shinjuku_Station "Shinjuku Station") train station, as well as one in [Kamakura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamakura "Kamakura") and a cafe/roastery in the [Kanagawa Prefecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanagawa_Prefecture "Kanagawa Prefecture"). Verve earned the highest score in the [coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee "Coffee") category at the [Good Food Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Food_Awards "Good Food Awards") in 2013[[6]](#cite_note-Sprudge-6) and was also named one of the top coffee roasters in the United States by [Thrillist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrillist "Thrillist"),[[7]](#cite_note-Thrillist-7) [Complex Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_Magazine "Complex Magazine"),[[8]](#cite_note-ComplexMag-8) and Food Republic [[9]](#cite_note-FoodRepublic-9) In 2018, they won the [Best Espresso at the Coffee Spot Awards](https://www.brian-coffee-spot.com/2018/12/29/2018-awards-best-espresso/), and in 2021 be nominated for the cafe in Japan at the [World Latitude Caffe Prize.](https://www.wl-c.org/honor-2021/en/verve-coffee-roasters-omotesando-tokyo-roppongi)

In 2024, Verve was selected as Macro Roaster of the Year by Roast Magazine, noting the company's innovations in sustainability, ethical growth, and positive employee culture.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

Since opening, Verve has expanded to ten cafe locations between Santa Cruz, Los Angeles, the San Francisco Bay Area and Tokyo. from Google & Yelp

"I try to come here whenever I’m in town. I believe this is the original location? Might be wrong about that. Either way, the coffee and pastries are always fantastic and so is the service and location"

"I live on the street near this place. The roasting operation puts out a constant hum of noise in addition to the beeping of trucks backing up and the smell of burnt marshmallows (not the yummy coffee smell I had hoped for). We have put up with it without complaint for years. Want to support local businesses and be a good neighbor. A few days ago I stopped in to ask whether they might be open to giving me their used coffee grounds for my garden compost and the girl working there was so rude. “No, we’re not going to do that.” The manager was a little nicer. She said they have space issues, and it is a small space, but they have two trash cans right there and space for one more. I offered to provide a bin for them to put right next to the trash cans to toss the grounds in and I would come by to pick up, but they wouldn’t even consider it. They did say that I could pick through their trash to pull out the coffee grounds! Maybe I will take them up on that. I feel like it’s not hard to make a small change for the environment, to not waste the nutrients and not contribute to climate change. So I am pretty disappointed with the company. The business is built on coffee beans grown in the earth, so putting the nutrients back into the soil just makes sense for sustainability."

"Coffee ☕️ roasters depot… fast, quality service. Loved the cold brew iced coffee with cream… just the thing for an afternoon pick n go pick-me-up! Great flavor/roast on the daily coffees!"

★★★★★

"Verve is great. The coffee is always on point. It’s hard to pick a favorite location, each one has its own vibe and is worth checking out! And if a barista messes up your order they’re very quick to make it right"

★★★★★

"Verve Coffee Roasters in Santa Cruz is a coffee lover's paradise that never fails to impress. This trendy and inviting café offers an exceptional coffee experience that is hard to match. The moment you step inside Verve Coffee Roasters, you're greeted by the rich aroma of freshly brewed coffee. The ambiance is warm and inviting, with cozy seating arrangements and an eclectic décor that creates a relaxed and comfortable atmosphere. The star of the show at Verve is, of course, the coffee. They take great pride in sourcing high-quality beans from around the world and roasting them in-house to perfection. Each cup of coffee is expertly prepared by their skilled baristas, resulting in a rich and flavorful experience that will please even the most discerning coffee connoisseur. Whether you prefer a classic espresso, a velvety latte, or a pour-over brewed to perfection, Verve has an impressive selection of coffee offerings to satisfy all tastes. They also offer a variety of brewing methods, allowing you to explore and appreciate the unique characteristics of different beans and flavors. In addition to their outstanding coffee, Verve Coffee Roasters also offers a small but delightful menu of pastries and snacks. These delectable treats pair perfectly with their coffee and provide a satisfying accompaniment to your beverage of choice. The service at Verve is friendly and knowledgeable. The baristas are passionate about their craft and are always happy to share their expertise and recommendations. Whether you're a coffee aficionado or a curious newcomer, they will guide you through the menu and help you discover new and exciting flavors. Verve Coffee Roasters is not just a café; it's a community hub for coffee enthusiasts. It's a place where people gather to connect, unwind, and appreciate the art of coffee. The vibrant energy and friendly atmosphere make it a favorite spot for locals and visitors alike. In conclusion, Verve Coffee Roasters is a must-visit destination for coffee lovers in Santa Cruz. With their exceptional coffee, inviting ambiance, and knowledgeable staff, they deliver an unforgettable coffee experience. Whether you're seeking your daily caffeine fix or looking to explore the world of specialty coffee, Verve will exceed your expectations and leave you craving for more."

★★★★★

# Onyx Coffee Lab Named 2026 James Beard Award Semifinalist, Breakthrough Moment for Specialty Coffee

PR Newswire

2 min read

*Recognition elevates specialty coffee to a national stage*

ROGERS, Ark., Jan. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- [Onyx Coffee Lab](https://onyxcoffeelab.com/?utm_source=mhpsi&utm_campaign=jamesbeard) has been named a semifinalist for the [**2026 James Beard Award**](https://www.jamesbeard.org/stories/james-beard-award-semifinalists-2026)[**®**](https://www.jamesbeard.org/stories/james-beard-award-semifinalists-2026)[**for Outstanding Bar**](https://www.jamesbeard.org/stories/james-beard-award-semifinalists-2026)**,** marking a milestone not only for the brand but for specialty coffee's growing presence in culinary landscape.

[![Onyx Coffee Lab](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///ywAAAAAAQABAAACAUwAOw==)](https://mma.prnewswire.com/media/2870219/Onyx.html)

Onyx Coffee Lab

 

The nomination places Onyx among select bars recognized by the **James Beard Foundation** — category historically dominated by cocktail and wine destinations. For specialty coffee, the recognition reflects a rare crossover moment, where craft, hospitality and culture meet on one of the food world's biggest stages.

"This nomination recognizes what specialty coffee has become," said Jon Allen, co-founder of Onyx Coffee Lab. "Coffee today is a culinary craft, a hospitality experience, and a cultural force. To see it acknowledged on this stage is a milestone not just for Onyx but for the industry."

Founded in Rogers, Arkansas, Onyx has built a global reputation for its uncompromising approach to sourcing, roasting and hospitality, most recently named one of the [Best Coffee Bars in America](https://theworlds100bestcoffeeshops.com/locales/onyx-coffee-lab/). The company is known for its transparent pricing model, producer partnerships, and cafés that prioritize design, service and education alongside exceptional coffee.

Andrea Allen, co-founder of Onyx Coffee Lab, said the nomination reflects a broader shift in how people experience coffee. "To see specialty coffee in the semifinals of the James Beard AwardsⓇ brings validation and legitimacy to what is not just a global industry but a craft that signifies the highest levels of excellence, execution, breadth of flavor, innovation and intentionality of service. We are thrilled and hope to see many coffee companies represented in the James Beard AwardsⓇ for years to come."

The nomination comes amid rising mainstream attention on specialty coffee, as consumers seek more thoughtful, experience-driven brands.

Finalists for 2026 will be announced later this spring, with winners revealed at the James Beard Restaurant and Chef Awards ceremony in Chicago.

**ABOUT ONYX COFFEE LAB**   
Headquartered in Rogers, Ark., [Onyx Coffee Lab](https://onyxcoffeelab.com/?srsltid=AfmBOopOPzRLIMEtf21DSFSmcJ25Q4iXwILLWZrhwUfA_zpSDdQmzsQV) is a globally recognized specialty coffee roaster and café operator known for its commitment to quality, transparency, and hospitality. Onyx is a Certified B Corporation and has received multiple international awards for excellence in coffee sourcing, roasting, and service. For more information, visit [onyxcoffeelab.com](https://onyxcoffeelab.com/) or follow @onyxcoffeelab on Instagram.

# HQ at the 1907

Located inside a historic building in downtown Rogers, our HQ is built to showcase each part of the coffee supply chain we engage in. From green coffee buying and sample roasting, to full production roasting, to training baristas and serving coffee in the cafe, our HQ allows each person working in various roles to see and appreciate each other's positions and talents inside of coffee. Amongst our own coffee concepts there’s a bakery, a taqueria and mezcal bar, a twenty-seat tasting restaurant, and a high-end cocktail bar all created by our favorite chefs and makers in the area.

In 1999, Starbucks experimented by opening eateries in the San Francisco Bay Area, under the Circadia restaurant brand. At the same time, Starbucks converted its Seattle Circadia restaurant into a Café Starbucks. The same year, Starbucks acquired Pasqua Coffee—a San Francisco-based retail coffee chain that had almost 60 locations in San Francisco, Los Angeles, and New York City.

In 2012, Starbucks had annual Frappuccino sales of over US$2 billion. In August 2012, the largest Starbucks in the US opened at the University of Alabama's Ferguson Centre. On June 25, 2013, Starbucks began to post calorie counts on menus for drinks and pastries in all of its U.S. stores. In July 2013, more than 10% of in-store purchases were made on customers' mobile devices via the Starbucks app.
