# Café de Flore Paris: An Enduring Piece of Parisian History

[Cafes & Bistros](https://mostlovelythings.com/category/french-finds/cafes-bistros/) | [Our French Finds](https://mostlovelythings.com/category/french-finds/)

There is no shortage of great bistros, cafes, or restaurants in Paris. As much time as we’ve spent in Paris, we rarely eat at the same one twice. But [Café de Flore](https://cafedeflore.fr/en/) is different. Yes, it’s touristy which is why many people skip it. But if you can look beyond that, there is so much more. We make it a point to stop by on almost every trip.

 

It’s located in Paris’ trendiest neighborhood, Saint Germain des Prés. With its mosaic-tiled floors, wicker chairs, and round cafe tables on the sidewalk, it’s more than just a cafe—it’s a living piece of Parisian history. For decades, famous artists, writers, creatives, intellectuals, and philosophers have gathered here to have a drink and talk.

We’ve been here on a warm, sunny afternoon sitting under its iconic awning. We’ve enjoyed the portable heaters on a cold and rainy evening. We’ve stopped for morning coffee and chocolate croissant. But no matter the time of day, season, or the weather, it always seems to live up to the magic of Paris.

## The cafe culture in Paris and Europe in general

One of my most favorite things about Paris is the cafe culture where eating is not just about consumption, it’s an event and something to look forward to and cherish. It’s something to make time for and enjoy the people and the moment every bit as much as the food.

## A little history of Café de Flore

Legend has it that Café de Flore opened in the 1880s (probably 1887) and in the early 1900s began to attract some of the most forward-thinkers of the time; Pablo Picasso, Simone de Beauvoir, and Trotzky just to name a few. Over the years, its famous clientele also included Ernest Hemingway who lived in Paris for a while.

Today, it’s just a great place for friends or business acquaintances to get together and share a meal or a drink and a snack.

## Is it hard to get a table at Café de Flore?

I must confess, we have never sat inside and had a proper dinner. It does look cozy with its mahogany booths and brass railings. But, every time we’ve opted for the sidewalk tables, the snacking menu, and the people-watching. And as touristy as its reputation is, we seem to always sit next to what appears to be locals.

In the early evenings, a line forms outside for the sidewalk tables. But we have never waited more than five minutes to be seated. The line moves quickly so don’t let that scare you off.

If, by chance, you can’t get seated, we’ve tried [Les Deux Magots](https://lesdeuxmagots.fr/en/) several times. Conveniently, it’s right next to Café de Flore.

## The menu at Café de Flore

 

Café de Flore is probably most well known for their legendary French hot chocolate – thick, creamy, and absolutely decadent. It is good but incredibly rich. Very few people, based on my observations, can finish one as you’ll see the serving pitchers still half full when the customers leave. I typically like to eat my dessert rather than drink it.

We have always opted for the snacking menu. Their French onion soup is as good as it gets and can easily pass as a meal – especially on a cold, rainy evening. I also love their Croque Monsieur with the side salad.

If you’re just there for a drink, they also bring you their version of black-peppered potato chips which are a great snack and accompaniment.

## Where is Café de Flore located?

 

Café de Flore is at the corner of Boulevard Saint-Germain (one of the most famous streets of Paris) and Rue Saint-Benoit.

There may be trendier spots in Paris, but few offer the charm, history, and people-watching quite like Café de Flore. Whether it’s your first or fiftieth visit, it’s a place that will remind you why you fell in love with Paris in the first place.

Café de Flore Paris.title: Café de Flore - Restaurant
Café de Flore Paris.content:
The Café de Flore is one of two cafes, with its eternal neighbour the two maggots, legendary venues in Saint-Germain-des-Prés. In this beautiful art deco room or on the terrace which opens onto the Boulevard Saint-Germain, celebrities cross paths with locals and tourists. Clients come here for a coffee, lunch or dinner. The hot chocolate is one of the house specialities. A hotspot for intellectual Parisians, the Flore holds the Prix de Flore each year, awarding young up-and-coming writers. # Café de Flore

 172 boulevard Saint-Germain - 75006 Paris Musée d'Orsay - Saint-Germain-des-Prés

![Image 130](https://parisjetaime.com/data/layout_image/8408_Caf%C3%A9-de-Flore-Saint-Germain-des-Pr%C3%A9s--630x405--%C2%A9-Wikimedia_landscape_3-2_xs.jpg?ver=1700683000)

 The Café de Flore is one of two cafes, with its eternal neighbour the two maggots, legendary venues in Saint-Germain-des-Prés. In this beautiful art deco room or on the terrace which opens onto the Boulevard Saint-Germain, celebrities cross paths with locals and tourists. Clients come here for a coffee, lunch or dinner. The hot chocolate is one of the house specialities. A hotspot for intellectual Parisians, the Flore holds the Prix de Flore each year, awarding young up-and-coming writers.

## Description

Stop for a break at no. 172 on Boulevard Saint-Germain. There, you'll savour the pleasure of sipping a coffee on the terrace or tucking into a delicious meal in the comfort of the red seats inside, under the golden Art Deco ceiling lights. The atmosphere is unique. Welcome to Le Flore.

### Art and literature unleashed

From the late 19th century, the Café de Flore attracted famous authors such as Charles Maurras. A few years later, it became the favourite haunt of Guillaume Apollinaire, who even made it is study! The Café de Flore thus became the cradle of **surrealism** and, later, **Dadaism**. Next, writers, poets, painters, sculptors, fashion designers, filmmakers, singers, musicians and other artists began frequenting the Flore, closely followed by intellectuals.  
 Among them were **Jean-Paul Sartre** and **Simone de Beauvoir**, the couple who turned the Café into a legend. The two philosophers felt at home at the Flore, where they would work in the morning and receive their friends. **Existentialism** was born and a wind of freedom blew over post-war Saint-Germain-des-Prés, accompanied by the sounds of Boris Vian’s trumpet and the voice of Juliette Greco.

### An institution in Saint-Germain-des-Prés

Still highly popular among the Parisian intelligentsia, a meeting place for politicians and the press, the Café de Flore has its established codes. A ‘Flore regular’ can phone to book a table, for example. Are you a newcomer? Visiting Paris for the first time? No worries, just order a ‘café pot’ and they’ll bring you an espresso served in a pot on a tray. Once you’ve accomplished this rite of passage, you’ll be ready to savour a glass of wine or one of the traditional dishes from the restaurant menu.

After your break at this key Parisian address, you can explore the lively Rue des Saints-Pères or Rue du Dragon. Both streets lead straight to the Sèvres-Babylone district, where you can admire the [stylish, unique collections on display in the boutiques](/en/inspiration/themed-guides/shopping-paris-saint-germain-des-pres) and the department store, [Le Bon Marché Rive gauche](/en/bon-marche-rive-gauche).

Pro tip

Check their Instagram for the monthly specials before you go. Arrive early, especially on weekends, as popular items sell out.

This is maybe the best place to eat croissant on Earth. Yes, this sounds like a hyperbole but trust me it is not.

It starts with the space, an old industrial warehouse in the hip neighbourhood of Fityroy, barely renovated houses the kitchen which is a ultra cool cube with same artistic light fixtures.

What a business model, every day from 8am to 3pm they serve a varying selection of croissants, danish and their own invention, the Cruffin.  
Every single pastry is amazingly good, perfectly executed, fresh from the oven and super delicious.  
But then they hit you with the Salty Caramel Croissant. I swear you will never, ever eat any pastry as good as this one. Onto the chocolate chip base they add very generously salts caramel and all this gets wrapped in the perfectly constructed layered dough.  
Unbelievable, no where in Vienna (where the croissant comes from) or Paris will you find anything as good as this. [Less](#)

Flour Bakery, located in Boston, MA, offers a variety of baked goods and meal options. The menu features items such as loaves of bread, pastries, and cakes, including their well-known double-crust apple pie. Customers can also order ready-to-bake kits for popular items like the Sticky Sticky Bun Kit, allowing them to recreate the bakery's signature treats at home.

In addition to baked goods, Flour Bakery provides catering services for events and monthly meal provisions through their dinner club. The place is notable for its emphasis on sharing love and gratitude through baking, making it a popular choice for both locals and visitors.

**Levain Bakery,** pronounced as (luh-ven),[[1]](#cite_note-1) is a retail bakery that opened in 1995 and is located at 167 [West 74th Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_74th_Street "West 74th Street"), on the [Upper West Side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_West_Side "Upper West Side") neighborhood of [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"). In June 2000 a second retail location was opened for seasonal business at 354 Montauk Highway, [Wainscott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wainscott,_New_York "Wainscott, New York"), in the [Hamptons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamptons "Hamptons") area of eastern [Long Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island "Long Island"). A third store is located in the [Harlem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlem "Harlem") neighborhood of [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"). In 2017, a fourth store was opened near the original location on the Upper West Side, and since then three more locations have opened on the [Upper East Side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_East_Side "Upper East Side") and in [NoHo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NoHo,_Manhattan "NoHo, Manhattan") and [Williamsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamsburg,_Brooklyn "Williamsburg, Brooklyn").[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3) In 2020, Levain opened their first store outside of New York, in [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_(Washington,_D.C.) "Georgetown (Washington, D.C.)"), [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[4]](#cite_note-4) In 2023, Levain opened a location in the Larchmont area of Los Angeles. As of June 2024, there are seventeen locations: nine in the New York City area, two each in Chicago, Washington D.C., and Boston, and one each in Los Angeles and Philadelphia.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Levain_Bakery&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Storefrontwainscott.jpg/250px-Storefrontwainscott.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Storefrontwainscott.jpg)

Front of Wainscott store

Founded and co-owned by Constance McDonald and Pamela Weekes, the bakery initially opened to serve a variety of fresh-baked [artisanal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slow_Food "Slow Food") breads.[[6]](#cite_note-6) The bakery has since become notable for its 6-ounce chocolate chip walnut cookies.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

McDonald and Weekes developed the signature cookie recipe while training for an [Ironman Triathlon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ironman_Triathlon "Ironman Triathlon"). They discovered they needed a large number of calories to offset the rigors of training and decided on a traditional chocolate chip cookie, but much bigger. The 6-ounce chocolate chip walnut cookie served the purpose and ultimately became a signature item in their bakery. The cookie has spawned copycats.[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9) In 1998 Levain Bakery expanded its cookie business to include mail order and in 2022 expanded their services to offer catering as well as nationwide shipping through Doordash.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

## Appearances in media

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Levain_Bakery&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Appearances in media")]

The Food Network has featured Levain Bakery in episodes of [Throwdown with Bobby Flay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Throwdown_with_Bobby_Flay "Throwdown with Bobby Flay"), Roker on the Road, [Unwrapped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unwrapped "Unwrapped"), Top 5, The Best Thing I Ever Ate, Sweet Dreams, and Worth It. In December 2007, Levain Bakery was featured on an episode of [Fashionably Late with Stacy London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashionably_Late_with_Stacy_London "Fashionably Late with Stacy London"). In June 2008, Budget Travel listed Levain Bakery #3 of “50 Reasons You Love New York City.”[[11]](#cite_note-11) They have been featured in the following books:

* *The Slow Food Guide To New York City*, Patrick Martins and Ben Watson.
* *New York's 50+ Best Places to Enjoy Dessert*, Andrea DiNoto and Paul Stiga.
* *A Day at the Beach*, Helen Schulman.
* *Cook What You Love*, Bob and Melinda Blanchard.
* *Jodi’s Shortcuts 2000* and *Jodi’s Shortcuts 2002*, Jodi Della Femina and Daniel Benedict
* Food and the city, Ina Yalof.

In 1995, our shared passion for breads urged us to open a little neighborhood bakery on W. 74th Street. The **Clinton Street Baking Company & Restaurant** (CSBC) is an American bakery and restaurant. It is located at 4 [Clinton Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_Street "Clinton Street") (between East [Houston Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Street "Houston Street") and [Stanton Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanton_Street "Stanton Street")), on the [Lower East Side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_East_Side "Lower East Side") of [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").[[1]](#cite_note-google1-1)[[2]](#cite_note-google2-2)[[3]](#cite_note-google3-3)

The restaurant is noted especially for its pancakes, its burgers, and its biscuits and other fresh-baked goods.[[3]](#cite_note-google3-3)[[4]](#cite_note-4) In December 2010, *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* described it as a "brunch magnet", and *[The New York Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Daily_News "The New York Daily News")* said the "legendary" dining destination was "the city's hottest breakfast nook".[[5]](#cite_note-nytimes1-5)[[6]](#cite_note-nydailynews1-6) *[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")* called it a "cult favorite".[[7]](#cite_note-autogenerated1-7) In 2011, *Poor Taste Magazine* rated it # 1 in its list of the 100 Best Brunch Spots in America.[[8]](#cite_note-poortastemag1-8)[[9]](#cite_note-villagevoice1-9)

## Restaurant

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Restaurant")]

The restaurant seats 32 people.[[6]](#cite_note-nydailynews1-6) It is located on Clinton Street, just off Houston Street, which the *[New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(magazine) "New York (magazine)")* magazine described as the "hippest restaurant row" on the Lower East Side.[[10]](#cite_note-nytimes2002-10) The restaurant is next to an 1853 [Romanesque Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanesque_Revival "Romanesque Revival") traditional synagogue, [Congregation Chasam Sopher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congregation_Chasam_Sopher "Congregation Chasam Sopher").[[10]](#cite_note-nytimes2002-10)[[11]](#cite_note-gothamist2006-11)[[12]](#cite_note-nymag2005-12)[[13]](#cite_note-13) It attracts a weekend brunch line that stretches around the corner of the block, which includes New York foodies and many foreign tourists.[[6]](#cite_note-nydailynews1-6)[[11]](#cite_note-gothamist2006-11)[[14]](#cite_note-nypost1-14)[[15]](#cite_note-eater1-15)

### Menu

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Menu")]

The restaurant serves refined [comfort food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comfort_food "Comfort food") and baked items, which are made daily on its premises, with breakfast (which it serves all day), lunch, brunch, and dinner.[[2]](#cite_note-google2-2)[[15]](#cite_note-eater1-15)[[16]](#cite_note-google4-16)[[17]](#cite_note-google5-17)[[18]](#cite_note-18)

Among the items that it is known for are its blueberry pancakes. *New York* magazine called them the best pancakes in town.[[12]](#cite_note-nymag2005-12) February is "Pancake Month" at the restaurant.[[19]](#cite_note-metromix2-19)[[20]](#cite_note-20)

It is also noted for its fluffy buttermilk biscuit sandwich with home-made tomato jam, and lauded for its baked goods, including its [scones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scone_(bread) "Scone (bread)") and muffins.[[12]](#cite_note-nymag2005-12)[[14]](#cite_note-nypost1-14)[[16]](#cite_note-google4-16)[[21]](#cite_note-21)[[22]](#cite_note-22)[[23]](#cite_note-nymag1-23) Its home-made desserts, including muffins, organic apple crumb, chocolate cake, maple-bourbon-pecan pie, creamy pumpkin cheesecake, and cherry pie, are topped with ice cream from the [Brooklyn Ice Cream Factory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Ice_Cream_Factory "Brooklyn Ice Cream Factory").[[17]](#cite_note-google5-17)[[24]](#cite_note-24)[[25]](#cite_note-25)[[26]](#cite_note-26)[[27]](#cite_note-27)

Its meals include [cage-free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cage-free "Cage-free") eggs, omelets, granola, brioches, grilled organic [free range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_range "Free range") chicken, buttermilk [fried chicken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fried_chicken "Fried chicken"), hamburgers, large warm buttermilk biscuits, cheese [grits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grits "Grits") fries, salads, and market soups.[[2]](#cite_note-google2-2)[[10]](#cite_note-nytimes2002-10)[[12]](#cite_note-nymag2005-12)[[16]](#cite_note-google4-16)[[28]](#cite_note-metromix1-28)[[29]](#cite_note-mirror1-29)[[30]](#cite_note-30) Drinks include lime [squash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squash_(drink) "Squash (drink)") and [bellinis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellini_(cocktail) "Bellini (cocktail)").[[31]](#cite_note-31)[[32]](#cite_note-32)

### Owners

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Owners")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/ff/DeDe_Lahman_and_Neil_Kleinberg.jpg/250px-DeDe_Lahman_and_Neil_Kleinberg.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DeDe_Lahman_and_Neil_Kleinberg.jpg)

Owners Neil Kleinberg and DeDe Lahman

It is owned by a husband-and-wife team of restaurateurs, seasoned chef Neil Kleinberg and DeDe Lahman.[[1]](#cite_note-google1-1)[[16]](#cite_note-google4-16) Kleinberg had originally planned to open the business with another partner, but Lahman, who was a former [advice columnist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advice_columnist "Advice columnist") and a [freelance writer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freelance_writer "Freelance writer") at the time running an apparel company, bought the partner out.[[11]](#cite_note-gothamist2006-11)[[33]](#cite_note-33) Kleinberg has responsibility for the restaurant's kitchen. Lahman is the restaurant's catering director and handles back-end responsibilities such as public relations.[[11]](#cite_note-gothamist2006-11)[[19]](#cite_note-metromix2-19)[[34]](#cite_note-34)

### History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: History")]

The restaurant began in 2001 as a bakery and a small coffee cafe, and over time became a full-fledged seven-days-a-week restaurant with a [liquor license](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquor_license "Liquor license").[[11]](#cite_note-gothamist2006-11) Kleinberg and Lahman host free cooking and healthy eating classes at the restaurant for neighborhood children.[[1]](#cite_note-google1-1)[[35]](#cite_note-35)

### Awards and accolades

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Awards and accolades")]

In December 2010, *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* described it as a "brunch magnet", and *[The New York Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Daily_News "The New York Daily News")* said that the "legendary" dining destination was "the city's hottest breakfast nook".[[5]](#cite_note-nytimes1-5)[[6]](#cite_note-nydailynews1-6) *Time* called it a "cult favorite".[[7]](#cite_note-autogenerated1-7)[[9]](#cite_note-villagevoice1-9) The restaurant has been one of [Zagat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zagat "Zagat")'s top picks on the Lower East Side.[[36]](#cite_note-usatoday1-36)

*Time* magazine cited it for having New York City's best pancakes in both 2005 and 2008.[[12]](#cite_note-nymag2005-12)[[23]](#cite_note-nymag1-23) The restaurant is noted especially for its fresh-baked goods.[[3]](#cite_note-google3-3) *[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")* described it as a "charming cafe with outstanding cherry pie".[[36]](#cite_note-usatoday1-36)

In January 2009, [Bobby Flay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Flay "Bobby Flay") challenged the owners of the restaurant to a "blueberry pancake showdown", which was filmed in an episode of *[Throwdown! with Bobby Flay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Throwdown!_with_Bobby_Flay "Throwdown! with Bobby Flay")* at the restaurant.[[37]](#cite_note-37)[[38]](#cite_note-38) In 2010, Kleinberg won [Godiva Chocolatier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godiva_Chocolatier "Godiva Chocolatier")'s SWEETest Challenge Award for his Warm Upside Down Pear Cake with pecan ice cream, caramel sauce, and [pecan brittle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pecan_brittle "Pecan brittle") at the third annual [Food Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_Network "Food Network") New York City Wine & Food Festival.[[39]](#cite_note-39)

In 2011, *Poor Taste Magazine* rated it # 1 in its list of the "100 Best Brunch Spots in America".[[8]](#cite_note-poortastemag1-8)[[9]](#cite_note-villagevoice1-9) In 2011, [Zagat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zagat "Zagat") ranked it 2nd out of 204, among traditional American restaurants in New York City.[[40]](#cite_note-40)

## Cookbook

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Cookbook")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/Clinton_Street_Baking_Co._%26_Restaurant_Eggs_Benedict.jpg/250px-Clinton_Street_Baking_Co._%26_Restaurant_Eggs_Benedict.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Clinton_Street_Baking_Co._&_Restaurant_Eggs_Benedict.jpg)

CSBC [Eggs Benedict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eggs_Benedict "Eggs Benedict")

The *Clinton St. Baking Company Cookbook: Breakfast, Brunch & Beyond from New York's Favorite Neighborhood Restaurant* (2010) was authored by Kleinberg and Lahman.[[41]](#cite_note-41) The book includes what *The New York Times* describes as the "celebrated" pancake recipe served at the restaurant, as well as the restaurant's other most popular recipes for [Eggs Benedict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eggs_Benedict "Eggs Benedict") and other preparations.[[5]](#cite_note-nytimes1-5)[[6]](#cite_note-nydailynews1-6) The book was identified by Julia Moskin of *The New York Times* as one of the year's best cookbooks, in December 2010.[[5]](#cite_note-nytimes1-5)

## Sister restaurant

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Sister restaurant")]

The owners opened up an eco-conscious sister restaurant, named "Community Food and Juice", that also serves American food.[[42]](#cite_note-nysun1-42) It is located at 2893 [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_(Manhattan) "Broadway (Manhattan)") between [112th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/112th_Street_(Manhattan) "112th Street (Manhattan)") and [113th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/113th_Street_(Manhattan) "113th Street (Manhattan)") Streets in [Morningside Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morningside_Heights "Morningside Heights"), Manhattan, and has an open kitchen and a bi-level dining room.[[43]](#cite_note-eater2-43)[[44]](#cite_note-nytimes3-44)[[45]](#cite_note-45)

## In popular culture

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Clinton_Street_Baking_Company_%26_Restaurant&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: In popular culture")]

The restaurant and its pancakes are mentioned in the 2011 book *Where I Belong*, by Gwendolyn Heasley.[[46]](#cite_note-46)

### Time Out says

If you grabbed brunch at Clinton St. Bakery and didn’t order the stack of fluffy blueberry pancakes, did you really even go? At least, that’s how sought-after the dish is among the early-morning (and breakfast-for-dinner) crowd. Chef Neil Kleinberg and DeDe Lahman, who co-own the Lower East Side hot spot, offer their iconic brunch items—think egg sandwiches and latke eggs Benedict—that New Yorkers line up for every weekend. Even on those mornings when it seems impossible to get out of bed, the duo beckons us to the Time Out Market for breakfast delights (and hangover cures).

4 Clinton St, New York, NY, 10002

When husband and wife team, Neil Kleinberg and DeDe Lahman, opened Clinton St. Baking Co in April 2001, their mission was to make the best baked goods in the city, using the freshest ingredients, hand-mixed in small batches. They bought dark French-roast coffee, ground it in house, and hired a college student to serve it with warm muffins, biscuits and scones. Soon the locals stumbled in, and mornings on Clinton Street came alive. Rumors of Neil's simple, delicious omelets, sandwiches and soups moved people to cluster, then crowd, and now form lines up the block. We're an unassuming storefront, with just 32 seats, and yet people travel from Tribeca and Toronto, and Tokyo to eat here. New York Magazine voted Neil's blueberry pancakes best in the city ( twice! ). Naturally, we agree, but the locals still come in for no-fuss-just-plain good food: a juicy burger and Brooklyn Lager, fried oysters with a spicy bloody Mary, or a decadent hot fudge sundae made with artisanal vanilla ice cream from the Brooklyn Ice Cream Factory. The lore about our brunch lines we cannot deny... but try us at dinner, when the lights are dim, the crowds calm, and the food is anything but ordinary, says the New York Observer. Okay, and Yes: You can still get a stack of pancakes after dark. Co-owner of Clinton Street and Community Restaurant, Neil Kleinberg raised himself in a crazy kitchen in Flatbush, Brooklyn, among 4 kids, 2 parents, 16 neighborhood cousins, and 6 aunts and uncles. At 10 years old, he became a one-boy culinary wonder who'd do anything to avoid his mother's famous dish: chicken in a pot ( the only dish in her repertoire ). His lunches, made assembly-line style for his relatives, were simple but classic: Tuna fish sandwiches on rye toast with crisp lettuce and beefsteak tomatoes, fresh corned beef w/mustard and sauerkraut, turkey and Swiss w/ Russian and slaw.

## [Tin Is In With Earnest Pursuit Coffee Roasting In New York City](https://sprudge.com/tin-is-in-with-earnest-pursuit-coffee-roasting-in-new-york-city-1528237.html)

# Build-Outs Of Coffee: Huckleberry Roasters In Denver, CO

![huckleberry roasters 1](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/huckleberry-roasters-1.jpg)
![huckleberry roasters 1](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/huckleberry-roasters-1.jpg)

[Huckleberry Roasters](https://huckleberryroasters.com/) has been bringing the denizens of Denver and beyond a taste of the lighter side of roasting for over a decade now. In that time, they’ve seen four of their own cafes open, and now this month, there will be a fifth. With their newest location, Huckleberry is expanding further into the northwest reaches of the city, while still keeping it tightly knit; the new cafe is but a mile west from their Tennyson location.

The opening of the latest location is imminent, so keep your eyes peeled for the all-new Huckleberry Roasters cafe in Denver, Colorado.

[![Pacific Foods](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/pacific-august-booc-laila-sprudge.jpg)](https://www.pacificfoodservice.com/ signature-drinks/?utm_campaign=38 781287-Pacific_Barista_Series&utm_ source=Sprudge&utm_medium=Dis play&utm_content=1170x600_Apple CiderCarmelo)![](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAP///////yH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

*The 2023 Build-Outs of Coffee is presented by [DONA.](https://drinkdona.com/) The**2023 Build-Outs of Coffee is sponsored by [La Marzocco](https://international.lamarzoccohome.com/en/), [Pacific Barista Series](https://www.instagram.com/baristaseries/), [Acaia](https://acaia.co/), and [Marco Beverage Systems.](http://www.marcobeveragesystems.com/)*

*As told to Sprudge by Mickayla Wawrousek.*

**For those who aren’t familiar, will you tell us about your company?**

We are a specialty coffee roaster based in Denver, CO started in 2011, with the core belief that business should build a sense of collective culture and community by investing in people.

**Can you tell us a bit about the new space?**

This is our fifth cafe that will be opening in the Denver area, we’ve renovated the entire interior with custom built-ins to best welcome folks into the space, signage was completed by local artists and we’ll be utilizing a drive-thru for service for the first time.

**What’s your approach to coffee?**

HUCK is committed to building a sustainable coffee business that prioritizes being a reliable roasting partner to the smallholder farms and coffee co-ops we work with. More generally, we seek to be a responsible business that actively supports local and global NGO’s and community-based organizations that support those who need it the most, both within and beyond the coffee industry.

![huckleberry roasters 3](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/huckleberry-roasters-3.jpg)

**Any machines, coffees, special equipment lined up?**

We’ll be using a [La Marzocco](https://lamarzoccousa.com/?utm_source=sprudge&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=build-outs-2023) for in-shop service and an [Eversys](https://www.eversys.com/) machine for drive-thru service.

**How is your project considering sustainability?**

The building is not ours and the building owner, while entirely nice and delightful, was not super interested in contributing to buildout hopes and dreams. So, we spend a pretty penny updating and/or bringing up to code decidedly non-sexy parts of the building like the roof, insulation for the entire building, and the windows to maximize our efficiency when it comes to heating/cooling the building. We also are being intentional about how we’re green-ifying the property and prioritizing low water, bees- and butterfly-friendly plants on the patio and a few city-owned green spaces. Long term, we’re always keen to throw solar panels on flat roofs when we’re able, but that’s not something we were able to do right away.

**What’s your hopeful target opening date/month?**

Within the first couple of weeks of August 2023.

**Are you working with craftspeople, architects, and/or creatives that you’d like to mention?**

Our general construction partners are [Interlock Construction](https://www.interlockcorp.com/), which is the same team that built out our roasting warehouse—love them! The radical in-the-round garden seating for the interior space is being fabricated by [The Public Works](https://www.thepublicworks.biz/). The initial space design and all architecture services are by [Shelterbelt Design](http://www.shelterbeltdesign.com/). All signage (menu, drive-thru, building, etc.) was created by our longtime partner Lisa Wright of [Obsesso Processo](https://www.obsessoprocesso.com/), and hand-painted signage and mural work was done by our BFF [Olive Moya](http://www.olivemoyastudio.com/).

**Thank you!**

Thank YOU!

*The 2023 Build-Outs of Coffee is presented by [DONA.](https://drinkdona.com/) The**2023 Build-Outs of Coffee is sponsored by [La Marzocco](https://international.lamarzoccohome.com/en/), [Pacific Barista Series](https://www.instagram.com/baristaseries/), [Acaia](https://acaia.co/), and [Marco Beverage Systems.](http://www.marcobeveragesystems.com/)*

*As told to Sprudge by Mickayla Wawrousek.*

**For those who aren’t familiar, will you tell us about your company?**

We are a specialty coffee roaster based in Denver, CO started in 2011, with the core belief that business should build a sense of collective culture and community by investing in people.

**Can you tell us a bit about the new space?**

This is our fifth cafe that will be opening in the Denver area, we’ve renovated the entire interior with custom built-ins to best welcome folks into the space, signage was completed by local artists and we’ll be utilizing a drive-thru for service for the first time.

**What’s your approach to coffee?**

HUCK is committed to building a sustainable coffee business that prioritizes being a reliable roasting partner to the smallholder farms and coffee co-ops we work with. More generally, we seek to be a responsible business that actively supports local and global NGO’s and community-based organizations that support those who need it the most, both within and beyond the coffee industry.

![huckleberry roasters 3](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/huckleberry-roasters-3.jpg)

**Any machines, coffees, special equipment lined up?**

We’ll be using a [La Marzocco](https://lamarzoccousa.com/?utm_source=sprudge&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=build-outs-2023) for in-shop service and an [Eversys](https://www.eversys.com/) machine for drive-thru service.

**How is your project considering sustainability?**

The building is not ours and the building owner, while entirely nice and delightful, was not super interested in contributing to buildout hopes and dreams. So, we spend a pretty penny updating and/or bringing up to code decidedly non-sexy parts of the building like the roof, insulation for the entire building, and the windows to maximize our efficiency when it comes to heating/cooling the building. We also are being intentional about how we’re green-ifying the property and prioritizing low water, bees- and butterfly-friendly plants on the patio and a few city-owned green spaces. Long term, we’re always keen to throw solar panels on flat roofs when we’re able, but that’s not something we were able to do right away.

**What’s your hopeful target opening date/month?**

Within the first couple of weeks of August 2023.

**Are you working with craftspeople, architects, and/or creatives that you’d like to mention?**

Our general construction partners are [Interlock Construction](https://www.interlockcorp.com/), which is the same team that built out our roasting warehouse—love them! The radical in-the-round garden seating for the interior space is being fabricated by [The Public Works](https://www.thepublicworks.biz/). The initial space design and all architecture services are by [Shelterbelt Design](http://www.shelterbeltdesign.com/). All signage (menu, drive-thru, building, etc.) was created by our longtime partner Lisa Wright of [Obsesso Processo](https://www.obsessoprocesso.com/), and hand-painted signage and mural work was done by our BFF [Olive Moya](http://www.olivemoyastudio.com/).

**Thank you!**

Thank YOU!

**What’s your approach to coffee?**

HUCK is committed to building a sustainable coffee business that prioritizes being a reliable roasting partner to the smallholder farms and coffee co-ops we work with. **How is your project considering sustainability?**

The building is not ours and the building owner, while entirely nice and delightful, was not super interested in contributing to buildout hopes and dreams. A beloved Denver coffee roaster has expanded outside its Northside headquarters and RiNo spinoff with a new cafe in the Dairy Block. Five-year-old Huckleberry Roasters opened its third location Wednesday at 1800 Wazee Street, and it’s one of the first new tenants on this activated downtown block that will soon see a host of openings from Milk Market to Run for the Roses and a permanent Denver Flea market. # Huckleberry Roasters Debuts its Downtown Location

The Sunnyside coffee shop has expanded to Dairy Block

by [Josie Sexton](https://www.eater.com/authors/josie-sexton)

![Huckleberry Roasters has opened a LoDo shop](https://platform.denver.eater.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/23/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/10140079/HuckleberryDairyBlock.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C4.4626593806922%2C100%2C91.074681238616&w=2400)

![Huckleberry Roasters has opened a LoDo shop](https://platform.denver.eater.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/23/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/10140079/HuckleberryDairyBlock.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C4.4626593806922%2C100%2C91.074681238616&w=2400)

Huckleberry Roasters has opened a LoDo shop

 Facebook

A beloved Denver coffee roaster has expanded outside its Northside headquarters and [RiNo spinoff](/2016/3/30/11332204/port-side-rino-huckleberry-roasters-chris-bell) with a new cafe in the Dairy Block. Five-year-old **Huckleberry Roasters** opened its third location Wednesday at 1800 Wazee Street, and it’s one of the first new tenants on this activated downtown block that will soon see a host of openings from [**Milk Market** to **Run for the Roses**](/2018/1/9/16856670/denvers-important-2018-restaurant-openings) and a permanent Denver Flea market. Existing businesses in the row of historic dairy buildings include The Maven Hotel and Kachina Southwestern Grill farther down Wazee Street.

This new [Huckleberry](/venue/18251/huckleberry-roasters) is everything a caffeine drinker could want in a modern coffee shop — pour overs, concrete floors, white countertops, and enough room for people-watching. **Toasts** too are here, with options for avocado on top or seasonal hummus and also a spicy-sweet aleppo pepper butter. **Waffles** come with Noosa yogurt, fruit, and maple, or jam and lemon-thyme ricotta. The shop’s signature music is to be expected, from an eclectic radio playlist to retail coffee beans named after songs by Bowie and Sufjan. And a new drink menu features **Huckleberry coffee milkshakes with Frozen Matter ice cream.**

Huckleberry at Dairy Block opens from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily. For fans in other parts of town, there is still the Huckleberry-owned **Port Side** with a fuller food menu (see breakfast sammies) and the original Sunnyside shop and roaster.

# Huckleberry — Bakery, Café, Catering

# huckleberry bakery & cafe

Huckleberry is THE Santa Monica Farmers’ Market bakery, café and marketplace that’s a one-stop destination for beautiful pastries, artisan coffee, gourmet provisions and a casual breakfast or lunch. We’re a living expression of the hard work and beauty that the local farmers provide us, and we’ve become a beloved, neighborhood gathering place since opening in 2009.

# THANKSGIVING CATERING

This year, we’re welcoming a new chef and a refreshed Thanksgiving menu, bringing a little something new to the table while keeping the dishes that make the holiday itself something to be grateful for.

We’re starting with **Milo + Olive breads and a whole new lineup of spreads**: from Cranberry Walnut Goat Cheese and Whipped Pumpkin Butter to Vegan Spinach & Artichoke Dip. Add a box of our house-made cornbread, pull-apart brioche rolls, or buttermilk biscuits, and you might find yourself filling up before dinner even starts.

For the main event, there’s **Mary’s Free Range Turkey with all the fixings**: slow-simmered gravy, Braised Leek & Celery Stuffing, our very special “Marry Me” Mashed Potatoes, Baked Mac & Cheese, Sweet Potato Casserole, Blistered Haricot Vert, Autumn Harvest Salad, and Cranberry Sauce.

And for your second dessert stomach: **Pumpkin Pie, Chocolate Pecan Pie, Apple Tarte Tatin, Turkey-Shaped Ginger Cookies**, and **Sweet Rose Creamery** **Ice Cream**.

Let Huckleberry handle dinner. You handle the people, the politics, and the inevitable leftovers, which, naturally, we’ve prepared for with a next-day Leftover Sandwich Kit.

***Thanksgiving orders are available for pickup on Thanksgiving Day, with orders closing Thursday, November 19 at 6pm.***

**Welcome to Gjusta Bakery** - To help us serve everyone smoothly and fairly, we use a ticketed ordering system. Please pull a ticket upon arrival and wait for a server to call your number, which will be displayed in red at the center of the bakery. Tickets are used for both dine-in and takeout, and allow you to order from our full menu.

**Express Line** - To-go pantry items, beverages, pastries, and bread are available first-come, first-served through our express line. Please queue along the ramp as directed.

# Gjusta

A pitch perfect version of a modern deli

## Photos

cuisine

Café/Bakery

Reviewed by [Krista Simmons](/contributor/krista-simmons)

**Tell us about your first impressions when you arrived.**  
To be totally candid, it's a bit of a mess. There's scarcely a moment in the day that it's not a fuss to place your order at the sprawling new American deli counter, but the wait is worth it. Once you do finally get your grub, make sure to sit outside for prime people watching.

**What was the crowd like?**  
Gjusta is peak Venice hipster. You'll find yourself elbow to elbow with actor and musician types ordering bialy breakfast sandwiches and smoked fish platters to take away.

**What should we be drinking?**  
There's no bar program, but there's great coffee, natural sodas, and, of course, smoothies.

**Main event: the food. Give us the lowdown—especially what not to miss.**  
Possibly the best modern deli in [Los Angeles](https://www.cntraveler.com/gallery/best-restaurants-in-los-angeles), if not the country. Having been several times over the course of a few years, it's hard *not* to recommend everything. The perfectly flaky pastries, the smoked fish platters, the deli sandwiches, it truly is all good.

**And how did the front-of-house folks treat you?**  
The place is a total zoo, especially at the tail end of the week and weekend, but the counter staff juggles it all deftly. Just don't expect to drop in for a quick bite, unless you're there at 7 a.m. on a Tuesday.

**Anything else to know?**  
Seating is not really conducive to large groups, so better to keep it an intimate affair.

Dahlia Bakery coffee roaster locations.content:
Alcazar continues to roast Dahlia’s custom blends at First Crack Coffee’s co-roasting facility, even as the business has grown enough to require a larger staff behind the bar and in the kitchen.

Dahlia has a team ready for the Old Brooklyn opening, including some staff members moving from the first shop, new hires and a manager who has been with the company the longest. [...] Dahlia’s growth has required Alcazar to expand beyond the largely solo operation she ran in its early days. At the Pivot Center, she was managing the business with a one-group espresso machine and one other worker, while also roasting, packing and shipping coffee. Her pregnancy pushed her to hire more staff, including a manager for the W. 114th Street shop.

“Before I got pregnant, I had a very small team,” Alcazar said. “It took a lot of trusting people.” [...] “Our team is really tight knit. Everybody really cares about Dahlia being successful, so I think we’ve built a good culture,” Alcazar said.

The opening comes as Alcazar continues to find new customers, even after Dahlia’s move to a more visible location on W. 114th Street. She said Clevelanders have fallen in love with the shop’s Mexican-inspired menu and its focus on quality, consistency and customer service.

# Dahlia Coffee Co. expands to two Cleveland cafes with Old Brooklyn shop



![Dahlia Coffee Co Cleveland](https://www.cleveland.com/resizer/v2/ZLQNHLFAXNFH7IXEIGWIMQDLN4.jpg?auth=9dbf1fe5ca1dbe067dfef188a43e7849aaad5c30df006dd742758f7d52826482&width=1280&smart=true)

Dahlia Coffee Co. opens Aug. 16 in the former Rebel Reserve space with Mexican-inspired drinks, bolillo bread sandwiches and local baked goods.Alex Darus

By 

* [Alex Darus, cleveland.com](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/adarus1/ "Alex Darus, cleveland.com")

CLEVELAND, Ohio — Dahlia Coffee Co. will open its second Cleveland location on Sunday, Aug. 16, bringing its Mexican-inspired coffee drinks, expanded food menu and a community-focused gathering space to the Old Brooklyn neighborhood.

The new cafe, at 4855 Broadview Road, takes over the space [most recently occupied by Rebel Reserve](https://www.cleveland.com/entertainment/2026/03/dahlia-coffee-opening-second-location-in-clevelands-old-brooklyn.html). Owner Natalia Alcazar said she had been searching for a second location when she saw the listing for the building, which sits on a busy, residential stretch of Broadview Road.

“I always thought this was a cool neighborhood,” Alcazar said. “Old Brooklyn is super, super tight knit.”

The Old Brooklyn shop joins [Dahlia’s original standalone cafe](https://www.cleveland.com/entertainment/2024/07/dahlia-coffee-co-is-moving-to-former-scoot-cold-brew-location-on-clevelands-west-side.html) at 2085 W. 114th St. The new location will operate the same hours — 7 a.m. to 3 p.m., Monday through Friday and 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., Saturday and Sunday.

For Alcazar, the opening represents a rapid next chapter for a business that began in 2023 with online coffee sales, wholesale accounts and a DIY cart at events. Dahlia opened its first physical cafe in [December 2023 inside the Pivot Center for Art, Dance and Expression](https://www.cleveland.com/entertainment/2024/01/dahlia-coffee-co-brings-mexican-coffee-culture-to-cleveland-with-new-cafe.html) before moving to its current flagship.

“The fact that I’m able to even step away and create another store, I really didn’t think it was going to happen this fast,” Alcazar said.

The timing was particularly intense, as Alcazar was pregnant. She signed the lease for the Broadview Road building on Feb. 1 before welcoming her baby on Feb. 12.

“I literally was eight and a half months pregnant when I signed the lease,” she recalled with a laugh.

Renovations began in April. Though the former coffee-shop space had a workable foundation, Alcazar said the project brought unexpected complications, including a lack of an occupancy permit and extensive electrical work that needed to be redone. The renovation also included new countertops, painted floors, storage walls and a new look for the cafe.

“Things kind of went a little slower because of getting permits approved,” Alcazar said.

![Dahlia Coffee Co Cleveland](https://www.cleveland.com/resizer/v2/GQ6J4OK6TNEIBHIDG64ORIRHGM.jpeg?auth=2d59399fac63b6f92c1d1ebc72897fbe6d7b0e0b662ce51d68316e8873ffc7d1&width=1280&smart=true)

Expanded seating at Dahlia's second cafe in Old Brooklyn.Alex Darus

The opening had originally been planned for June. Now, the completed space is designed as a sister location to Dahlia’s W. 114th Street shop, with the same warm color palette, neon signs, Mexican-inspired art and drink menu. The new space does feel evolved, with substantially more seating and room to develop the food program Alcazar had envisioned from the start.

“I want to try to do what I originally wanted to do with Dahlia at this shop,” she said. “I didn’t have the capacity to do everything I wanted to do.”

The Old Brooklyn menu will include breakfast burritos and breakfast sandwiches, followed by tortas for lunch. The sandwiches and tortas will use Mexican bolillo bread from Flying Pig Tacos in CentroVilla25. Dahlia will continue selling Jossi’s Bakery guava rolls at both locations, while adding baked goods and other menu items from local collaborators at the new shop.

That includes a cafe de olla cookie from Miriyumyums Baking Co., inspired by Dahlia’s drink of the same name, along with treats such as Tajin key lime pie. Another neighborhood local [Old Brooklyn Bagels](https://www.cleveland.com/entertainment/2024/07/old-brooklyn-bagels-brings-fresh-bagels-to-greater-cleveland-neighborhood-with-at-home-bakery.html) will offer small-batch bagels on the weekends at Dahlia .

The new food offerings and extra space create an opportunity for Alcazar to work with more small businesses, especially people who already live in Old Brooklyn. She hopes Dahlia can become a neighborhood hub that can also help other small businesses grow.

“I would really love to create a commercial kitchen in their neighborhood,” Alcazar said.

The new space also gives Dahlia room for programming beyond daily coffee service. Large garage doors at the front can open during warmer months, allowing for patio seating and parking lot events. She also hopes to improve the outdoor area behind the building for additional seating.

Dahlia’s growth has required Alcazar to expand beyond the largely solo operation she ran in its early days. At the Pivot Center, she was managing the business with a one-group espresso machine and one other worker, while also roasting, packing and shipping coffee. Her pregnancy pushed her to hire more staff, including a manager for the W. 114th Street shop.

“Before I got pregnant, I had a very small team,” Alcazar said. “It took a lot of trusting people.”

That shift was crucial in helping her business grow.

![Dahlia Coffee Co Cleveland](https://www.cleveland.com/resizer/v2/PESGQHCTG5EKPBSVDSR63XIRXA.jpeg?auth=dfa42ac14fd1551ddff1063c619898f64dc766f0d0f0586e67b0757109c51c05&width=1280&smart=true)

The cafe opens Sunday at 4855 Broadview Road.Alex Darus

“Once I hired a full-time manager and then I started hiring more employees, my businesses started growing a lot more,” Alcazar said. “Soon it was like, our sales went up three times as much.”

Alcazar continues to roast Dahlia’s custom blends at First Crack Coffee’s co-roasting facility, even as the business has grown enough to require a larger staff behind the bar and in the kitchen.

Dahlia has a team ready for the Old Brooklyn opening, including some staff members moving from the first shop, new hires and a manager who has been with the company the longest.

“Our team is really tight knit. Everybody really cares about Dahlia being successful, so I think we’ve built a good culture,” Alcazar said.

The opening comes as Alcazar continues to find new customers, even after Dahlia’s move to a more visible location on W. 114th Street. She said Clevelanders have fallen in love with the shop’s Mexican-inspired menu and its focus on quality, consistency and customer service.

“Customers really like that it’s so different than anything else they can get here in Cleveland,” Alcazar said.

And before the doors have opened in Old Brooklyn, Alcazar said neighbors have already made the business feel welcome.

“Everyone in this neighborhood has been really receptive of us coming in,” she said. “We have people that stop by like, every day” asking when the cafe will open.

“Cleveland has been really receptive to us, and that’s felt really good,” Alcazar said.

[![Alex Darus headshot](https://www.cleveland.com/resizer/v2/https%3A%2F%2Fauthor-service-images-prod-us-east-1.publishing.aws.arc.pub%2Fadvancelocal%2F684fef2e-e15a-4a11-abdf-0af924f04fd9.png?auth=3c6d4bc8cc4fd30a7e476c7a27c29a17a9b7b81b3613a6bc6f3b205794a6241d&width=180&smart=true&quality=90)](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/adarus1/)[Alex Darus](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/adarus1/)

## Fossette's 7. per person

Fossette = dimples in Italian. Fossette is a delicious Italian bread. A “dimpled” dough with a crispy crust and a soft and airy interior. Enjoy on its own or with savory toppings and sides. current flavors are: roasted garlic, asiago & rosemary. roasted cinnamon apple & honey. caramelized onion & nigella seed

## Oh Mochi donut's

A delicious solution for the gluten-free donut lover! These mochi donuts are silky, luscious, and effortlessly addictive! The yuzu glaze, a crowd favorite, is one of the most bright and enchanting flavors, combined with our bouncy textured dough, these treats truly sparkle in your mouth. These naturally gluten-free rice-based donuts will have both traditional (think chocolate and sprinkles)and untraditional glazes and toppings like our own togarashi for those who crave a sweet-savory combination.

# 2026 Best Coffee Shops in Portland Oregon for an Amazing First Visit

A Pacific Northwest itinerary isn’t complete without coffee. Luckily, the best coffee shops in Portland Oregon are some of the best in the PNW!

Between the following cafes, you’ll discover **instagrammable cafes**, **ube treats**, and incredible **speciality coffee roasters.**

I hope you have a great time in Portland. **But first, coffee.**

*Let’s Explore: Best Coffee Shops in Portland Oregon*

## 6 Best Coffee Shops in Portland Oregon

### Kalesa Coffee

As luck would have it, my favorite cup of joe during my trip to Portland was my last! (Don’t be like me and wait to visit **[Kalesa](https://www.instagram.com/kalesacoffee/?hl=en)** until the end of your trip!)

What makes this small but mighty coffee shop special is the heart it pours into its **Filipino-inspired drinks**.

My recommendation is to try the **Coconut Cold Brew with ube whipped cream.** It’s perfectly sweet, refreshing for summer days, and is totally instagrammable!

Ube whip gets its vibrant color from purple yams, and is a must-try. Try adding it to your go-to drink!

As someone with Filipino heritage, I love their [**mission**](https://www.kalesacoffee.com/about). And, the sense of community at Kalesa is so strong!

You’ll find them Tuesday-Saturdays in the corner of the Gotham Building, located at 722 N Page Street, Portland, Oregon 97227.

### Sisters Coffee Company

Originally brewed from a cabin in Central Oregon, [**Sisters Coffee Company**](https://www.instagram.com/sisterscoffee/?hl=en) now happily serves up delicious drinks, pastries, and brunch foods at 3 cafes. In Portland, their cafe is located in the **Pearl District.**

Hands down, this is one of the most walkable areas of the Rose City. The architecture is beautiful, the people are friendly, and there’s tons of great shops and places to eat.

Or, if you’re looking for a cafe to settle in for awhile, then you’ll love the abundant indoor (two stories) and outdoor seating. And, the way natural light pours into the space is lovely!

My recommendation is to take your pick of the barista specials, which vary by location. Plus, come hungry to make this a two-in-one stop with a [**generous food menu**](https://sisterscoffee.com/pages/pearl-cafe-portland) including sandwiches and toasts. Be sure to get your food order in before 2pm!

Sisters Coffee Company is open daily at 1235 Northwest Marshall St, Portland, Oregon.

{RELATED POST: **[Wonderful Things to do in Sisters, Oregon](https://yournorthwestiebestie.com/things-to-do-in-sisters-oregon/)**}

### Less and More Coffee

Looking for a quick coffee run downtown? Try [**Less and More Coffee**](https://www.instagram.com/lessandmorecoffee/?hl=en), housed in a vintage bus stop. While the kiosk is sure to catch your eye, it’s the aesthetically-pleasing drinks that will prove why it’s one of the can’t-miss coffee shops in Portland Oregon!

Known for their signature drinks with **homemade cream**, enjoy amazing drinks like the cloud cream mocha, black sesame creme latte, or hojicha latte (espresso + green tea from Japan).

Traveling with someone who isn’t a coffee drinker? Both my partner and best friend fall into this category, and they’ve both loved Less & More’s **ube latte**. It’s a hot, comforting blend of purple sweet potato and steamed milk. Plus, it looks so fun!

During your visit, [**tag me on Instagram**](https://www.instagram.com/yournorthwestiebestie/) so I can see your cute drinks!

You can even**[place your order online](https://lessandmorecoffee.square.site/#8).**

Head to 1003 SW 5th Ave, Portland, Oregon 97204 for the kiosk location. Or, consider their second location near Pioneer Courthouse Square at 811 SW 6th Ave, Portland, OR 97204 (not housed in a bus stop).

### Stumptown Coffee Roasters

Based in Portland, Stumptown Coffee Roasters is a **B-Corp** roaster that prioritizes sustainability.

In total, there’s 6 Stumptown locations in the city! Personally, my favorite is SW Washington. There’s a beautiful mural next door, and Powell’s Books (the **largest independent bookstore** in the world) is only a couple blocks away!

During summer, my favorite summer seasonal drink is the **rose gold latte**. Another fun one is the spicy strawberry mocha.

You can [**place an order online**](https://stumptowncoffee.craverapp.com/).

1140 SW Washington St, Portland, OR 97205

*Bestie Tip:* Stumptown Coffee Roasters has a **location within PDX**, the Portland airport. So you can grab it as soon as you land or take it with on your flight home!

{RELATED POST: [**Visitor’s Guide to the Best Coffee in Bend, Oregon**](https://yournorthwestiebestie.com/bend-oregon-coffee-shops/)}

### Ken’s Artisan Bakery

Out of all the best coffee shops in Portland Oregon, [**Ken’s Artisan Bakery**](https://kensartisan.com/bakery) is the only one we visited twice during out visit! Why? 3 words: **The Oregon Croissant.**

It’s a dreamy combination of blueberries, blackberries, and hazelnut cream. Be sure to **order it warmed** up and for-here, I promise it’s worth the wait!

Coffee is crafted using beans from **[Relevant Coffee](https://relevantcoffee.com/),** based out of Vancouver, Washington.

It’s wise to schedule a little extra time in for Ken’s Artisan Bakery, as this is a very locally loved spot. If you’re really dedicated, like me and my bestie, you may even wait in the line with your suitcases before heading to the airport haha!

You’ll find them daily at 338 NW 21st Avenue, Portland, OR.

### Coava Coffee Roasters

If you find yourself in the Central Eastside area of Portland, it’s worth swinging by [**Coava Coffee**](https://coavacoffee.com/)‘s roasting location. Here, they roast **single origin speciality coffee.**

Housed in a converted warehouse, their space is open, airy, and welcoming. Whether you’re catching up with a friend, replying to emails, or journaling, there’s **plenty of indoor space.**

Note that Coava Coffee doesn’t stock many syrups or sauces, so this is the place to enjoy **simpler drinks** and appreciate the **quality of the cup!**

Interested in stocking up? This is a great place to get **64 oz** matcha, cold brew, iced chai, or iced latte to take home with you.

1300 SE Grand Ave a, Portland, OR 97214

**This post was all about the best coffee shops in Portland Oregon.**

# Review: Ken’s Artisan Bakery

by [PDX Food Dude](https://portlandfoodanddrink.com/author/food-dude/)

[![Ken's Artisan Bakery Portland - Interior](https://portlandfoodanddrink.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/06/kens-artisan-bakery-interio.jpg "Ken's Artisan Bakery Portland - Interior")](https://portlandfoodanddrink.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/06/kens-artisan-bakery-interio.jpg)

Ken’s Artisan Bakery  
©Ken’s Artisan Bakery

*Updated 6/118. Text, details, photos.*

When I think of bakeries, my mind rushes back to Manhattan Beach in the ’60s. Once a week, my dad would stop on the way home from work and pick up all kinds of rolls for breakfast the next morning. It’s called Becker’s, and according to my mom, it is still thriving after all these years. It’s miles from where we lived but was the best around, and Dad always picked up a sampler of the simpler fare that was available then. No croissants, no tarts; instead, things like hot-cross buns, (do they still make those?), twists, and jelly rolls. He’d bring them home in a big pink box tied with white string, and my sisters and I would rush him to see what delights lay inside. Nowadays you only see this type of thing in grocery stores, and when you try them they usually taste like cardboard. Back then, though, they were the height of culinary baking, and nothing was better than one of those rolls, warmed slightly with a bit of butter, before school.  
 These days bakeries are a far different place. Ken’s is a pretty good example of state-of-the-art. When you walk in the front door, a dizzying array of colors and shapes greets you from the glass case. Fluorescent macaroons, multicolored tarts, and perfectly browned croissants fight for your attention. On a nice day, large open windows let in light and a warm breeze. The walls are painted in different blues and yellows, making it feel more spacious than it really is. This actually feels like a real French bakery, much more so than the Disneyland version at St. Honoré a few blocks away. A long community table with a huge vase of flowers crosses the space, with about ten small tables dotted about the room. Outside tables make a pleasant place to sip coffee or enjoy a sandwich on a nice day. This is a comfortable space to while away time.

[![Ken's Bakery Portland](https://portlandfoodanddrink.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/03/kens-bakery.jpg "ken's-bakery")](https://portlandfoodanddrink.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/03/kens-bakery.jpg)

Ken’s Bakery

To me, the best indication of the excellence of any bakery is the bread, and I haven’t had any better in Portland. Ken Forkish uses the best organic flours, French sea salt, and even more important, hours and hours of patience. The dough is fermented slowly, retarded, taking the time needed to develop the best flavor, a perfect complexity of tastes that makes it stand out from everywhere else. The naturally leavened (sourdough), bread is terrific, full of rich nutty taste that makes you dig into the depths of your brain, separating out all the flavors. The perfect crust shatters under your teeth, giving in to a rush of tangy piquancy, a perfect synergy of ingredients. The crust has greater scorch than most, an almost caramel brown. This is what bread should taste like. Available loaves are pain rustique ($2.95), a walnut baguette studded with fat walnuts ($4.95), huge crown loaves ($8.00), country boule ($3.95), country brown with a lovely nutty finish ($3.95), country demi-baguette ($2.95), Parisian baguette ($2.50), and others depending on the day.

A good rotation of sandwiches is also available, and they are some of the best in town. Over the past few weeks, I’ve been working my way through them. The pulled pork with a somewhat sweet barbecue sauce is loaded with lots of tender, moist meat on a perfect slice of bread. An accompanying slaw is a low acid, but after a few bites, you realize it really complements the sandwich with lots of raisins and a little bit of fresh thyme. The Croque monsieur is the best in Portland. Not that flat thing that so many places serve, but little waves of ham covered with Gruyère, on top of béchamel with more of the ubiquitous thyme on a thin slice of fresh country bread – transcendent. I also fell for the braised roasted beef with caramelized onions. A horseradish sauce gives a nice counterpoint to the beef without masking its nice meaty flavor. If you are in the mood for a summer classic, the roasted eggplant and mozzarella with fresh basil, tomato, and balsamic reduction are the perfect accompaniment to a sunny afternoon. All sandwiches are $6.45. They come with a bit of lightly dressed greens or a few blueberries that are still little flavor bombs, even in early September.

The pastries are more of a mixed bag. I am told to be here early in the morning when they first come out of the oven, or Saturday when they come in waves all day long. The butter croissants ($1.95) are marvelously layered, shattering into buttery flakes when you bite into them, never being greasy. Pick one with Valrhona French chocolate ($2.50), and it is like a dessert, pairing perfectly with a cup of coffee as you watch the parade of Portland chic pass by. Then suddenly you’ll realize, at that moment, you are one of them in the trendy little bakery, but it doesn’t really matter. Pretend.

[![Ken's Artisan Bakery Portland](https://portlandfoodanddrink.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/06/kens-bakery-eclairs.jpg "Ken's Artisan Bakery - eclairs")](https://portlandfoodanddrink.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/06/kens-bakery-eclairs.jpg)

Eclairs

A summer pudding ($3.75) is soaked in fruit syrup without being too sweet with a crème anglaise to counter the tartness. It is studded with blackberries, raspberries, and blueberries – most of the seeds are out, but a few have been left leaving a little crunch. I liked it, but it didn’t do anything for other people that tried it with me, and I have to say I probably wouldn’t order it again. A seasonal fruit amandine was okay with a good almond paste flavor on a light crust, but still, I’ve had better, especially for $3.50. St. Honoré Bakery is fairly well known for its almond croissants, and I went back to compare the two against each other. The Honoré is denser and less flaky with a sweeter, stronger almond flavor. I actually prefer the lighter Ken’s version, but the almond paste in both could be better. Finally, we come to the Canalet, a traditional treat from the Bordeaux region of France. Traditionally made with milk, eggs, sugar, flour, vanilla bean, and rum, they taste like a cross between a cake and a cookie and are quite addictive. They look simple but are extremely complicated to make. I like Ken’s for his dark, caramelized crust and creamy center.

My memory has failed me, but there was a bun filled with chocolate and fruit. I can’t remember what it was called. Maybe it is because I just didn’t think it worked. (I’ll update this next time I’m there.) While the bun itself had a nice texture, the filling was a bit harsh for me. I’d pass on it again. Same with the macaroons; an entire side of the case full of brightly colored cookies, but they were just too cloyingly sweet for me. Though mine were fresh, I am told they can taste a bit stale at times.

Coffee is Mr. Espresso – organic, free trade, sustainable. I didn’t care for it too much, but I’m used to Stumptown.

The pastries are fine, but the bread is the number one reason this bakery should be a destination.

* **Phone**: 503.248.2202
* **Address**: 326 NW 21st Avenue, Portland, 97209.  [Google Map](http://maps.google.com/maps?q=Ken%27s+Artisan+Bakery,+Northwest+21st+Avenue,+Portland,+OR&hl=en&sll=45.525382,-122.694068&sspn=0.012883,0.022745&oq=ken%27s&hq=Ken%27s+Artisan+Bakery,&hnear=1207+NW+21st+Ave,+Portland,+Oregon+97209&t=m&z=15)
* **Hours**: Mon-Sat: 7am-6pm, Monday Night Pizza: 5:30pm 9:30pm. Sun: 8am – 5pm

## Reader Interactions

### Comments

1. Marshall Manning says

   I haven’t had the full menu, but I’ve really liked the couple of sandwiches I’ve had at Ken’s. While I love the flavor of his breads, I wish the crusts weren’t so dark. He seems to be lightening up the crusts a bit from his earlier efforts, though, which were often scorched.
2. Anonymous says

   Of all the pastries at Ken’s, I prefer the Ham, Thyme, and Gruyere croissants for breakfast. They taste like they were made with a full stick of butter, and I feel like I should go straight to the gym after eating one, but they are incredibly tasty.

   I really dislike the coffee, though. Stumptown is just so much better than other choices, I don’t see the reason to use something else when you’re charging so much for a cup.
3. shuna fish lydon says

   the descriptions of the sandwiches make me hungry all over again, even though I have just come from having a big meal!

   I loved sitting there on that cool morning with the wall-windows opened up and enjoying my still- hot croissant.

   The cannele’s appareil is actually closer to a crepe than anything else. And that dark dark exterior is very purposeful, both for flavour and as a way to keep the interior custardy. The best ones are made with copper molds lined with beeswax. Nothing like the scent of them baking. goodness.
4. PDXFoodDude says

   St. Honore actually uses the copper molds lined with beeswax. I think Ken does too, the texture feels like it.
5. tha-krza says

   Does St. Honore (or any other patisserie in PDX, for that matter) make a fabolous creation called La Peche? The French bakery in Memphis made them when I was growing up and they were incredible. Basically they were the same pastery as an eclair filled with cream but in the shape of a peach. The were colored as if they were a natural peach and coated in sugar. I have been searching for them for eons.
6. [Susan](http://susurradeluz.blogspot.com) says

   hi!  
    Apparently the Meyers bakery up on the hill in PV still makes hot cross buns, because during Easter season my Dad stops by there and gets them once a week.

   But I’d much rather have a croissant.
7. admin says

   Actually I HATED hot cross buns, but they bring back fond memories of the time. Meyers bakery – the name rings a bell.
8. bluto says

   No review of Ken’s would be complete without an homage to pizza night which takes place on Mondays. The pizza is by far the best I have had in PDX and definitely a cut above the highly touted pies at Apizza Scholls. The crust is paper thin and perfectly crisp, while the tomato sauce has a residual sweetness which is very pleasant. Pies are dinner plate size which afforded two of us to try two different pies. The sausage with carmelized onions was wonderful with a generous portion of sausagew and perfectly cooked onions. The proschutto with basil was not quite as flavorful but generally very good. There is a good selection of beers and wines to accompany the food, and while it is very crowded at 5PM when pizza is served, it tapers off about 7:30.
9. Food Dude says

   Bluto: The only reason I didn’t mention it, is that I never had a chance to get there on monday night, so couldn’t comment. I have heard other comments similar t yours and will definetly try it when I update the review.
10. Cacahuete says

    Ken also has done a special cassoulet night (I think it was to celebrate their write-up in *Bon Appetit)* , though I’m not sure if he’s done it more than once. It was delicious—I’m not sure it’s legal to say, but I found it even more delicious than the cassoulet I’ve had in France. If anyone ever hears of his doing it again, please post! I dream about it sometimes.
11. Joyce Forbes says

    How long will almond paste that was purchased from a grocery store last?
12. Becca says

    Cacahuete-

    Ken had the cassoulet party to commemorate the closing of the dinner cafe service he had going for about eight months a few years ago; it’s been hard to forget receiving that pink slip. He didn’t bother doing much marketing of the dinner service as far as I know, so, even though we produced some of the most delicious and reasonably-priced cafe fare in the area at the time, very few people got to enjoy it and it was thus an unsustainable endeavor.

    For the record, the person who actually made the cassoulet was Rob, who was not only the person who made all the croissant and puff pastry doughs at the time but also oversaw the dinner cafe. He went on from Ken’s to be the sous chef under Rollie Wesen at Rivers, but I don’t know if he’s still there.
13. jane says

    I looooved Ken’s bread! I haven’t found any better in town. Though, their pastries are not their best. Even though, I understand the “disneyland” image for Saint Honore, I have to say that their chausson aux pommes and chouquettes are the only real deal in town and you cannot find it anywhere else.

    But as for the bread, Ken’s is the best.
14. Comfort Foodie says

    Ken’s good, Little T American Baker better!

  The bakery is nice, a little seating, light space and they have a great looking sandwich menu too. This is added to my "must stop" places when I'm

   7/13/2017

  My one year living in Portland, OR was a watershed in my understanding of good coffee, baked goods, and pizza, and Ken's Artisan Bakery being located one block from my apartment served to provide the trifecta in educating me on all the above.  
    
  Before Portland was known as a foodie destination for the masses, Ken's Artisan Bakery was one of the earliest institutions that laid the foundation for others to follow in its footsteps.  Opened in 2001, Ken's Artisan Bakery is a labor of love by Ken Forkish, a former Silicon Valley IT specialist who was inspired by prior trips to Europe to forge a new career path as an artisan baker (or in tech speak, this would be like a small bread-based startup).  Armed without any former training but possessing a keen sense of intense observation and meticulous study along with an obsessive attention to detail including plotting out tables to adjust bake settings and yeast proofing based on the surrounding temperature and humidity, the output is a continuous pursuit of baking perfection using the finest ingredients baked from scratch everyday.    
    
  Coffee: Serving Stumptown coffee, which has now gained national recognition, you'll be hard pressed to find a barista in this town that does not know how to craft an excellent latte.  
    
  Pastries:  If you've had the privilege to check out Tartine in San Francisco, the croissants and morning buns are made very much in the same style and form, although probably a little less decadent.  Their signature item is the Oregon Croissant made w/ mixed local berries, hazelnut cream, and playfully presented with fresh berries and sugar pellets lined within its open-faced lattice.  Other standout items include the Morning Bun w/ orange zest, the pain au chocolat, and the ham/gruyere/thyme savory croissant.  The almond croissant and cannelles are not quite as good.  There are also several seasonal fruit tarts and finer pastries on rotation.  
    
  Bread:  Great alone or paired w/ cheese and charcuterie, the walnut bread and country blonde are probably my favorites.    
    
  Ambience:  a neighborhood bakery in the truest sense, laid back unpretentious vibe with an open facade and regulars known on a first name basis, don't be surprised if you see a PhD with multiple tattoos and piercings riffing on astrophysics or a member from a local band coming in for their daily cup of joe.    
    
  Protip:  It's been awhile since I've been back, but Monday night at 530pm is Pizza Night, where they bake Neopolitan style pizzas out of their ovens, and a complimentary loaf of bread is thrown in for good measure.  Funfact: The success of this little side event led to the opening of Ken's Artisan Pizza in 2006, which is another beloved institution I will save for another review.

  Consistently 4 stars for this place.  
  I'm not a huge fan of American coffee.  Ken's main focus isn't on coffee, it's on food and one can tell.   
  The coffee isn't good.   They do serve Smith Tea, so that's a lot better.   
    
   Now let's talk food.   
  Today I went for lunch and ordered the Portobello Croque Monsieur on country blonde.   
  I'm more than familiar with the classic  Croque Monsieur and portobello mushroom seemed like a good idea.   
    
  It was excellent.   Something I can highly recommend.   I didn't care for the pickles; a harsh  
  combination with the rustic, yet subtle, portobellos mushroom flavor.   I didn't taste the thyme but definitely a hint of blue cheese.     
    
  Excellent choice for lunch.    Maybe tomorrow I do try the Croque Monsieur.   With a cuppa tea because the coffee isn't good.

  Ken Forkish, the owner of Ken's Artisan Bakery, received James Beard 2013 Outstanding Pastry Chef award nomination for his cookbook "Flour Water Salt Yeast" ([jamesbeard.org/blog/q-jb…](/redir?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.jamesbeard.org%2Fblog%2Fq-jbf-award-nominee-ken-forkish&s=79317a7612b60417f5fe406e195975ca913ac8c1161743b9a0a7745f855baccf)). In addition to   
  Ken's Artisan Bakery (opened since 2001), Ken also owns Ken's Artisan Pizza located 3 miles away from the bakery.  
    
  Parking: Street parking only ($1.60 per hour) and it was somewhat difficult to find an available parking space in this part of the neighborhood called the Alphabet District. Later I learned on their website that you can park at Bastas for free until 5 PM.  
    
  There's a good selection of French pastries to choose from (two of owner's favorite items were Country Blonde bread and Oregon Croissant), but they will run out certain pastries if you do come here a bit late (almond croissants were sold out at 1 PM). This place was completely packed and I couldn't grab a table, so I got my pastry to-go  
    
  \*\*\*  
    
  Ham, Thyme, and Gruyere Croissant ($4.75): Croissant was a bit cold, but it tasted very delicious. Just the right amount of ham, cheese, and dough.  
    
  \*\*\*  
    
  If I actually live around this area, then I would visit this place multiple times and try their other breads.  
    
  P.S. - They serves Stumptown Coffee.

  Went for Pizza night on Monday night and got free loaves of bread. I adore this bread. I have had a number of their loaves and all are incredible. Some of the best bread I have ever had. Their country brown (miche) is absolutely perfect. Wonderful crust, nice and chewy, great color. Inside is moist and flavorful with a nice open crumb. Wow! Great stuff. If you like more whitish loaves, the country blonde is an excellent loaf - great flavor and crust, light and airy. And the smell, Ummmm.... The walnut is nice too. Ah, hell, they are all great. You cannot go wrong here.  
    
  But we came for the pizza too. And it is awesome. Wonderful crust, thin and crispy. The sauce has a wonderful simple tomato taste - this is not an over seasoned sauce at all. Simple and tasty. Not much cheese (which is a plus, in my book). I had the arrabbiata. Nicely spiced! Definitely add the arugula to the pizza! It is a great addition. They add salt to it, so some might find that too much (I thought it great, but one member of our party wanted more cheese and less salt).  
    
  I really want one of these near me...
