   1/10/2012

  I love bread, and while I haven't tried all the bakeries in Portland, of the many I've tried, I do believe Ken's is the best in the bread department.  The bakery also does fabulous pastries, cookies, and great lunch options in the form of sandwiches, salads and soups.  I also love the bakery itself with its big windows and open kitchen.  It's so nice and inviting and makes me want to sit with a book and a coffee and just spend a few hours relaxing.    
    
  Back to the bread...The baguettes are delicious, crisp on the outside and chewy in the middle and their Walnut Loaf is dense and nutty, perfect toasted with some butter or smothered in a soft cheese.  My favorite bread from here though is the Country Blonde.  The Country Blonde is the perfect, everyday bread.  My Dad was so impressed with it when he visited Portland that now every time I go back to the bay I get in trouble if I haven't brought at least two loaves down with me.  The Blonde and it's sister bread, the Country Brown are great as an accompaniment to any meal with their crusty exterior and lighter airy interior.    
    
  I've also been here for lunch a few times and the sandwiches are good, the soups are great and the pastries are always tasty.  I love the butter croissants which are large and flakey and the Cannelle cakes that are crisp and caramelized on the outside and moist and custardy on the inside.  The Tuna Sandwich, served on a croissant was great and the Curried Cauliflower soup I had here warmed me up on a cold winter afternoon.    
    
  Ken's Bakery is great!  As an added bonus they also do pizza on Monday nights that is also quite good.

Ken’s Artisan Bakery is now well known for its breads, pastries and sandwiches, delivering bread to to many of Portland’s finest restaurants,a nd offering products at the bakery reminiscient of the classic and timeless boulangeries of Paris.

2011 marked the beginning of Bakery Lorraine's operations. They were successful in rapidly amassing a devoted customer base. Arrived as the farmer's market was setting up, so we tucked into Bakery Lorraine at the Pearl for coffee & pastries while we waited. Coffee was made perfectly and I am picky about that! However, the pastries were the star of the show!! We each tried something different and they were all amazing. Crispy and sweet and buttery and flavorful. We enjoyed our treats and felt very comfortable visiting on the patio watching the market vendors get ready. Staff members came by to check on us and were kind and friendly. Afterward we also enjoyed the farmers market which has a wide variety of produce, baked items, organic meats, cheeses, plants, home-made items, and fascinating international foods. Highly recommend this Bakery and the Pearl area.

# Bakery Lorraine

## About the Business

Bakery Lorraine is a well-known bakery and café in Boerne offering French-inspired pastries, Parisian macarons, breakfast dishes, artisan sandwiches, soups, salads, and a selection of wine and beer. Nationally recognized for its quality and craftsmanship, the bakery has earned praise from outlets including Food and Wine, Condé Nast Traveler, and Southern Living.  
Guests can stop in for coffee and pastries, enjoy a leisurely breakfast or lunch, or pick up beautifully made treats in a stylish, welcoming setting.

## PAPA D’AMOUR

**NOW OPEN!** A new concept by Chef Dominique Ansel exploring his love of Asian bread culture. Dedicated to his two young children, who are Taiwanese and French, “Papa d’Amour” means “Papa, my love” in French. “It’s what my kids call me,” says the chef. “Especially when they want something.”

We love blending cultures, techniques, and memories in the world of pastry. And we all know that when Papa is in the kitchen, there are no rules.

## Dominique Ansel Las Vegas – Caesars Palace

Chef Ansel’s iconic pastries are now available at the heart of the Strip at Caesars Palace Las Vegas for the very first time, including the Cronut®, Cookie Shot (including a 24/7 Cookie Shot Vending Machine!), DKA, and Frozen S’mores, along with a brand new collection of pastries made just for Las Vegas too.

## Dominique Ansel Marché – Paris Las Vegas

Our newest sister shop, Dominique Ansel Marché, is located at the heart of the Las Vegas Strip at the Paris Las Vegas.  Inspired by the sidewalk markets in France, enjoy fresh-baked croissants, juicy rotisserie chicken, made-to-order crêpes, savory sandwiches and salads, and more. Don’t miss our iconic signature pastries too, from the Cronut® to the DKA, Cookie Shot, and more.  For more details, check out: <https://www.caesars.com/paris-las-vegas/restaurants/dominique-ansel-marche>

***Join us here in Soho!***Dominique opened his celebrated Dominique Ansel Bakery in New York’s Soho neighborhood in November 2011. ### Papa d’Amour – Greenwich Village, NYC

**NOW OPEN!** A new concept by Chef Dominique Ansel exploring his love of Asian bread culture. Dedicated to his two young children, who are Taiwanese and French, “Papa d’Amour” means “Papa, my love” in French. “It’s what my kids call me,” says the chef. “Especially when they want something.”

We love blending cultures, techniques, and memories in the world of pastry. And we all know that when Papa is in the kitchen, there are no rules.

64 University Place (btw 10th & 11th Streets)  
 New York, NY 10003  
 [papadamourny.com](http://www.papadamourny.com)

Open daily 8AM-7PM

![soho](https://www.dominiqueansel.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/soho.jpg)

### Soho, New York, NY

#### Dominique Ansel Bakery

Dominique opened his celebrated Dominique Ansel Bakery in New York’s Soho neighborhood in November 2011. Centered upon the idea of creativity, the Bakery is the birthplace of many of Dominique’s signature desserts, including the DKA (Dominique’s Kouign Amann), Cookie Shot, Frozen S’mores, Blossoming Hot Chocolate, and the Cronut®.

***OPEN 8AM-7PM DAILY***

[Visit](http://dominiqueanselny.com/)

![DAW group FINAL LO RES](https://www.dominiqueansel.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/DAW-group-FINAL-LO-RES.jpg)

### Flatiron, New York, NY

#### Dominique Ansel Workshop

Our newest shop is a celebration of croissants,  located right inside of our pastry production kitchens here in Flatiron, NYC, just a block up from Madison Square Park. Stop in for a taste of all different types of croissants and breakfast viennoiserie, stroll to the park, and enjoy!

***NOW OPEN!  
 7AM-4PM  MON-FRI  
 8AM-5PM SAT-SUN***

[Visit](http://dominiqueanselworkshop.com/)

![Dominique Ansel Marche](https://www.dominiqueansel.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/EXTERIOR_STRAIGHT_ON_0116_vw1d_3CR-scaled.jpg)

### Dominique Ansel Marché – Paris Las Vegas NOW OPEN!

Our newest sister shop, Dominique Ansel Marché, is located at the heart of the Las Vegas Strip at the Paris Las Vegas.  Inspired by the sidewalk markets in France, enjoy fresh-baked croissants, juicy rotisserie chicken, made-to-order crêpes, savory sandwiches and salads, and more. Don’t miss our iconic signature pastries too, from the Cronut® to the DKA, Cookie Shot, and more.  For more details, check out: https://www.caesars.com/paris-las-vegas/restaurants/dominique-ansel-marche

***NOW OPEN!  
 MON-SUN 7AM-11PM***

**PARIS LAS VEGAS** 3655 Las Vegas Blvd South  
 Las Vegas, NV 89109

### Caesars Palace Las Vegas

Hey, Las Vegas! Dominique Ansel Las Vegas at Caesars Palace is now open daily in the heart of The Strip. Chef Dominique Ansel’s iconic pastries are making their Las Vegas debut, from the Cronut to the DKA and Cookie Shot and more, plus freshly-baked croissants and a collection of pastries made exclusively for the city. The original and most famous Dominique Ansel Bakery sits right in the heart of SoHo, at 189 Spring Street, New York, NY 10012. It’s an easy spot to get to; the C and E subway trains stop at Spring Street, and the N, R, and W trains are just a few blocks away at Prince Street. [...] Currently, there are five Dominique Ansel Bakery locations. The original, which gained worldwide attention for the Cronut, is still right here in SoHo, New York. Beyond that, you'll find Dominique Ansel Workshop in Flatiron, which focuses on croissants and gives you a peek into the production kitchens. [...] This neighborhood location puts you among distinctive 19th-century cast-iron buildings and plenty of shops. Inside the bakery, the space itself is often lively, but if you look carefully, you might find one of their "secret" outdoor patio areas for a quieter moment with your pastry and coffee.

## How many Dominique Ansel Bakery locations are there?

> **TLDR**: Dominique Ansel Bakery offers a unique New York City pastry experience, most famous for the Cronut. Expect inventive flavors, potential crowds, and a price tag that reflects the craft, but it's often worth a visit for something different.

I'll admit it: I visited [Dominique Ansel Bakery](https://www.dominiqueanselny.com/) because of the Cronut hype. Everyone was talking about this croissant-donut hybrid that people were lining up for at dawn, and I had to see what the fuss was about.

Several visits later, I've learned that while the Cronut is genuinely impressive, it's actually the DKA and Cookie Shot that keep me coming back to this unassuming corner of SoHo.

## What is the story behind Dominique Ansel Bakery?

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65329423a966d94a21420905/692702e79b47d946cf44bae8_attractions%252FChIJP0KOWoxZwokRmvPiQAIaH1A%252F1764163891887_dominique-ansel-bakery.webp)

Image by Photographing Travis [**(by)**](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/)

Imagine a quiet street in SoHo back in 2011. That's where French pastry chef Dominique Ansel, fresh from top kitchens in Paris and New York, opened his first bakery. He arrived in the city with a vision and not much else. Early on, his DKA (Dominique's Kouign Amann) – a caramelized croissant with tender, flaky layers – was already a local favorite.

Then came May 2013, and everything changed. Ansel spent two months perfecting a new idea, a hybrid between a croissant and a doughnut. Each one still takes three days to prepare. This creation, the Cronut, instantly drew block-long lines and landed on TIME Magazine's "25 Best Inventions." His commitment to fresh ideas and quality over mass production really defines the place.

## What is Dominique Ansel Bakery famous for?

Beyond that game-changing Cronut, which unveils a brand new, non-repeating flavor each month, the bakery is known for other playful, delicious creations.

Have you heard of the Cookie Shot? It’s a warm, pliable chocolate chip cookie, shaped like a shot glass, filled with cold milk – a delightful combination of textures. Then there are the Frozen S'mores, a toasted marshmallow exterior giving way to a cool, creamy center. Of course, the DKA, with its signature caramel crunch, remains a star.

Back when Cronuts first launched, the crowds were so thick, they even needed people to manage the queues, sometimes offering waiting customers warm drinks in winter or lemonade in summer.

## How much does a Cronut usually cost?

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65329423a966d94a21420905/692702e79b47d946cf44bad9_attractions%252FChIJP0KOWoxZwokRmvPiQAIaH1A%252F1764163904379_dominique-ansel-bakery.webp)

Image by LittleDaan [**(by)**](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/)

The Cronut, that sought-after croissant-doughnut hybrid, comes with a specific price tag. If you pre-order for pick-up at the bakery, you'll pay around $8.44, including New York City sales tax. Considering the three days of meticulous preparation that goes into each one, it's a specialty item.

If you opt for local delivery through services like DoorDash, two Cronuts might run you $20, meaning about $10 each. For those looking to share or send them nationwide, a four-pack shipped costs about $39.50, plus shipping, making each approximately $9.88. Remember, the flavor is unique every month and never repeats, so what you try today won't be there next time.

## Where is Dominique Ansel located?

The original and most famous Dominique Ansel Bakery sits right in the heart of SoHo, at 189 Spring Street, New York, NY 10012. It’s an easy spot to get to; the C and E subway trains stop at Spring Street, and the N, R, and W trains are just a few blocks away at Prince Street.

This neighborhood location puts you among distinctive 19th-century cast-iron buildings and plenty of shops. Inside the bakery, the space itself is often lively, but if you look carefully, you might find one of their "secret" outdoor patio areas for a quieter moment with your pastry and coffee.

## How many Dominique Ansel Bakery locations are there?

Currently, there are five Dominique Ansel Bakery locations. The original, which gained worldwide attention for the Cronut, is still right here in SoHo, New York. Beyond that, you'll find Dominique Ansel Workshop in Flatiron, which focuses on croissants and gives you a peek into the production kitchens.

A new concept called Papa d'Amour, opening in Greenwich Village soon, plans to explore Asian bread culture. Away from New York, if you're visiting Las Vegas, you can find two more spots: one at Caesars Palace and another at Paris Las Vegas. So, while the SoHo store is iconic, you have a few choices depending on what you're looking for.

## Can you order online from Dominique Ansel?

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65329423a966d94a21420905/692702e79b47d946cf44baec_attractions%252FChIJP0KOWoxZwokRmvPiQAIaH1A%252F1764163919408_dominique-ansel-bakery.webp)

Image by Edsel L [**(by-sa)**](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/)

Absolutely, if you want to skip the line or enjoy these treats from home, you have options. For local pick-up at the SoHo bakery, you can place pre-orders through their New York website. If you're within New York City and prefer delivery, select items, including Cronuts, are available via third-party apps like Caviar or DoorDash.

And for those outside the city, or sending a gift, many signature pastries like Cronuts, DKAs, and Cookie Shots can be shipped nationwide directly from their kitchens. A practical tip: if you're set on a Cronut, pre-orders for pick-up open promptly at 11 am EST every Monday for items two weeks out.

## Is it worth visiting Dominique Ansel Bakery?

Deciding if a visit is "worth it" really depends on what you seek. If you're an adventurous foodie eager to taste a globally recognized, innovative pastry like the Cronut, or enjoy seeing culinary artistry, then yes, it offers a unique experience. The creations are visually appealing and often delicious.

However, be prepared for potential downsides. The bakery can get very crowded, especially on weekends, making the small interior feel a bit tight. Prices are on the higher side for pastries, and some find the Cronut, while interesting, a little too sweet or perhaps overhyped for their personal taste.

If you're short on time, sensitive to crowds, or on a tight budget, you might weigh your options. Pre-ordering online or visiting early on a weekday morning can significantly improve the experience by avoiding the longest queues.

## What else can I do in New York?

Once you've had your fill of pastries, the vibrant SoHo neighborhood beckons. Step outside the bakery and stroll down the charming cobblestone streets.

You'll be [surrounded by the beautiful 19th-century cast-iron architecture](/en/articles/top-14-things-to-do-in-soho-nyc) that makes SoHo so distinct; it’s like walking through an outdoor gallery. The area is packed with high-end boutiques and art galleries, perfect for window shopping or discovering something truly unique.

A short walk away, you can find Washington Square Park, with its famous arch, street performers, and lively energy – a great spot to relax and people-watch. For an evening adventure, consider seeking out the hidden speakeasy at La Esquina for cocktails and upscale Mexican food, behind what looks like a casual diner.

# Papa d’Amour by Dominique Ansel — Japanese-French Bakery in Greenwich Village, NYC

A new concept by Chef Dominique Ansel exploring his love of Asian bread culture. Dedicated to his two young children, who are Taiwanese and French, “Papa d’Amour” means “Papa, my love” in French. “It’s what my kids call me,” says the chef. “Especially when they want something.”

We love blending cultures, techniques, and memories in the world of pastry. And we all know that when Papa is in the kitchen, there are no rules.

Located just between Greenwich Village and Union Square on one of our favorite pedestrian-friendly streets in New York, Papa d’Amour is a casual bakery near Washington Square Park offering a variety of breakfast, lunch, and dessert options. We welcome you to grab a quick bite for breakfast near NYU, or stay a little while and dine in. The coffee is always brewing, fresh-baked buttery aromas are always coming out of our ovens, and check back regularly for new menu creations.

Please note: we do not take reservations and are walk-in only. Order at the registers, find a table, and enjoy!

Press Reviews

## Word On The Street

Time Out New York

Named for the sweet sobriquet his two young children call him, the bakery pays tribute to his kids’ Taiwanese and French heritage with a spotlight on Asian bread culture—think fluffy shokupan and pillowy milkbreads, steamed buns, rich egg tarts, flaky layered pastries, and more. And this being an Ansel property, of course there will be plenty of playful inventiveness on the menu, too.

Observer

His new concept, named for an endearing nickname from his children, moves away from classic French techniques to Asian bread culture: think steamed buns, egg tarts, fresh-baked shokupan and more. Savory options, like the scallion basil blossom made with a scallion and Thai basil pesto and laminated brioche crust, will show off Ansel’s signature twists on flavor and ingredients.

Food & Wine

On a recent Sunday afternoon, I visited Papa d’Amour, Dominique Ansel’s newest bakery that is inspired by Asia’s diverse bread cultures. It has all the terrific pastries you’d expect, from a tender bun stuffed with chicken curry to a steamed bao croissant, and a banana bread that toes the line between snack and dessert.

James Beard Award-winning Pastry Chef, Dominique Ansel has shaken up the pastry world with innovation and creativity at the heart of his work.

Chef Dominique is responsible for creating some of the most fêted pastries in the world, including: the Cronut® (named one of TIME Magazine’s “25 Best inventions of 2013”).

### **Yakimochi Hot Chocolate**

As the weather gets chillier, we welcome our Yakimochi Hot Chocolate back to the menu. Yakimochi translates to “grilled mochi” in Japanese.

Our version at Papa d’Amour features rich and silky Valrhona dark hot chocolate, condensed milk whipped cream on top, and a soft and chewy mochi that’s gently grilled and brushed with honey butter soy sauce caramel to finish.

### **Elotes Sweet Corn Butter Soft Serve**

Summer corn is the star of this sweet treat, an Elotes sweet corn version of Papa d’Amour’s signature butter-dipped soft serve.

Silky sweet corn soft serve is swirled into a waffle cone, then dipped into a thin layer of our Isigny Ste. Mère French butter dip (the same butter Chef Dominique uses for all his croissant recipes). To finish: a sprinkle of Cotija cheese and Tajin for a subtle salty spicy kick, and a wedge of fresh lime to squeeze overtop.

Fresh Fruit Sandos

### **Fresh Fruit Sandos**

Our fresh fruit sandos feature beautifully ripe summertime fruits sandwiched on our freshly-baked Japanese-style shokupan bread. Choose from three flavors, including:

* Strawberries & Cream: Fresh strawberries, Chantilly cream with a hint of fennel, strawberry jam, & confit strawberries
* Banana & Black Sesame: Toasted black sesame Chantilly, vanilla Chantilly, fresh bananas, & banana caramel
* Honey Roasted Fig & Shiso: Fresh sliced Mission figs, shiso Chantilly, honey roasted confit figs, & fig jam

# Zak the Baker

People flock to this colorful cornerstone bakery for its kosher goods, and they stay for dishes from the cafe. Zak Stern opened the Wynwood storefront in 2014, and it has been a staple of the community ever since. Breads and pastries are local favorites, as well as bagels, soups, and sandwiches. Zak’s also has an assortment of coffee, teas, and a house passionfruit soda to wash down the meal.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Company based in Miami

| Zak the Baker |
| --- |
| Restaurant information |

| Head chef | Zak Stern |
| Food type | [Kosher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosher "Kosher") food, [bakery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bakery "Bakery") and [deli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delicatessen "Delicatessen") items |
| Location | 405 NW 26th St. (deli)  295 NW 26th S. (bakery), [Wynwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wynwood "Wynwood"), [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami"), [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida"), [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") |
| Website | [zakthebaker.com](http://zakthebaker.com) |

**Bakery** or **Zak the Baker** is a [kosher restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosher_restaurant "Kosher restaurant") in the [Wynwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wynwood "Wynwood") neighborhood of [Miami, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami,_Florida "Miami, Florida").[[1]](#cite_note-haaretz-hand-1)[[2]](#cite_note-miamiherald-baker-2) After the bakery was moved into a larger building,[[2]](#cite_note-miamiherald-baker-2) Zak the Baker opened a new [glatt kosher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glatt_kosher "Glatt kosher") [delicatessen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delicatessen "Delicatessen") in January 2017[[3]](#cite_note-nyt-florence-3) in the old bakery location.[[2]](#cite_note-miamiherald-baker-2) The associated bakery and café were both founded by local baker Zak Stern.[[4]](#cite_note-vice-bakery-4) The bakery closes on Saturdays, in keeping with kosher requirements.[[2]](#cite_note-miamiherald-baker-2)[[5]](#cite_note-bonappetit-bakery-5)

The bakery has developed a reputation for its [sourdough bread](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sourdough_bread "Sourdough bread"), among other items[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7) such as [challah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Challah "Challah") bread.[[1]](#cite_note-haaretz-hand-1)

## Recognition

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zak_the_Baker&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Recognition")]

In 2013, Zak Stern was named Best Baker by the *[Miami New Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_New_Times "Miami New Times")* in their Best of Miami Awards.[[8]](#cite_note-8) In 2014 the Zak the Baker Wynwood Bakery & Cafe won Best Bakery in the Best of Miami Awards,[[9]](#cite_note-mnt-award2-9) and Stern won the Baking & Pastry Chef of the Year award at the JWU Zest Awards for his work with the restaurant in 2015.[[10]](#cite_note-mnt-award-10)

###### Categories

###### Neighborhoods

Named after the street where it was first located in SoHo, Sullivan Street Bakery was established in 1994 by former sculptor and bread aficionado, Jim Lahey. Meeting him one afternoon, while grabbing a bite of some of the freshly baked flat breads and sandwiches, was a double treat for members of the Manhattan Sideways team. It is always nice to learn the history and hear the passion of a shop directly from its owner.  
  
After spending eight months living in Italy and studying the art of bread making in the early 90's, Jim came back to the States with a talent for baking some of the best loaves around. Though he could only bake in his Williamsburg garage between shifts at other jobs, he continued to experiment with his own recipes and eventually started selling his product at street markets. Auspiciously, the first time he sold his bread was at a market on the corner of Houston and Sullivan Street, close to the site of his future brick-and-mortar.  
  
Jim moved Sullivan Street Bakery to the current location in Hell's Kitchen in 2000 and remains as involved in his business as ever – in fact, he lives right above the shop. He is famous for his revolutionary bread baking technique, often referred to as no-knead baking. In short, instead of pounding bread into a table, Jim lets the dough sit for fourteen to twenty hours, allowing it to ferment, and then puts it in a 450 degree oven for about an hour. The simple technique has encouraged many, including my own husband, to bake bread at home and rave about the results.  
  
In addition to Jim's bakery on 47th, he also opened Co. (short for Company) in 2009, where guests are invited to sit at communal tables to indulge in his variety of pizzas and other scrumptious items on the menu. Having written two books – My Bread (2009) and My Pizza (2012) – Jim has become a figurehead in the movement that is raising the standard for bakers everywhere, especially in Manhattan. It is his ultimate hope that the art of bread making will become as much of a cultural practice here as it is in Italy.

### More places on 47th Street

Lost Gem

[### Gold Standard Watches & Jewelry

There was no question that Ellie Mendelsohn would stand behind the glass booth with her father, Hank, on 47th Street once she completed her college education. Her grandfather, who had introduced his son and granddaughter to the world of gold and jewelry, had retired to Florida, and now it was Ellie’s time to join the family trade. “The jewelry is my favorite part of the business, so I said, ‘Why not start my own line? ’” The first piece Ellie ever made was a pair of earrings, based on a necklace that her father had made for her mom. “I loved it so much, I decided to create earrings. ” Indeed, for those who work in the Diamond District, jewelry is much more than an accessory — it is a time-honored link to one’s heritage and family.](/discover/1mjqc7KMktMhOH1SC9Cvmx/gold-standard-watches-jewelry)

Lost Gem

[### The Actors' Temple

Ezrath Israel was originally established as a Jewish Community Center in 1917 by the West Side Hebrew Relief Association, a group of Orthodox Jewish shop owners. The area was known for its busy steamship ports, however, the entertainment business eventually became one of the biggest industries in this part of town. As show business grew, so did the number of congregants, and it became the place of worship for many prominent actors and performers, including Sophie Tucker and Shelley Winters. The Actors' Temple continued to thrive until shortly after WWII when people in the industry began journeying across the country to Hollywood. The synagogue then found its membership slowly decreasing. By 2005, there were only twelve members left in the congregation. A year later, when Jill Hausman became the rabbi, she found herself resuscitating what had once been a proud shul. Rabbi Hausman was pleased to report to us that in the eight years that she has been there, membership has increased to about 150, a marked improvement. Still, she has hope that the Actors' Temple will continue to grow. "We are a well-kept secret, " she says, "but we don't need to be. " To help maintain the synagogue, the sanctuary is shared with an Off Broadway theater company that performs on their "stage, " just a few feet in front of their sacred arc and collection of eleven torahs. Today, Rabbi Hausman welcomes all denominations of Judaism, even those who are "on the fringes of society. " She is a warm, sweet, bright woman who not only has her door open to everyone, but her heart as well. She emphasizes the importance of love and acceptance in her sermons and is adamant that the Actors' Temple is a "no-guilt synagogue. " People should come if they feel compelled to pray – Rabbi Hausman's only goal is to have them leave with a desire to return.](/discover/2D4hXGAkVWGs2iTruYWd5V/actors-temple)

Lost Gem

[### Rum House

Located next door to the Hotel Edison, Rum House embraces the hotel's legacy as a hot spot for New Yorkers to dine and dance. Today, it serves as a bar with live jazz and blues playing every evening.](/discover/2DrGGq1yDwNJ3OLkbOtgO5/rum-house)

Lost Gem

[### Phil's Stationery

For the first seven years, Phil Podemski had his shop on Park Row across from City Hall, but in 1973, with the help of his son, Sam, they came uptown and have resided on 47th Street ever since. "It was a good move on our part, " Sam admitted. "It has allowed us to weather each of the storms that have come our way. "Because Phil's Stationery is in the Jewelry District, there have always been customers in need of memorandum books, special jewelry bags for shipping, and other necessary items that Sam and his dad never allowed to run out of stock. "This has kept us alive. " That and the warm customer service that he strongly believes in. "Yes, I could close up shop and sell my goods solely on the internet, but I would miss the people — the human connection. " Sam's best connection, however, was with his dad. "We were together for forty years until he passed away in 1996. I have the best memories of him yelling at me throughout those years, always in the most loving way. "When Sam and his dad initially opened, they were not known as an office supply store. They carried an amalgam of health and beauty products, chocolate, and other novelty goods. As time progressed, they evolved into a full office supply shop carrying absolutely everything that one could want or need for their desk. In addition to having fun rummaging through the stacks of notebooks, journals, pens, markers, and an array of art supplies, it is the collection of Berol pencils made in the U. S. in the 1960s, the old Swingline staplers — and several other items that date back some fifty to sixty years — that will provide a noteworthy trip down memory lane for many.](/discover/2HrW3knfG62wiRZnoqFfO0/phils-stationery)

Lost Gem

[### Haven Rooftop

As the elevator doors open, a gust of vivacious conversation rushes to welcome every guest to the Haven atop the Sanctuary Hotel. This rooftop caters to three different spaces that gently correspond to the desired experience at hand. On the lower level, there are two bars. The first stands below geometrically alluring lights made to resemble stars. Dinner chosen from the Haven’s “French-Inspired” menu is served on this side of the roof where the mood is serene. On the other side, past the statue of a seahorse and the young trees, the volume rises and the crowd clings readily to this, the second bar. While some prefer to wind down with dinner, others are just trying to let loose. The Haven supports both pursuits. Upstairs, the uniform faded red lounge cushions fashion a more secluded setting that grants the wish for a private discussion or for the simple enjoyment of the mid-city view from a higher position. As is somewhat suggested by the name, “Haven, ” this rooftop is plainly reminiscent of a getaway, more specifically a beach house. The Haven happened to be where we stopped by the day the US was playing Belgium in the 2014 World Cup. It was a memorable moment standing beside dozens of New Yorkers as our national anthem was being played. Glass enclosed in the colder months, and serving a French-American menu both during the lunch and dinner hours, this was another great rooftop find.](/discover/2KA76p9QcNhwFp8Mi4EpiO/haven-rooftop)

# Build-Outs Of Coffee: Ritual Coffee Roasters In San Francisco, CA

![ritual coffee 8](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ritual-coffee-8-527x351.jpg)
![ritual coffee 8](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ritual-coffee-8-1044x696.jpg)

These are exciting times for [Ritual Coffee Roasters](https://ritualcoffee.com/), the seminal San Francisco specialty coffee brand founded in 2005. They’ve spent the last 21 years going from strength to strength whilst leading from the front, and now they’re opening a brand new cafe in the San Francisco Financial District. Let’s learn more!

*The 2026 Build-outs of Coffee is presented by [DONA](https://drinkdona.com/),[Pacific Barista Series](http://instagram.com/baristaseries), and [La Marzocco](http://instagram.com/lamarzocco.usa).*

[![DONA](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/dona-holiday-library-sprudge-booc.jpg)](https://drinkdona.com/pages/wholesale?utm_source=sprudge&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=library)![](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAP///////yH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

*As told to Sprudge by Eileen Rinaldi.*

**For those who aren’t familiar, will you tell us about your company?**

In 2005, when corporate coffee dominated American culture, Ritual unknowingly started a fun and exciting revolution that would ultimately help launch the new specialty coffee movement. By prioritizing sustainability and quality in our buying practices, we ensure we get our hands on the best beans in the world, but more importantly, that coffee farming remains a profitable business for coffee producers. Now a bona fide San Francisco original, we’ve also earned our iconic status as one of the best coffee roasting companies in the world. The mission of Ritual Coffee is simple: to make people happy by giving them the best coffee experience they’ve ever had. Ritual roasts in SoMa, and has cafes in San Francisco and Napa.

![ritual coffee 4](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ritual-coffee-4-1200x800.jpg)

**Can you tell us a bit about the new space?**

Our new cafe is a large, light-filled corner location in a gorgeous mid-century modern building in the Financial District. The location is iconically San Francisco, as it’s right along the California Cable Car line. We took inspiration from classic Italian coffee bars, our neighbor the Tadich Grill, and Edward Hopper’s painting “Nighthawks” to create a coffee oasis.

Fun fact! It’s the very same cafe where owner Eileen Rinaldi was dreaming up Ritual and managing a cafe there 23 years ago!

**What’s your approach to coffee?**

We want to give people an experience that will change the way they think about coffee. For us, there’s no better way to do that than to introduce them to some of our favorite coffees in a brewing method they enjoy. Our coffee program focuses on single-origin coffees (and one seasonal espresso blend!) sourced from small-holder producers, cooperatives, and coffee growing communities. Our cafe menus rotate often to reflect the seasonality of coffee, and we provide different flavor profiles for batch brew, pour-over, signature-beverage, and espresso options.

![ritual coffee 3](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ritual-coffee-3-1200x800.jpg)

**Any machines, coffees, special equipment lined up?**

Pour-over bar featuring V60s, and coffee for two, via Kalita plus a [La Marzocco](http://www.larmarzocco.com) espresso machine.

**How is your project considering sustainability?**

For this project, we looked primarily at sustainability through the lens of selecting materials that will be durable and age well with high volume. Having the experience of several other cafes under my belt, there are certain materials that are now go-tos for the cafe environment. We purchased as much of those products and materials as possible, using [Heath Ceramics](https://www.heathceramics.com/) tile, for example. Additionally, we’re in a LEED Gold certified building, so there is an additional layer of ensuring that we’re meeting that as a minimum standard, in terms of energy usage, ventilation and air quality, etc.

![ritual coffee 7](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ritual-coffee-7-1200x800.jpg)

**What’s your hopeful target opening date/month?**

Grand opening is slated for Thursday 10/22.

**Are you working with craftspeople, architects, and/or creatives that you’d like to mention?**

Yes! Seth Boor—[Boor Projects](https://boorprojects.com/)—he’s the brilliant architect behind many amazing coffee spaces, in the Bay Area and beyond. What I love about working with Seth is that he can translate the desired vision for a space into the architectural concept. I first worked with him back in 2007 on our second location, and it’s such a joy to get to work with him again on this and to see how his creative process has evolved.

**Thank you!**

Thank you!

We took inspiration from classic Italian coffee bars, our neighbor the Tadich Grill, and Edward Hopper’s painting “Nighthawks” to create a coffee oasis.

Fun fact! It’s the very same cafe where owner Eileen Rinaldi was dreaming up Ritual and managing a cafe there 23 years ago!

**What’s your approach to coffee?**

We want to give people an experience that will change the way they think about coffee. For us, there’s no better way to do that than to introduce them to some of our favorite coffees in a brewing method they enjoy. Our coffee program focuses on single-origin coffees (and one seasonal espresso blend!) sourced from small-holder producers, cooperatives, and coffee growing communities. Our cafe menus rotate often to reflect the seasonality of coffee, and we provide different flavor profiles for batch brew, pour-over, signature-beverage, and espresso options.

![ritual coffee 3](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ritual-coffee-3-1200x800.jpg)

**Any machines, coffees, special equipment lined up?**

Pour-over bar featuring V60s, and coffee for two, via Kalita plus a [La Marzocco](http://www.larmarzocco.com) espresso machine.

**How is your project considering sustainability?**

For this project, we looked primarily at sustainability through the lens of selecting materials that will be durable and age well with high volume. Having the experience of several other cafes under my belt, there are certain materials that are now go-tos for the cafe environment. We purchased as much of those products and materials as possible, using [Heath Ceramics](https://www.heathceramics.com/) tile, for example. Additionally, we’re in a LEED Gold certified building, so there is an additional layer of ensuring that we’re meeting that as a minimum standard, in terms of energy usage, ventilation and air quality, etc.

![ritual coffee 7](https://sprudge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ritual-coffee-7-1200x800.jpg)

**What’s your hopeful target opening date/month?**

Grand opening is slated for Thursday 10/22.

**Are you working with craftspeople, architects, and/or creatives that you’d like to mention?**

Yes! Seth Boor—[Boor Projects](https://boorprojects.com/)—he’s the brilliant architect behind many amazing coffee spaces, in the Bay Area and beyond. What I love about working with Seth is that he can translate the desired vision for a space into the architectural concept. I first worked with him back in 2007 on our second location, and it’s such a joy to get to work with him again on this and to see how his creative process has evolved.

**Thank you!**

Thank you!

Additionally, we’re in a LEED Gold certified building, so there is an additional layer of ensuring that we’re meeting that as a minimum standard, in terms of energy usage, ventilation and air quality, etc.

Grand opening is slated for Thursday 10/22.

Yes! Seth Boor—[Boor Projects](https://boorprojects.com/)—he’s the brilliant architect behind many amazing coffee spaces, in the Bay Area and beyond. What I love about working with Seth is that he can translate the desired vision for a space into the architectural concept. I first worked with him back in 2007 on our second location, and it’s such a joy to get to work with him again on this and to see how his creative process has evolved.

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Ritual_Coffee.jpg/250px-Ritual_Coffee.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ritual_Coffee.jpg)

Ritual Coffee

**Ritual Coffee Roasters** is a [coffee roaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_roaster "Coffee roaster") based in [San Francisco, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco,_California "San Francisco, California"), with six cafes in San Francisco and [Napa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa,_California "Napa, California").[[2]](#cite_note-NYT-2) Founded in 2005,[[3]](#cite_note-3) Ritual Roasters is considered part of the "[third wave of coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_wave_of_coffee "Third wave of coffee")" independent companies which both roast their own beans, wholesale, and operate cafes. Their peers include [Blue Bottle Coffee Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Bottle_Coffee_Company "Blue Bottle Coffee Company") and [Four Barrel Coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Barrel_Coffee "Four Barrel Coffee"),[[4]](#cite_note-4) among others. In March 2017, Somatik partnered with Ritual Coffee to make $12 marijuana-infused cold brew.[[5]](#cite_note-5)[[6]](#cite_note-6)

In 2021, the [Haight Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haight_Street "Haight Street") location of Ritual Coffee Roasters was damaged during a shooting in the area, when the café was struck by gunfire.[[7]](#cite_note-7) The incident was cited in later reporting as one of several challenges affecting the operation of the location. In March 2025, the company announced the closure of its Haight Street café, ending a nine-year presence in the neighbourhood, with the location scheduled to close on April 11.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

They have a line of canned coffee, partnered with [Juanita More](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juanita_More "Juanita More").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

# Our Roastery

[Contact Us](https://ritualcoffee.com/contact/)

##### About Our Roastery

We moved into our Roastery, a serendipitously painted red and white former door hardware factory, in 2009.

Manufacturing in the heart of the city was always something we’ve been passionate about, and this cavernous space on the edge of downtown is a place to do just that – featuring a working roastery outfitted with a vintage German Probat roaster, production line, and offices, along with our training lab. It’s where the magic happens, and we can hardly wait to resume hosting events and tours.

## History

[edit]

 to sell within 24 hours of roasting, as a home-delivery service. Blue Bottle soon ceased deliveries and opened as a traditional café.

Blue Bottle opened additional locations in San Francisco and elsewhere in the San Francisco Bay Area and opened its first New York location in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, in 2010. The company-owned stores carry off-menu items such as the "Gibraltar", a form of cortado. [...] [edit]

Originating in Oakland, California, the company soon expanded to other areas around the country. Blue Bottle first expanded to several cafés in locations around San Francisco, including the Ferry Building and the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art's rooftop garden. The company operates 150 stores as of October 2026, with locations in California, New York, Washington, D.C., Boston, Chicago, Seoul, Jeju City, Kyoto, Kobe, Tokyo, Osaka, Yokohama, Hong Kong, Shanghai and Singapore. [...] Blue Bottle Coffee, Inc., is a coffee roaster and retailer once headquartered in Oakland, California, United States. In 2017, a majority stake in the company was acquired by Nestlé (68%). In 2026, Centurium Capital acquired Blue Bottle's global retail operations from Nestlé for approximately $400 million. Blue Bottle Coffee is a major player in third wave coffee. The company focuses on single-origin beans.

**Blue Bottle Coffee, Inc.**, is a [coffee roaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_roaster "Coffee roaster") and retailer once headquartered in [Oakland, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland,_California "Oakland, California"), United States. In 2017, a majority stake in the company was acquired by [Nestlé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nestlé "Nestlé") (68%). In 2026, [Centurium Capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centurium_Capital "Centurium Capital") acquired Blue Bottle's global retail operations from Nestlé for approximately $400 million. Blue Bottle Coffee is a major player in [third wave coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_wave_of_coffee "Third wave of coffee").[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1) The company focuses on [single-origin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-origin "Single-origin") beans.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

## Locations

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blue_Bottle_Coffee&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Locations")]

Originating in [Oakland, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland,_California "Oakland, California"), the company soon expanded to other areas around the country. Blue Bottle first expanded to several cafés in locations around [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), including the [Ferry Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Ferry_Building "San Francisco Ferry Building") and the [San Francisco Museum of Modern Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Museum_of_Modern_Art "San Francisco Museum of Modern Art")'s rooftop garden.[[3]](#cite_note-CNN-3) The company operates 150 stores as of October 2026, with locations in [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston"), [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), [Jeju City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeju_City "Jeju City"),[[4]](#cite_note-4) [Kyoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyoto "Kyoto"), [Kobe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kobe "Kobe"), [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), [Osaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka "Osaka"), [Yokohama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yokohama "Yokohama"), [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong"), [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai") and [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore").[[5]](#cite_note-5)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blue_Bottle_Coffee&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/James_Freeman%2C_CEO_Blue_Bottle_Coffee%2C_May_2014.jpg/250px-James_Freeman%2C_CEO_Blue_Bottle_Coffee%2C_May_2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Freeman,_CEO_Blue_Bottle_Coffee,_May_2014.jpg)

W. James Freeman, CEO of Blue Bottle Coffee, in 2014

W. James Freeman founded Blue Bottle Coffee in the early 2000s in [Oakland's Temescal District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temescal,_Oakland,_California "Temescal, Oakland, California").[[6]](#cite_note-6) Freeman borrowed the name from one of Europe's first cafés, [The Blue Bottle Coffee House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blue_Bottle_Coffee_House "The Blue Bottle Coffee House"). Initially, he intended to roast coffee in small batches (6 lbs. per roast) to sell within 24 hours of roasting, as a home-delivery service. Blue Bottle soon ceased deliveries and opened as a traditional café.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

Blue Bottle opened additional locations in San Francisco and elsewhere in the [San Francisco Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area") and opened its first New York location in [Williamsburg, Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamsburg,_Brooklyn "Williamsburg, Brooklyn"), in 2010.[[8]](#cite_note-8) The company-owned stores carry off-menu items such as the "Gibraltar", a form of [cortado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortado "Cortado").[[3]](#cite_note-CNN-3)

In 2012, Blue Bottle received $20 million in [venture capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venture_capital "Venture capital") investment, led by True Ventures.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

In January 2014, Blue Bottle raised $25.75 million in a new round of funding.[[10]](#cite_note-10) In 2015, Blue Bottle completed a [venture capital round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venture_round "Venture round") in which it raised $70 million from investors led by [Fidelity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidelity_Investments "Fidelity Investments").[[11]](#cite_note-11)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Blue_Bottle_Coffee_Moynihan_Station_NY.jpg/250px-Blue_Bottle_Coffee_Moynihan_Station_NY.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Blue_Bottle_Coffee_Moynihan_Station_NY.jpg)

Blue Bottle Coffee stand in the [Moynihan Train Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moynihan_Train_Hall "Moynihan Train Hall") (Penn Station) New York

Since its inception, the company has raised $120 million from investors as of 2017.[[12]](#cite_note-12) In February 2015, Blue Bottle Coffee opened its first location in Tokyo, Japan, in the Kiyosumi neighborhood.[[13]](#cite_note-13) In September 2017, [Nestle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nestle "Nestle") S.A., the world's largest food and drinks company, acquired a majority stake of Blue Bottle.[[14]](#cite_note-14) While the deal's financial details were not disclosed, the *[Financial Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_Times "Financial Times")* reported "Nestle is understood to be paying up to $500m for the 68 per cent stake in Blue Bottle".[[15]](#cite_note-15) Blue Bottle expected to increase sales by 70% in 2017.[[16]](#cite_note-16)

In May 2019, Blue Bottle Coffee opened its first location in [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), South Korea.[[17]](#cite_note-17) In December 2019, Blue Bottle Coffee announced they would test eliminating [disposable cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disposable_cup "Disposable cup") at some of their shops to increase sustainability efforts, with the goal being zero waste within one year.[[18]](#cite_note-18) Nothing has been reported to date about this test and whether it was successful. In April 2020, Blue Bottle Coffee opened its first location in [Central, Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central,_Hong_Kong "Central, Hong Kong"). Amid COVID-19, the café opened daily from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. for takeaway only.[[19]](#cite_note-19)

In February 2022, Blue Bottle Coffee opened its first location in mainland China, Yutong Cafe. Yutong Cafe is located at a historic building by [Suzhou Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzhou_Creek "Suzhou Creek") in downtown [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai").[[20]](#cite_note-20)

In August 2024, Blue Bottle Coffee opened a gift-centric store in [Raffles City Shopping Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffles_City_Singapore "Raffles City Singapore"), Singapore.[[21]](#cite_note-21) In April 2025, this location was converted to a café and became the company's first location in South East Asia.[[22]](#cite_note-22) It has since gone on to open its second store in Singapore at [Paragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paragon,_Singapore "Paragon, Singapore") in July 2025.[[23]](#cite_note-23)

In December 2025, it was reported that Nestlé was considering selling Blue Bottle.[[24]](#cite_note-24)

In March 2026, Centurium Capital reached an agreement with Nestle to acquire Blue Bottle Coffee. At the time, Blue Bottle Coffee was operating at a loss.[[25]](#cite_note-25)

## Labor relations

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blue_Bottle_Coffee&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Labor relations")]

In April 2024, Blue Bottle Coffee’s [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") area locations filed to [unionize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_unions_in_the_United_States "Labor unions in the United States").[[26]](#cite_note-26) Baristas cited multiple grievances with the company as reason for unionizing, including not being paid a living wage, mishandling of sexual harassment,[[27]](#cite_note-27) and not being given input into café operations. The union requested voluntary recognition from the company, and subsequently engaged in a state-wide walkout when Blue Bottle Coffee refused to recognize the union.[[28]](#cite_note-28)

In September 2024, Blue Bottle Coffee fired union organizer Remy Roskin.[[29]](#cite_note-29) In May 2025, Blue Bottle Independent Union (BBIU) conducted another state-wide walkout across Blue Bottle Coffee’s greater Boston area locations in protest of multiple alleged unfair labor practices, including the company attempting to install surveillance cameras.[[30]](#cite_note-30)[[31]](#cite_note-31) On June 17 2025, four Blue Bottle cafés in California’s East Bay area (Berkeley, Old Oakland, Piedmont, and W.C. Morse) announced their intent to join BBIU.[[32]](#cite_note-32) The next day, June 18, Blue Bottle terminated union organizer BB Young,[[33]](#cite_note-33) which BBIU alleges was illegal retaliation. On July 31, the four East Bay area locations won recognition through an NLRB election in a 22–5 vote.[[34]](#cite_note-34) This vote resulted in nearly 12% of U.S. Blue Bottle locations being unionized.[[35]](#cite_note-35) In November 2025, roughly 80 Blue Bottle workers around Boston and 35 workers in California went on strike ahead of the Thanksgiving weekend, with workers accusing the company of negotiating with the union in [bad faith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_faith "Bad faith").[[36]](#cite_note-36)

# Blue Bottle – New York (US)

The Oakland coffee heavyweights operate one of New York's coolest coffee roasteries in the heart of Brooklyn.

Anyone who is even vaguely familiar with the US specialty coffee scene will most likely have heard of Blue Bottle at some point. This Oakland, California-based business was founded by former freelance musician W. James Freeman on the principle that his customers would enjoy only the freshest and highest quality coffees  out there and that they wouldn’t be older than 48 hours after being roasted. These days Blue Bottle is one of the fastest growing independent specialty coffee businesses with locations in San Francisco, Los Angeles, New York and Tokyo. I recently had the pleasure of visiting their Mint Plaza location in San Francisco where I enjoyed a perfectly prepared Ehtiopia Suke Quto. Read my San Francisco write up [here](https://thecoffeevine.com/blog/travel/discovering-san-franciscos-very-best-coffee-spots/).

[![Standing in line at the bar](https://thecoffeevine.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/IMG_0243-500x375.jpg)](https://thecoffeevine.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/IMG_0243.jpg)

Standing in line at the bar

**The** final stop of my US and Mexico tour was New York and on a stunningly sunny day, I popped down to the Blue Bottle roastery in Brooklyn where I got a little tour by Location Manager Felipe and had the chance to chat with Head Roaster Joe. The gorgeous space on Berry Street is more of a work space than a café, which is manifested in the limited seating at the front and large roasting lab and packing space at the back. Still, people come and in and queue to get their daily caffeine dose in the form of an expertly preperared espresso-based drink or drip coffee. In fact, the drip coffee set up is one of the most impressive I’ve ever seen. I counted a total to 10 Bonmacs that were almost all in use simultaneously.

[![10 v60s on the go](https://thecoffeevine.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/IMG_0245-500x667.jpg)](https://thecoffeevine.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/IMG_0245.jpg)

10 Bonmacs on the go

**As** Felipe and I made our way around the back area, I had the chance to sip on a beautiful Kenya Gikirima, which they only recently started offering. This particular roastery is responsible for roasting and distributing Blue Bottle coffee to all of their New York outlets as well as a number of local accounts such as the renown Grammercy Tavern.

**It** was also interesting to observe the clientele that visits this coffee shop. I saw a few extremely fashionable characters with stunning winter coats, tourists, local residents and people who work in one of the many funky businesses in the area. Considering the wonderful transformation that this part of Brooklyn has undergone in recent years, it should therefore not come as a surprise that a brand like Blue Bottle should set up shop here. Stumptown also has a large roastery in New York and Integlligentsia from Chicago runs a few stores in town, including a location in the Urban Outfitters on Herald Square.

[![Roaster Joe](https://thecoffeevine.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/IMG_0240-500x667.jpg)](https://thecoffeevine.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/IMG_0240.jpg)

Roaster Joe

**When** it comes to coffee experience, it is hard to beat Blue Bottle’s commitment to craftmanship although it has to be said that the smaller outlets like the Mint Plaza store in San Francisco have a better set up for experiencing their complete coffee offerings. I am still enjoying their delicious El Salvador Aida Batlle Kilimanjaro though at home in Amsterdam. Truly exquisite!

[![A Cappuccino in the making](https://thecoffeevine.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/IMG_0249-150x150.jpg)](https://thecoffeevine.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/IMG_0249.jpg)

A Cappuccino in the making

# Chinese coffee titan set to buy Oakland-born Blue Bottle Coffee

![](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/df4e8b33de192dda5b6ab41517a6877d6cbf48f37065779ca18e5e7ffb9687eb/lightyear_networkapi/resizefit_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fla_times_articles_853%2F946095210eb5a2a4a41bfabccbff018c)

A cup from Nestlé's Oakland-born specialty coffee company, Blue Bottle. (Eric Risberg / Associated Press)

Caroline Petrow-Cohen

2 min read

* [NESN.SW

  +1.77%](/quote/NESN.SW/ "NESN.SW")

Blue Bottle Coffee, the Oakland-born specialty coffee roaster owned by Nestlé, could soon be acquired by a Chinese investment firm that controls one of China's biggest coffee chains.

Centurium Capital, the majority shareholder of Luckin Coffee, is reportedly buying Blue Bottle for less than $400 million. The Chinese news outlet Yicai Global said [the deal](https://www.yicaiglobal.com/flashdetail/113290272167621) has been signed but not yet finalized.

Earlier this week, [Bloomberg reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-03-04/luckin-coffee-backer-centurium-is-said-to-be-in-advanced-talks-for-blue-bottle) that Centurium is in "advanced talks" to acquire Blue Bottle, according to people familiar with the situation.

Blue Bottle offers customers specialty coffee options, including a sweet and creamy New Orleans-style coffee, as well as espresso drinks and cold brew. The company has several locations in Los Angeles in Culver City, Santa Monica and West Hollywood.

Nestlé will retain Blue Bottle's consumer goods business, including instant coffee and ready-to-drink beverages, while Centurium will acquire Blue Bottle's global stores, according to reports.

**Read more:** [Peet's Coffee is closing outlets in Southern California](https://www.latimes.com/business/story/2026-01-29/peets-coffee-is-closing-outlets-in-southern-california?utm_source=yahoo&utm_medium=promo_module&utm_campaign=rss_feed)

Founded in the Bay Area in 2002, Blue Bottle has more than 70 U.S. locations as well as outlets in China, Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore and South Korea. The company was part of a movement toward expensive, single-origin coffee beans known in the U.S. as [third wave coffee](https://www.latimes.com/food/story/2019-10-04/third-wave-coffee-trish-rothgeb).

According to an exclusive report from one Chinese outlet, Blue Bottle is still operating at a loss. The company's revenue for the year ended June 30, 2025, was $250 million, with about $150 million coming from U.S. stores, [the outlet said](https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/3708291149148288).

Nestlé bought a majority stake in Blue Bottle in 2017, paying $425 million for 68% of the shares. Based in Vevey, Switzerland, Nestlé also makes hot chocolate and cookie dough, and has stakes in popular brands including Cheerios and Häagen-Dazs.

**Read more:** [Has the L.A. coffee scene reached peak cream top?](https://www.latimes.com/food/story/2025-06-06/maru-mandarin-coffee-stand-discontinue-cream-top-add-ons?utm_source=yahoo&utm_medium=promo_module&utm_campaign=rss_feed)

Centurium Capital became the largest shareholder of Luckin Coffee in 2022. In 2020, Luckin agreed to pay a $180-million penalty to settle charges brought by the United States Securities and Exchange Commission alleging fabricated sales.

Luckin reported more than [$7 billion in revenue](https://investor.luckincoffee.com/news-releases/news-release-details/luckin-coffee-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025) in 2025 and has more than 30,000 locations globally.

Blue Bottle, Nestlé and Centurium Capital did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

**Stumptown Coffee Roasters** is a [coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee "Coffee") [roaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_roasting "Coffee roasting") and retailer based in [Portland, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon"), [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"). The chain's first location opened in 1999. Three other cafes, a roastery and a tasting annex have since opened in Portland, as well as locations in [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle"), [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), and [Pasadena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasadena "Pasadena").[[2]](#cite_note-2) Stumptown is owned by [Peet's Coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peet's_Coffee "Peet's Coffee"),[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-:0-4) which in turn is owned by [Keurig Dr Pepper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keurig_Dr_Pepper "Keurig Dr Pepper"). The company was an early innovator with [cold brew coffee in nitro cans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitro_cold_brew_coffee "Nitro cold brew coffee") and have continued to develop other cold brew product innovations.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stumptown_Coffee_Roasters&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Founder [Duane Sorenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duane_Sorenson "Duane Sorenson") and Stumptown Coffee Roasters have been labeled as part of the [third wave of coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_wave_of_coffee "Third wave of coffee") movement.[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7) Sorenson and his employees visited coffee farms in person and reportedly paid high prices for beans, occasionally three or four times the [fair trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_trade "Fair trade") price.[[8]](#cite_note-8) He once set the record for highest price ever paid for coffee beans.[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-10)[[11]](#cite_note-11)

Sorenson also offered atypical perks to his employees such as paying for a compilation album to be produced of their various bands,[[12]](#cite_note-12) and hiring a full-time on-staff massage therapist.[[13]](#cite_note-Roast_2006-13) Stumptown received the *Roaster of the Year 2006,* an award from a technical trade magazine called *Roast Magazine*[[13]](#cite_note-Roast_2006-13)

In January 2014, the company began selling coffee, pre-mixed with milk, in grocery stores.[[14]](#cite_note-14) In 2015, Stumptown Coffee Roasters was bought by [Peet's Coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peet's_Coffee "Peet's Coffee") for an undisclosed amount.[[4]](#cite_note-:0-4)

### Locations

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stumptown_Coffee_Roasters&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Locations")]

Stumptown operates five cafes in Portland. They are located on SE 45th & Division St., SE 34th & Belmont, downtown at SW 3rd & Ash St., inside the [Ace Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_Hotel "Clyde Hotel") at 1022 SW [Stark Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stark_Street "Stark Street"), and at the Portland International Airport. The company also owns a roasting facility and a retail annex inside their headquarters at 100 SE Salmon St. The original location on SE Division was previously a hair salon called "The Hair Bender," whose name Stumptown adopted for one of their signature espresso blends.[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

In November 2007, Stumptown opened two cafes in Seattle.[[15]](#cite_note-15) In September 2009, the company also launched a cafe in New York's Ace Hotel.[[16]](#cite_note-16) A temporary "pop-up" location appeared in Amsterdam's De Pijp neighborhood in May 2010.[[17]](#cite_note-17) Opened by Sorenson, he claimed it was never intended to be permanent and closed its doors that same year.

In 2013, Stumptown opened a second New York City café and a café/roaster in Los Angeles.[[18]](#cite_note-18) Additional cafes have also opened in Chicago and New Orleans. Stumptown opened their third New York cafe in a historic Brooklyn firehouse in the summer of 2018.[[19]](#cite_note-19) A location at the [Portland International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_International_Airport "Portland International Airport") opened in 2024.[[20]](#cite_note-20)[[21]](#cite_note-21)

## Reception

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stumptown_Coffee_Roasters&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Reception")]

Stumptown won in the Best Coffee (Locally Roasted) category of *[Willamette Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willamette_Week "Willamette Week")*'s annual 'Best of Portland' readers' poll in 2006.[[22]](#cite_note-22) It was a runner-up in the Best Coffee Shop category in 2017 and won in the Best Coffee Roaster category in 2018.[[23]](#cite_note-23)[[24]](#cite_note-24) Stumptown was a runner-up and ranked second in the Best Coffee category in 2020 and 2022, respectively.[[25]](#cite_note-25)[[26]](#cite_note-26) It was a finalist in the same category in 2025.[[27]](#cite_note-27)

Sept. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Now in its second year, the Portland Craft Chocolate Festival (PDXCCF) will bring together more than 45 Oregon chocolate makers, confectioners, bakers, and other artisan producers for three days of tasting, discovery, competition, and community — returning October 2–4 at the historic Olympic Mills Building in Portland's Central Eastside. The festival debuted last year with more than 30 exhibitors and nearly 2,000 attendees. This year, organizers have expanded the experience both inside and outside Olympic Mills, adding more makers, special collaborations, food and coffee, family activities, and events extending into the surrounding neighborhood. "I was genuinely humbled by how Portland showed up for our first festival last year," said festival founder George Domurot. "This year, we've got some upgrades, and the response from makers, bakers, partners, and the community has been incredible. More than 300 entries for our first C⁴ competition alone — it really feels like Portland is making this festival its own." More than 300 cookies — one very serious question. Making its debut this year, the C⁴ Chocolate Chip Cookie Competition set out to find some of Portland's best chocolate chip cookies — and Portland responded. Over 300 entries were submitted across Youth, Home Baker, and Professional divisions. Final judging takes place at 3 p.m. Saturday, October 3, with a panel of professional bakers, chocolate experts, and Portland personalities. Portland Mayor Keith Wilson will join the final judging panel and announce the gold, silver, and bronze winners. Winners will earn prizes, bragging rights, and the distinction of being among the first C⁴ champions. Chocolate meets tea and takes over the street On Saturday evening from 4–7 p.m., festival neighbors Steven Smith Teamaker and Ranger Chocolate Co. will take the celebration outside for a special block party and launch event. The event will offer a sneak peek at a new Steven Smith Teamaker × Ranger Chocolate Co. collection of tea-infused bonbons, bringing together two longtime Portland makers and exploring the pairing of craft tea and chocolate. The six-piece collection features chocolate creations inspired by three Steven Smith Teamaker teas — Lord Bergamot, Golden Light, and Masala Chai. Coffee, food, and plenty for the whole family Stumptown Coffee Roasters will pop up outside the festival throughout the weekend, keeping festivalgoers well caffeinated between chocolate tastings. Aybla Grill food truck will also be on site Saturday and Sunday serving Greek and Mediterranean food. Families are encouraged to explore the festival together, with activities for younger chocolate fans and free admission for children eight and under. The weekend begins on Friday night PDXCCF begins Friday evening with its VIP Meet the Makers event, giving guests an opportunity to meet participating makers and get an early taste of festival weekend. The Friday night celebration will feature spirits from Straightaway Cocktails, non-alcoholic beverages from SENS Botanicals, and dessert from New Seasons Market (including the debut of a new Ranger Chocolate Co. gianduja ice cream). The public festival follows on Saturday and Sunday from 11 a.m.–5 p.m., filling the Olympic Mills Building with chocolate, confections, and tastings from makers across Oregon. Portland's chocolate community, all in one place PDXCCF was created to bring makers and chocolate lovers together while showcasing Oregon's growing craft chocolate and artisan food community. Rather than simply tasting products, attendees can meet the people behind them, learn how they're made, discover new flavors, and take home favorites directly from participating makers. "Chocolate is at the core of the festival, and it's what brings us together — but what I love is that we get to connect our local makers with the people who love what's at the core and in the DNA of our little Portland," Domurot said. "People get to meet the hardworking folks behind the scenes who give it their all to make our home extra special." Our Story

# **Coffee is about** pleasure.

It’s that moment when your hand is warmed by the mug, you raise it to your nose, inhale deeply, and then take a sip.

That sip is the culmination of years of work, three-thousand-mile journeys, and passion. These are the steps we take to ensure that each sip is perfect.

Stumptown Coffee Roasters is a specialty coffee roaster and retailer founded in Portland, Oregon, in 1999. The first cafe opened on Southeast Division Street in a former beauty parlor called "Hair Bender," which became the name of Stumptown's signature espresso blend. Stumptown now operates cafes in select cities across the US and as far away as Kyoto, Japan.

In 2003, Stumptown pioneered the Direct Trade sourcing model, beginning with a partnership with the Aguirre family of Finca El Injerto in Guatemala that continues today. Stumptown works with dozens of producer partners across four continents, and in 2024, over 90% of all coffee purchased came through Direct Trade relationships of three or more consecutive years, with 100% of purchases independently verified by Enveritas across 30 sustainability criteria.

## Tasting

While you are holding that cup of coffee, close your eyes. Open your mouth slightly. Breathe in deeply through your nose.

You’re smelling one of the most complex things humans consume. When people talk about the flavors of coffee—notes of orange or hints of clove—it’s because those organic molecules are contained in the coffee bean. If a coffee reminds you of apple pie, it's because coffee shares some of the same components as food, like malic acid.  
  
Inside that small bean are the same natural components that make flowers smell so lovely, the same ethers that let you know when a piece of fruit is ripe. Coffee has twice as much going on, molecularly speaking, as red wine.  
  
When tasting coffee, try waiting for it to cool down a little—you’ll be able to taste (and smell) the most when it’s the same temperature as your body.  
  
Flavor only matters in the context of you. What do you like? What does this scent remind you of? Are you looking for a full-body, or a delicate, tea-like finish? Chocolate aromas, or hints of jasmine?  
  
Don’t worry if you can’t describe it precisely, or have a different perception than someone else. Even when you can’t put it into words, you’ll know what you like.  
  
You’ll experience the full flavors of the coffee bean, if and only if, nothing has gone wrong during roasting.

## Roasting

We believe that the roasting process should be transparent and that it’s our responsibility to honor the hard work already invested in the coffee by roasting it to showcase its distinctive qualities.  
   
 Every roast cycle is like the arc of development in the belly of the roaster—each minute or experience is inextricably tied to the minute or experience before and after it. Our roasting team brings over 120 collective years of roasting experience to work with them each day. It’s that depth of knowledge that allows them to welcome our longtime offerings back to the menu like greeting an old friend—warmly, with familiarity and a practiced eye for the nuanced ways the coffee may have changed from its last visit.  
   
 Roasting is one of the most delicate and critical parts of the chain of events leading to a good cup of coffee. We attempt to highlight what makes that particular variety or farm exciting, rather than imparting our own fingerprint. We're here to bring out the best in the coffee, and if we do our job correctly, no one should even be thinking about the roast when they drink it.  
   
 We've roasted on Probat machines since the very beginning. When the first Stumptown opened on Southeast Division Street in 1999, it was one employee, a Ford Pinto for deliveries, and a single small vintage Probat roaster. More than two decades later, we still roast on Probats: the German-built, cast-iron machines that have anchored specialty coffee roasting for generations. Several of ours are refurbished vintage units, chosen because they're built to run for decades, and because their reliability lets our roasters keep their attention where it belongs, on the coffee rather than the equipment  
   
 Every roast is described by three qualities, roast level, acidity, and intensity, that help you find the cup you'll love. You can see how we read those scales in our blog: Stumptown Coffee Scales Explained. And when you order by subscription, your coffee is roasted to order and shipped on your schedule, so it reaches you fresh.

"Drinking coffee is a pleasure. Coffee drinking is fun, and it feels good, and underlying all our hard work is pride in cultivating pleasure."

**—Jim Kelso**,  
Director of Quality Assurance

## Sourcing

"Traveling the world to visit producers reminds us of the differences in every region, every farm, and our approach to sourcing and roasting aims to highlight and honor these distinctions. It’s humbling to be welcomed by producers with generosity and hospitality; this is also something we try to honor and reflect, in turn, to our customers."

**—Shauna Alexander,**  
Vice President of Coffee and Sustainability
