Since our beginnings, Stumptown has searched the world for the best coffee which grows in mountainous regions of the tropics—farms perched at high elevations with warm days, cool nights, and distinct rainy and dry seasons. Microclimates, soil composition, coffee cultivars, and post-harvest processing methods each contribute distinct dimensions to the cup.  
   
 Our coffee team travels regularly to these parts of the world, meeting directly with producer partners on their farms, at their mills, and in their cupping labs.  
   
 The effort is worth it. We’re not doing it the easy way by buying bulk, mid-quality beans anonymously from a trading house. Instead, we go right to the source of the best coffee. We hike through fields, stand among coffee drying decks, and sit down to share a meal and talk about the crop with producers we’ve met many times.  
   
 We understand that our coffee demands more work—hand-picking each cherry at ideal ripeness and processing it with great attention to detail –– and we routinely work with producer partners to pay a premium price for these efforts.

![]()

### Direct Trade

Direct Trade is a sourcing model in which a roaster buys coffee directly from producers rather than through anonymous intermediaries. Unlike Fair Trade, which is a third-party certification with standardized minimum prices, Direct Trade is relationship-based, with price premiums tied directly to cup quality – and typically well above Fair Trade minimums

Stumptown pioneered Direct Trade in 2003, and the model has since become widely emulated in specialty coffee.

Stumptown’s approach is built on three principles:

* Quality-based pricing — we pay prices tied directly to cup quality, assessed using the internationally recognized Q-Grading methodology.
* Full transparency — we work with producers we know, so both sides of the supply chain stay visible to each other.
* Long-term partnership — we sustain these relationships over many years to build truly collaborative partnerships.

![]()

### Price Incentives

Stumptown pays price incentives directly linked to a coffee's quality. As described in our Direct Trade principles above, that quality is assessed using the internationally recognized Q-Grading methodology, a standardized scoring system that gives both roaster and producer a shared, transparent framework for discussing quality.  
  
Producing great coffee is expensive, and we never expect to get it on the cheap. We pay stable prices across multi-year partnerships, so everyone along the supply chain can focus on what matters: producing, roasting, and serving some of the best coffee on the planet.

![]()

### Know the Producers

From the beginning, it's been critical to us that we know where our coffee is coming from—the regions, the farms, and the people. Stumptown founder Duane Sorenson pioneered this approach in 2003 when he began our foundational direct relationship with the Aguirre family of [Finca El Injerto](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/guatemala-el-injerto-bourbon), whose coffees are, to this day, vital and beloved menu offerings. Other early Direct Trade partners include Los Delirios (Nicaragua), [El Puente](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/honduras-el-puente-natural) (Honduras), and [Bella Vista](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/guatemala-bella-vista) (Guatemala). We’ve steadily grown our relationship network for more than two decades.  
  
Every region and producer is different. When many producers come together to form a community lot, as in the case of farmer associations or cooperatives, we negotiate with a representative of the producer group. This is the case with perennials like Colombia El Jordan, Indonesia Sumatra Ketiara Bies Penantan and Ethiopia Mordecofe. This level of transparency allows us to negotiate prices, whenever possible, directly with producers.  
  
In all cases, our coffee team aims to visit the producers regularly to walk the farms, visit the mills, choose the lots, and focus on our common goal: high quality, delicious coffee.

![]()

### Long Term Relationships

Direct Trade is our way of saying “we’re in it for the long run.” We don’t call a coffee Direct Trade until we have sourced it for at least three consecutive years with the intention to continue purchasing from that producer.

That commitment shows up in the numbers. In 2025, over 90% of all coffee Stumptown purchased came through Direct Trade relationships of three or more consecutive years, and 100% of our purchases were verified by [Enveritas](https://www.enveritas.org/). This international non-profit monitors and evaluates coffee supply chains across 30 sustainability criteria.  
  
We invest in relationships with suppliers who produce exquisite coffees. We both get better results as we invest and grow together over many years. In 2024, over 90 percent of all the coffees Stumptown purchased were through Direct Trade relationships of three or more consecutive years. In addition, 100% of our purchases were verified by Enveritas––an international non-profit organization that specializes in the monitoring and evaluation of coffee supply chains across 30 different sustainability criteria.

Stumptown works with producer partners across four continents: Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua in Central America; Colombia and Peru in South America; Ethiopia, Kenya and Rwanda in Africa; and Indonesia and Papua New Guinea in Asia. Some of these relationships reach back to 2003, when we began buying coffee directly from producers. The table above lists our long term Direct Trade partners and the year our work together began.

We don’t call them farmers, we call them producers, giving credit to the fact that they are the production experts. They are the ones who make this coffee great. They are the ones who go the extra mile for quality.  
  
Producers are the heart of what makes great coffee.  
  
Their skills, expertise, and craftsmanship are the difference between mediocre coffee and coffee that is like nothing you’ve ever tasted. The coffee will never get any better in quality once it lands in our hands, after all. A good roaster works tirelessly to preserve that coffee’s inherent greatness.  
  
The producers tend the coffee trees. They ensure the cherry is harvested at its ripest. They remove the outer fruit, leaving just the bean covered in a thin parchment. They rest the beans, let the beans develop into their full selves. Every producer does something slightly different—they may tend a small patch of coffee trees on the farm inherited by a grandmother, and she may oversee the cherry soaking in a big tank of water, fermenting at just the right rate.  
  
The producer partners we work with live on four continents. They speak at least 30 different languages. Some use traditional methods that are centuries old; some work with new top-of-the-line equipment in pursuit of refining their processes.  
  
It’s not the easy way. It’s not the fastest way. But it’s the right way, and it creates the best coffee possible.

## Varieties

### Coffee is a tree, and you probably prefer one branch to another, even if you don't know it yet.

There isn’t one kind of coffee, there’s a coffee family tree.  
  
For centuries, humans have been cultivating, hybridizing, and perfecting it, and today there are hundreds of types or varieties.  
  
The variety of coffee tree matters—or at least, it usually does. Just as different types of grapes yield different wines, the variety can have a profound impact on the finished cup.  
  
There are hundreds of varieties, and we’ve chosen roughly a dozen that we find truly special. But here are the first ones you should know.

![]()

#### Bourbon

Sweet, complex, and delicate, Bourbon is the pinot noir of coffee. The plants are fragile and don’t produce as much cherry as some other varieties, but they’re worth the effort. A cup of Bourbon-type variety is lush and classic. It’s the coffee of coffee. It charms the snob and the rookie alike. And no, it has nothing to do with the delicious brown adult beverage, though we at Stumptown are big fans of that kind of bourbon, too.

**Origin:**   
One of the two foundational Arabica varieties, alongside Typica. It developed on Bourbon Island, now Réunion, off the coast of Madagascar, before spreading to Latin America and East Africa in the 1800s.  
 **In the cup:**   
Bourbons are known for their balanced sweetness and lush mouthfeel. It yields less than modern hybrids and is more vulnerable to disease, which is part of why a good Bourbon is worth the effort.

##### Related:

SL28, Tekisik, SL34, Villa Sarchi, Caturra, Colombia, Castillo, Catimor, Maracatu, Catuai

![]()

#### Typica

A direct descendant of the heirloom Ethiopian varietals, Typica was first propagated across Yemen and Java in the 1700s, eventually making its way to the Americas. By the 1800s, Typica could be found in several coffee growing regions of the Caribbean and Latin America. It’s still cultivated today and known for its exceptional cup quality. Many sought-after varieties descend from Typica.

**Origin:**   
Alongside Bourbon, one of the two parent varieties most modern Arabicas descend from. It traveled from Ethiopia through Yemen and Java, then to the Caribbean and Latin America.  
 **In the cup:**   
Clean, sweet, and refined, with a soft profile. Naturally low-yielding, but long held up as a benchmark for quality.

##### Related:

Jember, Pacamara

![]()

#### Ethiopian Heirloom

The beauty of these varieties is in their mystery. They are the wildflower varieties, descended from the natural coffee forests of southwestern Ethiopia. Each village has its own variety, handed down over centuries and shaped by the soil, elevation, and weather.

**Origin:**   
Native to Ethiopia, the birthplace of Arabica coffee. "Heirloom," also called landrace, refers to the thousands of indigenous varieties found there, many never formally identified or named.

**In the cup:**Bright and aromatic, Ethiopian heirlooms are known for fruit and floral notes that can range from delicate to pronounced.

##### Related:

All of them, really but these in particular: Typica, Gesha

![]()

#### Gesha

Think of Gesha as coffee from an alternate dimension. It's like a Szechuan peppercorn, or the Sun Ra Arkestra—both complex and otherworldly. And with a delicate, black-tea body and zest of bergamot, it’s as far as it could be from diner coffee. Gesha is picky—it grows when, where, and how it wants, and in specific microclimates. But whether you grow it in Indonesia or the Americas, it’s always thoroughly itself.  
  
Which, finally, brings us to the very beginnings of coffee…

**Origin:**   
Originally from the Gori Gesha forest in southwestern Ethiopia, sometimes (incorrectly) spelled Geisha. It gained global recognition in 2004 when a Gesha lot from Hacienda La Esmeralda in Panama shattered auction price records.

**In the cup:**   
Delicate and tea-like, with jasmine, bergamot, and tropical fruit. Low-yielding and climate-sensitive, it often commands the sky-high prices in specialty coffee.

##### Related:

Nothing. It’s in its own orbit.

## History

### Ten thousand years ago, the Coffea trees grew wild and tangly on the mountain slopes of southwestern Ethiopia.

![]()

![]()

![]()

![]()

![]()

![]()

![]()

![]()

![]()

![]()

1 / 4

There, you can still find people performing traditional coffee ceremonies many times a day—one woman will prepare it for the circle of her friends and family who stand around her. She roasts it in a pan, grinds it, pours hot water over it, and serves it in the predetermined social order.  
  
The Dutch traders brought cuttings of the plants to Indonesia. French missionaries spread it throughout Africa and across the sea to the Americas. This complicated colonialist past brought coffee trees into cultivation in every hemisphere on four continents.  
  
In 70 countries, you will find those trees and their cherries. You’ll find the producers who tend them, the pickers who select them, the processors who obsessively convert fruit to bean. You’ll find the roasters who delicately transform them, and the people who drink the coffee.  
  
You’ll find the earliest riser in the backpacking crew that stokes the fire and sets the water on to boil. You’ll find the barista who pulls the first shot of the morning for the go-getter. You’ll find the group of 70-year-old men in the diner at 6 a.m., spending hours discussing the issues of the day over their bottomless cups.

When Stumptown Coffee Roasters opened its first cafe in Portland, Oregon, in 1999, we did so with the belief that the people who grow coffee deserve the same attention as the people who drink it.

"Our primary job in sourcing is to let the coffees do the talking - as a direct reflection of the craft and innovation of the many dedicated producers we have partnered with over the past 20+ years. We are simply the curators, connecting these great coffees to our customers, so they can enjoy all the work and care in that final delicious cup."

—Jessica Brooks,

Senior Manager Green Coffee Sourcing & Quality

Everything that came before—the trees, the farmer, the journey across the sea, the hybrids and the mutations—is for this moment. Because the only thing required for the smallest, quietest and most personal of coffee ceremonies are some good beans and a way to brew.  
  
You’ll hold that mug possessively. You’ll inhale deeply. And then you drink.

# Coffee

![Coffee](//www.stumptowncoffee.com/cdn/shop/collections/Stumptown-mug.gif?v=1761607895&width=110)

### How to Choose the Right Coffee

Finding your perfect coffee doesn’t have to be complicated—but a little know-how goes a long way. Whether you're chasing fruity and bright or bold and smoky, here are a couple key things to think about when you're dialing in your next bag.

#### Single Origin vs. Blend: What’s the Difference?

* Single Origin coffees come from [one specific farm or region](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/blogs/news/growing-a-sustainable-future), and they’re all about unique flavors and a sense of place. Like **[Colombia El Jordan](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/colombia-el-jordan)**, which delivers syrupy cherry, dark chocolate, and baking spice from the lush highlands. Or [**Indonesia Bies Penantan**](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/indonesia-bies-penantan), a medium roast with dark chocolate, pineapple, and clove notes from the rich volcanic soils of Sumatra.
* Blends are crafted by combining beans from multiple origins to create balance, consistency, and depth. **[Hundred Mile](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/hundred-mile)** is a smooth, easygoing blend with a chocolatey backbone and just enough fruit to keep things interesting.

Not sure where to start? If you’re curious about terroir and want to taste something distinct, [try a single origin](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/blogs/news/growing-a-sustainable-future). Want a crowd-pleaser that brews up solid every time? [Go with a blend](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/collections/signature-blends).

#### Light, Medium, or Dark: Know Your Roast

* **Light Roast**– Bright, juicy, and complex. A coffee like **[Homestead](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/homestead)** keeps it light on the roast. Expect a balance of chocolate, candied fruit, and nougat sweetness.
* **Medium Roast**– Balanced and approachable. **[Colombia El Jordan](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/colombia-el-jordan)** hits that sweet spot—full-bodied with notes of caramel, red fruit, and subtle spice.
* **Dark Roast** – Big, bold, and roasty. [**French Roast**](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/products/french-roast) is our classic dark roast that doesn’t mess around. Smoky, bittersweet, and built for those who appreciate a classic dark brew with big flavor.

There’s no wrong way to choose—just follow your flavor and your mood. [However you brew](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/brew-guide), we've got the coffee to match.

## Stumptown Coffee FAQ

### What is Stumptown Coffee Roasters?

Stumptown is a specialty coffee roaster founded in Portland, Oregon. We source our beans through direct trade relationships with producers across four continents, many of whom we've worked with for over a decade. We pioneered the Direct Trade sourcing model in 2003, paying premium prices tied directly to quality, and in 2024 over 90 percent of our purchases came through partnerships of three or more consecutive years. Every coffee we roast is built on those relationships. [Learn more about our story.](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/our-story)

### Does Stumptown sell ground coffee?

We do. In fact, some of our coffees are available in both [whole bean](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/collections/whole-bean-coffee) and [ground](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/collections/ground-coffee) options. Just select your preferred grind when adding to cart.

### Does Stumptown offer coffee subscriptions?

Yes. With a [Stumptown coffee subscription](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/subscribe), you get coffee roasted to order and shipped on your schedule. You can adjust your selections, frequency, or cancel anytime.

### How should I store my coffee to keep it fresh?

Keep your coffee in an airtight container at room temperature, away from direct sunlight and moisture. Avoid storing it in the fridge or freezer, as temperature changes can introduce condensation and affect flavor. For the best taste, try to use your coffee within two to three weeks of the roast date.

#### Forget About It With a Subscription

If you find your perfect roast, subscribe and let us do all the work. With a [Stumptown coffee subscription](https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/subscribe) you get:

* Coffee roasted to order and shipped on your schedule
* Flexible options to adjust anytime
* A steady supply of your go-to brew

Explore the lineup and find your flavor.

**Counter Culture Coffee** is a [Durham, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durham,_North_Carolina "Durham, North Carolina")–based [coffee roasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_roasting "Coffee roasting") company[[1]](#cite_note-1) founded in 1995. It has regional [training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Training "Training") locations in [Asheville, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asheville,_NC "Asheville, NC"); [Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta"); [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston"); [Charleston, South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleston,_SC "Charleston, SC"); [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"); [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas "Dallas"); [Durham, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durham,_NC "Durham, NC"); [Emeryville, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emeryville,_CA "Emeryville, CA"); [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"); [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami"); [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"); and [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[2]](#cite_note-Why_We_Love_Counter_Culture_Coffee-2) Counter Culture training centers provide education in the fundamentals of preparing and serving [coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee "Coffee") and serve as classrooms and event spaces. Training centers are not only for vendors of Counter Culture Coffee but are also available to anyone interested in coffee production. Training centers also host competition training, food events with guest chefs, and professional [workshops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workshops "Workshops").[[3]](#cite_note-3)

Counter Culture Coffee buys primarily from small coffee producers at prices between $1.30 and $25 a pound.[[4]](#cite_note-Fellner2008-4) As such, they are regarded as a "boutique" coffee roaster, a company which sources from multiple small [estates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estate_(land) "Estate (land)") and [cooperatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooperative "Cooperative") rather than a single large grower.[[5]](#cite_note-Dougherty2008-5)

## Company history

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Counter_Culture_Coffee&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Company history")]

Counter Culture Coffee started [roasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roasting "Roasting") coffee in Durham in 1995. Founded by Brett Smith and Fred Houk, their focus was creating custom coffee blends for some of Durham and [Chapel Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapel_Hill,_North_Carolina "Chapel Hill, North Carolina")'s southern restaurants.[[6]](#cite_note-6) They sold their first coffee to Pop's Restaurant in Durham in 1995.[[7]](#cite_note-A_Different_Kind_of_Coffee_Company-7) The company expanded its operations to areas along the [East Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Coast_of_the_United_States "East Coast of the United States"). The firm also diversified its line of products and services, offering [seasonal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seasonal "Seasonal") coffee selections and [educational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Educational "Educational") programs that focus on [sustainability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainability "Sustainability") and the [coffee brewing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_brewing "Coffee brewing") process.[*[needs update](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")*]

## Sustainability

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Counter_Culture_Coffee&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Sustainability")]

Counter Culture Coffee directly collaborates with [artisans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artisans "Artisans") who grow the coffee, and their partnership with [farmers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farmers "Farmers") is a basis for their [sustainable coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainable_coffee "Sustainable coffee") model, which involves working with [progressive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressivism "Progressivism") and environmentally sensitive farms in the trade. In 2008, they launched a third-party Counter Culture Direct Trade Certification, establishing [direct trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_trade "Direct trade") standards for sustainability, quality, and fairness in the coffee chain.[[2]](#cite_note-Why_We_Love_Counter_Culture_Coffee-2) Additional initiatives include their Sustaining Educational and Environmental Development at a Source (SEEDS) program and the company's Sustainability Scorecard. The SEEDS initiative aims to support sustainability and education on the origins of the products. At the same time, the Sustainability Scorecard measures the impact of the company's efforts toward building a more sustainable supply chain.

## Education

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Counter_Culture_Coffee&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Education")]

The firm also provides consumers, employees, and wholesale partners with educational programs on coffee brewing, origin, and history. Professional development courses include Brewing Science, Barista Fundamentals, Coffee Origins, Cupping Fundamentals, and Brewing: Technique & Troubleshooting.   
Public educational initiatives include free "Tastings at Ten" every Friday morning, as well as homebrew labs for coffee enthusiasts offered at a fee.[[8]](#cite_note-8) Educational courses are offered at twelve Counter Culture Training Centers across the country.[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-Thirsty_South-10)[[11]](#cite_note-:0-11)

## Locations

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Counter_Culture_Coffee&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Locations")]

Coffee is roasted in two production facilities in Durham, North Carolina (also the company's headquarters) and Emeryville, California.[[10]](#cite_note-Thirsty_South-10)[[11]](#cite_note-:0-11)

[Top Organic Single-Origin Coffee Brands in 2026: Traceable Picks for Flavor, Transparency, and Sustainability](https://techbullion.com/top-organic-single-origin-coffee-brands-in-2026-traceable-picks-for-flavor-transparency-and-sustainability/)

Apr 30, 2026

Organic certification speaks to farming standards, while single-origin labeling points to a specific source, such as a country, region, cooperative, farm, or even a distinct lot. Compared with blends built for consistency, single-origin coffees are prized for showing a sense of place. Elevation, soil, rainfall, varietal, processing method, and local agricultural traditions all influence flavor. When those coffees are also certified organic, the result is often a more transparent, sustainability-minded choice that still prioritizes taste. Below are some of the best organic single-origin coffee brands in 2026, selected for their sourcing practices, roasting quality, and ability to highlight origin character. 1. Dean's Beans Best for: Organic single-origin specialty coffee with direct cooperative sourcing and proven roasting craftsmanship Dean's Beans remains a standout in organic specialty coffee, thanks to its long-running commitment to certified organic sourcing and relationship-based trade. Founded in 1993, the company has built its identity around 100% organic coffee and long-term partnerships with coffee-growing cooperatives. Its single-origin offerings are sourced with traceability in mind and crafted to reflect differences in region, climate, and processing. These coffees are consistently positioned around organic practices, shade-grown cultivation, and Fair Trade commitments, making them a strong fit for drinkers who want both origin clarity and values-based sourcing. Because each origin expresses itself differently, the lineup can range widely in acidity, body, sweetness, and aroma. Roasting is another key strength. With decades of specialty experience and recognition in the specialty roasting world, Dean's Beans tends to roast in a way that emphasizes nuance rather than pushing everything into the same roast signature. The brand also releases limited microlots at times, offering more specific, small-volume coffees for those who like exploring distinct profiles. Dean's Beans also reinforces its mission through formal accountability. It became a certified B Corporation in 2018 and has received B Corporation “Best for the World” Community recognition in 2019 and 2022. For buyers prioritizing organic single-origin coffee with traceability, cooperative partnerships, and careful roasting, Dean's Beans is a particularly strong option in 2026. Key Features: 30+ years of specialty roasting experience 100% organic coffee since 1993 Single-origin coffees sourced through direct cooperative relationships Organic, shade-grown, and Fair Trade single-origin options Roasting approach designed to preserve terroir and origin detail Occasional limited microlot releases Certified B Corporation since 2018 B Corporation “Best for the World” Community honoree in 2019 and 2022 Pros: Deep track record in organic specialty coffee Single-origin profiles that reflect origin differences clearly Relationship-driven sourcing with cooperatives Strong emphasis on traceability and ethical standards Roasting that prioritizes flavor detail and balance Mission-led business with third-party recognition Cons: Microlot and limited coffees can sell out quickly Smaller scale than large commercial brands 2. Kicking Horse Coffee Kicking Horse Coffee is a widely available organic and Fairtrade brand known for consistency and bold roast styles. While it is often associated with blends, it remains a convenient choice for shoppers who want certified organic coffee from a brand that is easy to find online and in many stores. For single-origin buyers, the main tradeoff is specificity. The brand is typically less microlot-focused and may provide less detailed origin nuance than smaller specialty roasters, but it performs well for everyday organic coffee with strong accessibility. Key Features: Certified organic and Fairtrade positioning Broad retail and online availability Bold, crowd-pleasing flavor direction Consistent roasting across products Well-known mainstream organic brand Pros: Easy to purchase and reorder Reliable profile for darker, fuller-bodied preferences Organic and Fairtrade standards across the brand Good entry point for organic coffee shoppers Cons: Less emphasis on high-detail single-origin expression More blend-centered overall Limited origin transparency compared to smaller craft roasters 3. Counter Culture Coffee Counter Culture Coffee is an established specialty roaster recognized for transparency efforts, educational content, and sustainability reporting. It offers a rotating single-origin selection, and some offerings are certified organic depending on availability. While the company is not exclusively organic, it is frequently chosen by specialty drinkers who want solid sourcing practices and a roasting style that tends to be balanced and approachable, especially for those moving into single-origin coffee. Key Features: Specialty-grade single-origin coffees Organic options available seasonally or in rotation Sourcing transparency initiatives Sustainability reporting and education resources Balanced roast development Pros: Strong specialty reputation Transparent approach to sourcing Good variety of origins across the year Accessible for a wide range of brew methods Cons: Not an all-organic brand Organic single-origin options can vary over time Less centered on organic certification than organic-only roasters 4. Lifeboost Coffee Lifeboost Coffee is best known for organic, low-acid coffee marketed toward drinkers seeking a smoother, gentler cup. The brand highlights shade-grown production, clean-label messaging, and third-party testing related to toxins and contaminants. It can be a good match for consumers who want organic single-origin positioning with an emphasis on comfort and smoothness. However, shoppers looking for frequent microlot releases or highly detailed terroir storytelling may prefer a more specialty-focused roaster. Key Features: Organic single-origin positioning Low-acid profile emphasis Third-party testing for contaminants Shade-grown, non-GMO messaging Smooth, approachable flavor direction Pros: Good fit for low-acid preferences Organic single-origin identity is central to the brand Clean sourcing and testing emphasis Easy-drinking profile for everyday use Cons: Premium pricing Less focus on complex, origin-driven flavor exploration Origin details may be broader than microlot-oriented roasters 5. Purity Coffee Purity Coffee takes a wellness-focused approach to organic coffee, leaning into lab testing, clean production standards, and roasting methods designed around preserving certain compounds. It offers certified organic coffee and includes traceable single-origin options within its lineup. This brand often appeals to buyers who prioritize rigorous testing and a “clean coffee” message. For some specialty drinkers, the framing may feel more health-led than terroir-led, but it can still be a relevant option for organic shoppers. Key Features: Certified organic coffees Specialty-grade Arabica Single-origin options available Lab testing for contaminants Roasting positioned around wellness goals Pros: Strong clean sourcing and testing emphasis Organic and specialty-grade positioning Fits health-oriented coffee buyers Clear brand focus on purity standards Cons: Higher pricing Less emphasis on classic origin storytelling Some products may prioritize wellness positioning over flavor nuance 6. Onyx Coffee Lab Onyx Coffee Lab is known for high-precision roasting and detailed product information, often catering to drinkers who enjoy vivid tasting notes and lighter, clarity-driven profiles. The brand is not primarily an organic coffee company, but it can offer organic single-origin coffees occasionally depending on sourcing and seasonal availability. For shoppers who want strictly organic single-origin coffee, it is worth verifying current certifications on each release. When organic options are available, Onyx can deliver an especially detailed and flavor-specific experience. Key Features: Highly regarded specialty roaster Strong single-origin selection overall Detailed tasting notes and origin data Precision-focused roast style Producer recognition and transparency emphasis Pros: Excellent for flavor detail and exploration Strong specialty credibility Great for pour-over and lighter roast fans Clear, information-rich product listings Cons: Not an organic-first brand Organic offerings may be limited or seasonal Can be expensive relative to many organic brands 7. Aldo's Coffee Company Aldo's Coffee Company offers a small-batch, traditional craft-roasting feel, and for organic single-origin buyers, its Bali Blue Krishna Single Origin Dark Roast is a notable pick. This coffee is USDA organic and positioned as a dark roast with chocolate-forward richness, a velvety texture, and lower perceived acidity. It is a practical choice for drinkers who want organic single-origin coffee without leaning into lighter roast styles. As with many darker roasts, some origin-specific delicacy may be less prominent than it would be at a lighter roast level. Key Features: Bali Blue Krishna Single Origin Dark Roast USDA organic certification Small-batch roasting approach Chocolate-leaning sweetness and full body Low-acid, dark roast profile Pros: Strong match for dark roast single-origin preferences Organic certification for the featured coffee Smooth, full-bodied cup Small-batch appeal for traditional coffee drinkers Cons: Less ubiquitous than large retail brands Darker roast style can soften some origin nuance How to Choose an Organic Single-Origin Coffee Brand A few criteria make it easier to pick the right coffee for your preferences: Origin Transparency: Look for clear naming of country, region, cooperative, farm, or lot, plus processing details when available. Organic Certification: Certified organic coffee is grown without synthetic pesticides, herbicides, and fertilizers, and often supports healthier soil systems. Roast Style: Light and medium roasts usually show more acidity and origin character. Darker roasts tend to highlight body, roast sweetness, and chocolate-like depth. Sourcing Approach: Brands that invest in long-term producer relationships and cooperative partnerships often provide more consistent traceability and stronger producer support. Flavor Preferences: Single origins can be fruit-forward, floral, nutty, cocoa-rich, earthy, or spice-toned depending on origin and processing. Consistency vs. Limited Releases: Microlots can be exciting and distinct, but year-round single-origin staples may be easier to repurchase. Frequently Asked Questions What does organic single-origin coffee mean? It refers to coffee grown under organic standards and sourced from one identifiable origin, such as a specific country, region, cooperative, farm, or lot. Is single-origin coffee always better than blends? No. Single origins are ideal for tasting a specific origin's character, while blends are often designed for balance, consistency, and a specific flavor goal. Does organic single-origin coffee taste different? It can. Farming practices, terroir, varietal, and processing method all influence flavor, and organic production may align with cleaner, soil-focused growing systems. Why does organic single-origin coffee cost more? Common factors include certification costs, lower yields, more selective sourcing, traceability requirements, and specialty-grade roasting and quality control. What roast level is best for single-origin coffee? Light and medium roasts usually preserve more origin detail. Dark roasts can be better for those who prefer deeper, heavier flavors and reduced brightness. Organic Single-Origin Coffee in 2026: Flavor You Can Trace Organic single-origin coffee sits at the intersection of responsible farming and clear origin identity. For drinkers who want a coffee that reflects a particular place and also aligns with stricter agricultural standards, it is one of the most rewarding categories to explore. In 2026, brands like Dean's Beans continue to demonstrate how organic certification, cooperative relationships, and careful roast development can come together in coffees that feel both purposeful and distinctly origin-driven. Alongside other strong options in the market, these picks show why traceable, flavor-forward organic single-origin coffee continues to gain momentum.

**Intelligentsia Coffee** is an American [coffee roasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_roasting "Coffee roasting") company and retailer based in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois"). Founded in 1995 by Doug Zell and Emily Mange, Intelligentsia is considered a major representative of [third-wave coffee in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third-wave_coffee_in_the_United_States "Third-wave coffee in the United States"). In 2015, [Peet's Coffee & Tea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peet's_Coffee_&_Tea "Peet's Coffee & Tea") (itself part of [JAB Holding Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JAB_Holding_Company "JAB Holding Company")) acquired a majority stake in the company.[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2)

## History and locations

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Intelligentsia_Coffee_%26_Tea&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History and locations")]

Intelligentsia is headquartered at 1850 W. Fulton Street, Chicago, IL, and has several cafe retail locations throughout the Chicago area. They supply coffee to various Chicago-area cafes and restaurants, as well as other locations in the US and Canada.[[3]](#cite_note-CR-3)[[4]](#cite_note-LA-4)[[5]](#cite_note-WC-5) They generally buy their beans directly from growers in Central America, South America, East Africa, and Ethiopia.[[6]](#cite_note-eG-6) Their roasting facility is in Chicago with a 300 kilogram capacity Probat R1500R roaster alongside two Gothot roasters with a capacity of 90 and 23 kilograms respectively.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

On August 17, 2007, Intelligentsia opened its first store outside of Chicago at [Sunset Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunset_Junction "Sunset Junction") in [Silver Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Lake,_Los_Angeles,_California "Silver Lake, Los Angeles, California"), a district east of [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles") in [Los Angeles, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles,_California "Los Angeles, California").[[8]](#cite_note-LAT-8) Intelligentsia has opened two additional stores in the Los Angeles area, in Venice and Pasadena.[[9]](#cite_note-9) In 2013, Intelligentsia opened its first store in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") inside [The High Line Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_High_Line_Hotel "The High Line Hotel").[[10]](#cite_note-10) The second New York City location opened in June 2014, inside the [Urban Outfitters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Outfitters "Urban Outfitters") store in Herald Square. This is the first location to offer a full food menu.[[11]](#cite_note-11) They also have 2 stores in [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") and one in [Austin, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin,_Texas "Austin, Texas").[[12]](#cite_note-12) A 2008 decision to stop serving 20-ounce coffee and [espresso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Espresso "Espresso") beverages in stores was met with controversy. Zell stated that the proportions are altered at such large quantities and certain drinks become watered-down, arguing that 20-ounce drinks end up "masking and adulterating the pure, intense flavors we work hard to source, roast and produce. We don't want this to just be a [caffeine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caffeine "Caffeine") delivery device."[[13]](#cite_note-13)

In 2009 Intelligentsia acquired Ecco Caffè of [Santa Rosa, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa,_California "Santa Rosa, California"), and has retained the brand.[[14]](#cite_note-14)

In October 2015, it was announced that [Peet's Coffee & Tea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peet's_Coffee "Peet's Coffee") would buy a majority stake in Intelligentsia Coffee & Tea by the end of the year, as part of an expansion of Peet's into third wave coffee that also involved the acquisition of [Stumptown Coffee Roasters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stumptown_Coffee_Roasters "Stumptown Coffee Roasters").[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2) Intelligentsia was expected to continue operating independently, with founders Zell and Mange retaining a role in the company.[[15]](#cite_note-:1-15) The announcement came weeks after Intelligentsia had made known that it was seeking a private equity buy-out over $100 million.[[15]](#cite_note-:1-15)

In May 2022 employees working in Intelligentsia's Chicago locations and Roasting Works warehouse filed a petition for [union representation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_unions_in_the_United_States "Labor unions in the United States").[[16]](#cite_note-16) In August 2022, employees voted to unionize, and ratified their first [collective bargaining agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collective_bargaining_agreement "Collective bargaining agreement") in December 2022.[[17]](#cite_note-17)[[18]](#cite_note-18) They are represented by [IBEW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBEW "IBEW") 1220, the same branch of IBEW that represents [Colectivo Coffee Roasters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colectivo_Coffee_Roasters "Colectivo Coffee Roasters").[[19]](#cite_note-19)

# Our Story

# Our Story

Intelligentsia is a specialty coffee pioneer, rising from humble Chicago roots to a company driven by curiosity, contribution, and the never-ending quest for the most extraordinary coffee in the world.

Intelligentsia is a specialty coffee pioneer, rising from humble Chicago roots to a company driven by curiosity, empowerment, and the never-ending quest for the most extraordinary coffee in the world.

## The Story Begins in 1995

## The Story Begins in 1995

Doug Zell and Emily Mange just wanted freshly roasted coffee. It was really that simple. After moving from San Francisco to Chicago, they found that great tasting coffee in their new city was surprisingly elusive.

Doug Zell and Emily Mange just wanted freshly roasted coffee. It was really that simple. After moving from San Francisco to Chicago, they found that great tasting coffee in their new city was surprisingly elusive.

But instead of complaining or—even worse—settling for bad coffee, they hunkered down and wrote the original business plan for what would become Intelligentsia Coffee. Their dream was to open a café and roaster in the city’s emerging Lakeview neighborhood, and on October 9, 1995, the dream welcomed its first customers.

![ ]()

Roasting their coffee in-store with a Probat L12, they honed their coffee worldview one bag of  Black Cat at a time, building slowly and seeking nothing less than perfection in every aspect of the business. Little did Doug and Emily know, they were launching what would become a fundamental sea change in specialty coffee in the United States. And by placing a deep emphasis on sourcing the most exquisite coffee available on Earth, paying a fair price for that coffee, roasting it with purpose and precision, and connecting with the community—both in Chicago and around the globe—their scrappy little coffee company would grow and help shape an entire industry.

![ ]()

![ ]()

## Intelligentsia Today

## Intelligentsia Today

Fast forward to today, and Intelligentsia still holds these original values close, though at a scale that brings extraordinary coffee to tens of thousands of customers daily.

Intelligentsia Coffee coffee roaster loc.raw_content:
Peet's Coffee and Tea is on a buying spree.

On Friday, Peet's announced it will acquire a majority stake in Chicago-based roaster, Intelligentsia Coffee, according to Eater.

This is the second time in one month that Peet's bought a stake in a small coffee chain. It also acquired a stake in Portland-based Stumptown Coffee in early October.

Headquartered in Berkeley, California, Peet's has been expanding rapidly over the past few years.

After opening its first locations on the West Coast — like the other coffee giant, Starbucks — Peet's now has coffee shops in California, Colorado, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Oregon, Virginia, Washington, and Washington, DC.

Peet’s says it will let Intelligentsia and Peet's continue to operate independently.

Stumptown is most commonly known for its ready-to-drink cold brew. Peet's will keep Stumptown as a separate brand and will retail the brand's name across its cafes, wholesale, and grocery channels.

As for Intelligentsia, the coffee shop has a total of 10 locations in Chicago, Los Angeles, and New York. It boasts its acute observance of the farming, roasting and cooling process of its coffee — offering a detailed description on its website.

Intelligentsia’s co-founders are also planning to stay actively involved in the business.

Peet's Coffee & Tea CEO Dave Burwick, made this strategic move in order to continue to evolve to cater to millennials, according to the press release on the acquisition:

"We're excited to welcome Intelligentsia to the Peet's family as the growth of the super-premium coffee market continues to explode in the U.S. It's driven by 18-34 year-olds who are more affluent, purchase premium brands from other categories like craft beer and pressed juice, and seek variety and new experiences."

While Peet's may be driven by an 18-34 year old customer base, so is Starbucks, which has 21,366 locations world-wide.

With over 200 locations nationwide, Peet's has a way to go before being a major competitor of Starbucks.

**Verve Coffee Roasters** is a [coffee roaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_roaster "Coffee roaster") based in [Santa Cruz, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Cruz,_California "Santa Cruz, California"), founded by Colby Barr[[1]](#cite_note-1) and Ryan O'Donovan.[[2]](#cite_note-2) Verve opened in November, 2007[[3]](#cite_note-3) in [Pleasure Point, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleasure_Point,_California "Pleasure Point, California"). The company currently operates in several California-based locations,[[4]](#cite_note-VerveLocations-4) including four in [Santa Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Cruz,_California "Santa Cruz, California"), four in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), one in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), one in [Manhattan Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan_Beach,_California "Manhattan Beach, California"), one in [Palo Alto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palo_Alto,_California "Palo Alto, California"), and two in Menlo Park at the campuses of [Meta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_Platforms "Meta Platforms") and [SLAC.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SLAC_National_Accelerator_Laboratory "SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory")[[5]](#cite_note-5) They also have seven locations in Japan: five in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), including the [Shinjuku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shinjuku_Station "Shinjuku Station") train station, as well as one in [Kamakura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamakura "Kamakura") and a cafe/roastery in the [Kanagawa Prefecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanagawa_Prefecture "Kanagawa Prefecture"). Verve earned the highest score in the [coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee "Coffee") category at the [Good Food Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Food_Awards "Good Food Awards") in 2013[[6]](#cite_note-Sprudge-6) and was also named one of the top coffee roasters in the United States by [Thrillist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrillist "Thrillist"),[[7]](#cite_note-Thrillist-7) [Complex Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_Magazine "Complex Magazine"),[[8]](#cite_note-ComplexMag-8) and Food Republic [[9]](#cite_note-FoodRepublic-9) In 2018, they won the [Best Espresso at the Coffee Spot Awards](https://www.brian-coffee-spot.com/2018/12/29/2018-awards-best-espresso/), and in 2021 be nominated for the cafe in Japan at the [World Latitude Caffe Prize.](https://www.wl-c.org/honor-2021/en/verve-coffee-roasters-omotesando-tokyo-roppongi)

In 2024, Verve was selected as Macro Roaster of the Year by Roast Magazine, noting the company's innovations in sustainability, ethical growth, and positive employee culture.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

Verve Coffee Roasters is a specialty coffee company based out of Santa Cruz, CA. The company was founded in 2007 with the goal of sourcing the finest coffees in the world and sharing them with our community. Since opening, Verve has expanded to ten cafe locations between Santa Cruz, Los Angeles, the San Francisco Bay Area and Tokyo. We have a state-of-the-art roasting facility, and an incredible team of people that are supporting Verve's coffee program across the country.
We believe the coffee experience is our responsibility from seed to cup. Coffee is our craft, our ritual, our passion. It drives us and inspires us. With this simple truth and responsibility, we are bridging the gap from Farmlevel to Streetlevel.
We Are Verve. We custom craft the future of coffee.

hot. When I received the coffee, it was only around 4-5 ounces and, despite asking for it extra hot, it was barely warm--closer to cold than hot. Unfortunately, the taste was also extremely weak and watery, with very little coffee flavor. I was charged $5.50 for this. Considering the price, the very small portion, the temperature, and the quality, I found the experience unacceptable. Many other coffee shops in San Francisco offer a larger, properly prepared Americano at a lower price. There were other customers sitting nearby, so I chose not to make an issue of it at the time. However, I left feeling that I had simply wasted my money. I would not return, and I would strongly recommend that anyone considering visiting think twice before spending their money here. I am considering g all the reviews more than 2 stars as fake reviews.

**Onyx Coffee Lab** is an American specialty coffee roaster and café company based in [Rogers, Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers,_Arkansas "Rogers, Arkansas"). Founded in 2012 by Andrea Allen and Jon Allen, the company began in [Springdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springdale,_Arkansas "Springdale, Arkansas") and expanded into a specialty coffee business that includes roasting, retail cafés, wholesale, e-commerce, and coffee education.[[1]](#cite_note-TalkBiz2025-1) As of April 2026, the company's Northwest Arkansas footprint includes its Rogers headquarters and roastery, cafés in [Bentonville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bentonville,_Arkansas "Bentonville, Arkansas"), [Fayetteville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fayetteville,_Arkansas "Fayetteville, Arkansas"), and Springdale, a café at the Momentary in Bentonville, and the related Doyenne Café concept in Bentonville.[[2]](#cite_note-OnyxLocations-2)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Onyx_Coffee_Lab&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Andrea and Jon Allen founded Onyx Coffee Lab in 2012 in Springdale, Arkansas.[[3]](#cite_note-TalkBiz2023-3) Over the following decade, the company expanded from a local café business into a specialty coffee company with wholesale, online retail, and education operations.[[3]](#cite_note-TalkBiz2023-3)

In 2019, Onyx announced a move into a large headquarters space in downtown Rogers that combined a roastery, training lab, bakery, event space, offices, and green coffee storage.[[4]](#cite_note-TalkBiz2019-4) The move reflected the company's growth beyond a neighborhood coffee shop model into a vertically integrated specialty coffee business.[[4]](#cite_note-TalkBiz2019-4)

## Operations

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Onyx_Coffee_Lab&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Operations")]

Onyx Coffee Lab emphasizes traceability and transparency in coffee buying. According to the company, it publishes sourcing information for individual coffees, including pricing, scores, producer information, and related trade data.[[5]](#cite_note-OnyxStory-5) The company also states that it roasts and ships coffee daily from a facility powered in part by rooftop solar energy.[[5]](#cite_note-OnyxStory-5)

In addition to its retail cafés and online store, Onyx operates a wholesale division serving other hospitality businesses.[[2]](#cite_note-OnyxLocations-2) Its Rogers headquarters functions as both a production site and an education and training space.[[4]](#cite_note-TalkBiz2019-4)

## Cafés and related concepts

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Onyx_Coffee_Lab&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Cafés and related concepts")]

Onyx's cafés are concentrated in [Northwest Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Arkansas "Northwest Arkansas"). Publicly listed locations include Rogers HQ, a downtown Bentonville café, the Gregg Avenue and Fay Square cafés in Fayetteville, the café at the Momentary in Bentonville, and a Springdale café on Emma Avenue.[[2]](#cite_note-OnyxLocations-2)

In 2025, Onyx returned to Springdale with a three-story café and chocolate-focused concept in the former First Security Bank building on Emma Avenue.[[6]](#cite_note-Axios2025-6) The site also became the headquarters for *Terroir by Onyx*, the company's in-house chocolate brand.[[6]](#cite_note-Axios2025-6)

The company also operates or has operated related concepts such as **Doyenne**, a café and coffee program focused on coffees produced by women.[[2]](#cite_note-OnyxLocations-2)

## Competition and awards

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Onyx_Coffee_Lab&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Competition and awards")]

Onyx Coffee Lab gained national attention through barista competition. Andrea Allen won the 2020 U.S. Barista Championship.[[7]](#cite_note-BaristaMag2020-7)

In 2022, Morgan Eckroth won the U.S. Barista Championship and later finished as runner-up at the World Barista Championship, while Elika Liftee won the U.S. Brewers Cup and placed second at the World Brewers Cup.[[8]](#cite_note-ArkBiz2022-8) These placements further elevated the company's reputation within specialty coffee.[[8]](#cite_note-ArkBiz2022-8)

Onyx has also received recognition in roasting and product quality. Its public awards archive lists honors including the U.S. Roaster Championship, Good Food Awards, and recognition from Sprudge.[[5]](#cite_note-OnyxStory-5) One independently verifiable example is the company's 2021 Good Food Award for its Panama Lamastus Family coffee.[[5]](#cite_note-OnyxStory-5)

## Recognition

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Onyx_Coffee_Lab&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Recognition")]

In 2025, Onyx Coffee Lab became a [Certified B Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_B_Corporation "Certified B Corporation").[[9]](#cite_note-BCorp-9)

In 2026, Onyx Coffee Lab's Rogers location was named a finalist for the [James Beard Foundation Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Beard_Foundation_Award "James Beard Foundation Award") in the *Outstanding Bar* category.[[10]](#cite_note-JamesBeard2026-10) In the same year, *Food & Wine* reported that Onyx was ranked first on the *World's 100 Best Coffee Shops* list after placing second the year before.[[11]](#cite_note-11)

## Legacy

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Onyx_Coffee_Lab&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Onyx Coffee Lab has been associated with the growth of specialty coffee culture in Arkansas and the broader American South.[[3]](#cite_note-TalkBiz2023-3) Commentators have cited the company's competition success, sourcing transparency, design-driven retail identity, and combination of cafés, roasting, wholesale, and education as factors in its prominence within American specialty coffee.[[3]](#cite_note-TalkBiz2023-3)[[5]](#cite_note-OnyxStory-5)

# Onyx Coffee Lab Named 2026 James Beard Award Semifinalist, Breakthrough Moment for Specialty Coffee

PR Newswire

2 min read

*Recognition elevates specialty coffee to a national stage*

ROGERS, Ark., Jan. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- [Onyx Coffee Lab](https://onyxcoffeelab.com/?utm_source=mhpsi&utm_campaign=jamesbeard) has been named a semifinalist for the [**2026 James Beard Award**](https://www.jamesbeard.org/stories/james-beard-award-semifinalists-2026)[**®**](https://www.jamesbeard.org/stories/james-beard-award-semifinalists-2026)[**for Outstanding Bar**](https://www.jamesbeard.org/stories/james-beard-award-semifinalists-2026)**,** marking a milestone not only for the brand but for specialty coffee's growing presence in culinary landscape.

[![Onyx Coffee Lab](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///ywAAAAAAQABAAACAUwAOw==)](https://mma.prnewswire.com/media/2870219/Onyx.html)

Onyx Coffee Lab

 

The nomination places Onyx among select bars recognized by the **James Beard Foundation** — category historically dominated by cocktail and wine destinations. For specialty coffee, the recognition reflects a rare crossover moment, where craft, hospitality and culture meet on one of the food world's biggest stages.

"This nomination recognizes what specialty coffee has become," said Jon Allen, co-founder of Onyx Coffee Lab. "Coffee today is a culinary craft, a hospitality experience, and a cultural force. To see it acknowledged on this stage is a milestone not just for Onyx but for the industry."

Founded in Rogers, Arkansas, Onyx has built a global reputation for its uncompromising approach to sourcing, roasting and hospitality, most recently named one of the [Best Coffee Bars in America](https://theworlds100bestcoffeeshops.com/locales/onyx-coffee-lab/). The company is known for its transparent pricing model, producer partnerships, and cafés that prioritize design, service and education alongside exceptional coffee.

Andrea Allen, co-founder of Onyx Coffee Lab, said the nomination reflects a broader shift in how people experience coffee. "To see specialty coffee in the semifinals of the James Beard AwardsⓇ brings validation and legitimacy to what is not just a global industry but a craft that signifies the highest levels of excellence, execution, breadth of flavor, innovation and intentionality of service. We are thrilled and hope to see many coffee companies represented in the James Beard AwardsⓇ for years to come."

The nomination comes amid rising mainstream attention on specialty coffee, as consumers seek more thoughtful, experience-driven brands.

Finalists for 2026 will be announced later this spring, with winners revealed at the James Beard Restaurant and Chef Awards ceremony in Chicago.

**ABOUT ONYX COFFEE LAB**   
Headquartered in Rogers, Ark., [Onyx Coffee Lab](https://onyxcoffeelab.com/?srsltid=AfmBOopOPzRLIMEtf21DSFSmcJ25Q4iXwILLWZrhwUfA_zpSDdQmzsQV) is a globally recognized specialty coffee roaster and café operator known for its commitment to quality, transparency, and hospitality. Onyx is a Certified B Corporation and has received multiple international awards for excellence in coffee sourcing, roasting, and service. For more information, visit [onyxcoffeelab.com](https://onyxcoffeelab.com/) or follow @onyxcoffeelab on Instagram.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

International café chain and brand

| Starbucks Reserve |
| --- |
| Industry | Coffee |
| Founded | 2010; 16 years ago (2010) |
| [Parent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parent_company "Parent company") | [Starbucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starbucks "Starbucks") |
| Website | [www.starbucksreserve.com](https://www.starbucksreserve.com/) |

**Starbucks Reserve** is a program by the flagship international coffeehouse chain [Starbucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starbucks "Starbucks"). The program involves operation of worldwide roasteries; currently seven are in operation. Also part of the program are 28 coffee bars preparing Starbucks Reserve products, what Starbucks considers its rarest and best-quality coffees, usually [single-origin coffees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-origin_coffee "Single-origin coffee"). Some Starbucks Reserve coffee is also sold in about 1,500 of the chain's traditional outlets.

[![Map](https://maps.wikimedia.org/img/osm-intl,0,41.6,1.55,250x190.png?lang=en&domain=en.wikipedia.org&title=Starbucks_Reserve&revid=1366420931&groups=_0e8cbc615686f5cd26563b0b69c02afe496b154e&parser=parsoid)](/wiki/Special:Map/0/41.6/1.55/en)

Map of Starbucks Reserve roasteries

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starbucks_Reserve&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The program began as Starbucks desired to compete in the high-end coffee market, competing against premium coffee retailers like [Stumptown Coffee Roasters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stumptown_Coffee_Roasters "Stumptown Coffee Roasters"), Dillanos Coffee Roasters and [Blue Bottle Coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Bottle_Coffee "Blue Bottle Coffee").[[1]](#cite_note-NYT-1)

Starbucks began its Starbucks Reserve program in 2010 through online sales and a small number of its retail locations, selling small-batch arabica coffees. Later, the company opened its first Reserve location, a three-story store in Latin America, solely selling [Colombian coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_coffee "Colombian coffee"). The first Starbucks Reserve roastery opened in December 2014 in [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle").[[2]](#cite_note-Seattle-2)

## Types

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starbucks_Reserve&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Types")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/Starbucks_Reserve_Bar_%40_Pender_x_Granville_street_%2831392330957%29.jpg/250px-Starbucks_Reserve_Bar_%40_Pender_x_Granville_street_%2831392330957%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Starbucks_Reserve_Bar_@_Pender_x_Granville_street_(31392330957).jpg)

A Starbucks Reserve Bar in [Vancouver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver")

Starbucks Reserve includes three different types of locations: the "Starbucks Reserve Roastery", the "Reserve Bar", and the "Reserve Store". The roasteries, usually tens of thousands of square feet (thousands of square meters), are often described as a theme park experience, including coffee bars with tastings, cocktail bars, areas to observe the roasting and brewing processes, areas to purchase food, and local artwork throughout. The facilities also roast, package, and ship coffee to stores in their regions.[[3]](#cite_note-store_types-3)

The company currently operates a total of five roasteries, in [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai") (2017), [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan") (2018), [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") (2018), [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo") (2019), and [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago") (2019). The company initially planned to open at least 20 roasteries, though it announced in 2019 that it would be scaling back its plans, with Chicago being the last roastery to be built at the moment.[[4]](#cite_note-4)[[5]](#cite_note-5)

Reserve Bars are traditional Starbucks locations that sell some Starbucks Reserve products, supplied by a regional roastery. There are 43 locations, all of which include the regular Starbucks menu, and also have a coffee bar for a similar experience to the coffee bars in the roasteries.[[3]](#cite_note-store_types-3) There are currently approximately seven Reserve Stores in operation, located in New York, Mumbai, [Prague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague "Prague") and Shanghai; and the newest in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. These stores sell merchandise, food and drink such as Reserve Coffee, Princi food items, and locally-unique merchandise similar to that of the roasteries.[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8)

## Roasteries

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starbucks_Reserve&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Roasteries")]

### Seattle

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starbucks_Reserve&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Seattle")]

Main article: [Starbucks Reserve Roastery (Seattle)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starbucks_Reserve_Roastery_(Seattle) "Starbucks Reserve Roastery (Seattle)")

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Seattle_-_May_2024_-_15_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Seattle_-_May_2024_-_15_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Seattle_-_May_2024_-_15_(cropped).jpg)

Exterior of the Seattle roastery, 2024

The first Starbucks Reserve roastery opened in December 2014 in the [Capitol Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitol_Hill_(Seattle) "Capitol Hill (Seattle)") neighborhood of Seattle.[[2]](#cite_note-Seattle-2) It had 15,000 square feet (1,400 m2) and is rumored to have cost about $20 million. The roastery included a [split-flap display](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Split-flap_display "Split-flap display"), a departure board style common in 20th century railway stations. The board was created by [Solari di Udine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solari_di_Udine "Solari di Udine") and displays the coffees being roasted.[[1]](#cite_note-NYT-1) It was announced in 2025, the Seattle Reserve location will be closing.[[9]](#cite_note-9) The location closed in September 2025.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

### Shanghai

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starbucks_Reserve&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Shanghai")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/Starbucks_Reserve_Roastery.jpg/250px-Starbucks_Reserve_Roastery.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Starbucks_Reserve_Roastery.jpg)

Shanghai roastery

The roastery in Shanghai, China, is located in the [HKRI Taikoo Hui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HKRI_Taikoo_Hui "HKRI Taikoo Hui") [mixed-use development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed-use_development "Mixed-use development"), on the luxury shopping strip [Nanjing Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanjing_Road "Nanjing Road"). It opened in December 2017 and was the largest Starbucks location in the world at that time, since surpassed by the Chicago roastery. The Shanghai roastery has 30,000 square feet (2,800 m2) between two stories. It is typically fully packed with customers, with lines out the door typical in peak times.[[11]](#cite_note-Shanghai-11)

The Shanghai roastery has a roasting facility, three coffee bars, a Teavana tea bar, and an [augmented reality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augmented_reality "Augmented reality") feature designed by [Alibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alibaba_Group "Alibaba Group"): information about coffees and the roasting process viewable by opening the company's [Taobao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taobao "Taobao") app and pointing it in different places. The store also includes a marketplace, a wine and beer tasting area, a bar for scooping bags of beans to purchase, and places to sample different coffees throughout the store. Similar to other roasteries, a two-story bronze cask sits at the center of the store. The cask is decorated with 1,000 [traditional Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_Chinese "Traditional Chinese") stamps, hand-engraved, telling stories of the company and coffee. The cask weighs 40 short tons (36 t), and holds beans roasted in the facility, which are periodically dispersed through pipes around the facility for use. One of the roastery's coffee bars is 88 feet (27 m) long, the longest Starbucks coffee bar in existence. Similar to Seattle, the building also features an old-fashioned split-flap display board, showing which varieties are being roasted, and information about their flavors and origin. Many of the roastery's beans were grown in China's [Yunnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yunnan "Yunnan") province. The roastery also includes a Princi location, selling pizzas and [focaccia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focaccia "Focaccia"). A coffee library includes books on the history of coffee, brewing methods, coffee art, and the history of Starbucks. The Teavana bar is popular due to China's traditional tea culture; the bar has a wide variety of teas, brewing methods, and tea-based drinks.[[11]](#cite_note-Shanghai-11)

### Milan

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starbucks_Reserve&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Milan")]

Main article: [Starbucks Reserve Roastery (Milan)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starbucks_Reserve_Roastery_(Milan) "Starbucks Reserve Roastery (Milan)")

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Palazzo_Broggi_-_ora_sede_di_Starbuck%27s_Reserve_Roastery.jpg/250px-Palazzo_Broggi_-_ora_sede_di_Starbuck%27s_Reserve_Roastery.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Palazzo_Broggi_-_ora_sede_di_Starbuck's_Reserve_Roastery.jpg)

Milan roastery

The roastery in Milan is located in the [Palazzo Broggi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palazzo_Broggi "Palazzo Broggi"), formerly the city's stock exchange and main post office building. The building sits in the [Piazza Cordusio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_Cordusio "Piazza Cordusio"), a plaza in the center of the city. The roastery opened on September 7, 2018, becoming the first of any Starbucks in Italy, and the first and only roastery in Europe. It is the largest Starbucks in Europe, with 25,000 square feet (2,300 m2).[[12]](#cite_note-Milan-12)[[13]](#cite_note-Chicago-13)[[14]](#cite_note-Milan_design-14) The location was chosen as the city of Milan was where [Howard Schultz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Schultz "Howard Schultz") visited in 1983, inspiring him to add espresso drinks to Starbucks, develop cafés, and create the coffeehouse chain out of the single original location.[[14]](#cite_note-Milan_design-14)

### New York City

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starbucks_Reserve&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: New York City")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/Starbucks_Reserve_Roastery_-_New_York_City_%282022%29_2.jpg/250px-Starbucks_Reserve_Roastery_-_New_York_City_%282022%29_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Starbucks_Reserve_Roastery_-_New_York_City_(2022)_2.jpg)

New York City roastery

The New York location is in [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan")'s neighborhood of [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea,_Manhattan "Chelsea, Manhattan"); it opened on December 13, 2018.[[15]](#cite_note-15) It occupies the first floor of 61 [Ninth Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninth_Avenue_(Manhattan) "Ninth Avenue (Manhattan)"). The location has 23,000 square feet (2,100 m2), and includes a coffee roastery, two coffee bars, a cocktail bar, bakery, and a terrarium. The bakery, operated by Princi, has baked goods, pizzas, salads, and breads. The cocktail bar, a branded "Arriviamo Bar", has coffee- and tea-based cocktails. The interior ceiling has artistic squares and rectangles resembling the building's exterior architecture. The terrarium resembles Hacienda Alsacia, a coffee farm in [Costa Rica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costa_Rica "Costa Rica"), and the first and only farm owned by Starbucks.[[16]](#cite_note-NYC-16)

### Tokyo

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starbucks_Reserve&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Tokyo")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/Starbucks_Reserve_Roastery_Tokyo_-_Sep_09_2019.jpg/250px-Starbucks_Reserve_Roastery_Tokyo_-_Sep_09_2019.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Starbucks_Reserve_Roastery_Tokyo_-_Sep_09_2019.jpg)

Tokyo roastery

The Tokyo roastery opened in Tokyo's [Nakameguro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakameguro "Nakameguro") district on February 28, 2019. The roastery has about 32,000 square feet (3,000 m2), and was designed by [Kengo Kuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kengo_Kuma "Kengo Kuma") and built with [Japanese cedar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_cedar "Japanese cedar"). It is the only Reserve Roastery building purpose-built; the other roasteries repurposed existing buildings. The interior has four floors, each including decorative elements of Japanese culture. The first floor holds the main coffee bar, while the second floor holds a [Teavana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teavana "Teavana") tea bar offering 18 different teas and tea-based beverages. The third-floor cocktail bar, branded a "Arriviamo Bar", has coffee- and tea-infused cocktails, Japanese versions of classic cocktails, and nonalcoholic cocktails. The fourth floor has the "Amu Inspiration Lounge", an event space planned to be certified as a training location by the Specialty Coffee Association of Japan.[[17]](#cite_note-Tokyo-17)

Central to the space is a 56-foot-tall (17 m) copper cask, made of 121 copper plates hand-hammered in the Japanese tsuchime technique. The cask holds roasted coffee beans, allowing them to settle and gas to escape before brewing or packaging. Around the cask are 2,100 copper cherry blossoms suspended from the ceiling, an homage to the nearby [Meguro River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meguro_River "Meguro River"), popular for its numerous blossoming cherry trees. Extending from the cask are copper pipes that deliver coffee beans across different areas of the store. The facility has two roasters, a 260-pound (118 kg) Probat G-120 and a 35-pound (16 kg) Probat P25 roaster, able to roast up to 4,000 pounds (1,800 kg) of coffee each day. The coffee is used in the roastery and shipped to retailers throughout Japan.[[17]](#cite_note-Tokyo-17)

### Chicago

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starbucks_Reserve&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Chicago")]

Main article: [Starbucks Reserve Roastery (Chicago)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starbucks_Reserve_Roastery_(Chicago) "Starbucks Reserve Roastery (Chicago)")

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Chicago%2C_Illinois%2C_U.S._%282023%29_-_033.jpg/250px-Chicago%2C_Illinois%2C_U.S._%282023%29_-_033.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chicago,_Illinois,_U.S._(2023)_-_033.jpg)

Exterior of the Chicago roastery, 2023

The Chicago roastery, which opened November 15, 2019, is the largest Starbucks location in the world and latest roastery to be built. The building at 646 North Michigan Avenue on the [Magnificent Mile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnificent_Mile "Magnificent Mile") has five stories at 35,000 square feet (3,300 m2); it was formerly a flagship store for [Crate & Barrel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crate_&_Barrel "Crate & Barrel").[[18]](#cite_note-18)

## Reception

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starbucks_Reserve&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Reception")]

An article for *[Business Insider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_Insider "Business Insider")* described Starbucks Reserve as more expensive than regular locations, and more like an "[art studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_studio "Art studio")" than a cafe, due to the art work lining the walls.[[19]](#cite_note-BusinessInsider-19)

# Starbucks Roastery, Reserve & Reserve Kitchen

Calling all experience-makers, storytellers and hospitality enthusiasts to bring the bean-to-cup story vibrantly to life

[Search jobs](https://apply.starbucks.com/careers?query=reserve+roastery&start=0&pid=481078428338&sort_by=relevance)

![An individual standing at a coffee siphon, carefully stirring the contents with a long-handled spoon.](https://careers.starbucks.com/uploads/2024/04/RR_Hero_20230223_PA036_MilanRoasteryPhotoshoot_FY23_72.jpg)

## The Art of Craft & Coffee

Here, you’ll help bring the bean-to-cup story vibrantly to life at our locations in NYC and Chicago. Creating the flagship experience takes large teams, up to 250 people, of dynamic professionals who thrive in lively, passionate environments.

 

### Explore Roles

A Starbucks Reserve Roastery barista is an expert in their craft, eager to share knowledge of brewing methods, pairings, bean origins and more. If this sounds like you, and you have a strong passion for service and a desire to create unforgettable experiences, we’d love to hear from you.

Starbucks Reserve bartenders are master mixologists of liquid craft, honoring ingredients and process, with a spotlight on Starbucks Reserve coffee. If you’re passionate about engaging customer connections, storytelling and meticulous craft cocktailing, let’s talk.

Starbucks Reserve Kitchen teams use their knowledge and expertise to craft freshly baked pastries and food offerings with impeccable ingredients to inspire and delight customers. These are energetic enviorments for culinary ambassadors who want to deliver consistent quality in handcrafted pastries, cakes, focaccia-style pizza, artisanal baked breads and more.

Hospitality and hotel professionals – we’re looking at you. Inspire large teams (up to ~250 people) to create a world class customer experience in a fully immersive, theater-like experience. You’re a coach and a mentor, developing leaders that drive business performance and operational. All while enjoying Starbucks benefits and an emphasis on work life balance.

From preparing raw coffee beans to the mesmerizing roasting process, craft rare and exotic, micro-lot coffee that cannot be found anywhere else in the world. You’ll captivate our customers with the artistry of roasting in front of their eyes, with the opportunity to share knowledge in an experience they can only get in our roasteries.

### Melanie

Siren Retail Associate Manager

As a girl from Texas, my experience in the Empire State Building feels like a movie. Every day walking up and being able to see the lights shining above me is so magical. My favorite part of being here is meeting people from all over the world. Getting to know just a piece of their stories and getting to be a piece of their once in a lifetime trip is something that I look forward to everyday.

![Starbucks partner holds a trophy for regional Starbucks Barista Champion. She smiles at the camera.](https://careers.starbucks.com/uploads/2024/08/Trophy-470x630.jpg)

Our mission and values, our social impact, our emphasis on personal and professional growth – come see what makes working at Starbucks a different kind of job.

More than free coffee, our benefits are designed to support our health and mental health, our families, our financial lives and even our passions outside of work.

Cody Coffee Roaster, located in Cody, Wyoming, offers a variety of specialty coffees sourced from regions such as Nicaragua, Guatemala, and Ethiopia. Notable selections include the Ole Faithful Washed Nicaraguan Dark Roast, characterized by hints of brown sugar and cocoa, and the Bears Brew Espresso, a blend ideal for espresso drinks.

The business also features a Coffee of the Month subscription, providing customers with a curated selection of coffee delivered monthly. Emphasizing sustainability, many of their products support smallholder farms and women-owned coffee producers.
