Panera Bread coffee roaster locations.raw_content:
Panera Bread said Wednesday that it will be repurchasing Au Bon Pain.

The company did not disclose the terms of the acquisition of Au Bon Pain, which has about 300 locations. The deal is slated to close in the fourth quarter.

However, Panera CEO Ron Shaich is no stranger to Au Bon Pain, having merged his cookie store, the Cookie Jar, with the bakery in the 1980s, creating the Au Bon Pain Company. In the early '90s the company acquired the Saint Louis Bread Company, which would go on to be renamed Panera.  
 In 1991, the company went public, with Shaich on board as the CEO. However, seven years later, Shaich sold all of the Au Bon Pain divisions to focus on growing the Panera brand.  
"With the acquisition we are announcing today, we are bringing Au Bon Pain and Panera together again," Shaich said in a statement Wednesday. "This acquisition offers the strategic opportunity for us to grow in several new real estate channels."

The acquisition will allow Panera to grow its business in locations with a smaller footprint. Au Bon Pain has shops in transportation terminals, universities and hospitals that a traditional Panera restaurant would not fit into.  
 The purchase of the bakery comes just six months after Panera was purchased by JAB Holding for about $7.5 billion. Shaich said at the time that Panera had proven to be a successful public company, but that he would be able to do more as a private business.  
 JAB, a privately held company headquartered in Luxembourg, may not be a household name, but its brands are. The company owns Keurig Green Mountain and Krispy Kreme Doughnuts. Dunkin' Brands, a long-speculated target for JAB, recently saw shares jump amid renewed chatter. Its stock closed down 3.73 percent following the Au Bon Pain announcement.   
 Meanwhile, JAB has been selling off several of its luxury brands in order to focus on faster-growing consumer sectors and has been steadily creating a coffee and breakfast empire over the last five years.

# Panera Bread to reopen several locations across north Houston after going dark last summer

![Jovanna Aguilar](/_next/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fassets.communityimpact.com%2Fuploads%2Fauthors%2F219-b3bdc87ebc5c.jpg&w=1920&q=75)
![Panera Bread to reopen several locations across north Houston after going dark last summer](/_next/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fassets.communityimpact.com%2Fuploads%2Fimages%2F2026%2F04%2F30%2F422122.jpg&w=1920&q=75)

Per a July 9 [Hamra Enterprises](https://hamraenterprises.com/panera-bread-in-texas-reopening/) release, several locations have plans to reopen across the North Houston area after going dark since August 2025.

Stores reopening per the release include seven locations in Katy, Cy-Fair, Spring and Conroe and will begin with the Spring and Katy locations in July, CEO Mike Hamra told Fast Company in a statement.

**The details**

After abruptly shutting down several locations in the wake of a high-profile dispute last summer, per the release, new owners with Hamra Enterprises confirmed several Houston area re-openings.

“The Houston-area restaurants have been dark since August 2025, when their previous owner—ordered by a judge to stop using the Panera name—closed them down and sought Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection,” read the release.

Hamra Enterprises is a family-owned franchise that already owns dozens of Panera Bread locations across the Southeast.

**Also of note**

The Panera Bread restaurants are Hamra’s first in Texas and will mark the company’s expansion into its 12th state. It has been a Panera Bread franchisee since 1997, according to the release and includes 88 Panera cafés across eight states.

Hamra Enterprises also owns and operates Wendy’s, Noodles & Company, and Caribou Coffee restaurant locations.

Known for its freshly baked breads Panera Bread is a U.S. based company founded in 1987 and offers sandwiches, salads, soups, baked goods and breakfast items.

**_Opt Out of Sales and Sharing for Cross-Context Behavioral Advertising or Targeted Advertising_**

You may exercise the right to opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising or targeted advertising purposes by toggling “Targeting Cookies” to the left and clicking “Confirm My Choices” at the bottom. If you would like to opt out of the sales or sharing of personal data about you for cross-context behavioral advertising or target advertising purposes using other data about you, such as your email address, please submit a request by clicking [“Your Privacy Rights”](https://www.krispykreme.com/about/contact-us), emailing us at [ITCompliance@krispykreme.com](mailto:ITCompliance@krispykreme.com), or contacting us at 1-800-457-4779.

Additionally, to the extent required by applicable law, we will honor an opt-out preference signal recognized by Krispy Kreme, such as a Global Privacy Control signal, as a valid request to opt out of the sales or sharing of personal information for cross context behavioral advertising or targeted advertising purposes.

Krispy Kreme UK Ltd has been operating in the UK since its launch in Harrods in 2003. We are a retailer of premium, high quality doughnuts and coffee. Krispy Kreme UK currently operates over 120 locations and has a presence in over 1100 in-store cabinets with retail partners including Tesco, Morrisons, Costco and Center Parcs outlets across the country.
In 2018, we went across to the Emerald Isle in Ireland and opened our first Theatre store in Blanchardstown, Dublin, with further expansion into Northern Ireland in 2025 with the opening of Krispy Kreme Belfast.
Traditionally, Krispy Kremes are sold in dozens – a unique taste treat to be shared and enjoyed with your friends, colleagues or if you want, just you alone! In addition, all shops offer Krispy Kreme’s signature coffee, which is made from high-quality coffee beans roasted by Krispy Kreme to exact specifications.
We remain on a journey of offering a unique one of a kind doughnut so our customers everywhere can share the magic of a Krispy Kreme moment. We continue to achieve this by having talented, committed people who day in and day out ensure the highest possible standards. We believe our service experience is unique, especially when you couple it with our product.
We are so passionate about our Brand and world-class Product; we pride ourselves on being an exciting, hard-working, and fun place to be, and ensure everyone loves working at Krispy Kreme! and we are all totally committed to bringing Magical Moments to all our Customers!

**Krispy Kreme, Inc.** (previously **Krispy Kreme Doughnuts, Inc.**) is an American multinational [doughnut company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doughnut_shop "Doughnut shop") and [coffeehouse chain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffeehouse "Coffeehouse"). Krispy Kreme was founded by [Vernon Rudolph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_Rudolph "Vernon Rudolph") (1915–1973), who bought a yeast-raised recipe from a [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") chef, rented a building in 1937 in what is now historic [Old Salem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Salem "Old Salem") in [Winston-Salem, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston-Salem,_North_Carolina "Winston-Salem, North Carolina"), and began selling to local [grocery stores.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grocery_store "Grocery store")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-:0-4) Steady growth preceded an ambitious expansion as a [public company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_company "Public company") in the period 2000 to 2016, which ultimately proved unprofitable. In 2016, the company returned to private ownership under [JAB Holding Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JAB_Holding_Company "JAB Holding Company"), a private Luxembourg-based firm. In July 2021, Krispy Kreme became publicly traded again on the [Nasdaq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasdaq "Nasdaq").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-ibd-ipo-july2021-1) The brand name is a [deliberate non-standard spelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensational_spelling "Sensational spelling") of "crispy cream", for marketing effect.

## History

### Early years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krispy_Kreme&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early years")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Krispy_Kreme_logo.svg/250px-Krispy_Kreme_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Krispy_Kreme_logo.svg)

The original logo of Krispy Kreme Doughnuts. It is still used alternatively.

[![Image 12: Commemorating the original Krispy Kreme doughnut shop. Founded by Vernon Rudolph, July 13, 1937. 534 South Main Street, Winston-Salem, North Carolina. Dedicated July 2012.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Krispy_Kreme_Plaque%2C_Winston-Salem.jpg/250px-Krispy_Kreme_Plaque%2C_Winston-Salem.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Krispy_Kreme_Plaque,_Winston-Salem.jpg)

Plaque in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, that commemorates the first Krispy Kreme

In 1933, eighteen-year-old Vernon Rudolph, along with his brother Lewis Rudolph, began working for his uncle, Ishmael Armstrong, who owned a small general store in [Paducah, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paducah,_Kentucky "Paducah, Kentucky"), that sold a wide variety of goods, including its very popular doughnuts.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-Chronicle-5) While the exact origin of the doughnut recipe remains partially a mystery, it is believed that Ishmael Armstrong was inspired by an Ohio River barge cook named Joseph LeBeouf who was famous for his light and fluffy doughnuts, which contained [potatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potato_doughnut "Potato doughnut").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-:0-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-Chronicle-5)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f0/Krispyvan.jpg/250px-Krispyvan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Krispyvan.jpg)

Krispy Kreme delivery truck, c.1939

The store struggled during the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression"). In 1934, Vernon and Ishmael decided to move to the larger city of [Nashville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee "Nashville, Tennessee"), where they hoped business would be better. The uncle and nephew focused solely on selling their doughnuts and opened "The Krispy Kreme Doughnut Company" in a rented store on Gallatin Road.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-Chronicle-5) The shop did so well that Vernon's father, Plumie, also left Kentucky and moved to Nashville to help sell doughnuts. In 1937, Rudolph opened his own store, deciding on [Winston-Salem, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston-Salem,_North_Carolina "Winston-Salem, North Carolina"), for the location when he learned that his favorite cigarette company, [Camel Cigarettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camel_(cigarette) "Camel (cigarette)"), was headquartered in the small North Carolina city.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-Chronicle-5) Rudolph primarily sold to convenience stores; however, he also sold hot doughnuts to individual customers who came during production time between midnight and 4 a.m.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-Chronicle-5) The first store in North Carolina was located in a rented building at 534 South Main Street in Winston-Salem in what is now called historic [Old Salem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Salem "Old Salem"). The Krispy Kreme logo was designed by Benny Dinkins, a local architect. The first Krispy Kreme bakery outside the South opened in [Akron, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akron,_Ohio "Akron, Ohio"), in 1939.

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Krispy_Kreme_Corporate_Offices.JPG/250px-Krispy_Kreme_Corporate_Offices.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Krispy_Kreme_Corporate_Offices.JPG)

Reception desk at Krispy Kreme corporate offices

Expansion occurred in the 1950s, including an early store in [Savannah, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savannah,_Georgia "Savannah, Georgia"). By the 1960s, Krispy Kreme was known throughout the [Southeast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_United_States "Southeastern United States"), and it began to expand into other areas.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-6) In 1976, Krispy Kreme Doughnut Corporation became a wholly owned [subsidiary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subsidiary "Subsidiary") of [Beatrice Foods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Foods "Beatrice Foods") of [Chicago, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago,_Illinois "Chicago, Illinois"). The headquarters for Krispy Kreme remained in Winston-Salem. A group of [franchisees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franchising "Franchising") purchased the corporation back from Beatrice Foods in 1982.

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/A_modern_Krispy_Kreme_shop_in_the_Winston-Salem_area.jpg/250px-A_modern_Krispy_Kreme_shop_in_the_Winston-Salem_area.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:A_modern_Krispy_Kreme_shop_in_the_Winston-Salem_area.jpg)

A modern Krispy Kreme shop in [Clemmons, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clemmons,_North_Carolina "Clemmons, North Carolina")

Krispy Kreme began another phase of rapid expansion in the 1990s, opening stores outside the southeastern United States where most of their stores were located. In December 2001, Krispy Kreme opened its first store outside the US in [Mississauga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississauga "Mississauga"), [Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontario "Ontario"), Canada.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-7) The minimum investment amount to open a Krispy Kreme franchise ranges from approximately $450,000 to above $4M.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-8)

### IPO and accounting scandals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krispy_Kreme&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: IPO and accounting scandals")]

On April 5, 2000, the corporation went [public](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") on the [NASDAQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASDAQ "NASDAQ") at $21 using the [ticker symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ticker_symbol "Ticker symbol") KREM.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-9) On May 17, 2001, Krispy Kreme switched to the [New York Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Stock_Exchange "New York Stock Exchange"), with the ticker symbol KKD, which it carried until its private acquisition. The stock reached what would be its all-time high of $50 on the New York Stock Exchange in August 2003, a gain of 135% from its IPO price. For the fiscal year ending in February 2004, the company reported sales of $665.6 million and operating profits of $94.7 million from almost 400 stores (including international locations). The market initially considered the company as having "solid fundamentals, adding stores at a rapid clip and showing steadily increasing sales and earnings."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-cfo-10)

In May 2004, the company missed quarterly estimates for the first time and suffered its first loss as a public company. Chairman and CEO [Scott Livengood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Livengood "Scott Livengood") attributed the poor results to the [low-carbohydrate diet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-carbohydrate_diet "Low-carbohydrate diet") craze. This explanation was viewed with skepticism by analysts, as "blaming the [Atkins diet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atkins_diet "Atkins diet") for disappointing earnings carried a whiff of desperation",[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-cfo-10) and as rival doughnut chain, [Dunkin' Donuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunkin'_Donuts "Dunkin' Donuts"), has not suffered from the low-carb trend over the same compared period.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-businessweek-11)

By 2005, the company's stock had lost 75–80% of its value, amid earnings declines, as well as an [SEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Securities_and_Exchange_Commission "U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission") investigation over the company's alleged improper accounting practices.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-12) A turnaround plan in December 2005 aimed to close unprofitable stores in order to avoid bankruptcy.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-cfo-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-13)

Analysts suggested Livengood expanded too rapidly post-[IPO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering"), over-concentrating certain markets.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-businessweek-11) While this approach initially grew revenues and profits at the parent-company level, due to [royalty payments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royalty_payment "Royalty payment") from new franchisees, this reduced the profitability of individual franchisees in the long run as they were forced to compete with one another. For the 2003–04 fiscal year, while the parent enjoyed a 15% increase in second-quarter revenues, same-store sales increased only a tenth of a percent. Krispy Kreme also had supermarkets and gas stations carry their doughnuts, which soon contributed up to half of the chain's sales, creating further market saturation as well as increasing competition to its franchisees. All this expansion devalued Krispy Kreme brand's novelty by making the once-specialty doughnuts ubiquitous, particularly as the newer sales outlets required pre-made doughnuts as opposed to the ones made fresh in factory stores, which alienated brand devotees.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-cfo-10)

Besides royalty payments from new stores, the parent company also enjoyed significant profits by requiring franchisees to purchase mix and doughnut-making equipment from the parent's Krispy Kreme Manufacturing and Distribution (KKM&D) division. KKM&D earned $152.7 million in 2003, which made up 31% of sales, with a reported operating margin of 20% or higher, but these mark-ups were largely at the expense of its franchisees. By comparison, rival chain Dunkin' Donuts generally avoids selling equipment or materials to its franchisees which "keeps company and franchisee interests aligned", as well as having a royalty stream based on same-store sales.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-cfo-10)

Krispy Kreme has been accused of [channel stuffing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_stuffing "Channel stuffing") by franchisees, whose stores reportedly "received twice their regular shipments in the final weeks of a quarter so that headquarters could make its numbers".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-cfo-10) The company was also dogged by questionable transactions and self-dealing accusations over the buybacks of franchisees, including those operated by company insiders.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-businessweek-11) A report released in August 2005 singled out then-CEO Livengood and then-COO John W. Tate to blame for the accounting scandals, although it did not find that the executives committed intentional fraud.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-14)

On March 4, 2009, the SEC issued a cease and desist order against Krispy Kreme for its actions inflating their revenues and engaging in illicit activities regarding the purchasing of its own stores to prop up revenues and setting up mechanisms to guarantee that it beat earnings estimates by $0.01, which eventually resulted in Krispy Kreme reducing net income over two years by over $10.5 million. In it, the SEC proposed remedial actions for Krispy Kreme to take.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-15)

### Return to private ownership

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krispy_Kreme&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Return to private ownership")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Krispy_Kreme_donut_shop_NYC.jpg/250px-Krispy_Kreme_donut_shop_NYC.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Krispy_Kreme_donut_shop_NYC.jpg)

Krispy Kreme shop open in Times Square, 2026

In May 2016, [JAB Holding Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JAB_Holding_Company "JAB Holding Company"), a German investment firm, announced that it made an offer to purchase the company for $1.35 billion over the following two months that would make the company privately owned.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-16) The transaction closed on July 27, 2016. In December 2017, Krispy Kreme moved its corporate headquarters to [Charlotte, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte,_North_Carolina "Charlotte, North Carolina"); while Winston-Salem retained the majority of operational departments and the Krispy Kreme Support Center.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-South_End-17)

Also in 2010, Krispy Kreme Express, a delivery service for businesses, began testing at the Battleground Avenue location in [Greensboro, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greensboro,_North_Carolina "Greensboro, North Carolina").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-18) In the early 2010s, the company began developing shops with tunnel ovens, which allow for an all-day "Hot Now" hot doughnut experience.

On February 24, 2015, Krispy Kreme opened its 1,000th shop, in Kansas City, Kansas.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-19)

In 2018, Krispy Kreme acquired bakery chain [Insomnia Cookies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insomnia_Cookies "Insomnia Cookies") at a $175mm enterprise value, which continues to operate independently.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-investors.krispykreme.com-21) On August 25, 2020, the first Krispy Kreme vending machine was launched in North Carolina, featuring three-packs of doughnuts available 24 hours a day.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-22)

In 2022, Krispy Kreme began operating new sales models in a "hub and spoke" model to distribute donuts to more access points like convenience and grocery stores and [McDonald's restaurants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald's_restaurants "McDonald's restaurants").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-23) At the end of 2023 Krispy Kreme had reached 14,000 different points where its donuts are sold.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-24)

### Going public again

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krispy_Kreme&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Going public again")]

In May 2021, Krispy Kreme confidentially filed for an initial public offering to once again go public.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-ipo-may2021-25) The company went public again on the [Nasdaq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasdaq "Nasdaq") on July 1, 2021, under the name Krispy Kreme Inc.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-26)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-ibd-ipo-july2021-1)

On March 26, 2024, Krispy Kreme and McDonald's announced a partnership where Krispy Kreme doughnuts would be gradually rolled out to all McDonald's locations nationwide by the end of 2026. This followed a successful [test market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Test_market "Test market") experiment in [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky"). Markets such as [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh "Pittsburgh") and [Columbus, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus,_Ohio "Columbus, Ohio"), were selling Krispy Kreme products at McDonald's by the end of 2024.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-29) By June 2025, Krispy Kreme announced the McDonald's partnership would be terminated due to "unsustainable operating costs" and insufficient demand.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-30)

In 2024, Krispy Kreme sold a majority stake of Insomnia Cookies, to Verlinvest and Mistral Equity Partners, at a $350mm enterprise value.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-investors.krispykreme.com-21)

In October 2014, Krispy Kreme opened another store at Colombia in [Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogot%C3%A1 "Bogotá") and [Chía, Cundinamarca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%ADa,_Cundinamarca "Chía, Cundinamarca").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-investor.krispykreme.com-37) On December 12, 2013, Krispy Kreme opened its first store in [Taipei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taipei "Taipei"), Taiwan.

On May 18, 2015, Krispy Kreme announced it had signed a development agreement with KK Doughnuts SA (Pty) Ltd., to open 31 Krispy Kreme shops in South Africa over the following five years. This marked the company's first venture into Africa.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-38) On September 10, 2015, Krispy Kreme signed a development agreement with Agape Coral, SAC to open 24 shops over the next five years in Peru.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-39) On November 25, 2015, Krispy Kreme opened its first store in [Rosebank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosebank,_Gauteng "Rosebank, Gauteng"), [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), South Africa. On December 2, 2015, Krispy Kreme opened its largest store in the United Kingdom in [Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasgow "Glasgow"), Scotland.

On May 5, 2016, Krispy Kreme opened their first store in Bangladesh at [Banani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banani_Model_Town "Banani Model Town") in [Dhaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhaka "Dhaka") and quietly left the country around 2020. On July 27, 2016, Krispy Kreme was acquired by [JAB Beech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JAB_Holding_Company "JAB Holding Company"). Under the terms of the transaction, company shareholders received $21 per share in cash for each share they own. As a result of the completion of the acquisition, Krispy Kreme's common stock ceased trading on the [New York Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Stock_Exchange "New York Stock Exchange"). On November 5, 2016, Krispy Kreme opened its first store in [Kópavogur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B3pavogur "Kópavogur"), Iceland.

On January 12, 2017, Krispy Kreme opened its first store in [Panama City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_City "Panama City"), Panama.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-40)

On January 27, 2018, Krispy Kreme opened its first store in [Guatemala City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala_City "Guatemala City"), Guatemala. On February 28, 2018, Krispy Kreme opened its first store in [Manukau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manukau "Manukau"), Auckland, New Zealand.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-41) On March 10, 2018, Krispy Kreme opened its first store in Ikeja City Mall, [Lagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagos "Lagos"), Nigeria. On September 26, 2018, Krispy Kreme opened its first store in [Dublin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin "Dublin"), Ireland, which has since become the most profitable store worldwide.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-42)

On May 13, 2023, Krispy Kreme opened its first store in Costa Rica.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-43) It expanded to France in December 2023 with its first [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris") store, which was expected to make 45,000 doughnuts per day. The company's menu was tweaked to appeal to French customers, including a gingerbread flavored doughnut.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-44)

On August 9, 2024, Krispy Kreme opened its first store in Morocco.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-45)

On April 29, 2025, Krispy Kreme opened its first store in Brazil.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-46) By late 2025, Krispy Kreme operated four locations in Costa Rica.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-47)

On November 17, 2025, Krispy Kreme opened its first store in [Tashkent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tashkent "Tashkent"), Uzbekistan.

On June 29, 2026, the company announced an agreement with Apollo Group to bring Krispy Kreme to [Estonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estonia "Estonia"), with the country's first shop expected to open in late 2026.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-48)

## Products

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krispy_Kreme&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Products")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/Krispy_Kreme_Doughnuts_by_Japan_Line-Up_%28Tachikawa_LUMINE_Shop%29.jpg/250px-Krispy_Kreme_Doughnuts_by_Japan_Line-Up_%28Tachikawa_LUMINE_Shop%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Krispy_Kreme_Doughnuts_by_Japan_Line-Up_(Tachikawa_LUMINE_Shop).jpg)

An assortment of doughnuts on display in a shop in Tachikawa, Tokyo

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Krispy_Kreme_Doughnuts.JPG/250px-Krispy_Kreme_Doughnuts.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Krispy_Kreme_Doughnuts.JPG)

Krispy Kreme doughnuts

On February 19, 2007, Krispy Kreme began selling the Whole Wheat Glazed doughnut in an attempt to appeal to the health conscious. The doughnut has nearly the same number of calories as the original glazed doughnut (180 calories vs. 190 calories) but contains more fiber (2 grams vs. 0.5 grams). As of January 2008, the [trans fat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trans_fat "Trans fat") content of all Krispy Kreme doughnuts was reduced to 0.5 of a gram or less. The [U.S. Food and Drug Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_and_Drug_Administration "Food and Drug Administration"), in its guidelines, allows companies to round up to 1 g in its [nutrition facts label](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutrition_facts_label "Nutrition facts label") when the food contains as much as 0.5 of a gram per serving. Krispy Kreme benefited from this regulatory rule in its subsequent advertising campaign, touting its doughnuts as "trans fat-free" and having "0 grams trans fat!".[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-Reuters-49) On July 1, 2010, Krispy Kreme introduced a doughnut that included the [soft drink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_drink "Soft drink")[Cheerwine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheerwine "Cheerwine"), which was to be sold in grocery stores in [North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina") and [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina") during July.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-50) The doughnuts proved so popular that the [Salisbury, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salisbury,_North_Carolina "Salisbury, North Carolina"), Krispy Kreme location (the town where Cheerwine is made) sold them as well.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-51) After July 31, this was the only place to get them.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-52) The Cheerwine Kreme doughnut returned for July 2011 and made its debut in [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee") and [Roanoke, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roanoke,_Virginia "Roanoke, Virginia").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-53)

[Video 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/0/06/Krispy_Kreme_donuts_%28stabilized%29.ogv/Krispy_Kreme_donuts_%28stabilized%29.ogv.240p.vp9.webm)

Krispy Kreme doughnuts being prepared ([high quality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Krispy_Kreme_donuts_(stabilized).ogv "File:Krispy Kreme donuts (stabilized).ogv"))

On May 25, 2017, Krispy Kreme doughnut-flavored [Jelly Belly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jelly_Belly "Jelly Belly") jelly beans were announced.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-54)

On August 5, 2019, Krispy Kreme released two new [Reese's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reese's_Peanut_Butter_Cups "Reese's Peanut Butter Cups")-branded "chocolate lovers" and "peanut butter lovers" doughnuts to the public.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-55)

In July 2020, Krispy Kreme launched several candy-coated doughnuts with [Nerds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerds_(candy) "Nerds (candy)"), Jelly Belly jelly beans, sour gummies, and [marshmallows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshmallow "Marshmallow").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-56)

Krispy Kreme introduced a seasonal Pumpkin Spice Doughnut Collection in September 2020 with four flavors: 1) Pumpkin Spice Original Glazed Doughnut, 2) Pumpkin Spice Cake Doughnut, 3) Pumpkin Spice Original Filled Cheesecake Doughnut, and 4) Pumpkin Spice Cinnamon Roll Doughnut.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-57)

During [Veganuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veganuary "Veganuary") in January 2021, [Krispy Kreme UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme_UK "Krispy Kreme UK") launched its Original Glazed vegan doughnut.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-58) In December 2021, Krispy Kreme UK launched three more vegan doughnut flavors, Fudge Brownie Bliss, Caramel Choc Delight, and Apple Custard Crumble.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-59)

In 2024, the Dolly Southern Sweets Doughnuts Collection included four new flavors available for a limited time in restaurants and some grocery stores—Dolly Dazzler, Peachy Keen Cobbler, Banana Puddin' Pie and Chocolate Creme Pie. Inspired by [Dolly Parton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Parton "Dolly Parton"), the flavors were the company's first inspired by a celebrity.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-60)

## Promotions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krispy_Kreme&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Promotions")]

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/NASCAR_88_Earnhardt_Jr.%2C_Gordon_RIR-2_%2829507869642%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-NASCAR_88_Earnhardt_Jr.%2C_Gordon_RIR-2_%2829507869642%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NASCAR_88_Earnhardt_Jr.,_Gordon_RIR-2_(29507869642)_(cropped).jpg)

Krispy Kreme sponsorship on a NASCAR vehicle

Although based on informal advertising such as word-of-mouth, in 2006, Krispy Kreme moved into television and radio advertisements, beginning with its "Share the Love" campaign with heart-shaped doughnuts.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-61) Since 1955, the company has offered fundraising kits for organizations to sell boxes of doughnuts; Krispy Kreme would then split the proceeds with the organizations to raise funds for various causes.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-62)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

In 2014, Krispy Kreme released a $1,685 doughnut as part of fundraising efforts for [The Children's Trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Children's_Trust "The Children's Trust"). It was covered with 24-[karat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karat "Karat") gold and was decorated with edible diamonds. The inside was made from [Dom Pérignon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dom_P%C3%A9rignon "Dom Pérignon") champagne jelly.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-63)

In March 2021, Krispy Kreme announced that they were providing a free Original Glazed doughnut every day (except [Thanksgiving Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanksgiving_Day "Thanksgiving Day") and [Christmas Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_Day "Christmas Day")) for the rest of that year to customers in the US who could prove they have received a [COVID-19 vaccine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccine "COVID-19 vaccine").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-64) Multiple physicians criticized this move, with former Baltimore health commissioner [Leana Wen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leana_Wen "Leana Wen") tweeting that a person who ate a doughnut every day without making other lifestyle changes could gain 15 pounds by the end of the year.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-65) Others criticized the physicians: Elyse Resch, a nutrition therapist, wrote: "It's an oppression. Weight stigma, fat-shaming, [fatphobia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_stigma_of_obesity "Social stigma of obesity")—it's oppressive, like every other oppression in the world. And it's so wrong. We all deserve to have satisfaction in our eating, and having a doughnut is a delicious thing."[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-66) In response to the criticisms, Krispy Kreme said, "Like many sweet treats, Krispy Kreme Doughnuts are an occasional indulgence best enjoyed in moderation. And we know that's how most of our guests enjoy our doughnuts. We're certainly not asking people to get a free Original Glazed doughnut every day, we're just making it available through the end of the year, especially given that not every group is eligible to get vaccinated yet."

## Controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krispy_Kreme&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Controversies")]

### Krispy Kreme Klub Wednesday

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krispy_Kreme&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Krispy Kreme Klub Wednesday")]

In February 2015, a Krispy Kreme branch in [Kingston upon Hull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingston_upon_Hull "Kingston upon Hull"), England, announced during the [half-term break](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_term "Half term") of schools that it was launching, among other events that week, "Krispy Kreme Klub Wednesday", during which children could decorate doughnuts. However, it attracted controversy after it was promoted as "KKK Wednesday" on [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook"), due to it sharing an abbreviation with the [Ku Klux Klan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ku_Klux_Klan "Ku Klux Klan"), an American [white supremacist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_supremacist "White supremacist") group. Krispy Kreme promptly apologized, canceled the event, pulled all marketing relating to it, and launched an internal investigation.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-69)

### Cage-free eggs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krispy_Kreme&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Cage-free eggs")]

In 2016, Krispy Kreme committed to sourcing 100% cage-free eggs in the US by 2021, and globally by 2026.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-70) In 2024, the company stated it had achieved the goal of 100% cage-free egg use in U.S. operations, but commented that the supply constraints from [avian flu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avian_influenza "Avian influenza") drove them to review the commitment and timing of the global goal, stating intentions to set a new target once the supply chain stabilized.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krispy_Kreme#cite_note-71)

Tim Hortons' shares are soaring on the news that Burger King is in talks to buy the Canadian coffee chain.

Both companies' shares increased on the news. The move would create the third largest fast food company in the world.

Combined, the companies would be worth about $18 billion and have more than 18,000 restaurants in 100 countries.

Tim Hortons alone is worth about $8.4 billion. It's the largest coffee chain in Canada with 4,546 restaurants, including 866 in the U.S.

The chain boasts that it sells eight out of 10 cups of coffee in Canada, where it has 3,630 outlets. That's equal to about 36,000 locations in the U.S. on a per capita basis, which is double the number of McDonald's in the U.S., the New York Times writes.

The map below shows Horton's locations in the U.S. and Southern Canada.

Tim Hortons sold just one coffee blend until last week, when it added a dark roast. The company promises that all of its coffee is served within 20 minutes of being brewed, or it's thrown out.

The chain, once called Canada's "most treasured brand," also sells tea, smoothies, and food including donuts, made-to-order paninis, wraps and soups.

The company was founded by hockey legend Tim Horton. The first location opened in Ontario in 1964 and it made its U.S. debut 20 years later.

Wendy's bought Tim Hortons in 1995 when it had just 1,000 stores, then spun it off in 2006. During its decade of ownership, Wendy's opened a number of joint stores, like the one pictured below.

The chain's same-store sales grew 2.6% in Canada and 5.9% in the U.S. in the most recent quarter. Traffic has been declining for nine consecutive quarters in Canada, however, and it was flat in the U.S. last quarter, compared to the previous year.

Tim Hortons CEO Marc Caira blamed the traffic trends on a "new era of low growth, competitive intensity, evolving consumer demands and changing technology," in a recent earnings call.

The company is betting on menu innovation to keep driving sales growth and eventually attract new customers.

"We have identified some key trends we are seeing in the market, including changing demographics, increased emphasis on nutrition, health and wellness and a desire for bold flavors along with fresh quality ingredients," Caira said. "Menu innovation is also an important part of our strategy to grow [customers'] average check. We plan to introduce more value-added premium products, as well as appealing side dishes that will encourage our guests to purchase combos."

For decades, the chain was best known for its coffee and donuts. Now, the chain is putting more emphasis on its made-to-order sandwiches, like the Angus Steak Melt Panini below.

The breakfast menu includes sandwiches, paninis and bagels with a combination of eggs, cheese, bacon, sausage or turkey sausage. The chain also sells pastries and muffins.

Monmouth Coffee sources coffee beans from individual farms and roasts them in its roastery in Bermondsey. Its staff visit producers to find new suppliers, then the company signs long term contracts to secure its supply of high-quality coffee.

**Monmouth Coffee Company** is a coffee roaster, retailer and wholesaler in London, which was founded in 1978. It played an important role in regenerating [Neal's Yard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neal's_Yard "Neal's Yard") and [Borough Market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borough_Market "Borough Market"). It has remained focused on roasting and selling coffee beans and was one of the foundations for the [third wave of coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_wave_of_coffee "Third wave of coffee") in London after the year 2000.

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Monmouth_Coffee_Company&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Monmouth Coffee was founded in 1978 by [Nick Saunders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Saunders_(activist) "Nicholas Saunders (activist)") and Anita Le Roy. Le Roy later took over the business.[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3) Together with [Neal's Yard Dairy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neal's_Yard_Dairy "Neal's Yard Dairy") and Saunders' other businesses, Monmouth Coffee transformed the run down area around [Neal's Yard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neal's_Yard "Neal's Yard") in [Covent Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covent_Garden "Covent Garden"), [central London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_London "Central London").[[4]](#cite_note-Fort-4) The original shop is at 27 [Monmouth Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monmouth_Street "Monmouth Street") ([51°30′51.7″N 00°07′36.5″W﻿ / ﻿51.514361°N 0.126806°W﻿ / 51.514361; -0.126806﻿ (Covent Garden)](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Monmouth_Coffee_Company&params=51_30_51.7_N_00_07_36.5_W_&title=Covent+Garden)), a [grade II listed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Listed_building "Listed building") 18th-century terraced house.[[5]](#cite_note-5) The basement was used to roast coffee and the ground floor as a tasting room.[[6]](#cite_note-6) In its early years, the shop sold three or four kinds of green or roast coffee beans in sacks containing one, three, seven or ten pounds.[[7]](#cite_note-7) Le Roy wanted to buy coffee from individual farmers, but that was not possible until 1996, when a new coffee importer, Mercanta, opened. Monmouth Coffee was one of their early customers.[[8]](#cite_note-8) Monmouth Coffee and Mercanta were a foundation for the [third wave of artisan coffee shops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_wave_of_coffee "Third wave of coffee") in London after 2000 and several Monmouth Coffee baristas went on to found their own coffee businesses.[[9]](#cite_note-Wain-9)[[10]](#cite_note-10)

Monmouth Coffee has expanded gradually, while remaining focused on roasting and selling coffee beans.[[11]](#cite_note-Dowdy-11) A coffee stall was opened in [Borough Market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borough_Market "Borough Market") in 1999,[[12]](#cite_note-12) followed by a second shop in a former fruit and vegetable warehouse in the market ([51°30′19.8″N 00°05′29.1″W﻿ / ﻿51.505500°N 0.091417°W﻿ / 51.505500; -0.091417﻿ (Borough)](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Monmouth_Coffee_Company&params=51_30_19.8_N_00_05_29.1_W_&title=Borough)) in 2001.[[9]](#cite_note-Wain-9)[[13]](#cite_note-13)[[14]](#cite_note-Coles_2021-14): 95 Along with Brindisa and Neal's Yard Dairy, Monmouth Coffee played an important role in the revival of Borough as a retail food market.[[15]](#cite_note-Parham-15) In 2007 the roastery was moved to three railway arches in Maltby Street, [Bermondsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bermondsey "Bermondsey").[[14]](#cite_note-Coles_2021-14): 92 In 2009 an arch was opened to sell coffee on Saturdays and other local traders followed suit, forming [Maltby Street Market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maltby_Street_Market "Maltby Street Market").[[16]](#cite_note-16) In 2018 the company headquarters moved into five railway arches ([51°29′46″N 00°04′05″W﻿ / ﻿51.49611°N 0.06806°W﻿ / 51.49611; -0.06806﻿ (Bermondsey)](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Monmouth_Coffee_Company&params=51_29_46_N_00_04_05_W_&title=Bermondsey)[[Geographic coordinate system|Coordinates]]: {{#parsoid\u0000fragment:18}}[https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Monmouth\_Coffee\_Company¶ms=51\_29\_46\_N\_00\_04\_05\_W\_&title=Bermondsey 51°29′46″N 00°04′05″W﻿ / ﻿51.49611°N 0.06806°W﻿ / 51.49611; -0.06806﻿ (Bermondsey)][[Category:Pages using gadget WikiMiniAtlas]]"}}" id="mwaw" about="#mwt43" typeof="mw:Extension/indicator">) at [Spa Terminus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spa_Terminus "Spa Terminus") in Bermondsey,[[17]](#cite_note-17)[[11]](#cite_note-Dowdy-11) where Monmouth Coffee, Neal's Yard Dairy and a property company had taken a lease on a stretch of railway arches around the former [Spa Road railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spa_Road_railway_station "Spa Road railway station") to provide accommodation for food manufacturers and wholesalers.[[18]](#cite_note-18)

## Activities

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Monmouth_Coffee_Company&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Activities")]

Monmouth Coffee sources coffee beans from individual farms and roasts them in its roastery in Bermondsey. Its staff visit producers to find new suppliers, then the company signs long term contracts to secure its supply of high-quality coffee.[[19]](#cite_note-19)

It sells coffee beans direct via its website, and via its two retail shops, which also serve coffee to drink. The roastery also opens as a retail shop on Saturdays.[[11]](#cite_note-Dowdy-11)

## About Us

We source and roast coffee from single farms, estates and cooperatives. When we taste a coffee that we like, we want to know where it comes from and who grows, picks and processes it. We travel extensively throughout the year, visiting the producers and cooperatives with whom we currently work and looking for interesting cultivars of coffee and new farms from which to buy. During these visits we talk with farmers, learning more about the coffee they grow and process and the challenges that they face. We then look to establish a relationship with the grower and exporter of that coffee. We believe that where such a relationship exists, quality, quantity and price requirements can be discussed in an open and equal way. We see this as sustainable, fair and equal trade.

# Monmouth Coffee Company

Specialist coffee retailer and cafe

2 park st

## MONMOUTH WAS A TRUE PIONEER IN THE RECENT RENAISSANCE OF CAFE CULTURE

Among the first wave of specialist retailers to arrive at Borough Market in the late 1990s, Monmouth Coffee Company has gone on to become one of the most revered names in British coffee and a pioneer in the recent renaissance of cafe culture. The company imports a wide variety of single origin coffee beans from farms, estates and cooperatives around the coffee-growing world, which are then skilfully roasted in nearby Bermondsey. Coffee is available to buy as whole or ground beans, while the cafe serves single cone filter coffee and espresso-based drinks.

Single-use paper cups for takeaway coffees are no longer be available at Monmouth Coffee Company. Customers are encouraged to bring their own re-usable cups for takeaway beverages.

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Caf%C3%A9_de_Flore%2C_172_boulevard_Saint-Germain%2C_Paris_6e.jpg/250px-Caf%C3%A9_de_Flore%2C_172_boulevard_Saint-Germain%2C_Paris_6e.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Café_de_Flore,_172_boulevard_Saint-Germain,_Paris_6e.jpg)

A view of the Café de Flore in [Saint-Germain-des-Prés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Germain-des-Prés "Saint-Germain-des-Prés")

Thé **Café de Flore** (French pronunciation: [[kafe d(ə) flɔʁ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")) is one of the oldest [coffeehouses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffeehouse "Coffeehouse") in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), known for its emblematic shopfront and celebrated for its famous clientele, which in the past included influential writers, philosophers, and members of Parisian high society ([tout-Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tout-Paris "Tout-Paris")). The café is located in [Saint-Germain-des-Prés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Germain-des-Prés "Saint-Germain-des-Prés"), a historic quarter on the [left bank of the Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rive_Gauche "Rive Gauche"). It sits the corner of [Boulevard Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boulevard_Saint-Germain "Boulevard Saint-Germain") and Rue Saint-Benoît, in the [6th arrondissement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/6th_arrondissement_of_Paris "6th arrondissement of Paris").

The nearest underground station is [Saint-Germain-des-Prés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Germain-des-Prés_(Paris_Métro) "Saint-Germain-des-Prés (Paris Métro)"), served by [line 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Métro_Line_4 "Paris Métro Line 4") of [Paris Métro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Métro "Paris Métro"). While attracting numerous tourists due to its historic cachet,[[1]](#cite_note-1) the coffeehouse remains a popular hang-out spot for Parisians and celebrities alike.

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Caf%C3%A9_de_Flore&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Caf%C3%A9_de_Flore_-_1900.jpg/250px-Caf%C3%A9_de_Flore_-_1900.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Café_de_Flore_-_1900.jpg)

The Café de Flore, c. 1900

 [![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/6/6c/Le_flore_philippe_derome.jpg/250px-Le_flore_philippe_derome.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Le_flore_philippe_derome.jpg)

[Philippe Derome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Derome "Philippe Derome"), *Le Flore*, oil on canvas, 1974

The café appeared in the 1880s, during the [Third Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Third_Republic "French Third Republic"); however, the exact opening date remains unknown. The name is taken from a sculpture of [Flora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flora_(mythology) "Flora (mythology)"), the goddess of flowers and the season of spring in [Roman mythology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_mythology "Roman mythology"), located on the opposite side of the boulevard. Authors [Joris-Karl Huysmans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joris-Karl_Huysmans "Joris-Karl Huysmans") and [Remy de Gourmont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remy_de_Gourmont "Remy de Gourmont") were two of the first well-known regulars. In the late 19th century, [Charles Maurras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Maurras "Charles Maurras") wrote his book *Au signe de Flore* on the café's first floor, where in 1899 the *[Revue d'Action Française](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revue_d'Action_Française "Revue d'Action Française")* was also founded.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

The Café de Flore became a popular hub of famous writers and philosophers. [Georges Bataille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georges_Bataille "Georges Bataille"), [Robert Desnos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Desnos "Robert Desnos"), [Léon-Paul Fargue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Léon-Paul_Fargue "Léon-Paul Fargue"), [Raymond Queneau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Queneau "Raymond Queneau") were all regulars, as was [Pablo Picasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Picasso "Pablo Picasso").[[3]](#cite_note-3) [Chinese Premier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_of_the_People's_Republic_of_China "Premier of the People's Republic of China") [Zhou Enlai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhou_Enlai "Zhou Enlai") was known to be a frequent patron of Café de Flore during his years in France in the 1920s.[[4]](#cite_note-4) The classic [Art Deco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Deco "Art Deco") interior of all red seating, mahogany and mirrors has changed little since [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/080410_Caf%C3%A9_de_Flore_01.JPG/250px-080410_Caf%C3%A9_de_Flore_01.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:080410_Café_de_Flore_01.JPG)

Hot chocolate at the Café de Flore

Like its nearby rival, [Les Deux Magots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les_Deux_Magots "Les Deux Magots"), Café de Flore was frequented by numerous French intellectuals during the post-war years. In his essay "A Tale of Two Cafes" and his book *[Paris to the Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_to_the_Moon "Paris to the Moon")*, American writer [Adam Gopnik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Gopnik "Adam Gopnik") mused over the possible explanations of why the Flore had become, by the late 1990s, much more fashionable and popular than Les Deux Magots, despite the fact that the latter café was associated with [Jean-Paul Sartre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Paul_Sartre "Jean-Paul Sartre"), [Simone de Beauvoir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simone_de_Beauvoir "Simone de Beauvoir"), [Albert Camus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Camus "Albert Camus"), and other famous thinkers of the 1940s and 1950s.

A Romanian thinkers league also frequented the place, notably [Emil Cioran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Cioran "Emil Cioran"), [Eugene Ionesco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugene_Ionesco "Eugene Ionesco") and essayist [Benjamin Fondane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Fondane "Benjamin Fondane").[[5]](#cite_note-5)

The [Prix de Flore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prix_de_Flore "Prix de Flore"), a literary prize inaugurated by [Frédéric Beigbeder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frédéric_Beigbeder "Frédéric Beigbeder") in 1994, is awarded annually at the Café de Flore.

## In popular culture

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Caf%C3%A9_de_Flore&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: In popular culture")]

* [James Baldwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Baldwin "James Baldwin") wrote much of his 1953 classic "[Go Tell It On The Mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_Tell_It_on_the_Mountain_(novel) "Go Tell It on the Mountain (novel)")" while drinking cognac and coffee on the cafe's second floor.[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Designer [Yves Saint Laurent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yves_Saint_Laurent_(designer) "Yves Saint Laurent (designer)") named an ensemble in his bohemian-influenced Autumn 1960 [Dior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dior "Dior") collection "Café de Flore".[[7]](#cite_note-7)
* Café de Flore appeared in the 1963 film *[The Fire Within](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fire_Within "The Fire Within")*.
* The café is mentioned in the 1975 song "Et mon père" by [Nicolas Peyrac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Peyrac "Nicolas Peyrac").
* [Amanda Lear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Lear "Amanda Lear") filmed her music video "[Égal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Égal_(song) "Égal (song)")" in Café de Flore in 1981.
* The café was a setting and featured in the dust jacket of *[Ravelstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ravelstein "Ravelstein")*, written by [Saul Bellow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saul_Bellow "Saul Bellow").
* The café was featured in the 3rd episode ("Paris") of [series 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolutely_Fabulous_(series_4) "Absolutely Fabulous (series 4)") of *[Absolutely Fabulous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolutely_Fabulous "Absolutely Fabulous")* in 2001.
* The coffeehouse appeared in the lyrics of the 2002 song "L'Entarté" by [Renaud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaud "Renaud").
* It is the subject of *[Les Amants du Flore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les_Amants_du_Flore "Les Amants du Flore")* (2006), a film about [Jean-Paul Sartre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Paul_Sartre "Jean-Paul Sartre") and [Simone de Beauvoir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simone_de_Beauvoir "Simone de Beauvoir").
* Parts of the 2011 film *[Love Lasts Three Years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Lasts_Three_Years "Love Lasts Three Years")* were filmed in Café de Flore.
* Season 1, episode 6 of *[Emily in Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_in_Paris "Emily in Paris")* contains a scene filmed in Café de Flore.
* "Cafe de Flore", 2022 song by the Moldovan singer *[The Motans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Motans "The Motans")* which appears on the album "Great Expectations"

# Paris: Café de Flore

[blog](https://www.niksnacksonline.com/search/label/blog)   November 21, 2012

You can find cafes on every street in Paris (sometimes multiple right next door to one another). The cafe culture here is like none other in the world. Cafes have always been a gathering place for intellectuals to meet and debate, for artists to display their works and for writers to pen novels. Parisians and tourists alike sit outside smoking cigarettes, sipping coffee, people-watching and watching the world go by.  
   
 Café de Flore opened in 1887 at the corner of Boulevard Saint-Germain and Rue St. Benoit in the 6th Arrondissement.   

|  |
| --- |
| The only thing missing is a moped/scooter |

  
 One of the oldest and the most prestigious places in Paris, Café de Flore is known for its famous clientele and nowadays, people say its merely an overpriced tourist trap. Associated with Hemingway, Picasso, Sartre, Simone de Beauvoir, Camus and other famous artists and thinkers, they say little has changed about the decor since WWII.  
   
 I put the cafe on my MUST DO list. I pictured myself sitting outside on the sidewalk, legs crossed, oversized sunglasses on, sipping an espresso while people watching. Very chic. Very glamorous.  
   
 It *kinda* happened like that. After a few hours of shopping and walking the streets of Paris from [Saint-Sulpice](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Sulpice,_Paris), we exited the Swarovski store and I looked up and saw the cafe! I wasn't hungry or thirsty, but I was going to take an espresso at Café de Flore! I had to explain to my aunt the significance of this place and I wasn't doing a very good job. THEN--we ordered the chocolat chaud Viennoise for her and expresso for me.  

|  |
| --- |
| Un espresso e chocolat chaud Viennoise |

Then--I think she got it. Served in a traditional metal pitcher with a champagne glass full of freshly whipped cream this was the most delicious, smooth, unctuous hot chocolate we've ever had. The espresso was just espresso... but it came with wrapped sugar cubes. You can view the full menu [here](http://www.cafedeflore.fr/accueil/menu/menu/), but I wasn't here for food. You can get an *omelette* or *croque monsieur* anywhere.  
   

|  |
| --- |
| Awww sugar, doot doot doot doot doot-doot; Honey, honey... |

|  |
| --- |
| Hemingway sat here. And so must I. |

Inspired by my time here people watching and sipping on beverages, here is a recipe for hot chocolate. Use the highest quality chocolate available. And this doesn't mean Hershey's. Valhrona, Ghirardelli, Lindt or keep it local and in North Carolina--pick up some [Escazu](http://www.escazuchocolates.com/) or [French Broad](http://frenchbroadchocolates.com/shop/french-broad-chocolates) chocolate.  
   
 Hot Chocolate\*  
 Serves 2   
   
 2 cups milk  
 1/4 cup Dixie Crystals Extra Fine Granulated Sugar  
 3 oz. bittersweet chocolate, finely chopped  
 Fresh whipped cream for garnish  
   
 In a medium saucepan, combine the milk and sugar. Place over medium heat and whisk occasionally until the sugar is dissolved. Bring the mixture just to a boil. Remove the pan from the heat and whisk in the chopped chocolate. Transfer it to a blender or use a hand-held immersion blender and whirr for 1 minute. If using a traditional blender, be careful because hot liquids expand when blended. The finished mixture should be very smooth and frothy. Top with fresh whipped cream.  
   
 Serve immediately.  
   
 \*NOTE: Because I'm obsessed with creativity and amazing flavors, I like to add either 1T pink peppercorns OR 1T dried lavender during the boiling step for added flavor (and straining them out before I add the chopped chocolate) OR 2 tsp rose water before blending in the blender.

Flore Prize

**A brief history**

Le Prix de Flore fut fondé un jour de mai 1994, autour d’une des tables du Flore, dans le but de couronner un auteur au talent « prometteur ». Les critères de sélection étant l’originalité, la modernité, la jeunesse.

The Jury, chaired by Frédéric Beigebeder, is made up of Jacques Braunstein, Manuel Carcassonne, Carole Chrétiennot, Michèle Fitoussi, Jean-rené Van Der Plaetsen, François Reynaert, Jean-pierre Saccani, Bertrand de Saint-Vincent, Christophe Tison, Philippe Vandel, Arnaud Alive.

The jury is distinguished by its independence, its freedom, its insolence. It is in November that the Prize is awarded during an evening at the Café de Flore. Mr Miroslav Siljegovic, honorary president, presents the winner with a check for 6100 euros as well as a glass of Pouilly engraved in his name, to be consumed without moderation during a year at the Flore.

Joffrine Donnadieu

The Prix de Flore 2022 was awarded in the third round to Joffrine Donnadieu for her novel “Chienne et Louve” (Editions Gallimard) by 8 votes against 4 to “L’inconduite” by Emma Becker (Editions Albin Michel).

She succeeds Abel Quentin, and joins a demanding list of winners that includes Michel Houellebecq, Aurélien Bellanger, Tristan Garcia, Virginie Despentes, Christine Angot and Amélie Nothomb.

Founded in 1994 by Carole Chrétiennot and Frédéric Beigbeder, this prize has been awarded since its creation to an audacious young author with promising talent who receives a check for 6,150 euros and the right to drink Pouilly-fumé every day for one year in a glass engraved with his or her name. Françoise Sagan was the godmother of the first edition.

The Jury is composed of Frédéric Beigbeder, Jacques Braunstein, Manuel Carcassonne, Carole Chrétiennot, Michèle Fitoussi, François Reynaert, Jean-Pierre Saccani, Bertrand de Saint-Vincent, Christophe Tison, Philippe Vandel, Arnaud Viviant
