# REVIEW: Tatte Bakery & Cafe, A Boston Favorite in 2026

ByAmanda  Published   Last updated

[Tatte Bakery & Cafe](https://tattebakery.com/boston/) is one of the most popular bakeries in the [Boston](https://myvintagemap.com/24-hour-boston-itinerary/) metro area, with 16 locations in Boston, 4 in Cambridge, and 4 in Brookline. If you’re planning a trip to Boston, it’s highly likely you will stumble across Tatte at some point.

Hopefully this post will convince you that it’s worth stepping inside and ordering something special from their menu. You might fall in love with it just like I did!

## Why I love Tatte Bakery & Cafe

Here are some of the reasons why I return to Tatte over and over again:

### They have a lovely aesthetic.

I’m a sucker for pretty interiors, so I enjoy going to Tatte for the sheer aesthetic of the place. Their elegant tiling mixed with wooden furnishings and fancy lighting is so pleasing to the eye.

The vibe feels partly like a trendy [Parisian](https://myvintagemap.com/is-paris-stroller-friendly-exploring-the-city-with-a-toddler/) cafe and partly like a cozy, farm-to-table restaurant. Each Tatte location looks a bit different, too, which means it’s fun to try more than one!

### They have unique and delicious brunch options.

Of course, what really brings me back to Tatte over and over again is their menu. The first time I ever went to Tatte was for brunch.

I was immediately intrigued by the names and unique ingredients of their meal options—things like a Halloumi Sunny-side Breakfast Sandwich, Lamb Hash, and Prosciutto & Fig Panini.

Many of the dishes are inspired by the founder’s Israeli heritage, but there are influences from other cultures around the world as well, including Greek, North African, and Italian.

### They’ve got good coffee.

Most of the time, I go to Tatte to relax with a nice cup of coffee and something sweet. Their regular lattes and iced coffee are delicious, but if you’re looking to try something a little different, they also serve seasonal options such as a Turmeric & Honey Latte or a Beet Latte.

### And Not Surprising: They Have Amazing Sweets.

For dessert, you’ll have a large selection of items to choose from. There are delicious tarts, cakes, cookies, scones, croissants—you name it. There’s sure to be something to satisfy your sweet tooth!

## Know before you go

* Tatte gets very crowded, especially on the weekend. It’s not uncommon to see a line out the door, especially at the Beacon Hill location. To get the shortest wait time, you’ll be better off going on a weekday or in the afternoon on the weekend (after the brunch rush).
* You need to order your food at the front counter, even if you plan to sit at a table. They’ll give you a number to place on your table so the servers can bring your order to you (tips aren’t expected).
* Tables aren’t reserved and are available on a first come, first served basis.

## Want to order something from Tatte now?

[**Order pick-up**](https://tattebakery.com/online-ordering/)

[**Order delivery**](https://www.doordash.com/business/tatte-bakery-%26-cafe-6137/)

## What is Tatte Bakery & Cafe known for?

Tatte is well known in Boston for their amazing brunch, but they also are a local favorite for coffee and sweets. You really can’t go wrong!

## How do you pronounce “Tatte”?

It rhymes with “latte!” You’ll even see that phrase on their cups and employee t-shirts. 🙂

## What does “Tatte” mean?

Tatte is Yiddish for “daddy.” The founder of Tatte, Tzurit Or, [said she started the bakery with nostalgia](https://www.israel21c.org/the-israeli-behind-bostons-beloved-tatte-bakery-cafe/#:~:text=Speaking%20with%20ISRAEL21c%20from%20Boston,family%E2%80%9D%20from%20her%20Israeli%20childhood.) for the simple, delicious food she grew up with in Israel.

## Who founded Tatte?

Tatte was founded by Israeli-born and former film producer Tzurit Or in 2007. It all started with her baking 20 hours a day in her kitchen and selling her creations at Boston farmers’ markets. She eventually got her own brick and mortar store and the rest is history.

## Is Tatte Owned by Panera?

No, Tatte Bakery & Cafe is now owned by Panera founder and former CEO Ron Shaich, who sold Panera Bread several years ago.

Shaich is Managing Partner and Owner of Act III Holdings, a company that invests in restaurant businesses. He owns or invests in several other Boston-based restaurant chains, including Cava, Clover, and Life Alive.

# Tatte Bakery Review

Published  By [Julia](https://www.savorytooth.com/author/julia/) [Leave a Comment](https://www.savorytooth.com/tatte/#respond)This post may contain [affiliate links](https://www.savorytooth.com/privacy-policy/).

Tatte[1](#d86d23e6-b629-4cfc-9817-88f1c081f96e) is a popular bakery and cafe with over twenty locations in the greater Boston area. Known for baked goods and brunch plates, their menu is seasonal and has Israeli, Mediterranean, and European influences. This review is based primarily on their South Boston location.

## Tatte (South Boston)

**Overall Rating:** ★★★★★ out of 5 stars  
**Address:** 60 Old Colony Ave, Boston, MA 02127  
**Neighborhood:** South Boston  
**Perfect For:** Pastries and savory brunch plates in an inviting cafe atmosphere  
**Hours:** Mon – Sat 7am – 4pm, Sun 8am – 4pm  
**Reservations:** No  
**Parking:** Street  
**Links:** [Website](https://tattebakery.com/), [Menu](https://tattebakery.com/menus/)  
**Cost:** $20 per person (food only)

The entrance to Tatte’s South Boston location is bright and airy with high ceilings. Ordering takes place at the counter, and all seating is first-come, first serve. As is the case with many of Tatte’s locations, there is never enough seating and it can be hard to secure a free table. Note that Tatte is walk-in only and does not accept reservations. To skip the lines, you can [place an online order](https://order.tattebakery.com/) for pickup.

Tatte’s South Boston location is unusual in that you can watch their cooks making pastries alongside machines efficiently flattening out dough and then rolling it up. I picked a high top seat that had a great view of the pastry production area.

Ready-to-eat pastries are on display near the ordering counter, showcasing their freshly prepared cakes, pies, croissants, buns, biscuits, scones, muffins, tarts, and cookies.

Their brunch menu has a number of offerings, such as tartines, quiche, soup, shakshuka, and egg sandwiches, and is similar to their all-day menu. I ordered the lamb hash, Greek style pancakes, and morning buns.

I’ve had their lamb hash a handful of times now at various locations. This dish features lamb cooked in warm spices alongside sweet potatoes, carrots, and pickled red cabbage. It’s topped with a poached egg and green dressing, and paired with fresh tomatoes and challah. I enjoy this dish every time and I love the depth and combination of rich savory flavors going on here. The execution is mostly consistent; most recently my challah bread was disappointingly hard and dry, when in the past it has had a soft pillowy interior.

The Greek style pancakes were good, but nothing extraordinary. They were standard pancakes, thick and fluffy, topped with sesame seeds and served with Greek yogurt and pear jam.

The morning buns were delicious. They have a dry and flaky exterior and top, and the bottom has a sweet and sticky coating. I’ve also had other baked goods from Tatte in the past that were quite good, such as their linzer cookies, gingerbread tile, and brownies.

Service at Tatte is average. Across different locations, the workers at the ordering counter are consistently indifferent, neither friendly nor hostile. Food is delivered relatively promptly, and empty plates and trash are efficiently cleared off tables by the staff.

Overall, I enjoy going to Tatte for my favorite menu items and I like knowing that I am getting a consistent experience no matter which location I am at. I’m interested in trying some new dishes, too — in particular, I’ve heard that their shakshuka is phenomenal. Shakshuka is one of my favorite breakfast dishes, and I usually follow [this recipe](https://www.savorytooth.com/spinach-shakshuka/) for my homemade version.

---

1. The word *tatte* is a Hebrew nickname for *grandmother* and its pronunciation rhymes with *latte* [↩︎](#d86d23e6-b629-4cfc-9817-88f1c081f96e-link)

American restaurant chain

**Tatte Bakery & Café** is an American-Mediterranean gourmet [fast-casual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_casual_restaurant "Fast casual restaurant") bakery and café founded by Israeli-born [Tzurit Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tzurit_Or "Tzurit Or"). Tatte operates 54 locations, with half in the [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") area, and the remainder in the [metro D.C. region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_metropolitan_area "Washington metropolitan area") and [New York Tri-State area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_metropolitan_area "New York metropolitan area").[[1]](#cite_note-1)[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Tatte_Bakery_%26_Caf%C3%A9&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[Tzurit Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tzurit_Or "Tzurit Or"), a former film producer who immigrated from Israel to the United States in 2003, began baking family recipes in her kitchen, first selling them in 2007 at the [Copley Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copley_Square "Copley Square") Farmer's Market in [Boston, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston").[[4]](#cite_note-JI-4) She baked for 20 hours a day to keep up with the demand.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

After one summer at the farmer's market, in May 2008, she opened her first [brick and mortar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brick_and_mortar "Brick and mortar") storefront, Tatte Fine Cookies & Cakes, in the town of [Brookline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brookline,_Massachusetts "Brookline, Massachusetts").[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-:1-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8) In the coming years, Or began expanding into the greater Boston area. She expanded into the [Kendall Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendall_Square "Kendall Square") neighborhood of [Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge,_Massachusetts "Cambridge, Massachusetts") in 2012, opening three locations in Cambridge within two years.[[7]](#cite_note-:1-7)[[9]](#cite_note-9) Or's fifth storefront opened in 2015 on [Beacon Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beacon_Hill,_Boston "Beacon Hill, Boston")'s historic [Charles Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Street_(Boston) "Charles Street (Boston)"), the first Tatte location in Boston proper.[[10]](#cite_note-10) After opening a spacious [Harvard Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Square "Harvard Square") location in 2016, Or began ramping up expansion in the Boston area.[[11]](#cite_note-11) Tatte expanded into [downtown Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Boston "Downtown Boston") in 2019 with its [Summer Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Street_(Boston) "Summer Street (Boston)") location, followed by a location at [One Boston Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Boston_Place "One Boston Place").[[12]](#cite_note-12)

[Ron Shaich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Shaich "Ron Shaich"), who then became CEO of [Panera Bread](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panera_Bread "Panera Bread"), purchased over 50% ownership of Tatte in 2016.[[13]](#cite_note-13) After Shaich parted ways with Panera, he bought Panera's stake in Tatte and continues to be a lead investor.[[14]](#cite_note-14)[[15]](#cite_note-15) Despite Shaich's majority stake, Tatte continues to operate as an independent company.[[16]](#cite_note-16) Or stepped down as CEO in July 2020 following discrimination complaints.[[17]](#cite_note-AP_step_down-17)[[18]](#cite_note-JPost_step_down-18)

Tatte opened its first Washington, D.C. bakery in August 2020, located in the [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_(Washington,_D.C.) "West End (Washington, D.C.)") neighborhood,[[19]](#cite_note-19) subsequently expanding into [U Street/Cardozo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U_Street_(Washington,_D.C.) "U Street (Washington, D.C.)") and [Dupont Circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dupont_Circle "Dupont Circle"),[[20]](#cite_note-20) then into D.C. suburbs [Bethesda, Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethesda,_Maryland "Bethesda, Maryland") and [Arlington, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington_County,_Virginia "Arlington County, Virginia").[[21]](#cite_note-21)

In 2025, Tatte announced the opening of many locations across the New York Tri-State area. Locations in New York and New Jersey opened in late 2025 and early 2026, and a location in Connecticut is slated to open at the end of 2026.[[22]](#cite_note-22)[[23]](#cite_note-23)

## Food

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Tatte_Bakery_%26_Caf%C3%A9&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Food")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/Tatte_Chickpea_and_fava_plate.jpg/250px-Tatte_Chickpea_and_fava_plate.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tatte_Chickpea_and_fava_plate.jpg)

Tatte's chickpea and fava plate.

Tatte offers a variety of pastries, as well as breakfast dishes, sandwiches, salads, soups, and their signature [Shakshuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakshouka "Shakshouka"). [[24]](#cite_note-24)

## Name

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Tatte_Bakery_%26_Caf%C3%A9&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Name")]

Or's daughter inspired the business' name. Although Tatte means "daddy" in [Yiddish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yiddish "Yiddish"), young Hebrew speakers often say "tatte" in place of the Hebrew word for grandmother, "savta." While Or was working on her farmer's market stand logo, her young daughter said "tatte" out loud when looking at a photo of her grandmother, which led Or to name her farmer's market stand "Tatte."[[4]](#cite_note-JI-4)

## Current locations

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Tatte_Bakery_%26_Caf%C3%A9&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Current locations")]

* [![Tatte location in Dupont Circle, Washington, D.C.](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/68/Tatte_Dupont_Circle.jpg/120px-Tatte_Dupont_Circle.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tatte_Dupont_Circle.jpg "Tatte location in Dupont Circle, Washington, D.C.")

  Tatte location in [Dupont Circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dupont_Circle "Dupont Circle"), Washington, D.C.
* [![Tatte in Boston, Ink Block](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Tatte_Ink_Block_Boston.png/120px-Tatte_Ink_Block_Boston.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tatte_Ink_Block_Boston.png "Tatte in Boston, Ink Block")

  Tatte in Boston, Ink Block

Tatte's 28 Boston area stores are located in [Arlington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington,_Massachusetts "Arlington, Massachusetts"), [Belmont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belmont,_Massachusetts "Belmont, Massachusetts"), [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston"), [Brookline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brookline,_Massachusetts "Brookline, Massachusetts"), [Burlington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burlington,_Massachusetts "Burlington, Massachusetts"), [Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge,_Massachusetts "Cambridge, Massachusetts"), [Hingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hingham,_Massachusetts "Hingham, Massachusetts"), [Lexington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexington,_Massachusetts "Lexington, Massachusetts"), [Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton,_Massachusetts "Newton, Massachusetts"), [Somerville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somerville,_Massachusetts "Somerville, Massachusetts"), and [Wellesley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellesley,_Massachusetts "Wellesley, Massachusetts").[[25]](#cite_note-25) Tatte also has locations on the campuses of three universities in the city of Boston: [Berklee College of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berklee_College_of_Music "Berklee College of Music"), [Emerson College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emerson_College "Emerson College"), and [Northeastern University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northeastern_University "Northeastern University").[[26]](#cite_note-26)[[27]](#cite_note-27)[[28]](#cite_note-28)

Tatte's Washington, D.C. area stores include locations in [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_(Washington,_D.C.) "West End (Washington, D.C.)"), [Dupont Circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dupont_Circle "Dupont Circle"), and [Foggy Bottom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foggy_Bottom "Foggy Bottom"), as well as [Bethesda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethesda,_Maryland "Bethesda, Maryland") and [Arlington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington_County,_Virginia "Arlington County, Virginia").[[29]](#cite_note-:2-29) As of September 2024[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tatte_Bakery_%26_Caf%C3%A9&action=edit), Tatte has 21 locations in Washington, D.C. and nearby suburbs.[[29]](#cite_note-:2-29)

Tatte's New York Metropolitan area locations include [Gramercy Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gramercy_Park "Gramercy Park"), [Garden City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_City,_New_York "Garden City, New York"), [Paramus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramus,_New_Jersey "Paramus, New Jersey"), [Morristown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morristown,_New_Jersey "Morristown, New Jersey"), [Ridgewood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ridgewood,_New_Jersey "Ridgewood, New Jersey"), and an upcoming location in [Darien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darien,_Connecticut "Darien, Connecticut").[[29]](#cite_note-:2-29)[[30]](#cite_note-30)

# [John Tanner's Barbecue Blog](https://johntannersbbqblog.wordpress.com/)

## One man's search for a rich, full life — mainly barbecue.

[![](https://johntannersbbqblog.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/cropped-john-tanners-bbq-blog.png)](https://johntannersbbqblog.wordpress.com/)

# Tatte Bakery & Café, Various Locations

This summer our church, Georgetown Presbyterian, where Nancy and I were married in August 1975, has a “pick-up” Sunday choir, and Nancy has participated in these as well as other choruses from here to China and New Zealand. They rehearse at 8:45 Sunday morning, and I drove Nancy down this last Sunday. That left me with a lot of time before the service, so I went around the corner to [Tatte Bakery and Café](https://tattebakery.com) at 1545 Wisconsin Avenue in Georgetown.

Tatte was the child of Tzuric Or, an Israeli native who started selling baked goods at a farmers market in Boston in 2007. The next thing you know, Tatte branches blanketed the Boston area, and in 2020 Tatte invaded Washington. As of this writing, their website lists 46 [locations](https://tattebakery.com/locations) (click on “all locations” and go from there) in DC, Maryland, Virginia, New Jersey, and, of course, Massachusetts. This particular location is a former bank with a very high ceiling, white walls, and a patterned tile floor. As you enter you’re staring down the barrels of some delicious looking muffins, croissants, and other breads and pastries. I can report from previous visits that you’ll love any you choose.

I preferred not to look at the pastries lest I turn to stone, or perhaps a pillar of salt. A couple of pilasters and the coffered ceiling soften the lines visually as, I suppose, do the large HVAC pipes, but the hard surfaces portend a lot of noise when the place is full. But it was fine when I was there and it was merely busy. There’s also some outside seating in the bank’s former parking lot.

You order with one of three cashiers at the counter, pay, get a numbered “flag,” and pick a table.

The order comes pretty quickly. I’d looked over the very extensive menu and initially thought of shakshuka, but remembering that I was wearing a seersucker suit, a white shirt, and a tie, three elements with a magnetic attraction for tomato stains, I reconsidered. Then I noted that several new additions featured corn and spinach. I can take a hint, and chose the Cilbir ($10.95).

It’s a Turkish dish with a base of labneh (basically Greek yoghurt strained an even longer time, to make it thicker and creamier) with, in this case, corn and spinach and a poached egg graced with a relish and oil infused with Aleppo pepper.

It was delicious, with lots of contrasting and complementing flavors. The oh, so rich and creamy labneh was tart, cool, and had been dosed with garlic. The corn was just off the cob fresh and in fact, still raw. I actually prefer top quality corn raw for its flavor and wonderful juiciness, and here each and every kernel added a light crunchiness and a burst of flavor. The spinach had been sautéed and added its own texture, slight astringency, color, and flavor. The poached egg was nice and runny and spread its goodness when broken. Finally, I’m not sure what was in that relish, but it was tart, bright, and with the Aleppo pepper, gently hot. All of that within that creamy labneh!

That sourdough toast came unbuttered. The sourdough element was hard to discern, but the bread was chewy and I enjoyed some cirbil on the bread, but mainly sopped up every bit with the bread. I also had a cup of drip coffee, black, and it tasted good.

I left with my clothes unstained, and some compliments on my seersucker suit, which shines like a good deed in a charcoal gray city. More important, I left well satisfied by my meal, and confident that you’ll enjoy the quality of the food at the Tatte near you. If there isn’t one now, there probably will be one soon. When you see one, try it.

**UPDATE**: Our Special Consultant, Liz Claire Boyd, recently tried Tatte’s almond croissant.

Here assessment was marked by “a deep sigh of satisfaction.”

\*\*\*

And while you’re at it, click “**follow**” on our front page to receive blog posts in your email box. Or bookmark us and check in from time to time. We’re on **Instagram**  (**johntannerbbq**) and **X/Twitter** (**johntannerbbq1).** If you’re planning a trip, you can “**Search**” the name of the destination city, state, or country for good restaurants (in Europe, often close to sites, like the [Louvre](https://johntannersbbqblog.wordpress.com/2019/06/25/where-to-eat-near-the-louvre-le-fumoir/), [Prague Castle](https://johntannersbbqblog.wordpress.com/2023/08/17/kuchyn-prague-castle-district-prague-czech-republic/), [Vienna’s Old City](https://johntannersbbqblog.wordpress.com/2023/08/23/gosser-bierklinik-vienna-austria/), or the [Van Gogh Museum](https://johntannersbbqblog.wordpress.com/2016/05/09/where-to-eat-in-amsterdam-besides-pendergast/), that you’ll want to visit in any event.  We welcome comments and questions, and eagerly seek suggestions of places to eat and stories to cover.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

International chain of bakery-restaurants

Le Pain Quotidien

| Le Pain Quotidien, [Chelsea, London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea,_London "Chelsea, London") |
| Founded | 26 October 1990; 35 years ago (26 October 1990) |
| Founder | [Alain Coumont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Coumont "Alain Coumont") |
| Headquarters | [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") (U.S. division) |
| Website | [www.lepainquotidien.com](https://www.lepainquotidien.com) |

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/The_interior_of_a_Le_Pain_Quotidien_bakery-restaurant_in_Washington%2C_D.C.jpg/250px-The_interior_of_a_Le_Pain_Quotidien_bakery-restaurant_in_Washington%2C_D.C.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_interior_of_a_Le_Pain_Quotidien_bakery-restaurant_in_Washington,_D.C.jpg)

The interior of a Le Pain Quotidien in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")

 [![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Le_Pain_Quotidien%2C_Bryant_Park.jpg/250px-Le_Pain_Quotidien%2C_Bryant_Park.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Le_Pain_Quotidien,_Bryant_Park.jpg)

A Le Pain Quotidien in [Bryant Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryant_Park "Bryant Park"), New York City

**Le Pain Quotidien** (French for *the daily bread*) [listen](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/1/11/Pronunciation_for_Le_Pain_Quotidien.ogg/Pronunciation_for_Le_Pain_Quotidien.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](/wiki/File:Pronunciation_for_Le_Pain_Quotidien.ogg "File:Pronunciation for Le Pain Quotidien.ogg") is an international chain of bakery-restaurants.[[1]](#cite_note-1) It sells baked goods, bread, salads, sandwiches, beverages, and [tartines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_sandwich "Open sandwich").[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Le Pain Quotidien operates more than 260 bakery-restaurant locations worldwide in 20 countries, including Argentina, Uruguay, Belgium, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, France, India, Switzerland, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, Colombia, Turkey, Spain, United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Qatar, Russia, Japan, and the United States. The US, UK, Belgium and Paris restaurants are fully company-owned and operated, while all other international branches are franchises.

A common theme in all Le Pain Quotidien locations is a long, wooden "communal table".

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Le_Pain_Quotidien&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/aa/The_first_LPQ.jpg/250px-The_first_LPQ.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_first_LPQ.jpg)

The first Le Pain Quotidien - Rue Dansaert, Brussels

Founder Alain Coumont opened Le Pain Quotidien on 26 October 1990 at 16 rue Dansaert in [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels").[[3]](#cite_note-3) As a young chef, Coumont was dissatisfied with the quality of bread available in Brussels, so he began making his own, mixing flour, water and salt into the familiar loaves of his childhood. He furnished the store with cabinets scoured from antique stores and a large table made of wood reclaimed from the floors of retired Belgian trains purchased at a local flea market: the first of Le Pain Quotidien's communal tables.[[4]](#cite_note-4)[[5]](#cite_note-5)

The first location in the United States opened on [Madison Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Avenue "Madison Avenue") in New York City in 1997.[[6]](#cite_note-6)

By 2005, the founder was receiving 50 emails per day from people wanting to secure a franchise.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

In 2011, the company had a [public relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_relations "Public relations") incident when a customer in New York City found a mouse in her salad.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

In 2016, Doug Satzman became CEO of the U.S. operations and Vincent Herbert became global CEO.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

In March 2018, Vincent Herbert resigned.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

In December 2019, Cobepa, majority owned by [Spoelberch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spoelberch "Spoelberch"), increased its stake in the company from 32% to 43% and the French group Norac Foods sold its 25% interest.[[11]](#cite_note-11)

In May 2020, the parent company filed for insolvency in Belgium and the United States division filed for [Chapter 11 bankruptcy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapter_11_bankruptcy "Chapter 11 bankruptcy") protection.[[12]](#cite_note-12) The same month the parent company signed a deal agreement with the New York-based Aurify Brands which would provide a bridge financing of $522,000 to continue the operations and ultimately acquiring all U.S. units for $3 million. Aurify Brands planned to reopen at least 35 units and to create 1,000 jobs.[[13]](#cite_note-13)

In July 2023, the company collapsed into administration in the United Kingdom and shuttered all but one of its locations in the UK.[[14]](#cite_note-14) By 2024, all locations in Hong Kong has also closed permanently.

The worldwide turnover for Le Pain Quotidien is 270 MEUR for 220 restaurants, of which 80% are franchised. The CEO Annick Van Overstraeten announces in 2025 the intention to open up to 100 restaurants in India.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

### Tasty and nutritious: our “Better Choices”!

![A group of people sit around a table in a cozy restaurant, talking and smiling. One woman in the center gestures while speaking, and another in a striped shirt listens beside her. Dishes, glasses, and menus are on the table.](https://www.datocms-assets.com/138964/1732694639-guillaumezha_lpq_tcsuprisedelight-65.jpeg?auto=format&fit=max&w=3840&q=75)

### Relationships forged around a communal table

Our first communal table on Rue Dansaert in Brussels was made out of wood recovered from the floors of Belgian trains that had been taken out of service. Those simple planks became a tradition. Today, this same rough, reclaimed wood continues to bring rustic comfort to our restaurants, and the communal tables have become our centerpieces. We believe that the community is what nurtures, inspires, and feeds the soul. Our tables are long enough for all to fit and narrow enough for all to talk; they are where friends reconnect, and new friendships, relationships, and career paths are forged over the shared appreciation of delicious food and good company.  For every new table, the old wood is planed and sanded until it feels completely smooth, and the surface only gets better after years of guests’ hands touching it and hosts cleaning it.

[Read article](/us/en/magazines/relationships-forged-around-our-communal-table)

![A man in a blue shirt stands smiling in a rustic kitchen, holding a bowl. Pots and pans hang overhead, and vegetables, bottles, and kitchen tools fill the shelves and counter around him.](https://www.datocms-assets.com/138964/1728645749-20170711lepainquotidien15775_2500.jpg?auto=format&fit=max&w=3840&q=75)

### Our History

Alain Coumont learned the beauty of baking when he was just a little boy. Too small to reach the counter, his aunt Simone would pull a chair over for Alain to stand on so he could watch her make the dough for bread. On Sundays, they’d bake, not just loaves and boules, but a dozen tarts too. His taste for baking up happiness reaches far back into the legacy of his past. Alain’s mother’s parents owned a restaurant near Liège in Belgium, and his father trained as a chef. Alain even studied at the same hotel school that his father attended in Namur, Belgium. He followed in their footsteps until it was time to mark his own path.

**Philz Coffee** is an American [coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee "Coffee") company and [coffeehouse chain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_coffeehouse_chains "List of coffeehouse chains") based in [San Francisco, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco,_California "San Francisco, California"), which helped popularize [third wave coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_wave_of_coffee "Third wave of coffee").[[2]](#cite_note-2)[*[dubious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Accuracy_dispute#Disputed_statement "Wikipedia:Accuracy dispute") – [discuss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Philz_Coffee#Dubious "Talk:Philz Coffee")*] Philz Coffee focuses on making pour over [coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee "Coffee"). Philz Coffee has locations spread throughout the [San Francisco Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area"), greater [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego"), [Sacramento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento,_California "Sacramento, California"), and [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"). Philz was founded by Phil Jaber and his son Jacob, both of whom are located in the San Francisco area.

In addition to coffee and drinks, Philz also sells merchandise and bagged coffee blends for purchase online.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Philz_Coffee&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Phil Jaber, born in [Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_American "Palestinian American"),[[4]](#cite_note-SavorGood-4) and his son Jacob founded Philz Coffee in 2003. Phil operated a corner grocery in San Francisco's [Mission District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_District,_San_Francisco "Mission District, San Francisco") for over 25 years and had strong ties to the community.[[5]](#cite_note-5) Phil's son, Jacob Jaber, later assumed the role of CEO and built the company from a single store to nearly 70 locations across the United States. In 2021, Jacob and Phil stepped away from the day to day operations of the company. [[6]](#cite_note-6)

Philz Coffee secured a round of funding in 2013 by [Summit Partners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit_Partners "Summit Partners")[[7]](#cite_note-7) and a few private investors to expand into new markets, leading to the first Philz Coffee outside the [Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area") in [Santa Monica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Monica,_California "Santa Monica, California") California.[[8]](#cite_note-8) In February 2015 they secured a $15M Series B round to help them expand in the United States.[[9]](#cite_note-9) In September 2016, they closed a $45M Series C round from San Francisco-based [private equity firm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_equity_firm "Private equity firm") [TPG Growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TPG_Capital "TPG Capital") to continue the expansion.[[10]](#cite_note-10) In August 2025, Philz was acquired by private equity firm Freeman Spogli & Co. for $145 million.[[11]](#cite_note-SFStandard-Takeover-11)

## Locations

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Philz_Coffee&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Locations")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Philz_Coffee_-_24th-Folsom_-_SF%2C_CA.jpg/250px-Philz_Coffee_-_24th-Folsom_-_SF%2C_CA.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Philz_Coffee_-_24th-Folsom_-_SF,_CA.jpg)

Original Philz Coffee Location in San Francisco, CA

From its origins in San Francisco, investor funding allowed Philz to expand its presence to include southern California, Chicago, and the [District of Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_of_Columbia "District of Columbia"), [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland"), and [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia") (DMV) area.[[12]](#cite_note-Eater-FilterOut-12) However, in 2022, Philz began closing some of its retail locations. The first stores to close were located in the DMV area, and by the beginning of 2023 the company had exited the region, citing "business conditions".[[12]](#cite_note-Eater-FilterOut-12) As of August 2025, Philz Coffee has 79 locations, entirely in California and Chicago.[[1]](#cite_note-MissionLocal-EmployeePayments-1)[[13]](#cite_note-13)

In October 2023, the company also closed its original location in the Mission District of San Francisco. The store lead, Chris Watts, stated that the closure followed a decision not to renew the location's lease.[[14]](#cite_note-14) However, the staff of the Mission location has stated that the building was in a state of disrepair and that the store needed to find a more modern location.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

In January 2024, the company announced that it was moving its corporate headquarters to Oakland, CA from its original location in the Dogpatch neighborhood of San Francisco.[[16]](#cite_note-16)

## Products

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Philz_Coffee&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Products  ")]

### Popular drinks

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Philz_Coffee&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Popular drinks")]

Philz Coffee’s menu is based around [drip coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drip_coffee "Drip coffee"), as they do not sell espresso.

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Philz_Mint_Mojito_Coffee_1_2017-04-10.jpg/250px-Philz_Mint_Mojito_Coffee_1_2017-04-10.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Philz_Mint_Mojito_Coffee_1_2017-04-10.jpg)

Iced Mint Mojito

The most popular drink at Philz Coffee is the Iced Mint Mojito. It contains a blend of coffee and freshly pressed mint leaves. According to the company’s current CEO, Mahesh Sadarangani, the drink accounts for about 30% of their orders.[[17]](#cite_note-:0-17)

Another popular drink is the Oatmeal Cookie Cold Brew, which was originally a "secret menu item".[[18]](#cite_note-18) Local guides describe the coffee as a mix of hazelnut coffee, cinnamon, and [oat milk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oat_milk "Oat milk").[[17]](#cite_note-:0-17)

Other popular drinks include the [Iced Coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iced_coffee "Iced coffee") Rose, which is a blend of coffee, rose water, and rose petals, and the Mocha Tesora, which contains a chocolate coffee, milk, and [Ghiradelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghirardelli_Chocolate_Company "Ghirardelli Chocolate Company") cocoa powder.[[19]](#cite_note-19)

### Cream and sugar levels

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Philz_Coffee&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Cream and sugar levels")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/San_Francisco_%2826523762079%29.jpg/250px-San_Francisco_%2826523762079%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:San_Francisco_(26523762079).jpg)

Philz Coffee Menu in San Francisco, CA Location

Philz Coffee has their own system of sweetness and milk levels. A "sweet and creamy" coffee contains a normal amount of cream and sugar. A coffee "Philz’s way" contains reduced amounts of cream and sugar. Finally, a "straight up" coffee contains neither cream nor sugar.

Cream options include heavy cream, milk, [almond milk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almond_milk "Almond milk"), and oat milk. Sugar options include granulated sugar, artificial sweeteners, and honey.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

### Merchandise

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Philz_Coffee&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Merchandise")]

In addition to their drinks, Philz Coffee sells a variety of merchandise both in-store and online. Examples include tumblers, hats, shirts and sweatshirts.[[21]](#cite_note-21) In addition, they sell both coffee grounds and [Keurig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keurig "Keurig") pods of their most popular blends as well as Keurig pods for two of their most popular blends.[[22]](#cite_note-22) On their website, they also offer a subscription service for their coffee grounds.[[23]](#cite_note-23)

## Controversies

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Philz_Coffee&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Controversies")]

### Pandemic layoffs

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Philz_Coffee&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Pandemic layoffs")]

During the pandemic, multiple employees from various stores reported Philz to OSHA for workplace violations related to masks and social distancing. Following these reports, Philz Coffee laid off 181 employees across the country. Despite the company claiming that the reports and the layoffs were not related, many people online linked the two events.[[24]](#cite_note-24)

### Police discount firings

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Philz_Coffee&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Police discount firings")]

Following the [George Floyd murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_George_Floyd "Murder of George Floyd"), many employees began protesting Philz Coffee's 20% discount that they offer for law enforcement. This controversy began when a shift lead of the Mission district location posted a story to their social media that captioned, "What's your favorite iced coffee drink, because ours is Arrest the cops that killed [Breonna Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breonna_Taylor "Breonna Taylor")." Following the incident, the shift lead was fired.

On top of protesting the 20% discount for law enforcement, employees also began protesting the placement of police badges on the stores community boards. Although the company allowed each store to decide whether they would allow the placement of these badges, stores reported that it was difficult for them to actually report to the company that they would not allow the placement of badges. In fact, three baristas in the Costa Mesa location (Southern California) tried to remove the badges from their store. As a result, they were all fired for damaging the store.

Many employees stated that the company's pro-police stance created a hostile environment for their black employees. In response to this controversy, the company launched a diversity, equity, and inclusion program.[[25]](#cite_note-25)

### Palestine pins

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Philz_Coffee&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Palestine pins")]

At the end of 2023, five employees were sent home from the Gilman Street location for wearing Pro-Palestine pins. Despite asking for a written statement from management about why the pins were not allowed, the employees never received any information from management. The employees were sent home and the entire staff unionized.[[26]](#cite_note-26)[[27]](#cite_note-27)

### Gluten free class action lawsuit

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Philz_Coffee&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Gluten free class action lawsuit")]

In January 2024, a class action lawsuit was filed against the company for allegedly branding gluten containing products as gluten-free. The plaintiff, Ayaunna Martinez, suffered an allergy attack after consuming a supposedly gluten-free product from a Philz Coffee location. Although the Philz coffee app does state that they cannot guarantee that all products are free of allergens, the lawsuit is seeking that Philz Coffee change its false advertising of their products and pay the members of the lawsuit for damages.[[28]](#cite_note-28)

### Private equity takeover

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Philz_Coffee&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Private equity takeover")]

In August 2025, private equity firm Freeman Spogli & Co. acquired Philz for $145 million. While CEO Mahesh Sadarangani received a payout from the deal, current and former employees who had invested in the company through its [employee stock ownership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Employee_stock_ownership "Employee stock ownership") and [stock option](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Employee_stock_option "Employee stock option") programs saw their [common stock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_stock "Common stock") canceled and rendered worthless.[[11]](#cite_note-SFStandard-Takeover-11)[[29]](#cite_note-29) Initially, Sadarangami had announced that he would be reinvesting part of his windfall into Philz; after local news coverage criticized the deal, he revised his position to reinvest all of his post-tax proceeds. The company subsequently offered current baristas bonuses of $525, with managers receiving larger amounts; the ten former employees affected received no consideration.[[1]](#cite_note-MissionLocal-EmployeePayments-1)

### Pride flag ban

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Philz_Coffee&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Pride flag ban")]

In April 2026, Philz Coffee ordered the removal of all LGBT pride flags from its locations, with the stated reason by CEO Mahesh Sadarangani being to create "a more consistent, inclusive experience across all our stores". This was met with a [change.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Change.org "Change.org") petition started by the chain's baristas, who said that, "Removing these flags risks alienating a core group of team members and loyal customers". The petition reached 4,000 signatures by April 10.[[30]](#cite_note-30)[[31]](#cite_note-31) On April 17, Philz Coffee announced that the change was being scrapped and pride flags would be permitted to remain in stores.[[32]](#cite_note-32)

## About Philz Coffee

Welcome to Philz Coffee, nestled conveniently at 1030 Davis St, Evanston, IL. This unique cafe has transformed the coffee experience into an art form, inviting coffee lovers and casual patrons alike to savor not just a drink, but a moment of bliss. If you haven't yet indulged in their offerings, you're in for a delightful journey through flavors and aromas.

At Philz, every cup is crafted with care. Their medium blends, like the **Silken Splendor** with notes of dark cocoa, citrus, and butterscotch, provide a comforting warmth that dances on your palate. For those craving something darker, the **Jacobs Wonderbar** delivers a rich tapestry of dark chocolate, smoke, and nuts, ideal for a cooler day. Each variety, whether hot or from a 1 LB bag, reveals a commitment to quality and taste that sets Philz apart from typical chain cafes.

The atmosphere in Philz Coffee is just as inviting as the beverages. Customers rave about its cozy vibe, making it an ideal spot for meeting friends or enjoying a solitary moment with your thoughts. One guest, John, perfectly captured this sentiment, highlighting the warm, friendly environment that welcomes both locals and students alike.

It’s not just coffee that shines here; their treats deserve a standing ovation too! The **Mint Mojito**, praised by Shawna Moorad, is a refreshing delight that deftly balances creaminess with a kick of fresh mint. And don’t miss out on the carrot muffin, a perfect companion to your cup of bliss, according to Hailey Kim.

However, every cafe has room for improvement. While some patrons have wished for a reward program to complement their loyalty, the overall customer experience is one of warmth and attentive service. George Zakharia’s review suggests there’s a learning curve with some of their food offerings, indicating that while the flavors are exciting, a little practice may enhance your enjoyment.

So, if you're in Evanston or merely passing through, make Philz Coffee a stop. Immerse yourself in the rich variety of their brews and let the friendly faces of the baristas elevate your coffee game. There's a world of flavor waiting for you, and it’s as much about the coffee as it is about the connections you make over these magical cups. Cheers to new experiences!

The Food Institute News Envelope Icon TikTok News, Data, and Trends Since 1928 Why Apple May Be Fall’s Safest Flavor Choice Pumpkin spice season may have kicked off earlier than ever , but that doesn’t necessarily mean that it’s the undisputed king of the fall flavor charts – especially not when apple is in the running. According to Datassential, 87% of consumers either love or like apple, compared with just 59% for pumpkin and 47% for pumpkin spice. “Apple also carries a polarity score of just 17, versus 94 for pumpkin and 99 for pumpkin spice, meaning apple appeals to a much wider audience,” said Ian O’Neil, director of consumer intelligence for Rubix Foods. O’Neil told FI that August has historically been the busiest month for apple LTO activity, while September has been peak pumpkin season. “Across top national chains, there were 47 new or limited-time menu items featuring apple flavors in August alone, a nearly 60% increase from August 2025, according to Datassential. Of those 47 apple introductions, 70% were beverages,” O’Neil explained. O’Neil cited multiple examples of recent launches exemplifying the flavor trend, including: Krispy Kreme’s new line of Apple Crisp beverages Wendy’s limited-edition Apple Crumble Frosty McDonald’s two new Caramel Apple Pie drinks “Every fall, it feels like pumpkin spice shows up just about everywhere,” said Andy Mai, chief business officer at Philz Coffee, which just launched an Apple Cinnamon Roll flavor of cold brew. “We’ve always done things a little differently. This year, we looked to classic and beloved fall flavors. They’re familiar and nostalgic, yet not something our customers can get everywhere else,” Mai told FI. On the F&B retail side, OLIPOP recently unveiled a Caramel Apple LTO, with just 5 grams of sugar. Additionally, Hiyo launched a limited-edition RTD Apple Cinnamon flavor of its alcohol-free ‘social tonic’ beverage, which the brand’s co-founder and chief retail officer George Youmans described as “a delicious invitation to slow down after summer, get cozy with those you hold close, and celebrate the holidays with more connection, presence, and intentionality.” “Apple and cinnamon have always been synonymous with that cozy time of year as temperatures drop and seasons change,” Youmans told FI. Apples to Apples O’Neil told FI that Rubix Foods has also noticed that brands are getting more specific about the types of apple they’re using as a way to “make a very familiar flavor feel more distinctive.” He highlighted the following examples: Cracker Barrel’s new Granny Smith Apple Tea Peet’s Coffee & Tea’s green apple energy drink Caribou’s new line of Honeycrisp apple beverages Rubix has been tracking renewed interest in apple for several years now, according to O’Neil. “Our 2025 fall flavor research showed that apple butter, apple cider, and apple cinnamon were the top three flavors consumers were most excited to see on menus, ahead of profiles like brown sugar, cinnamon roll, and maple,” he explained. Speaking of apple butter, I recently used Monin’s Caramel Apple Butter syrup to whip up some Italian sodas for my friends, which were a big hit. “Apple cinnamon was particularly strong with Gen Z, with 50% naming it a go-to fall flavor. Cinnamon works especially well alongside apple because it immediately adds the warmth and familiarity consumers associate with fall, while still giving brands flexibility in how they bring the flavor to life,” O’Neil said. As restaurant traffic continues to soften, O’Neil feels differentiated innovation must be a key focus for brands looking to drive incremental visits. “Apple gives operators an interesting advantage because it combines seasonal relevance with unusually broad consumer appeal. At a time when brands need innovation to attract traffic without alienating their core customer, that makes apple a relatively safe platform to build around.” Share this article Like this? **Heart Coffee Roasters** is a small specialty coffee roasting company with cafes in [Portland, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon"), United States. It was established in 2009 by Wille and Rebekah Yli-Luoma.

## Description and history

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Heart_Coffee_Roasters&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Description and history")]

Wille and Rebekah Yli-Luoma opened Heart in 2009.[[1]](#cite_note-McIntyre-1)[[2]](#cite_note-CNT-2) Heart's original location, known as the Eastside Cafe, is located at 2211 [East Burnside Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnside_Street "Burnside Street") in Portland's [Kerns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerns,_Portland,_Oregon "Kerns, Portland, Oregon") neighborhood.[[2]](#cite_note-CNT-2) Its second location, known as the Westside Cafe, opened in 2013 and is located at 537 Southwest 12th Avenue in [downtown Portland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Portland "Downtown Portland")'s West End.[[3]](#cite_note-TP-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Locations-4) Another location operates in [southeast Portland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Portland,_Oregon "Southeast Portland, Oregon")'s [Woodstock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock,_Portland,_Oregon "Woodstock, Portland, Oregon") neighborhood.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

## Reception

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Heart_Coffee_Roasters&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Reception")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1e/Barista_%28Heart_Roasters%29.jpg/250px-Barista_%28Heart_Roasters%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Barista_(Heart_Roasters).jpg)

Heart [barista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barista "Barista") preparing a cappuccino

*[Condé Nast Traveler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condé_Nast_Traveler "Condé Nast Traveler")* called Heart's drinks "uncommonly clean and complex and said, "[Chemex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemex_Coffeemaker "Chemex Coffeemaker")- and [Aeropress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AeroPress "AeroPress")-brewed '[pour-over](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brewed_coffee "Brewed coffee")' coffees are perhaps the best way to sample the results, though espresso drinks are excellent here, too."[[2]](#cite_note-CNT-2)

In 2013, Dan Gentile of [Thrillist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrillist_Media_Group "Thrillist Media Group") included Heart in his list of "The Top 10 Coffee Roasters in the Nation, as Voted by Super-Serious Coffee Nerds".[[6]](#cite_note-6) He also included Heart in his 2016 list of "The 21 Best Coffee Roasters in the Country", writing: "Portland isn't in short supply of sleekly designed coffee shops, but in addition to a design sense that would make a Scandinavian proud, Heart's coffee shop is literally built around a functioning black Probat roaster that fills the space with the smell of not-too-light, and definitely not-too-dark coffees."[[7]](#cite_note-Gentile-7)

In 2016, Eater.com's Emily McIntyre included Heart on her list of the "20 of the Best Coffee Shops in Portland". She wrote:

> Few cafes have such a strong aesthetic and presentation as Heart on Burnside. Enter and think yourself lucky, because the rare espresso machine (currently Kees van der Westen), the expansive, simple menu, the beast of a vintage coffee roaster, and the 'do not touch signs' have the effect of creating an exclusive experience... While I recommend any seasonal drink here (and the summertime paleo affogato is delicious), my go-to at Heart is a cup of drip coffee.[[1]](#cite_note-McIntyre-1)

# Coffee Guide: Heart Coffee Roasters

by [CuisineBonneFemme](https://portlandfoodanddrink.com/author/cuisine-bonne-femme/)

[![Heart Coffee Roaster Portland](https://portlandfoodanddrink.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/04/Heart-3-303x450.jpg "Heart Coffee Roaster")](https://portlandfoodanddrink.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/04/Heart-3.jpg)

Heart Coffee Roasters. Photos ©Tim Roth, Pupil Photo

Things you don’t need to know about Heart Coffee Roasters, but I’m going to tell you anyway: Owner Wille Yli-Luoma is Finnish, and he’s a well-regarded pro-snowboarder. Why does this matter? It adds to the distinctive personality that is Heart Coffee. He has a Finnish sensibility around nature and science, combined with a professional sportsman’s intensity.

“I don’t believe in iced coffee,” Yli-Luoma says to me immediately when I ask if he is planning anything iced for the summer. Then he goes on to tell me iced coffee – including the popular toddy and cold brew drip processes – ruins the oils and does not bring out the delicate flavors and aromas found in good roasts. He’s adamant that his coffee is treated more like tea, gently, and with a ritualistic precision, in both roasting and beverage making.

Yli-Luoma works carefully with the beans in each batch, keeping the flavors more on the juice and berry side, and adjusting accordingly. This brings out nuances other roasters would be wise to think about, but they are sometimes an acquired taste. Heart is of the lighter roast school, which isn’t everyone’s cup of amber, but certainly has its fans for a more delicate coffee-tasting experience. The *New York Times* [called Heart](http://www.nytimes.com/2012/02/12/travel/portlands-purist-coffee-scene.html) “…advanced coffee…”

Heart Coffee Roaster’s approach is obsessive, but this obsession does produce an outstanding product that is often both complex and more accessible than some other “rougher” roasts. To me, Heart’s roasts are more floral, delicate, and layered than some others in town. Four roasts are usually available at any given time, along with a decaf roast. On their website, Heart sticks to the basic facts of each coffee, listing location, farm, altitude, varietal, and processing. The product descriptions are one-line and to the point. Under Rwanda Coko, for example, it simply states, “Cherry, hibiscus, milk chocolate”, while a batch of Guatemala El Limonar reads, “Milk chocolate, peach, lemon, honey”. No thesis statements or marketing spin here.

Yli-Luoma is less a mystic and more into the science, botany, and art of coffee. He’s entirely friendly and accessible and was more than willing to share his knowledge and spend an enormous amount of time chatting with me, even though I showed up at the café unannounced. He loves what he does.

The café itself is austere but comfortable. I’d call it Scandinavian Zen, although it does have seating, WiFi, teas, cookies, and toast, and all the other café comforts. But still, the coffee is the focus here, with the roaster itself taking center stage in the middle of the café.  And yes, Coffee is available by the siphon method. Just don’t ask for iced coffee.

Heart is sold at their roastery/café, a few local cafes such as Red E on N. Killingsworth, a handful of restaurants, and on their website. A second small café is now open within [West End Bikes](http://westendbikespdx.com/) on 11th and SW Stark.

I like Heart because of its distinctive personality and balance between art and science. They are pushing the envelope and challenging consumers to taste and experience coffee in new ways, putting it all together to make a consistently stellar product.

* **Address 3**: 5181 SE Woodstock Blvd, Portland, OR 97206
* **Website**: [HeartRoasters.com](http://heartroasters.com)

### *Related*

#### About CuisineBonneFemme

Lizzy writes about the types of food she likes to cook the most; simple dishes based on the freshest ingredients and gently coaxed to bring out their best qualities. Things like roast chicken with crackling skin, meat stews, all kinds of soups, and anything on toast. You know, peasant food like your French/Southern/Thai/Lebanese Mother might make.

In her past she held many a food service job, from a high-end traditional Japanese restaurant to a grease-pit diner off of Interstate 5. And she claims to still have nasty case of espresso wrist from the 10 billion lattes she made during her barista years.

Lizzy has an educational background that includes food sciences and politics, and has been a past writer for both cultural and academic publications. She takes a big picture view of the role that all things gastronomic are having in shaping the economy, culture, identity, and ever changing food scene both here and elsewhere. She believes Portland is at a pivotal and creative time food wise, and is constantly amazed and surprised at the bounty our city has to offer.

## Reader Interactions

### Comments

1. ej says

   I appreciated the review, thank you!

   But, I can’t leave without commenting about one small detail of the piece:

   Wille Yli-Luoma may well have a Scandinavian sensibility (as might a person of any nationality or ethnicity), but if he is a Finn he is probably not a Scandinavian himself, as the author implies. “Scandinavian” is a term used to describe the peoples and languages of Norway, Sweden, and Denmark. Finland is not part of Scandinavia, and the Finnish language is unrelated to the Scandinavian languages. (Though there are many Finns who are ethnically Swedish, which complicates this whole matter!)

   I mention this only to help clarify a muddy issue that is often confused — I definitely don’t intend the author to feel harshly corrected or criticized.

   Thanks again for the review!

   * bhodda ba'aag says

     Sisu!
2. [Kacie](http://gorgeinthegorge.com/) says

   I love Heart and listed them on my website recently (<http://gorgeinthegorge.com/>) under Drink.. Coffee. They are such a treat for me when I make it to Portland. AND their mugs are the best.
3. James says

   you’re right when you say it’s not for everyone. i am definitely not a fan of most of their coffees. the space is too sterile for me. feels like i am sitting in IKEA.

**Heart Coffee Roasters** is a small specialty coffee roasting company with cafes in [Portland, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon"), United States. It was established in 2009 by Wille and Rebekah Yli-Luoma.

## Description and history

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Heart_Coffee_Roasters&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Description and history")]

Wille and Rebekah Yli-Luoma opened Heart in 2009.[[1]](#cite_note-McIntyre-1)[[2]](#cite_note-CNT-2) Heart's original location, known as the Eastside Cafe, is located at 2211 [East Burnside Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnside_Street "Burnside Street") in Portland's [Kerns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerns,_Portland,_Oregon "Kerns, Portland, Oregon") neighborhood.[[2]](#cite_note-CNT-2) Its second location, known as the Westside Cafe, opened in 2013 and is located at 537 Southwest 12th Avenue in [downtown Portland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Portland "Downtown Portland")'s West End.[[3]](#cite_note-TP-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Locations-4) Another location operates in [southeast Portland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Portland,_Oregon "Southeast Portland, Oregon")'s [Woodstock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock,_Portland,_Oregon "Woodstock, Portland, Oregon") neighborhood.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

## Reception

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Heart_Coffee_Roasters&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Reception")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1e/Barista_%28Heart_Roasters%29.jpg/250px-Barista_%28Heart_Roasters%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Barista_(Heart_Roasters).jpg)

Heart [barista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barista "Barista") preparing a cappuccino

*[Condé Nast Traveler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condé_Nast_Traveler "Condé Nast Traveler")* called Heart's drinks "uncommonly clean and complex and said, "[Chemex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemex_Coffeemaker "Chemex Coffeemaker")- and [Aeropress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AeroPress "AeroPress")-brewed '[pour-over](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brewed_coffee "Brewed coffee")' coffees are perhaps the best way to sample the results, though espresso drinks are excellent here, too."[[2]](#cite_note-CNT-2)

In 2013, Dan Gentile of [Thrillist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrillist_Media_Group "Thrillist Media Group") included Heart in his list of "The Top 10 Coffee Roasters in the Nation, as Voted by Super-Serious Coffee Nerds".[[6]](#cite_note-6) He also included Heart in his 2016 list of "The 21 Best Coffee Roasters in the Country", writing: "Portland isn't in short supply of sleekly designed coffee shops, but in addition to a design sense that would make a Scandinavian proud, Heart's coffee shop is literally built around a functioning black Probat roaster that fills the space with the smell of not-too-light, and definitely not-too-dark coffees."[[7]](#cite_note-Gentile-7)

In 2016, Eater.com's Emily McIntyre included Heart on her list of the "20 of the Best Coffee Shops in Portland". She wrote:

> Few cafes have such a strong aesthetic and presentation as Heart on Burnside. Enter and think yourself lucky, because the rare espresso machine (currently Kees van der Westen), the expansive, simple menu, the beast of a vintage coffee roaster, and the 'do not touch signs' have the effect of creating an exclusive experience... While I recommend any seasonal drink here (and the summertime paleo affogato is delicious), my go-to at Heart is a cup of drip coffee.[[1]](#cite_note-McIntyre-1)

# Heart Coffee Roasters

[Featured Coffee Shops](/featured-coffee-shop/category/Featured%20Coffee%20Shops)

Written by [Jeff Newton](/featured-coffee-shop?author=565f2ba4e4b0731886040230)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475782318753-M3G4OWDNF2KWZX1Y46FH/image-asset.jpeg)

I had the privilege of visiting both the east and west side locations of [Heart Coffee Roasters](http://www.heartroasters.com) in Portland mid last year. Their coffee is served in multiple shops throughout Los Angeles and beyond so I'm familiar with and have purchased their coffee for at home brewing. I love using their coffee's in my Aeropress while on the road - and Chemex while at home.

## Part 1. Westside

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475782524931-I04YJZFEX06SC3IRPGLH/image-asset.jpeg)

I started my day off at their Westside location in the downtown area of Portland. A sick looking shop with beautiful natural light coming in those huge windows. The photographer in me wanted to shoot natural light portaits in there all day long.

![newton_150318_9999.jpg]() ![newton_150318_0101.jpg]() ![newton_150318_0014.jpg]()

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475782770049-BTSQ1KC3UX4RUHLYUKZZ/image-asset.jpeg)

[View fullsize ![newton_150318_0027.jpg]()](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475800148381-OG1SRHJ2VDARJZ8E7XGM/newton_150318_0027.jpg)

[View fullsize ![newton_150318_0068.jpg]()](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475800150484-LBBMPYBMGHTXN7HAFLAG/newton_150318_0068.jpg)

[View fullsize ![newton_150318_0136.jpg]()](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475800152514-7JKVB457HEFBBQXN4VVT/newton_150318_0136.jpg)

Some of the Westside Crew doing their thing.

![The amazing selection of food trucks just a few blocks away led to a nice lunch break for not only the baristas but also myself. ](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475800042962-6J7APRAJZ9MI4YBAFO8I/image-asset.jpeg)

The amazing selection of food trucks just a few blocks away led to a nice lunch break for not only the baristas but also myself.

## Part 2. Eastside

After lunch, I made my way over to their original Eastside location, that up until recently also served as their main roasting operations. They now have a roasting facility that looks impressive from the few photo's I've seen of it online.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475800320156-1ZSVO2KHIHA1P21GKO0W/image-asset.jpeg)

[Heart](http://www.heartroasters.com) was founded by Wille and Rebekah Yli-Luoma in 2009. Wille was a professional snowboarder who started roasting at home - was rocking out some amazing coffee and BOOM [Heart](http://www.heartroasters.com) was born. Ok, I skipped a few steps in the timeline but you get the point. They're doing their thing and doing it well.

Unfortunately, I wasn't able to meet either of them in person. Rebekah was out on maternity leave and Wille was roasting while I was shooting. But lets' just say that that dude was so focused - never even looked my way - that I didn't get the vibe that he wanted to be disturbed. It was only after he left that I found out he was the co founder from one of the baristas.

They even have a sign above their [Probat](http://www.probat.com/en/roasters/probat-roaster/passion/) that says, "Please do not disturb the roaster operator". And I didn't. Ha.

![Wille doing his thing, rocking out some sick coffee - even the bearded dude to the right is eyeing that coffee saying, ](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475827322745-7ITSU3EXWF6I16ORDH8I/image-asset.jpeg)

Wille doing his thing, rocking out some sick coffee - even the bearded dude to the right is eyeing that coffee saying, "Gimme that coffee"

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475827446658-RERRF63OL0MK0STAC2Y5/image-asset.jpeg)

![Check out that blue/purple flame from the roaster. So sick. ](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475827471291-9BURASDJR2OW3SVOVZ6N/image-asset.jpeg)

Check out that blue/purple flame from the roaster. So sick.

![Shooting the cafe behind me through reflections/items on the bookshelf](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475828046225-1TSGZQSYCQCJ9C58EIV8/image-asset.jpeg)

Shooting the cafe behind me through reflections/items on the bookshelf

![newton_150318_0191.jpg]() ![newton_150318_0193.jpg]() ![newton_150318_0199.jpg]() ![newton_150318_0189.jpg]()

![I loved the lighting in both of their locations](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475828013762-9UI6IYCYGQKXGR3TKZNX/image-asset.jpeg)

I loved the lighting in both of their locations

[View fullsize ![newton_150318_0255.jpg]()](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475827786041-N1UOXMMDLIBIAHV4YR7N/newton_150318_0255.jpg)

[View fullsize ![newton_150318_0297.jpg]()](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57011ac64d088e778102bd66/1475827793416-VQZXJL81LDLBW56YKRLK/newton_150318_0297.jpg)

The Westside crew rockin' out in that beautiful light.

Lastly, I want to apologize to both Wille and Rebkah for the delay in getting this post out. I am grateful to you both for allowing me to feature Heart on this site, so I appreciate your patience.

## OUR STORY

heart’s doors opened in 2009 with the idea that a great cup should highlight the distinct fruit flavors that are found in coffee. Built from the love to innovate and create an exceptional coffee experience, heart is owned and operated by Rebekah & Wille Yli-Luoma.

With 2 retail cafés & a roasting facility located in Portland, Oregon, we strive to provide a positive, comfortable, supportive & safe workplace for our employees.

We believe this type of environment is necessary in order to provide excellent customer service & hospitality.

Our hope is to foster a community space that is welcoming all humans--regardless of race, ethnicity, cultural or religious practices, sexual orientation & gender identification.

\*\*When visiting our cafes, you may find we do not have WiFi. You are welcome to use your hot spot, but our intention with this is to support a more unplugged environment for our guests.

![Farmer standing with coffee plant]()

## DIRECT RELATIONSHIPS

Over the last 14 years, we’ve been building relationships with producers in Kenya, Ethiopia, Colombia, Honduras, Mexico, Brazil & Guatemala.

We visit the farming partners we purchase coffee from throughout the year, maintaining a healthy working relationship built on open communication, trust and respect.

Our goal is to provide financial stability to our farming partners, so that our relationships will last and be mutually sustainable.

heart is in it for the long-run. We want to be sure our partners feel good about the relationship they have with us.

## SEASONAL COFFEE

We secure green coffee during its peak time of the year. This is referred to as ‘seasonal’ or ‘current crop’ buying. Being an agricultural product; there are specific growing, picking and processing seasons for each type of coffee.

We believe the coffee's vibrancy is most apparent when it is fresh. heart travels to origin during and at the end of harvest times to show support, assist with quality control and select the best crops.

[*Read our most recent & detailed Transparency Report*](https://www.heartroasters.com/pages/2022-transparency-report "https://www.heartroasters.com/pages/2022-transparency-report")*.*

[SHOP BEANS](/collections/beans)

![man holding two bags of coffee cherries.]()

![]()

## COFFEE PURCHASING

Producing a high quality product requires high quality ingredients.

heart has a reputation for sourcing some of the best green coffee in the world.

In coffee purchasing, the term FOB stands for “Free On Board,” and refers to the prices negotiated by us and the producers in-country.

FOB includes services such as milling, packaging, and anything else until the coffee is ready for export.

We take these costs into account when negotiating prices with our producer and export partners. The cost of coffee on a global level is dictated by the Commodity Market or “C-Market.”

The quality of coffee that heart works with is not affected by C-Market pricing.

## PRODUCT

Our goal is to roast consistent, user-friendly coffee, so that brewing is easy and enjoyable.

We buy exceptional coffee from growers who care deeply about their crops. Treating the coffee with care is important to us.

Because of this, we do not label our coffee as light, medium or dark roast coffee. Our focus is to roast the coffee *evenly* without any roast byproducts.

All of our offerings have a specific roast profile that highlights the clarity of flavors within each coffee.

During the roasting process, we focus on even development throughout the bean, maximizing sweetness, without over-roasting uneven roasting or baking the coffee dry.

This style of roasting results in pronounced sweetness & fruit tones with a juicy finish.

Every bag of heart coffee is tagged with a roast date and batch number.

The batch # directly relates to a specific roast in our database, which was tested for quality.

Any roast batches that do not meet our standards of quality are donated to the local food bank.

We do not compromise quality, so that you can enjoy the best we have to offer.

[SHOP COFFEE](/collections/beans)

![]()

![]()

## BREWING AND CONNECTING

Improper brewing is the most common mistake resulting in an unpleasant cup of coffee.

Here are a few tips to making a good one:

*• Freshly roasted coffee*  
*• A burr grinder (we do not recommend blade grinders, as they produce uneven grounds)*  
*• Filtered water*  
*• Digital Scale*  
*• Proper coffee to water ratio (1 to 16)*  
*• Oxidized coffee filters (we do not recommend brown filters, as they taint the flavors of coffee)*

If you have further questions, we welcome you to give us a call, stop by our cafes, or email us.

We want to help you brew the best coffee you can at home!

# Photo Menu: Heart Coffee Roasters

---

[Cafe](https://lamarzoccousa.com/news/blog/category/cafe/)

02/20/2017

![Wille & Rebekah](https://lamarzoccousa.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/WilleRebekah.jpg)

On Valentine’s Day, we welcomed [Heart Coffee Roasters](https://srv/users/lamarzoccousa/apps/lamarzoccousa/public.heartroasters.com/) from Portland, OR, our 10th Partner in Residence to the La Marzocco Cafe. As is the case each time a new Roaster takes over, we reorganized the bar and dialed-in our equipment to make coffee the same way it would be prepared at Heart’s cafes in Portland, and implemented a completely new menu.

Heart’s motivation behind coffee is simple and is on full display at the Cafe: uncompromising quality aimed at bringing guests a focused and exceptional experience. Heart’s founder, Wille Yli-Luoma, started the company after much experimentation as a home roaster. Over time, he began to appreciate the coffee he was roasting at home more than what he was experiencing elsewhere. Wanting to share that appreciation with others, he decided to start Heart Roasters. Eight months after launching, Wille’s wife Rebekah jumped in to help out where she could and has been there ever since—together they now run the business.

Wille says he roasts his coffee, “so you can taste where the coffee comes from.” He roasts on the lighter end of the spectrum and always uses washed coffees. Wet process, or washed coffee, is a method of processing coffee where the fruit and pulp covering the coffee seed is completely removed before being dried.

Heart boasts an impressive selection of Single Origin coffees across their menu. The La Marzocco Cafe will rotate through these, and will serve each two ways—as espresso and as drip coffee off of the Fetco batch brewer.

One coffee we’re particularly excited about bringing to the Cafe is Colombia La Morelia. Harvested just five months ago by coffee Producer Miller Walles, this limited-edition microlot has juicy acidity with molasses, pomegranate and rose notes.

Leaning heavily on single origin coffees and the unique flavors each possess, Heart has just one coffee blend on their menu–Stereo Seasonal Blend. Heart uses Stereo as the default coffee for all their milk-based drinks, including macchiatos, cappuccinos and lattes. Stereo is a great choice for guests who are looking to drink espresso with rich, chocolatey flavors and lower acidity.

Guests will find a Seasonal Special on Heart’s menu–their Honey Cardamom Latte. It includes steamed milk, Stereo espresso, raw honey and cardamom. Try this for something sweet and satisfying.

Heart’s take on the Mocha combines espresso, steamed milk and a chocolate syrup made with cocoa powder, Madagascar vanilla beans, Himalayan pink salt and chocolate bitters. The steamed milk is poured into a dusting of cocoa powder that makes for a beautiful presentation.

The Heart Chocolate is a coffee-free option that is made by melting Valrhona chocolate ganache into hot water, half and half cream, and steamed milk.

For tea enthusiasts, Heart’s menu offers two selections from [renowned](https://songtea.com/) [Song Tea](https://songtea.com/): Fragrant Leaf–a rich green tea with the scent of sweet grass and honey, and Carrot–a botanical tea with dried carrots, ginger, cinnamon and burdock.

Finally, Friday’s just got even sweeter at the cafe. In addition to our regular (and free!) Coffee Tastings at 10 am, Heart’s menu will include a selection of [General Porpoise Doughnuts](https://srv/users/lamarzoccousa/apps/lamarzoccousa/public.gpdoughnuts.com/) each Friday during their Residence.

Heart will be serving their menu at the La Marzocco Cafe through March 20, 2017. Be sure to come by to get a taste of Portland here in Seattle. To view the full menu, head [here](https://lamarzoccousa.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/02/Heart-Menu-for-La-Marzocco-Final.pdf).
